text:
WHY INDIA LOST THE AI RACE

In 2025, American organisations released 59 notable AI models, Chinese organisations released 35, and South Korea released 8. India did not make the list. That count comes from the Stanford AI Index 2026, and it is the cleanest single number for where India stands in the part of AI that decides who owns the technology.

The money tells the same story. By Stanford's count, American private AI funding hit $285.9 billion in 2025. China was at $12.4 billion, the UK at $5.9 billion, and India at $4.09 billion, behind France and Canada. Four American companies, Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft and Meta, have guided to between $720 billion and $740 billion of capital spending in 2026 alone, most of it for AI data centres. India's entire national AI mission is roughly $1.2 billion spread over five years.

What lost actually means

India has not lost at using AI. It is one of the biggest user bases for ChatGPT, Gemini and other assistants, ranked number two worldwide for GitHub AI contributions according to figures the government cites, and third in Stanford's Global AI Vibrancy ranking from November 2025.

What India lost, or is losing on its current path, is narrower and more important. It is the race to train frontier foundation models, to own the compute those models run on, to produce the research that moves the frontier, and to keep the economic rent that comes from all three. In that race the finalists are the United States and China. Everyone else, including India, Europe, Japan and the Gulf, is deciding how dependent they are willing to be on those two.

India still benefits from AI. It just pays for intelligence rather than selling it, while the margins, platform control and strategic leverage sit elsewhere.

The model scoreboard

Look at who trains frontier models. In the US, OpenAI, Google DeepMind, Anthropic, Meta and xAI each train systems on clusters measured in hundreds of thousands of accelerators. In China, DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen team, ByteDance, Moonshot, Zhipu, Baidu and others ship competitive open and closed models on a cadence of months. Stanford also finds the US and China now trade the top spot: in March 2026 the best American model was ahead of the best Chinese one by only about 2.7 percent on the Arena leaderboard. In 2025 alone, OpenAI was credited with 20 notable models, Google with 14 and Alibaba with 11.

India's list looks different. Sarvam AI released Sarvam 1, a 2 billion parameter model, in October 2024. In May 2025 it released Sarvam-M, a 24 billion parameter model built on top of Mistral Small from France. Uptake on Hugging Face in the first days was tiny, and a prominent Silicon Valley investor publicly called it embarrassing, a view he later revised. In February 2026, at the India AI Impact Summit in New Delhi, Sarvam unveiled 30B and 105B mixture-of-experts models trained from scratch in India on IndiaAI Mission compute, and open-sourced them in March 2026. The 30B model activates about 1 billion parameters per token and was pre-trained on roughly 16 trillion tokens. The 105B model has a 128,000 token context window.

That is real progress. But a 105B open-weight MoE model in early 2026 is roughly where leading Chinese labs were with open releases more than a year earlier. Sarvam's own claim is that the model is competitive for its class and leads on Indian language benchmarks, not that it is at the frontier.

The government's other flagship is BharatGen, an IIT Bombay led consortium, whose launched outputs include Param2 at 17B parameters, a 7B vision-language model called Patram, and a speech recognition model, Shrutam-2. https://t.co/98us7uZMFA has a 5B speech-to-speech model. Under the IndiaAI Mission's call for proposals, 506 applications were received and 20 foundation model proposals were picked for support, 12 large multimodal models and 8 small language models. Many of the outputs listed in an August 2026 Lok Sabha reply are in the 40 million to 17 billion parameter range.

Small, efficient, Indic-tuned systems will matter for voice, government services and cheap deployment. But useful and frontier are different categories. India has many teams building the first and none building the second.

Compute is the race

Frontier AI since 2020 has been, above everything else, a compute race. Capability rises predictably with more compute, data and parameters, and the labs that believed this early and could pay for it pulled ahead.

The IndiaAI Mission's compute pillar is its most visible success. As of the latest PIB release, 38,231 GPUs have been onboarded from 14 empanelled providers, offered to startups and academia at an average subsidised rate of around Rs 65 per GPU hour. By August 2026, 15 compute providers had been empanelled over four rounds, 237 projects had been approved, and 93.18 lakh GPU hours had been sanctioned. A purchase order has also gone out for a government AI compute system of about 1.1 exaflops at the NIC data centre in Delhi.

Compare that with the frontier. Roughly 38,000 GPUs spread across many providers and hundreds of projects is a national pool. A single American lab's training cluster can be several times that, concentrated in one place, with fast interconnect and a single engineering team optimising it for months. And 93.18 lakh GPU hours, about 9.3 million, sounds large until you divide it by 237 projects. The average works out to under 40,000 GPU hours per project. A frontier pre-training run consumes tens of millions of GPU hours on its own, before experiments, failed runs, post-training and inference.

The distribution model is the deeper issue. India chose a voucher system: pool capacity from private operators such as Yotta, subsidise it, and let many teams apply. That lowers the cost floor for startups. It is not how frontier models are built. Frontier labs own or exclusively lease their clusters and run them continuously. Spreading a small pool thinly guarantees many medium experiments and no large ones.

India also does not make any of the hardware. Every accelerator in the IndiaAI pool is imported, mostly from Nvidia. The government's own answer to Parliament says plainly that the compute ecosystem draws on globally sourced GPUs. That leaves India exposed to supply allocation, pricing and policy decisions made in Santa Clara and Washington.

The export control scare

That exposure became concrete in January 2025, when the outgoing US administration published its AI diffusion rule. It sorted countries into tiers. Close allies got near-unrestricted access to advanced chips, adversaries such as China were blocked, and a large middle tier, which included India, faced country-level caps on how much advanced compute could be shipped. The rule was rescinded in May 2025 by the next administration, so it never bit. But the episode showed that India's access to the core input of the AI economy depends on a foreign government's annual mood.

China's response to far harsher controls was to build around them. DeepSeek trained competitive models on export-compliant H800 chips and squeezed efficiency out of them through engineering, and Huawei and others pushed domestic accelerators. China could do that because it had a decade of semiconductor subsidies, a large domestic chip design base, and state-directed capital. India's semiconductor programme is real but young. As of August 2026 the government reported 12 approved semiconductor projects with committed investment of Rs 1.64 lakh crore, three of which had started commercial production. Most of these are assembly, testing, packaging and mature-node fabrication. None of them will produce a leading-edge AI accelerator this decade. On compute, India is a pure price-taker.

The money gap is not closing

Here is the capital picture in plain numbers, all from the Stanford AI Index 2026 unless noted.

United States private AI investment in 2025: $285.9 billion, up 160 percent from 2024. China: $12.4 billion, and that figure misses most Chinese state money; Stanford cites an estimate of about $184 billion routed to AI companies through government guidance funds over 2000 to 2023. India: $4.09 billion. Nearly 2,000 American AI startups got first-time funding in 2025, over ten times any other country.

Now look at the best funded Indian model company. In June 2026 Sarvam announced a $300 million Series B at a $1.5 billion post-money valuation, with a first close of $234 million and HCLTech putting in $150 million as lead strategic investor. A further Nvidia-led extension followed. Total funding is now reported at around $350 million. That is the biggest model-building raise in Indian history, and it is a fraction of what a single American lab spends on compute in a quarter. OpenAI's March 2025 round alone was $40 billion. Anthropic raised $13 billion in a single round in September 2025.

Indian venture capital grew up on consumer internet, fintech and SaaS: modest capital needs and exits in five to eight years. A foundation model company needs hundreds of millions before meaningful revenue, burns cash on hardware that depreciates in three years, and competes with free products from the richest companies on earth. Few Indian funds have the size or mandate for that, and global funds that do prefer US labs.

A mission funded in tranches

The IndiaAI Mission was approved on 7 March 2024 with Rs 10,371.92 crore to spend across five years. That headline number is already small by global standards: at current exchange rates it is roughly $1.2 billion in total, across compute, foundation models, datasets, applications, skilling, startup financing and safety. The US CHIPS and Science Act set aside about $52 billion for semiconductors. China's state funds have committed far more.

The year-by-year allocation, disclosed in a Lok Sabha reply in August 2026, is more revealing. The mission received Rs 173 crore in 2024-25, Rs 800 crore in 2025-26 and Rs 1,000 crore in 2026-27. That adds up to under Rs 2,000 crore in the first three years of a five-year Rs 10,372 crore mission. The government's explanation is that funds are released according to the implementation schedule and the absorption capacity of each component. That is a reasonable accounting practice. It is also a description of a mission that is moving slower than its own plan, in a field where a year is a model generation.

The process has been careful in a way frontier AI does not reward. The foundation model call went out on 30 January 2025 and was evaluated in rounds. Support is calibrated to actual compute usage plus a 25 percent allowance for data and people. Each choice is defensible; together they optimise for auditability across many applicants, not concentrated speed on a few serious bets.

Compare that with how the frontier was actually built. OpenAI's partnership with Microsoft gave it access to dedicated supercomputers before it had a product. DeepSeek was funded out of a quantitative hedge fund that had already bought thousands of Nvidia GPUs before US controls tightened. Neither went through a tender. The countries leading the race either had private capital willing to make enormous concentrated bets, or a state willing to direct capital without asking whether the money would be spent evenly.

Indian procurement is built to prevent favouritism. In a winner-take-most race, spreading money thinly across many contenders is how you make sure nobody wins.

Krutrim: the cautionary case

If Sarvam is the best case, Krutrim is the warning. Founded by Ola's Bhavish Aggarwal in 2023, it became India's first generative AI unicorn after raising $50 million in early 2024. The pitch was a full stack: Indian large language models, Indian AI chips, and an Indian cloud. In February 2025 Aggarwal committed Rs 10,000 crore to the effort.

What followed was a steady retreat. Krutrim-2 was built on Mistral NeMo rather than trained fully from scratch. Leadership in its AI and chip units left. Headcount, according to reporting by Inc42 and the Economic Times, fell from more than 550 in August 2025 to around 150 to 160 by March 2026. In late 2025 the company paused next-generation foundation model work and chip design. The Bodhi 1 chip was dropped. The consumer assistant Kruti was pulled from app stores in April 2026. In May 2026 the company said it was pivoting to AI cloud services. Its FY25 revenue was about Rs 101.7 crore against expenses near Rs 159.4 crore, and reports said around 90 percent of revenue came from Ola group companies.

A famous Indian entrepreneur with unicorn status and a large balance sheet still could not fund a model and chip programme. That says a lot about how much patient capital exists for this category in India.

Talent: trained here, shipped elsewhere

India produces a very large number of engineers and a meaningful share of the world's top AI researchers by undergraduate origin. The problem is where they end up. A large fraction of the strongest Indian-born AI researchers did graduate work in the US and stayed, and the IP and equity they create accrue to American firms. Indian-origin engineers and scientists are prominent at Google, Microsoft, Meta, OpenAI, Anthropic and Nvidia. Several of the largest American tech companies are run by people who grew up in India.

Pay at a US frontier lab, including equity, is many times what an Indian lab can offer. More importantly, only a handful of places let a researcher run experiments at frontier scale. You have to go where the GPUs are.

There is a shift worth noting. Stanford's 2026 data shows the inflow of AI talent into America has collapsed: down 89 percent from 2017 levels, and down 80 percent in the most recent year alone. That is an opening for India, but only if there is frontier-grade work to do at home, and right now there is very little.

Academia does not fill the gap. More than 90 percent of notable models now come from industry, and India lacks the industrial labs that turn research into deployed systems. India's gross expenditure on R&D sits around 0.64 percent of GDP, against roughly 2.4 percent in China and about 3.5 percent in the US. Private sector R&D intensity is especially low.

The data problem nobody likes to discuss

The standard pitch for sovereign Indian AI is linguistic. India has 22 scheduled languages, hundreds of dialects, and a population that is poorly served by English-first models. That argument is correct as a market observation. As a source of competitive advantage in model training, it is weaker than it sounds.

Frontier capability comes overwhelmingly from huge volumes of high quality text, code and increasingly synthetic and multimodal data. The open web is dominated by English. Indian languages make up well under one percent of large public web crawls by most published estimates, and a lot of what exists is low quality, machine translated or duplicated. Hindi, with hundreds of millions of speakers, is thinly represented relative to its population. Smaller languages are thinner still.

That means an Indian lab building a model around Indian languages has two choices. It can train mostly on English and code like everyone else, which puts it in a direct contest with labs with vastly more compute. Or it can invest heavily in collecting, cleaning and digitising Indian-language data, which is valuable but slow, and which does not by itself produce reasoning or coding capability. Sarvam has done serious work here, including digitising tens of millions of pages and processing hundreds of thousands of hours of audio a month, and AI4Bharat at IIT Madras has built important open datasets. The government's AIKosh platform hosts public datasets. But none of this changes the basic fact that general intelligence in these models is learned mostly from English and code.

Meanwhile every major frontier model now handles Hindi and several other Indian languages competently, because those labs have the compute and a commercial reason to serve India. The window for Indic capability as a moat narrows every release cycle. Where Indian models still lead is on specialised Indic benchmarks, speech, cost per token and on-premise deployment for government and regulated industries. Those are real but narrow niches.

The services trap

India's technology industry is built on services. TCS, Infosys, Wipro, HCLTech and Tech Mahindra together employ well over a million people and earn their money by billing for engineering time on systems that other companies own. This model made India rich in software skills and built a large middle class. It also shaped the industry's instincts in ways that hurt in the AI race.

Services firms do not need to own core IP. In AI their natural move is to become the best implementers of OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, Meta and Microsoft models, not to build rivals. Their R&D intensity is low next to product companies, and their margins depend on billing large workforces, which is exactly what generative AI threatens. TCS announced around 12,000 job cuts in 2025, and the whole sector is now trying to show it can sell AI-led productivity without cannibalising its billing base.

The same logic now applies to infrastructure. In late 2025 Google committed $15 billion over 2026 to 2030 for an AI hub and data centre campus in Visakhapatnam. Microsoft pledged $17.5 billion over 2026 to 2029 for cloud and AI infrastructure. Amazon pledged $35 billion by 2030, later reported to rise further. These are welcome. They also mean the largest AI compute buildout on Indian soil will be owned by American companies running mostly American models. India becomes a very important customer and landing zone, not a principal.

China is the honest mirror

It is tempting to say India cannot be expected to compete with the US, which has the deepest capital markets on earth. That excuse does not survive contact with China. In 2010 China and India were both large developing economies with strong engineering talent. China then made a set of choices India did not.

It spent heavily on R&D for two decades. It built a protected domestic internet industry whose giants, Alibaba, Tencent, ByteDance and Baidu, had the balance sheets to fund AI labs. It directed state capital at semiconductors and AI through guidance funds. It trained and retained a much larger research base; Chinese institutions now lead the world in AI publication volume, citations and patents according to Stanford. And when US export controls arrived, it had enough domestic capability to respond with efficiency engineering and local chips.

DeepSeek is the key example because it disproved the claim that only American-scale budgets can reach the frontier. Its V3 and R1 releases in late 2024 and early 2025 matched or nearly matched leading American models for a small share of the reported training bill. But DeepSeek came from a profitable quant fund that already owned a large GPU stock, inside an ecosystem with dense research talent and a habit of shipping open models fast. India had some of those ingredients, never all of them in one place.

The lesson is not that India should copy an authoritarian industrial model. It is that the gap comes from fifteen years of consistent decisions on R&D, domestic platforms and concentrated capital. India made different decisions, for reasons that made sense at the time. They did not produce a frontier AI industry.

What India still has

India has real assets. It has one of the world's largest pools of English-speaking software engineers, and one of the largest user markets for AI products, which gives it negotiating power with global labs. It has a track record in digital public infrastructure. Aadhaar and UPI showed the Indian state can build population-scale systems that work, and that approach could extend to public AI services.

It has late-mover options. Open-weight models from Meta, Mistral, Alibaba, DeepSeek and now Sarvam itself mean India does not have to train everything from scratch to deploy capable systems. Compute prices for a given capability level keep falling. Inference, fine-tuning, agents, evaluation and domain applications are areas where India can build real companies without a frontier training budget. And the subsidised compute pool, whatever its limits for frontier work, has lowered the cost floor for hundreds of startups and research teams.

What would actually change the trajectory

If India wants a genuine seat in frontier AI rather than a strong position as a user and integrator, the fixes have to match the scale of the problem.

1. Concentrate compute. A national pool of roughly 38,000 GPUs spread across many projects cannot produce a frontier model. One or two dedicated clusters at the 50,000 to 100,000 accelerator scale, run by a single team with multi-year access, would.

2. Spend the money already approved, faster. A five-year Rs 10,372 crore mission that has allocated under Rs 2,000 crore in three years is not constrained by budget approval. It is constrained by disbursement. Releasing the remaining Rs 8,000 crore or more on time would matter more than any new announcement.

3. Back a small number of bets. Choosing 20 proposals is a reasonable startup support programme. A frontier effort needs two or three teams funded at levels that let them fail and retry, with milestones tied to capability, not paperwork.

4. Raise R&D intensity. Moving gross R&D spending from about 0.64 percent of GDP toward 1.5 percent would not alone make India a frontier player, but no country has reached the frontier at India's current level. Tax and procurement policy should push large IT firms and conglomerates to fund research, not only deployment.

5. Treat Indian-language data as public infrastructure. Large, clean, licensed corpora of Indian-language text and speech, built with the same seriousness as Aadhaar or UPI, would benefit every Indian model builder and lower the cost of local models. It will not close the reasoning gap alone, but it is the one data advantage India can actually build.

6. Make it worth coming home. The decline in AI talent flows to the US is the biggest gift India has received in this race. Research positions with real compute, competitive pay and equity in Indian labs are what would convert that into returning researchers.

The bottom line

India did not lose the AI race because Indian engineers are less capable. It lost the frontier race, or is losing it on the present trajectory, because of four structural choices: a research budget too small for a country of its size, capital markets and conglomerates that never took the concentrated risk frontier models demand, a technology industry built on services rather than owned IP, and a state that spreads a small AI budget evenly and slowly when the race rewards concentrated speed.

The US and China now spend at a scale India cannot match on compute for many years, even with perfect policy. The realistic question is no longer whether India will train the world's best model. It is whether India becomes a serious second-tier AI power with its own capable models, its own public compute, and enough research depth to stay relevant, or settles permanently into the role of the world's largest and most skilled customer. The current numbers point to the second outcome. Changing them is still possible, but it would take the kind of concentrated, impatient spending India has so far avoided.

Proposal Transformation to The 5Th Bank Era -
Housing availability and the cost of living are foundational—not peripheral—to Sweden’s (and Europe’s) ability to compete in the 2025–2035 global environment of energy abundance, AI/synthetic intelligence (SI), and export-driven growth.

Without stable, accessible housing, the talent, mobility, real incomes, and capital reallocation required for competitiveness erode, regardless of energy or AI/SI progress.

Transformation to The  “5th Bank Era” proposal (Bankresan - framed as a 2027–2035 structural reset and potential EU pilot) treats residential housing finance as national infrastructure.

The state assumes high risk-weighted-asset (RWA) mortgage portfolios from the major banks, releasing Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital currently locked in lower-yield, capital-intensive housing assets for redirection into AI/SI compute, semiconductors, energy infrastructure (including nuclear/SMRs and grids), and export-oriented sectors.

The speculative economy—which has persisted for over 40 years since the lifting of credit restrictions—along with the irresponsible conduct, incompetence, and  bankruptcy of Gota Bank on January 24, 1991, served as the catalyst for Sweden’s crisis in the 1990s.

Proposal Transformation to The 5th Bank Era is a structural capital-reallocation proposal that treats residential housing finance as national infrastructure.

By transferring large performing mortgage portfolios from 4-Big Banks banks to the state via true-sale structures, it aims to free Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital currently locked in low-yield, capital-intensive assets for redirection into higher-yield strategic growth sectors.

This aligns with Mario Draghi’s 2024 competitiveness diagnosis while addressing a specific bottleneck in Europe’s still bank-dominated system.

Dual Challenge:
Investment Gap and Capital Lock-In
Draghi’s report identifies an annual additional investment need of €750–800 billion (~4.4–4.7% of EU GDP) concentrated in innovation/digital, energy/decarbonisation, and security/defence to close the productivity gap with the US and China.

Energy is repeatedly flagged as a core competitiveness drag (high costs relative to peers, need for firm low-carbon power and grids).

In parallel, European banks hold large stocks of performing residential mortgages that consume significant regulatory capital under risk-weight floors while delivering compressed margins and low returns on equity (estimated pure-mortgage ROE around 3%, below typical cost-of-equity thresholds).

The proposal frames banks as having become “mortgage warehouses,” with CET1 trapped in low-velocity assets rather than deployed for growth. Swedish housing-secured lending stood at approximately SEK 5,562 billion as of June 2026.

Sweden applies a 25% average risk-weight floor on mortgages under Article 458 CRR (extended through end-2027), which alone corresponds to a material capital requirement (prior estimates ~SEK 115 billion / ~21% of large banks’ total capital requirement). Banks already operate with strong CET1 ratios (often high teens).

Financial Mechanics of the Transformation
The core sequence is:
True-sale transfer of performing mortgage portfolios from banks to a state or public vehicle.

RWA reduction as the assets leave bank balance sheets.

CET1 relief / expanded headroom above Maximum Distributable Amount thresholds and other constraints.
Redeployment of freed capital into higher-spread strategic lending (proposal framing of 4–6% spreads versus compressed mortgage margins) in priority sectors.

Simplified illustrations show meaningful ratio improvements (e.g., illustrative movement from ~10% toward ~14% CET1 by shedding mortgage RWA), though real Swedish banks start from stronger bases; the absolute capacity unlocked remains material (tens to low hundreds of billions of SEK in strategic headroom depending on scale, residual exposures, and regulatory treatment). Household debt levels themselves do not change—only the holder does.

On the sovereign side, ongoing mortgage cash flows (interest + amortisation) can largely cover funding costs and expected losses if valuation is realistic, given Sweden’s historically very low mortgage credit losses.

The vehicle can therefore be substantially self-funding. Sweden’s low public debt (~35% of GDP Maastricht) provides fiscal space relative to most large European peers. Full immediate transfer of the ~SEK 5.5–6 trillion stock would be a large one-off exposure; phased, partial, or guarantee-based approaches moderate the impact while still releasing capital. Careful design is required for covered-bond continuity, CRR significant-risk-transfer rules, valuation methodology, and state-aid compliance.

Alignment with Draghi’s Pillars and Target Sectors

The proposal Transformation to The 5Th Bank Era  maps directly onto Draghi’s three pillars and related EU instruments (Chips Act, AI Gigafactories, Clean Industrial Deal elements, Technological Sovereignty Package, etc.):
Innovation:
AI/data centres, semiconductors, compute infrastructure.

Energy & Decarbonisation:
Nuclear (including SMRs for firm 24/7 power), solar parks, grids and interconnectors—critical because data centres and advanced manufacturing need reliable low-carbon electricity.

Security & Strategic Autonomy:
Reduced critical dependencies, supply-chain resilience, defence-related industrial capacity, and export-oriented strategic industries.

Housing availability and cost of living are treated as foundational infrastructure: without stable access, talent mobility, real incomes, and the human capital needed for AI/energy/advanced manufacturing hubs erode.

Freed bank capacity supports these sectors while housing finance becomes more predictable and less sensitive to bank capital cycles.

Outcomes targeted include higher-skill employment, stronger export performance, expanded tax base, and more stable real incomes supporting the welfare model.

Sweden is positioned as a plausible first-mover/pilot (low debt, efficient banks with relatively low cost/income ratios, existing nuclear base, digital maturity, low historical mortgage losses), with potential extension to Proposal Partners such as France, Spain, and Italy.

Draghi implementation trackers have shown only partial progress on the broader agenda.

A bank balance-sheet tool can operate more at national level while still feeding into EU co-financing.

Bottom Line
The analysis of capital lock-in in mature, low-risk but capital-intensive mortgage books is valid and material for a bank-dominated system seeking strategic competitiveness in energy and AI/SI while sustaining a high-tax welfare model.

The Proposal Transformation to The 5th Bank Era offers a concrete national (and potentially multi-country) mechanism to free CET1 for growth capital, complementary to Draghi’s analysis of the investment gap, CMU needs, and possible joint instruments.

Success depends on independent valuation/governance of any public vehicle, clear productive-use conditionality, integration with energy and industrial policy, and careful management of sovereign exposure.

Full-scale transfer is high-ambition; It is one structural lever to help move capital "from housing to growth capital" in service of European competitiveness versus the US and China.

The Affordable Care Act (ACA), often called Obamacare, has been a central subject of economic and political debate since its passage. Critics and supporters frequently evaluate its impact on market competition, legal costs, and administrative bureaucracy.

Cross-State Competition

Critics point out that the ACA maintains state-level health insurance marketplaces, which limits the ability of insurers to sell identical policies across state lines without complying with each individual state's regulations.
The Critique: Restricting interstate sales reduces competition, leading to higher premiums and fewer choices for consumers in certain regions.
The Counterargument: The ACA actually includes a provision (Section 1333) allowing states to form "health care choice compacts" to sell insurance across state lines, provided the plans meet the essential health benefits of both states. However, few states have utilized this option due to the complexity of aligning local provider networks and state regulatory frameworks.

Tort Reform and Lawsuits

The ACA did not include federal caps on medical malpractice lawsuits or statutory limits on non-economic damages (pain and suffering), which was a major point of contention for critics who favored tort reform.
The Critique: Failing to limit malpractice lawsuits drives up healthcare costs by encouraging "defensive medicine," where doctors order unnecessary tests purely to protect themselves from potential litigation.
The Counterargument: Proponents of the law argued that malpractice reform is traditionally a state-level issue rather than a federal one. Instead of statutory caps, the ACA funded state-level demonstration projects to test alternative medical liability models, such as administrative health courts and "disclosure and offer" programs.

Administrative Bureaucracy Costs

The law significantly increased regulatory and administrative requirements for insurers, healthcare providers, and employers.
The Critique: The extensive reporting mandates, compliance checks, and the creation of new governmental oversight bodies structuralized an expensive layer of bureaucracy. Critics argue these administrative burdens divert financial resources away from actual patient care and raise overall system costs.
The Counterargument: Supporters maintain that much of the administrative framework was necessary to enforce consumer protections (such as banning denials for pre-existing conditions) and to transition the healthcare system from a "fee-for-service" model to a "value-based care" model, which aims to lower long-term costs by improving patient outcomes.

text:
Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii: the casinos, blackjack, poker, and everything worth picking up

All right, this is another one where you can spend a lot of time playing without realizing you're working toward several different things. You've got the chip challenges, a crew member, another treasure, clothes, and soundtrack CDs. So here's where to go, what each place has, and how I'd approach getting through it without turning a couple of prizes into an entire night at the table.

Getting into the casinos

Start in Madlantis's Bar District, outside Dunghill. The casino staff and card tables are right there. This is where you play low- and high-stakes blackjack and poker. Talk to the chip seller before approaching a dealer. Chips cost $1 each in game money.

The VIP tables are inside the Royal Casino at the Luxury Palace Hotel. Advance through the Pirates' Coliseum until you clear the one-star Pirates' Championship. Follow the resulting hotel access, then use the casino inside. If you're still outside Dunghill wondering where the VIP option went, you're at the earlier tables.

The Japanese Gambling Hall in Honolulu is a separate stop for Koi-koi and Oicho-kabu. Its wooden tags aren't what you're buying here.

What completion actually wants

Blackjack:
• Earn 10,000 chips: 1,000 Reputation.
• Earn 50,000 chips: another 3,000.
• Earn 150,000 chips: another 5,000.

Poker:
• Earn 5,000 chips: 1,000 Reputation.
• Earn 25,000 chips: another 3,000.
• Earn 75,000 chips: another 5,000.

All six challenges together give 18,000 Reputation. Those are separate game counters. Buying chips to afford a reward doesn't replace earning chips through the relevant game. Check the challenge screen after a session instead of treating your current wallet balance as the completion counter.

Blackjack: the numbers to know

The starting betting ranges are:
• Low stakes: 10–100 chips.
• High stakes: 100–500.
• VIP: 1,000–2,000.

Winning consecutive hands increases the maximum:
• Low: 300 after one win, 500 after two, 1,000 after three.
• High: 1,000, then 2,000, then 3,000.
• VIP: 3,000, then 5,000, then 10,000.

The maximum stops increasing after the third consecutive win. Break the streak and it returns to the starting limit. That's why the VIP table makes such a difference when you're working toward 150,000.

You're trying to beat the dealer without going over 21. Number cards use their printed value, face cards count as ten, and an ace can count as one or eleven. A natural blackjack is the initial two-card ace-plus-ten-value combination. Reaching 21 after taking extra cards isn't the same payout.

Hit takes another card. Stand keeps what you've got. Double Down doubles your stake but gives you only one additional card. Split separates an eligible matching pair into two hands with an additional stake. Surrender gives up the hand and returns half the bet. Insurance is an extra side bet offered against a dealer ace; don't confuse it with protecting every losing hand.

A normal win returns twice the stake, including the stake you put in. A winning natural blackjack returns 2.5 times it. For example, a 2,000-chip natural returns 5,000, a 3,000-chip profit. The game also has Six Under: six cards without busting wins.

If you're learning, use the cheap table first. Don't keep taking cards simply because the total isn't 21 yet. A hard 17 or higher is generally a stopping point. A soft hand with an ace still counted as eleven needs different decisions, so don't apply that shortcut blindly to every ace hand. These are starting tips, not a promise that a particular hand will win.

Using the casino items

Kamulop's shrine is on Fuji Street in Little Japan, east of Revolve. Once his Chapter 2 introduction is done, exchange fortune slips there for these items:

• Blackjack Amulet: 10 Fortune Points. Gives natural blackjacks for five hands.
• Bust Amulet: 5 points. Makes dealer busts more likely for five hands.
• Royal Joker Card: 5 points. Helps your poker hand for one hand.

These are consumables. Save before spending them and use the table's item command at the appropriate prompt. I'd hold them for the Royal Casino instead of burning them on the first cheap game available. Kamulop's initial supply is limited, so don't plan around buying an unlimited stack.

For a blackjack amulet, use the largest bet you can afford within the table limit and increase it as the winning streak raises that limit. Don't double down on a natural or start taking extra cards because you think that will make the payout bigger. Keep enough chips available to actually place the next bet.

If you reload an earlier save after a bad session, you also lose everything earned since that save. Save again after progress you want to keep.

Poker: what you're actually playing

This is Texas Hold'em. You get two private cards. Three shared cards appear on the flop, followed by the turn and river, bringing the shared total to five. Betting happens between those stages. Your strongest five-card combination wins; you don't have to use both private cards.

The entry bankrolls are 100 chips for low stakes, 1,000 for high, and 10,000 for VIP. Those are the chips needed to sit down at that level, not a claim that every individual bet costs that amount.

Check passes without adding chips when nobody has bet. Call matches the current bet, Raise increases it, and Fold gives up the hand and the chips already committed. Folding a bad hand is part of playing, not something you need to avoid at all costs.

Hands, strongest first:
• Royal flush: suited 10, J, Q, K, A.
• Straight flush: five consecutive cards of one suit.
• Four of a kind.
• Full house: three of one rank and two of another.
• Flush: five cards of one suit.
• Straight: five consecutive ranks; A-2-3-4-5 is the lowest.
• Three of a kind.
• Two pair.
• One pair.
• High card.

Look at what the shared cards allow everyone else to make. Your pair doesn't become safe just because it looked good before the flop. Likewise, a strong-looking shared board might be helping everybody. Equal best five-card hands split the pot.

For the chip grind, save a bankroll before moving to VIP. Use a Royal Joker when opponents are staying in and there is a worthwhile pot developing. Repeatedly raising until everybody folds can win the hand but leave you with much less than you were hoping to collect. Don't treat the item as a guaranteed enormous payout.

Every casino reward

Outside Dunghill:
• Yappi-kun: 1,500 chips.
• Sea Dog Attire (Rough): 200.
• Cabaret Manager Eyepatch: 150.
• Persona 3 Reload soundtrack CD: 25.
• Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance soundtrack CD: 25.

Those five unique rewards total 1,900 chips. Yappi-kun becomes available during Chapter 2 recruitment progression. He's a silver attacker with a maximum level of 30. At level 30 his listed stats are 7,125 HP, 350 cannon power, 320 maintenance, 410 attack, and 375 defense. His captain trait increases attack; he has no first-mate trait.

Royal Casino:
• Wooden Treasure Chest: 2,000 chips. Contains Stonebreaker Pocket Watch, Treasury entry 24.
• Cabaret Manager Suit: 200.
• Cabaret Manager Suit (Unbuttoned): 200.
• Cabaret Manager Pants: 200.
• Metaphor: ReFantazio soundtrack CD: 25.
• Persona 5 Tactica soundtrack CD: 25.

Those six unique rewards total 2,650 chips. Both counters together take 4,550 for the unique collection. If you only want Yappi-kun and the treasure, set aside 3,500.

Both counters also exchange chips for:
• Bronze Plate: 10.
• Silver Plate: 100.
• Gold Plate: 500.
• Platinum Plate: 1,000.
• Swiss Watch: 2,000.
• Vintage Luxury Watch: 5,000.

For cash, plates are the straightforward option to take to a pawn shop. Check the selling offer before unloading watches; published price lists disagree about their resale values.

You can buy the chips outright if you just want the collectibles. There's no requirement to win the treasure through poker specifically. But if you're finishing the whole challenge list, do both games, check all six milestones, and collect the unique rewards before spending your remaining chips on things to sell.

text:
Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii: unlocking and beating the Amon Pirates

All right, Amon is another one where unlocking the fight and actually winning it are two different projects. This time you have to deal with his ship, his crew, and then Taiyo Amon himself. Don't finish the boarding battle and assume you've done the whole thing.

How to unlock it

Go to the Pirates' Coliseum reception in Madlantis and clear every ordinary match across all four categories. That includes the Swashbuckler Showdowns tied to the Devil Flags captains. You need to finish the Devil Flags storyline through Captain Zeus, then complete those unlocked Coliseum fights too.

Keep progressing the main story if a Tournament of Captains entry is still locked; one of its later fights is story-gated in Chapter 4. Raising Pirate Rank alone doesn't unlock everything. You don't need S-ranks everywhere, but you do need the wins.

When the ordinary Coliseum list is cleared, watch the scene introducing the Amon challenge. The Ultimate Pirate Crew Showdown appears under Tournament of Captains. That's the ship and boarding portion. The one-on-one fight is offered afterward, separately through reception.

Before entering

Upgrade the Goromaru's durability and weapons, put your strongest suitable crew on the cannons, and improve your boarding squads. Having a strong character in the wrong assignment isn't the same as having a strong team.

For support, Noah's healing is useful, and Okasana-chan helps reduce damage. Level the people you're actually bringing and restore their morale. A first mate who improves your repair allowance, such as Nishida, gives you more room during the naval battle. These are recommendations, not a required roster or a reason to buy DLC.

Bring Majima's health and attack upgrades up before the duel. Stock healing and Heat recovery items as well. You can use inventory recovery in the one-on-one fight, and you get time to prepare between the crew victory and accepting that last challenge.

The ship battle

The Amon vessel has 10,000 health. It uses homing missiles, explosive barrels and mines, plus lasers and flamethrowers. The dangerous part is staying beside it taking repeated hits while trying to squeeze out one more broadside.

Save boost for getting away from incoming missiles and dangerous patches of explosives. Watch where the ship drops mines before turning back toward it. If you're burning, deal with the status rather than continuing to trade damage as though nothing happened.

Get your shots in, reposition, and repair before your remaining health becomes too small to survive the next volley. Since there is only one enemy vessel, keep it in view and pay attention to its attacks instead of circling blindly.

The boarding battle

Now you have 50 enemies to clear. Prioritize their leaders while your squads handle the crowd. Leaving the leaders active gives the enemy more chances to use its special attacks, including lightning and flaming boomerangs.

Use your own support ability rather than saving it until everyone is down. Healing keeps the rest of your crew fighting, which is a lot better than trying to clean up the entire deck alone. If a leader isn't safely reachable, thin the nearby enemies first instead of charging through the whole group and losing Majima.

Taiyo Amon's duel

Once reception offers the individual challenge, take the preparation break. Heal, restock, check your rings, then return and accept.

Early on, avoid throwing out long attacks while he's ready to counter. His hook can leave you stunned for a follow-up, and some attacks break your guard. Dodge, get around him, punish the opening, then reset instead of assuming you can hold block through everything.

When he summons clones, clearing them becomes the priority. Switch to Sea Dog and use the violin's shark summon when your Madness gauge is ready to damage several together. Removing the extra attackers makes the rest of the fight much easier to read.

Watch for the suspended blades that rain down afterward. Guard through that attack rather than trying to attack into it. Sea Dog's all-direction guard is useful here. The problem is the clones can interrupt your defense, which is why leaving them alive while chasing the real Amon is such a bad trade.

Use recovery items before you're one hit from death. Spend Heat on attacks you can land safely, clear the clones, and return to dodging and punishing Amon's openings. You don't need to win a damage race against the entire screen.

Finish the duel and collect the Champion's Ring from reception. It gradually builds Heat during combat. Defeating the Amon Pirates also earns Legend of the Coliseum. The crew win alone isn't the final completion check: make sure Taiyo's individual challenge is finished too.

# Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii: All 11 Goro Kingdom Animals

Goro Kingdom gives you cooking ingredients, ten additional support recruits, and a reason to keep coming back to Rich Island. Here’s where every animal is, what you need to recruit them, and how feeding and rewards work.

## Before you start

Goro Kingdom opens during Chapter 1 on Rich Island. Goro and Phoenix are your first residents. In Chapter 2, the story takes you through Substory 4, The Kitten in District Five, and adds Onigiri. That unlocks the other Animal Rescue encounters, marked by white pawprints on Honolulu’s map.

For the optional rescues, bring:

- $3,000 for Sanzen.
- One Pet Food for Barkley. The regular $10 bag works.
- One Wild-Caught Sashimi for The Gourmand. Grayson sells it for $1.60.
- The Goromi clothing set for Allure. You find this in a container rather than buying it.

That’s $3,011.60 if you buy both food items, before taxi fares or food for raising affection.

## Every animal and how to recruit them

### 1. Goro, the tiger cub

No separate rescue is needed. Noah’s companion is included when Goro Kingdom opens on Rich Island.

Feed Goro alongside the other animals. He already becomes a support crewmate through the story, so his maximum-affection reward is different: speak to him after filling the gauge to receive 50 Bear Meat.

### 2. Phoenix, the chicken

Obtained during Chapter 1’s Goro Kingdom introduction on Rich Island, around the visit to Stella’s Shop. Follow the story and take Phoenix to the enclosure. You do not need to find an additional Honolulu rescue marker.

At maximum affection, Phoenix becomes a support recruit with Restorative Medicine, which restores a little health to everyone.

### 3. Onigiri, the cat

Encountered during Chapter 2 in The Kitten in District Five, on the story route toward Diamond Head. Defeat the man threatening the kitten and finish the scene.

Onigiri joins Goro Kingdom, and the other Honolulu animal rescues become available. The eventual support skill is Auto Guard, which slightly reduces incoming damage.

### 4. Allure, the cat

Find Allure on Aloha Street near Aloha Bridge, west of L&L Hawaiian Barbecue. Speak to the person beside the cat to learn why ordinary coaxing will not work.

To get the required outfit:

1. Go to LiberTea in the Cultural District, west of Anaconda Shopping Center. The Night Street taxi stop is nearby.
2. Open the silver container in LiberTea’s covered outdoor seating area.
3. Return to Revolve and use the upstairs changing area.
4. Select the Goromi clothing set and apply it.
5. Return to Allure and speak to the nearby person while wearing it.

Owning the outfit is not enough. Wear the set for the encounter.

### 5. CoCo, the chimpanzee

Look for the coconut tree beside Cream & Berry on River Street, near Aloha Bridge. Speak to the woman looking up at CoCo.

Use all three choices:

- “Shake the tree”
- “Toss a coconut”
- “Strike a cool-ass pose”

The order does not matter. Work through the remaining options until the scene finishes and CoCo comes down.

### 6. Zoomies, the Labrador

Go to the Pier taxi stop in the Harbor District, by the Shipper’s Wharf. Speak to the man trying to catch the dog.

After Zoomies runs away, follow the new marker around to the western side of the building. Interact with the dog and move the intensity meter until it says “Be gentle.” Confirm there to calm Zoomies and complete the rescue.

### 7. The Gourmand, the Labrador

Find the hungry dog on Riverside Walk, south of the Diamond Head taxi stop. Speak to the person beside him and hand over one Wild-Caught Sashimi.

The straightforward way to get it is to swim out to Grayson’s Weapons at Sea, the merchant on a raft off Aloha Beach. Buy the sashimi for $1.60, then bring it back to the rescue marker.

You can also find sashimi while catching fish by hand in the sea, but buying one avoids waiting for a random catch. Check the item name: Wild-Caught Fried Shrimp is a different item.

### 8. Turtle, the Shiba Inu

Find Turtle at the corner of Waikiki Street and Kaku Avenue, west of Crêpes for Me.

Approach the two men mistreating the dog and defeat them. Finish the conversation to send Turtle to Rich Island. No food or payment is required for this rescue.

### 9. Alarm Cluck, the chicken

Search the small residential alley between Fuji Street and Ayame Street in Little Japan. It is west of the Ayame Street taxi stop and northwest of Ahi Poke Garden.

Interrupt the angry resident threatening the chicken, win the fight, and finish the scene. Alarm Cluck then joins the kingdom.

### 10. Barkley, the Shiba Inu

Go to the north/northeastern entrance of Anaconda Shopping Center and speak to the woman beside the barking dog.

Give her Pet Food. A regular bag is enough, so there is no need to spend $150 or $500 on this recruitment step. If you have none, buy the $10 version from an ABC Store.

### 11. Sanzen, the cow

Find Sanzen and the farmer in Sunset Park, near the pavilion at the northern end of Sunset Street in Downtown Honolulu.

Pay $3,000 when offered the cow. This is the only animal rescue here with a substantial cash requirement, so keep that money aside before shopping for upgrades.

## Feeding and affection

Rescued animals move to Goro Kingdom by the Rich Island docks. Feed them there to raise their affection and receive cooking ingredients.

The three individual food tiers are:

- Pet Food: $10, a small affection increase.
- High-End Pet Food: $150, a larger increase.
- Ultimate Pet Food: $500, the strongest of these three.

ABC Stores sell the pet food tiers. Stella’s Shop is convenient for regular Pet Food when you are already on Rich Island. Ultimate Pet Food can also be bought at Wink Mini Mart on Waikiki Street.

Better food gives more ingredients per feeding. Higher affection improves the ingredients themselves. Those are separate benefits, so an expensive bag does not replace the need to build the relationship.

You cannot repeatedly feed an animal without a break. Check the feeding indicator or timer and return when the food-bowl marker is available again. Fit visits around other activities instead of standing at the enclosure waiting.

Once an animal’s affection gauge is full, interact with it again to receive its final reward. Filling the bar alone is not the last step.

## Essence of Pet Snacks

This is the group-feeding recipe. It raises affection for every animal currently in Goro Kingdom and collects their ingredient gifts together.

During Chapter 2, once you can return to Rich Island after upgrading the Goromaru, revisit the enclosure as you add animals. A conversation with Noah unlocks the recipe. If that scene has not appeared, finish the remaining Honolulu rescues and return to the kingdom.

The precise minimum animal count for the scene is not firmly established. Seven pets is the confirmed trophy requirement, not a reliable reason to stop checking the other rescues.

One batch needs:

- 3 Meat
- 5 Bugs
- 5 Fish
- 5 Produce
- 5 Eggs/Milk ingredients

Cook it at Goro Goro Kitchen, then interact with the Snack Box inside the enclosure. Having it in your inventory is not enough to feed everyone.

Snack quality affects the return:

- One star: one ingredient from each animal.
- Two stars: two ingredients from each animal.
- Three stars: three ingredients from each animal.

Higher-quality snacks also give a better affection increase. Use better ingredients and complete the cooking minigame well when you want more value from each batch.

Group snacks have a ten-minute cooldown. Their feeding allowance is separate from individual Pet Food, so you can use the Snack Box and still feed animals individually during the same visit.

## What each animal gives you

Ingredient rewards improve as affection rises. The progression is:

- Goro: Rabbit Meat, then Pheasant Meat, then Bear Meat.
- Phoenix and Alarm Cluck: Egg, Quality Egg, Golden Egg.
- Onigiri and Allure: Aweoweo, Humuhumunukunukuapua’a, Oarfish.
- Barkley, Turtle, Zoomies and The Gourmand: Flounder, Salmon, Mahi Mahi.
- CoCo: Coconut, Quality Mango, Superb Pineapple.
- Sanzen: Fresh Milk, Quality Fresh Milk, Superb Fresh Milk.

The dogs supply fish. Goro supplies meat. Keeping both kinds of animals fed helps cover different cooking categories.

## All support rewards

At maximum affection, speak to each of the ten animals other than Goro to recruit them. Their skills are:

- Barkley: Bump Up, increases everyone’s Attack.
- The Gourmand: Guard Wall, reduces incoming damage.
- Sanzen: Cure All, restores everyone’s health.
- Onigiri and Zoomies: Auto Guard, a smaller damage-reduction effect.
- Allure and Turtle: Hard Attack, a small Attack increase for everyone.
- Phoenix and Alarm Cluck: Restorative Medicine, a small group heal.
- CoCo: First Aid, a small heal for Majima.

These animals fill support slots for boarding fights. They are not additional cannon operators. You can take up to three support members, and using their skills develops them further.

Goro already has Goro’s Mighty Roar, an Attack buff for allies. His special kingdom reward is the one-time 50 Bear Meat mentioned above.

## Completion checklist

- Rescue seven animals for Making a Menagerie. The three story animals count, so four optional rescues are enough for that trophy or achievement.
- Collect all eleven to fill the kingdom and access every animal’s rewards.
- Unlock and cook Essence of Pet Snacks. It counts toward Domestic Pirate, which requires cooking all fourteen recipes.
- Max affection and speak to all ten recruitable animals for their crew unlocks.
- Speak to Goro at maximum affection for his Bear Meat reward.

For an inexpensive start, rescue Turtle and Alarm Cluck through their fights, get CoCo by exhausting the dialogue, and catch Zoomies gently. Then handle the food deliveries, Goromi outfit, and Sanzen when your inventory and cash are ready.

The useful routine is simple: rescue animals, feed them on return trips, use group snacks once unlocked, and talk to them again when their affection is full.

text:
Like a Dragon: Infinite Wealth: Ounabara Vocational School

All right, this is one of those things that's worth doing even if you're not trying to finish every single thing in the game. Ounabara gives Ichiban a lot of Personality points, and those stats matter when you're trying to open up more of what he can do. But the exams cost money, so I want to cover what you're actually paying for instead of just telling you to go take some tests.

GETTING STARTED

The school is on Harbor Street in western Honolulu. You can get into this in Chapter 4 through Substory 21, Playing with Fire. Speak to Maeda at the reception desk. Hawaii Proficiency Tier 2 is your free introductory exam.

There are 20 regular exams and one final exam. A regular exam gives you five questions drawn from that subject's pool of ten. You need three correct answers to pass. Most questions give you 30 seconds, so read the actual question before picking something that looks familiar. Some of these deliberately ask for the answer that is FALSE or the thing that DOESN'T belong.

Failing means paying the entry fee again. Once you've passed a subject, you can retake it for free, but you don't keep collecting its Personality reward. This isn't an unlimited stat-farming trick.

EVERY EXAM, ITS PRICE, AND ITS REWARD

These are Personality points, not entire Personality levels. The money below is the exam fee in dollars.

• Sports Proficiency: $300. Passion +30, Confidence +30.
• Hawaii Proficiency Tier 2: free. Passion +30, Charisma +30.
• Hawaii Proficiency Tier 1: $500. Passion +50, Charisma +50.
• Marine Life: $500. Confidence +50, Kindness +50.
• Alcohol Expertise: $500. Style +120.
• World Landmarks: $300. Passion +30, Intellect +30.
• Muscular Science: $500. Passion +60, Confidence +60.
• Gardening Proficiency: $300. Kindness +30, Style +30.
• Underworld Studies: $500. Confidence +120.
• SEGA Proficiency Tier 2: $300. Confidence +30, Charisma +30.
• SEGA Proficiency Tier 1: $500. Confidence +50, Charisma +50.
• Honolulu City Proficiency: $500. Passion +60, Charisma +60.
• Gem Proficiency: $500. Style +120.
• Sujimon Mastery: $500. Kindness +60, Style +60.
• Mathematics: $500. Intellect +120.
• Outer Space: $500. Kindness +120.
• World History: $500. Intellect +120.
• Trivia King Tier 2: $300. Charisma +30, Kindness +30, Intellect +30.
• Trivia King Tier 1: $500. Charisma +60, Kindness +60, Intellect +60.
• Trivia King Special Tier: $1,000. Charisma +90, Kindness +90, Intellect +90.
• Ounabara Proficiency: $1,000. Passion +100, Confidence +100, Style +100.

Passing everything on your first attempt costs $10,000 in exam fees. Failed attempts and optional help cost extra. So if you're coming in with exactly $10,000, don't assume you have room to fail a few times.

The combined first-clear rewards are Passion +360, Confidence +440, Charisma +400, Kindness +440, Intellect +450, and Style +430. That's why this is worth remembering when you're short of a Personality requirement elsewhere.

WHAT I'D PRIORITIZE

If you only need a particular stat, pick the exams that help with that instead of paying for whatever happens to be at the top of the list.

For Style, Alcohol and Gem each give 120. For Intellect, Mathematics and World History each give 120. Underworld gives 120 Confidence. Outer Space gives 120 Kindness. Honolulu City and Muscular Science both help Passion while also raising another stat. The Trivia exams spread their rewards across Charisma, Kindness, and Intellect.

If you're working toward certificates rather than one stat, do the free Hawaii exam first and then work through the subjects you know. Finish the lower tier before moving up a tiered subject. You don't need to tackle the hardest trivia first just because it's there.

Ten passed certificates earn the 30 Mins or It's Free trophy/achievement. That's ten, not all 21. All 21 is for finishing the school and its related content.

THE OPTIONAL HELP

Ikari in the lobby offers two exam assists:

• Hyper Focus costs $1,000 and adds 30 seconds to one question. You can activate it once during an exam.
• Divine Pencil costs $5,000 and removes two wrong answers from one question. You can activate it once during an exam.

Those are expensive compared with the individual tests. I'd have the answer reference ready before paying for help. They're options if you want them, but neither is required to pass.

Don't build your whole plan around pausing the game to look things up. Have the reference open before starting, and identify the question by its wording rather than by the position of an answer on the screen. For picture questions, identify the object itself. An answer like “top right” isn't useful if you can't be sure you're looking at the same arrangement.

THE FINAL EXAM

Pass the first 20 exams to unlock Ounabara Proficiency. This one pulls five questions from the earlier subjects, and you need all five right. The normal three-out-of-five pass mark does not apply here.

It costs $1,000 per paid attempt, so this is where rushing gets annoying. Keep the whole answer reference available, not just the final regular subject you finished. You could get a sports question followed by a SEGA question and then something completely different. There's no separate fixed five-answer final-exam list.

LAURA MAEDA AND CERTIFIABLE LOVER

Finishing the exams isn't the only thing attached to this place. Laura Maeda has Substory 47, Certifiable Lover. Complete all 21 exams, then continue her conversations and gift requests. If a conversation isn't available, keep developing Ichiban's Personality and return rather than assuming passing the last exam automatically finishes everything.

The requested gifts are an ABC Store Gift Set, Hawaiian Cosmetics, and a Plumeria Bouquet. The ABC Store in Anaconda Shopping Center sells the gift set, Seaworthy Treasures sells the cosmetics, and Melia's Leis and Flowers sells the bouquet. Give her the requested items and follow the conversations through to the concluding scene. Laura also becomes available as a Dondoko Island guest.

So for this one, the checklist is pretty simple: introductory exam, ten certificates for the trophy, all 20 regular exams if you're finishing the school, then the perfect-score final and Laura's remaining conversations. Don't confuse getting the trophy with being done with everything here.
