text:
Sujimon in Like a Dragon: Infinite Wealth: from your first recruit to King and the Divine League

Ichiban goes to Hawaii and somehow ends up managing a competitive fighting team made up of men who absolutely should not be left unsupervised. Sujimon is ridiculous, but there is a proper battle system under the joke.

This is the route through it: how to recruit and improve a team, get past each trainer-rank gate, beat the Discreet Four and King, and finish the Stadium. Boss names and Sujimon-side-story rewards are covered below.

GETTING STARTED

The Sujidex and the Sujimon League unlock separately. Chapter 2 introduces the enemy encyclopedia. The team-building minigame arrives in Chapter 4 through Substory 37, Choosing Your Starter, at the Anaconda Shopping Center.

Finish that introduction before hunting for recruitment options. It gives you access to the League menu and the systems around it. Your starter choice is not something you need to restart the game over. More recruits are coming, and the useful question is whether your next fighter fills a hole in the team.

Keep three kinds of progress separate:

• Trainer Rank unlocks your next major challenge.
• Individual Sujimon levels improve their stats, up to your current cap.
• Awakening and evolution improve the fighter beyond simply feeding it more EXP.

If every Sujimon has stopped at level 10, that is a League progression gate. More food will not get around it. If you are winning sparring matches but your Trainer Rank is not moving, that is also normal: sparring trains the fighters, while the trainers around Honolulu are the route to raising your rank.

RECRUITING WITHOUT EMPTYING YOUR WALLET

After some normal battles, an enemy will stay behind with a recruitment prompt. Approach them, choose a Suji Gift, time the offer, and follow the button prompt. Better gifts improve your chances, so keep the good ones for recruits you actually want.

Raids give you another recruitment opportunity after you win. The fight itself uses Ichiban and the normal RPG party, not your Sujimon lineup. Check the enemy level before entering. A great collection does not make a level-60 raid safe for a low-level Ichiban.

Gacha is the other main route. Basic and type-focused pulls help build a roster and supply duplicates. Japan Gacha draws from a different pool and uses Japanese Master Tickets or more money. Use the tickets earned from trainers, raids and the Stadium before turning this into a cash sink.

Visit Suji Spots as you travel. Pick up available items, strengthen useful recruits and sort the roster there. Keep an eye on trainer rewards too. A fight that gives you tickets, food and a type-specific Sujimon Box can solve several problems at once.

Don't throw away every duplicate. Those are upgrade materials. Equally, don't consume your only useful backup just because the Awakening menu will let you.

HOW TO BUILD A TEAM THAT ACTUALLY WORKS

You have six slots: three active fighters and three reserves. Start with a reliable damage dealer, enough Speed to get turns, and a healer for longer fights. Build coverage around those jobs.

The type chart is small:

• Blaze beats Nature.
• Nature beats Frost.
• Frost beats Blaze.
• Light and Shadow beat each other.

Light into Shadow is a damage opportunity with a risk attached. Your Light fighter is also vulnerable to the return hit. If it cannot survive that hit, a sturdy neutral matchup may work better.

Speed is the stat that can make two otherwise similar teams feel completely different. The Speed of your three active Sujimon contributes to the SP gauge, which decides when your side acts. Fast reserves do not help while they are sitting on the bench.

Check attack cost alongside attack power. A cheap basic attack leaves your SP gauge closer to its next turn. Sometimes that gets you another action before the opponent moves. A more expensive attack is worth it when the extra damage secures a knockout or prevents a much worse enemy turn.

You can swap two Sujimon once on your turn before attacking. That can reposition your active fighters or bring someone in from reserve. Plan the swap around both the attack you want now and the frontline you are leaving exposed afterward.

The central attacker can hit the entire enemy front row, with reduced damage to the side targets. An attacker on an outside position hits that side and the middle. Check the targeting lines rather than automatically putting your hardest hitter in the middle every turn. Removing one dangerous opponent is often better than leaving three opponents injured and ready to hit back.

Basic attacks build MP for special moves, with favorable type matchups helping. Not every Sujimon has a special. When you use one, the roulette result changes its effectiveness: red is best, green is usable, and blue is the poor result. Keep enough MP for healing when the fight is becoming an endurance test. An offensive special is much less impressive if the whole team falls over immediately afterward.

USEFUL PICKS WITHOUT A DLC TEAM

Sodachi is a perfectly useful Blaze anchor while you build the collection. For healing, look at the Bummer Strummer line, which progresses through Freakalele to Strummageddon. Later, Munanugget Messiah is a strong Nature option with healing and good Speed.

Scarred Yakuza is a useful fast Frost fighter. Suji Black Belt is a powerful Light attacker. Bonecleaver and Suji Delinquent are worthwhile Shadow options if you get them. These are options to build around, not a shopping list you must complete before challenging a gym.

The five Kiwami Sujimon are exceptionally strong, but waiting for a lucky pull is unnecessary for the story. The legendary raid route also asks your normal party to handle level-60 enemies. Finish the next achievable challenge with the team you have instead of treating a rare recruit as a prerequisite.

LEVELING, AWAKENING AND EVOLUTION

Sujimunch adds EXP through Strengthen Sujimon. Sparring is convenient for training, and outdoor trainer battles advance your Trainer Rank as well. Put the food into the fighters doing useful work rather than spreading it evenly across the whole collection.

Awakening fills the stars beneath a Sujimon's rarity symbol. For the standard three-star progression, the stages need one, then two, then three infusion units. That is six consumed units in total, plus the fighter you are keeping. Suitable Committee Agents can substitute for duplicates.

An eligible fighter can evolve once it has three Awakening stars. Normal evolution does not require you to reach a separate experience level. Evolution can change stats and attacks, and resets the Awakening stars for the new form. Check the evolution menu because not every recruit has another form.

Later Super evolutions are a separate investment with higher material requirements. Read the menu's requirement before committing your agents. The ordinary six-unit calculation is not a promise that every late-game upgrade costs the same.

After beating a gym leader, speak to the Committee Agent outside the gym for the free Awakening agents. It is easy to leave after the cutscene and forget to collect them.

THE LEAGUE ROUTE AND ITS LEVEL CAPS

Your starting Sujimon cap is 10. The main route is Jack at Trainer Rank 10, Queen at 20, Ace at 30, Joker at 40, then King. Each of the first four wins raises the cap by ten: 20, 30, 40, then 50.

Those ranks are access requirements. The team levels suggested below are preparation targets. King becomes available after Joker's storyline is complete; you do not need to grind Trainer Rank 50 just to unlock his match.

1. JACK: THE CEO OF SUJI

At Rank 10, go to the Regal Jack Resort on Aloha Street by River Street. Beat the Section Chief and the Manager before challenging Jack. Use the breaks to adjust your team instead of carrying a bad matchup through the whole gym.

Jack's lineup is around levels 9–10. His Light fighters include Clawmmander, Slammed Dancer and Dope Dope, with Poach Roach, Monster Heel and Dungeon Troll supplying Nature, Blaze and Shadow coverage.

Bring a developed Shadow attacker for the Light-heavy team, but don't fill every slot with fragile Shadow fighters. Keep Blaze available for Poach Roach and Frost for Monster Heel. Focus down a target when you can rather than handing Jack several extra turns to work through your lineup.

Winning gets the Hotel Badge and raises your cap to 20. It also unlocks the Sujimon Stadium and Ichiban's Sujimancer job. This is the first big payoff, even if you aren't planning to finish the entire League immediately.

2. QUEEN: THE QUEEN'S SUBILEE

At Rank 20, head to the isolated resort at the west end of Aloha Beach. You reach it by swimming around the obstruction and returning to shore. Sara and Layla are the warm-up fights.

Aim for a level-20 team. Queen is heavily weighted toward Frost, so Nature is your main answer. Jaws of Death, Captain Cruncher and Death Sentencer are important Frost threats. Dojo Master is Blaze, and Hotstepper is Light.

Bring more than one useful Nature option, but keep a Frost fighter ready for Dojo Master. Leaving your whole front row as Nature gives that Blaze opponent exactly what it wants. Deal with Hotstepper when you can so its support does not stretch the battle out.

The Resort Badge raises the cap to 30 and opens the next stretch of trainer and Stadium progression.

3. ACE: A TRUE GYM BATTLE

At Rank 30, head to Ace's dojo on Fuji Street in Little Japan. Beat his Disciple and Captain first. Frost is particularly useful against their Blaze-heavy lineups, but keep an answer for the Nature fighters mixed in.

Ace's team sits around levels 28–30 and spreads its coverage across Blaze, Nature and Light. Watch Pandora's Boxer and Dosukoi Gigantes on the Blaze side, Abstracted Defiance and Sturmworm on the Nature side, and Sparkle Juggernaut among the Light fighters.

A single-type team is much less comfortable here. Use Frost against the Blaze threats, Blaze against the Nature pair, and a durable Shadow option against Light. Check the reserve row before committing your only counter to an unfavorable matchup.

Win the Dojo Badge to raise the cap to 40. Yokawa and Kuraki leave temporarily for story reasons afterward. Plan your next lineup without relying on them.

4. JOKER: SODACHI'S REVENGE

This section has an extra story step. At Trainer Rank 35, follow the message back to Ace's dojo. Sodachi leaves to train. Reach Rank 40, return to the dojo for the next scene, then follow the lead to Joker's warehouse near Harbor Street and the pier.

Bring a healthy team around level 40 and a healer. Before Joker, you face three underling teams in succession without healing between those bouts. The opening group is around level 20; the later groups are around level 30. Blaze is useful against their Nature fighters, with Light helping against Shadow if it can take the return damage.

Your team recovers before the Joker match itself, so getting through the underlings is the endurance part.

Joker's six are Slycanthrope, Pleatherface, Executioner, Boomstick Banneret, Bonecleaver and Tank Commander. That gives him one Frost, two Nature and three Shadow fighters, at levels 37–40.

Blaze handles the Nature pair. A tough Light attacker can punish the Shadow fighters, but keep its health in mind. Nature covers Slycanthrope. Super Sodachi is useful during this story stretch, but do not assume the special story form means every Sujimon now evolves automatically.

The Underground Badge raises the cap to 50. There is also an ordinary RPG fight against Joker and his men, who are level 11. Finish the scenes afterward to unlock the champion challenge.

Each of the Discreet Four also gives a Japanese Master Ticket and a bundle of Sujimunch appropriate to that stage. Use those rewards to prepare for the next cap instead of leaving them in the bag.

5. KING: ATOP THE PLATEAU

Return to the Stadium through the Sujigami PC Shop in the Anaconda Shopping Center. Prepare both teams before speaking to the Committee Agent: your Sujimon for King, and your ordinary RPG party for what follows.

King's roster is:

• Dr. Crimson: Frost, level 48.
• Judgment Spray: Blaze, level 48.
• Big Endgame Hunter: Nature, level 48.
• Pyromaniac: Light, level 48.
• Weeping Archdemon: Shadow, level 50.
• Suji Machine: Blaze, level 50.

A developed level-50 lineup with all five types covered gives you room to respond. Frost earns its slot against the two Blaze fighters. Keep Blaze ready for Big Endgame Hunter, Nature for Dr. Crimson, and your Light/Shadow choices ready for the relevant targets.

Suji Machine can take punishment. Don't waste your best Frost option before it arrives. Keep healing available, make swaps with the next enemy turn in mind, and finish enemies rather than spreading every attack across fresh targets.

After winning, you receive the Stadium Badge, $1,000 and the Suji League Trophy. Then the game switches back to ordinary RPG combat against three level-31 Committee Agents. They are weak to Electric. This is the part that can stop an early-game run even after your Sujimon have done everything right.

Finish the resolution for the Dragon Soul Bat and Sodachi becoming available as a Dondoko Island guest. The League storyline is now finished. The Stadium still has work for you if you want it.

THE STADIUM: WHAT EACH LEAGUE IS FOR

The Stadium opens after Jack, but its first events can already be above your current level cap. Unlocking an event does not mean you need to clear it immediately.

Also, Stadium battles are for prizes and points. They do not directly award the normal Sujimon EXP and Bond gains. Sujimunch prizes can train your team afterward, which is a different thing. Don't grind the Stadium expecting it to unlock your next Trainer Rank challenge.

Challenge League is a continuous fight against up to 30 enemies. Clear all 30 for Gold. Gold matters because a partial clear does not satisfy the final Divine League unlock.

• Pseudotrash Challenge: opens after Jack, recommended level 20, up to 1,050 points.
• Pest Challenge: opens after Queen, recommended level 30, up to 2,100 points.
• Power Challenge: opens after Joker, recommended level 45, up to 6,600 points.

These are your Sujimunch events. The Gold first-clear reward is 50 Super Sujimunch for Pseudotrash, 50 Hyper Sujimunch for Pest, and 50 Ultimate Sujimunch for Power. The corresponding repeat Gold rewards are 20 of those same items.

Survival League runs successive trainer battles without restoring your team's health between them. A healer is particularly useful here. You need a lineup that can finish the whole run, not one that wins the opener with a single fighter barely standing.

• Vs. City's Best: opens after Jack, recommended level 25, 1,200 points. Repeat reward: 10 Sujimon Gacha Tickets.
• Vs. Committee Agents: opens after Queen, recommended level 30, 2,000 points. Repeat reward: 20 tickets.
• Vs. Stadium's Finest: opens after Joker, recommended level 40, 2,500 points. Repeat reward: 30 tickets.

The first-clear rewards are better: City's Best lists 20 regular tickets and 5 Warrior's Musk; Committee Agents lists 20 regular tickets, 5 Japanese Master Tickets and 5 Warrior's Musk; Stadium's Finest lists 30 regular tickets, 10 Japanese Master Tickets and 5 Warrior's Musk. Treat those as one-time rewards, not a repeatable source of Master Tickets.

Grand League gives you a run of tougher trainer battles, with healing between bouts.

• Great League: opens after Ace, recommended level 35, 4,000 points. First-clear prize: 10 Japanese Master Tickets. Repeat prize: 10 regular tickets.
• Elite League: opens after King, recommended level 45, 6,000 points. First-clear prizes: 10 Japanese Master Tickets and a Legendary Warrior's Musk. Repeat prize: 20 regular tickets.
• Divine League: opens after clearing every other Stadium event, including Gold in all three Challenge events. Recommended level 50, 10,000 points. First-clear prizes include 10 Japanese Master Tickets, 10 Master Suji Gifts and Legendary Warrior's Musk. Repeat prize: 25 regular tickets.

ELITE AND DIVINE: THE ACTUAL ENDGAME

Elite puts you against True Jack, True Queen, True Ace and True Joker. These are stronger rematches, not a quick victory lap with the same low-level teams. Bring your developed level-50 roster and keep the counters that got you through their original fights.

Divine's sequence is Ralph, Spencer, Frank, True King, then Professor Morikasa, the Sujimon Sensei. The first three trainers specialize in Blaze, Frost and Nature respectively. Prepare Frost for Ralph, Nature for Spencer, and Blaze for Frank. Those teams bring the corresponding Kiwami fighter, so do not assume the opening match is free.

True King has a mixed team. Morikasa's final lineup includes High Necromancer, Scarred Yakuza, Gifted Gatherer, Arminator, Munanugget Messiah and Super Sodachi. You need coverage, enough Speed to keep acting, and healing that can recover from a bad exchange. Save MP when necessary rather than spending it as soon as a special lights up.

This is a sensible place to invest in stronger recruits and their upgrades. Getting through the League story and clearing every Stadium event are different finish lines.

WHAT TO BUY WITH YOUR POINTS

Useful exchange targets include:

• Kunoichi's Sword: 70,000 points. This matters for the Kunoichi's ultimate-weapon crafting route.
• Dynamite Nunchaku: 45,000 points.
• Level Booster: 15,000 points.
• Giant Demon Statue (Jiro) Blueprint: 8,000 points for Dondoko builders.

For repeat point farming, compare the time your team takes rather than looking only at the largest payout. Power Challenge gives 6,600 points for a full clear and can be a comfortable repeat run once your team is strong. Divine pays 10,000, but asks you to beat several serious teams. The larger number is not automatically the quicker purchase.

Keep Legendary Warrior's Musk for when your main party can handle the legendary raids it enables. Winning a Sujimon tournament is not proof that Ichiban is ready for that regular-combat encounter.

SUJIMANCER, DONDOKO AND COMPLETION

Beating Jack unlocks Sujimancer, but you still need to equip Sujimon in Ichiban's Gear menu. The job has five elemental slots. Check them when your collection improves rather than assuming the League lineup automatically supplies the right fighters.

Sujimancer skills cannot be inherited by other jobs. Play it because you want to use its summons, not because you expect to move its whole skill set onto Hero later.

Dondoko Farm opens when the resort reaches two stars and gives spare Sujimon another use through training and work assignments. A recruit outside the battle team can still help your island.

Finally, the Sujidex is not the same checklist as the recruitable roster. Sujimon Sensei asks you to register 200 enemy types in the Sujidex. Sujimon Snag 'Em asks for 10 recruits from battle. Gacha pulls are useful for the League, but they do not replace that battle-recruitment requirement.

If you are stuck, check this in order: the next story message, Trainer Rank, the current level cap, your active team's Speed, then type coverage and healing. Most walls come from one of those. Fix the thing actually blocking you, beat the next challenge, and leave the perfect collection for when you feel like collecting.

text:
Dondoko Island: a full route from the first rubbish pile to a five-star resort

Dondoko Island starts with a broken resort and somehow ends with Ichiban deciding whether the island needs another convenience store or a love hotel. Both are perfectly respectable planning decisions here.

The five-star run becomes much easier once you know what each system actually wants. This covers the progression gates, money, building, guests, farm and final fight, without getting into Infinite Wealth’s main-story spoilers.

GETTING STARTED

Dondoko opens during Chapter 6. Finish its introduction and the dolphin transport becomes available, letting you return to Hawaii and come back later through the Dondoko Island pickup point on Aloha Beach.

You don’t need to finish the resort in one sitting. The resort and farm stop progressing while you’re back in Hawaii. Farm jobs use timers measured in minutes, so start them before doing other island activities, rather than expecting a trip to Honolulu to finish them.

Learn the signboard fast-travel system early. Once more land opens, walking everywhere eats time that could be spent collecting, crafting or dealing with guests.

THE NUMBERS THAT ACTUALLY MATTER

Satisfaction is the resort score raised by furnishings placed outside. Popularity comes heavily from collecting specialties and reaching their Dokopedia milestones, with buildings and advertising providing other gains. Guest Approval belongs to each individual visitor and affects how their stay goes. Livability belongs to Ichiban’s house and improves his island health.

Building Talent is another separate requirement. Crafting raises it, and clearing later areas requires specific levels. A rich island can still get stuck because Ichiban hasn’t made enough things.

Here’s the certification route. The two numbers on each line are Satisfaction, then Popularity:

• One star: 1,000 / 700. Clear the Entrance and Great Tree. Those areas require Building Talent 5 and 10 respectively.
• Two stars: 5,000 / 2,000. Clear the Hills at Talent 15 and Lighthouse at Talent 20.
• Three stars: 15,000 / 4,500. Clear the Fields at Talent 25, and win the battle at the Lake. You need to build the separate bridges to both destinations.
• Four stars: 28,000 / 8,000. Clear the Cave at Talent 30 and Forest at Talent 40. Build Dondoko Bridge for the Cave and Leafy Leaf Bridge for the Forest. The Forest also opens through the island’s progression after the farm boar event, so follow that event if you’re waiting for access.
• Five stars: 43,000 / 13,000. Complete the public-safety objective and concluding Washbuckler battle.

Speak to Matayoshi when the current requirements are complete. Having enough points doesn’t automatically certify the island.

CLEARING LAND WITHOUT EMPTYING YOUR WALLET

Smashing every rubbish pile today doesn’t permanently reclaim an area. You still have to pay at its sign and meet the Building Talent requirement. Until then, the rubbish returns on later days.

Repeated cleanup improves the area’s cleanliness rank and lowers its clearing fee. These are the starting prices and the lowest, S-rank prices, all in Dokobucks:

• Entrance: 30,000 → 9,000.
• Great Tree: 50,000 → 15,000.
• Hills: 250,000 → 75,000.
• Lighthouse: 350,000 → 105,000.
• Fields: 700,000 → 210,000.
• Cave: 800,000 → 240,000.
• Forest: 1,000,000 → 300,000.

Bridges cost another 200,000 each. They aren’t included in the clearing fee. The Fields and Lake bridges become available at two stars; the Cave and Forest routes come later at three stars.

That makes the two bridges plus the cheapest Fields clearing 610,000 altogether. The two later bridges plus the cheapest Cave and Forest clearings total 940,000. Those are useful savings targets, not prices you must wait to reach.

If you’re short of money, clean again tomorrow while working on Popularity and Talent. If you already have every other requirement and can afford the current fee, paying sooner may be worth more than another discount. Don’t spend three days protecting a saving that’s smaller than the benefit of unlocking the next part of the resort.

MAKE MATERIALS LESS OF A CHORE

The basic crafting materials are wood, stone, cloth, plastic, iron, glass and semiconductors. Purple trees supply wood, rocks supply stone, and rubbish supplies the other materials. Check the ingredient you’re actually missing before doing a full gathering lap.

After reclaiming land, collect the daily materials beside Matayoshiya. Clearing an area doesn’t mean its resource supply is gone forever. More reclaimed land improves that collection.

Check Matayoshiya’s exclusive furnishings as your rank rises. Waste dumps, Woodworking Areas and Stoneworking Areas add to daily production. Buy and place useful ones as the budget allows. These are functional investments, not decorations to leave in storage.

Resource producers can go in awkward corners. They don’t need the prime road frontage you want for guest attractions. Keep that distinction in mind when the central plaza starts getting crowded.

Early spending should solve the next problem: a bat upgrade if gathering is slow, a lodging if you have nowhere to put guests, a material producer if crafting keeps stalling, or expansion money if land is the last certification requirement. There’s no need to buy every available upgrade the moment it appears.

BUILD WITH A PURPOSE

Use the DIY bench outside Ichiban’s house. Compare Satisfaction, ingredients and footprint before crafting. A huge score is less useful when the building doesn’t fit anywhere you’ve cleared.

Large buildings are especially useful because you’re increasing Building Talent while making something that can raise Satisfaction. Recheck the recipes after leveling. Bottles on the beaches and blueprints acquired elsewhere in the main game can also expand the selection.

Once you have access to them, these are useful examples of substantial Satisfaction gains:

• Kotobuki Drugs: 1,847, Rustic.
• Cafe Alps: 2,540, Elegant.
• Akuashimaru: 3,694, Pop.
• Love Hotel: 4,498, Sleazy.

You don’t need those exact four buildings. They illustrate why a handful of useful structures can do more for certification than filling every gap with tiny objects. Keep an eye on which materials each one consumes so you don’t exhaust the same scarce ingredient repeatedly.

The Cabaret Club is worth 9,121 Satisfaction, but it also needs rare ore. Don’t put your whole resort on hold waiting for a prestige building when several ordinary structures would clear the same requirement.

The four genres are Rustic, Sleazy, Pop and Elegant. Building a mixture helps you meet more guest preferences. You aren’t required to choose one theme for the whole island, and you don’t need to max every genre to finish the story.

GET POPULARITY MOVING EARLY

If Satisfaction is already above the next target, more buildings may be solving the wrong problem. Open the Dokopedia and look for collection milestones you’re close to reaching.

Collect familiar fish and bugs as well as new ones. Repeated catches matter. Plants, shells, produce and souvenirs also contribute through their entries, so a collecting route should include more than the fishing spots.

A good habit is to pick things up while traveling between necessary jobs. Once the farm opens, use its gathering spots too. You get another set of specialties without having to abandon your other progress.

Upgrade the net or harpoon when those activities are regularly slowing you down. And before selling everything, check whether any of it is needed for a recipe you’re about to make. Selling a specialty doesn’t erase its discovery from the Dokopedia, but it does remove the ingredient from your inventory.

LODGINGS: PRICE, CAPACITY AND WHEN TO UPGRADE

Guests open up after the one-star stage. Buy their lodgings from Kenzo and place them before trying to fill the island with visitors.

The options are:

• Cozy Cardboard Home: F rank, three guests, 30,000 Dokobucks.
• Simple Tent: E rank, three guests, 50,000.
• Wooden Shack: D rank, four guests, 100,000.
• Sturdy Wooden Shack: C rank, four guests, 150,000.
• Rustic Cottage: B rank, four guests, 250,000.
• Exquisite Cottage: A rank, four guests, 350,000.
• Opulent Cottage: S rank, five guests, 500,000.

The first two are available at one star, the shacks at two, and the cottages at three. You can eventually place five lodgings, so five S-rank cottages give a maximum capacity of 25 guests per tour.

You don’t have to buy every intermediate rank. For example, if you’re already close to affording an S cottage, buying an A cottage first may delay the upgrade you actually want. But an affordable shack that lets you accommodate useful guests now can still earn its place.

Leave space for larger replacements. The better lodging has to fit, not just exist in your shopping budget.

LAY OUT THE RESORT FOR PEOPLE WHO HAVE TO WALK

The lodging limits are regional: two across the southern areas, two across the Fields/Cave area, and one in the Forest. You can’t put all five around the main plaza.

A practical layout is two southern lodgings near the central plaza, two in the Fields/Cave area, and the last in the Forest, with a small cluster of facilities around each group. This keeps useful attractions close rather than scattering them around the whole map.

Place interactive facilities next to paths with their entrance facing the path. Look for the “Available for Guest Leisure” confirmation. A road touching the back of a building can still leave its entrance unusable.

The building’s placement score and a guest’s ability to use it are separate concerns. A decorative arrangement can help your numbers while doing very little for visitors if nobody can reach the useful objects.

Use free paths to make short, accessible streets. Keep a mix of facilities that offer guest enjoyment and spending opportunities. Put production equipment in the less convenient space instead of building a hotel district around a rubbish dump.

HOW TO PICK AND PLEASE GUESTS

A tour lasts three island days. Read the four requests before inviting someone:

1. Minimum lodging rank.
2. Minimum island Satisfaction.
3. A genre condition, such as a theme level or a required number of themed objects.
4. A particular specialty registered in the Dokopedia.

That fourth request catches people out. If somebody asks for a certain fish, bug or ore, discovering it satisfies the collection requirement. You don’t have to keep one forever or hand it to that guest.

For theme requests, check Dondoko Island Information. The genre bars have marked thresholds. “Slightly,” “Fairly,” “Very” and “Extremely” correspond to increasing levels, so you can see whether one more themed item is likely to help.

Start with visitors whose requests you already meet. A higher-paying guest with unsuitable lodging and several unmet conditions isn’t automatically the better booking. Better-than-requested lodgings can help Approval, so assign the beds carefully.

Greet visitors each day and check anyone who is falling behind. Give souvenirs where they’re useful rather than waiting until the tour is over to discover a guest never became happy. Very unhappy guests can leave early.

Subaru handles souvenir development and production at Dondoko Beach. Developing a recipe costs money and can have a Building Talent requirement; making it then consumes the listed materials. Keep a small supply rather than spending your last resources producing gifts for guests who are already delighted.

Once Subaru offers campfires, 100,000 Dokobucks buys a group Approval boost, once per tour. It happens when you end that day. This is most attractive with a large group that still needs help. It’s an unnecessary expense when everyone you’re hosting is already happy.

MORE GUESTS AND COMMERCIALS

New visitors also come through main-game progress, substories and people you meet outside Dondoko. You don’t have to unlock the entire guest list before making the resort work.

At three stars, Subaru offers a Local TV commercial for 100,000 Dokobucks. At four stars, the Online Broadcast option costs 200,000. Advertising adds Popularity and can bring new potential guests.

Check Subaru’s menu for when another slot is available rather than budgeting around buying unlimited ads in one day. Keep collecting while an ad is active. Advertising helps finish a Popularity gap, but it shouldn’t consume the money you still need for a bridge or a workable guest setup.

DONDOKO FARM: WHAT TO ASSIGN AND WHY

After reaching two stars and the following introduction, use the raft at Mukku Beach. The farm connects your recruited Sujimon to four useful facilities.

Each facility can have up to three workers. One is enough to start a job, but filling the team, using higher-Friendship Sujimon and matching the relevant type improves the chance of Huge Gains. A mismatched team can still complete the work, so don’t leave everything idle because you lack a perfect roster.

Workshop: earns Dokobucks.

• Lickety Split: 10 minutes, 20,000 expected Dokobucks, Blaze affinity.
• Hyperfocused: 20 minutes, 45,000, Frost.
• Slow & Steady: 30 minutes, 100,000, Nature.
• Mastercrafting: 60 minutes, 300,000, Light.

Those are the listed expected payouts before a possible bonus. Mastercrafting has the strongest base return per minute of these four, so it’s a sensible choice when you’ll be busy on the island for a while. The short job is useful if you need a smaller payout sooner.

Crop Patches: grow produce for collections, souvenirs and selling. Choose the duration, select three crops, then assign workers. You can repeat the same crop in multiple slots. Match the workers to the crops’ displayed types and use the yield preview to see what the arrangement does.

Choose crops for a reason. If a souvenir needs a specific vegetable, grow that. If you’re trying to improve Popularity, look at the produce entries closest to another milestone. Longer assignments are convenient when you don’t want to keep returning to the raft.

Recycling Center: produces crafting resources. Read the actual output list rather than picking whichever job is longest. Semiconductor Salvage takes 30 minutes and targets semiconductors. That can be much more useful than another mixed batch when one material is blocking your next few buildings. Use the affinity shown in your game when assigning the team.

Training Spot: costs Dokobucks to give Sujimon EXP. Better courses can have Friendship requirements. Use it for recruits you want to develop, but remember that Sujimon League progression controls their level caps. Training on the farm doesn’t remove those caps.

Interact with the Sujimon while visiting. Greetings and the available encouragement interaction improve Friendship, which feeds back into farm performance. Check finished jobs, collect the output and set up the next assignment.

Later, pests can interrupt production. Deal with the farm alert using a Sujimon battle and keep a usable battle team available. Running around the main island for another hour won’t fix an interrupted station.

The farm is useful support. It doesn’t replace the rest of the island, and you don’t need to become Sujimon champion before making worthwhile use of it.

KEEP ICHIBAN READY FOR THE FIGHTS

Dondoko combat uses the island bat and heart meter. Your normal party setup isn’t what carries these encounters.

Kenzo’s three tool upgrades cost 50,000, 150,000 and 300,000 Dokobucks. The bat is usually the first priority because it helps both clearing and combat. Improve the gathering tools afterward according to what you spend time doing.

Furniture inside Ichiban’s house raises Livability. Get some extra hearts before the harder fights instead of leaving his house empty while the resort gets every luxury. Kenzo offers home expansion once you’ve progressed far enough, but you can get useful health gains by furnishing the initial space first.

Go to bed through the house calendar instead of always staying outside until the game ends the day for you. Resting earlier recovers health; using every last moment of the day can leave you without that recovery. Carry healing food for fights where sleeping isn’t an option.

When Washbucklers attack, check the map and stop them, especially around occupied lodgings. In combat, use space, dodge swings and attack openings rather than standing inside a group mashing the bat button.

THE FIVE-STAR FINISH AND THE MONEY

Once you have 43,000 Satisfaction and 13,000 Popularity, speak to Matayoshi about the remaining public-safety objective. Prepare your health, healing items and bat, then follow the event to the boat at Dondoko Beach and finish the Washbuckler showdown.

The five-star completion gives $300,000 and Essence of Dondoko Beam. Across all five certification bonuses, the mainland cash rewards total $490,000: $10,000, $30,000, $50,000, $100,000 and $300,000.

Dokobucks are separate. Dolphine can convert them at 1,000 Dokobucks to $10. Leave the resort enough working money before exchanging the surplus. An extra $1,000 in Honolulu isn’t much help if the island now can’t afford the next thing you need.

After five stars, choose what you actually want to finish. Hosting 100 guests, building a prettier resort, filling the Dokopedia and earning more money are different projects. Keep tours running if you’re chasing the guest total rather than assuming the story ending completes it for you.

A DAILY ROUTINE THAT KEEPS EVERYTHING MOVING

• Collect the daily resource supply and check today’s tasks.
• Greet guests, spot anyone struggling, and deal with intruders.
• Clear rubbish in the next area you want to reclaim.
• Craft toward the next Satisfaction and Building Talent requirements.
• Collect specialties on the way, concentrating on nearby Dokopedia milestones.
• Collect and restart farm assignments when they finish.
• Spend on the next actual bottleneck, check certification progress, then rest before health recovery is lost.

If progress stops, identify the missing requirement before doing another lap. It might be one bridge, ten more catches, a Talent level or an island event. Knowing which one is a lot more useful than building a sixth shop and hoping the inspector notices.

text:
🌞⚡️💡
Like the petals of a giant sunflower turning toward the sun, 27,135 heliostats spread across the Gobi Desert—part of a 50 MW concentrated solar power (CSP) plant in Delingha, in China’s northwestern province of Qinghai. They harness sunlight to generate clean electricity.

The project provides enough clean energy annually to power more than 80,000 households, while simultaneously reducing carbon dioxide emissions by approximately 124,000 tons per year.

💥These images offer a striking look at a concentrated solar power (CSP) tower plant. In this technology, thousands of computer-controlled mirrors (heliostats) precisely direct sunlight onto the top of a central tower. The extreme heat generated there is used to heat molten salt or water vapor, which in turn drives a turbine—enabling the production of electricity even after the sun has set.💥

text:
Brysen Wright was in eighth grade when Miami became the first college to offer him a scholarship in December 2023.

Today the #1 prospect in the SC Next Class of 2028 committed to Miami over Florida and Texas. He's also reclassifying to 2027.

With Wright, it wasn't just raw talent. His father took a very intentional approach to his youth development.

Here's how he went from an eighth-grade phenom to the most coveted recruit in the country...

1. Build a Multi-Sport Foundation

Before narrowing his focus to football, Wright built a broad athletic base. At 13, he was playing both football and basketball year-round, practicing about 4 days a week.

Basketball builds footwork, body control and ball skills that translate directly to playing receiver.

2. Teach the Body Before Adding Weight

When Wright started lifting, the goal wasn't to put up big numbers. It was to get his body used to resistance and tension.

His coaches had him use a hex bar, which keeps the weight centered and puts less stress on the lower back — a safer way to learn to lift.

3. Master the Fundamentals of the Position

Everything in his workouts is tailored to what a wide receiver actually needs on the field.

He relentlessly drills the basics:
- Footwork and agility work
- Catching the ball high, low and over the shoulder
- Hand work to beat press at the line

4. Train Like a Pro (At the Right Dose)

Wright trains at a facility in Ponte Vedra, Florida, that has worked with 46 NFL players, 27 NFL quarterbacks and three top-five draft picks.

They use force plates and velocity-based training to measure his explosiveness, and he's already clocking 20.8 mph on a treadmill sprint.

But the coaches know you can't train a teenager like a pro.

Their NFL clients train 4 hours a day, 5 to 6 days a week. High schoolers have far less time and very different recovery needs.

So the coaches titrate down their NFL offseason system, giving him pro-level stimulus without burning him out.

Most parents skip straight to step 4.

Wright's father didn't, and now his son is the #1 prospect in the country.

text:
Army Rewards Soldier ₦500,000 For Rejecting Kidnapper’s Bribe

A Nigerian soldier has been rewarded with ₦500,000 after refusing to accept money offered by a suspected notorious kidnapper to secure his release.

The soldier, identified as Private Utim Terwase, reportedly intercepted the suspect following an attempted escape. Rather than accept the money offered to him, Terwase maintained his position and handed the suspect over to the appropriate authorities.

His decision has now earned him commendation and financial recognition from the Nigerian Army.

The reward was approved by the General Officer Commanding (GOC) of the Army’s 3 Division and Commander of Operation Enduring Peace, Major General Maxwell Dangana.

The presentation took place on behalf of the GOC and was carried out by the Commander of Sector 6, Colonel Philimon Malgwi.

Speaking through Malgwi, Dangana praised the soldier for demonstrating integrity, discipline and professionalism, noting that his actions showed he was unwilling to trade his responsibility for personal benefit.

The Army chief said Terwase had upheld the values expected of military personnel by refusing to compromise his duty and ensuring the suspect remained in the hands of the authorities.

Interestingly, the ₦500,000 reward presented to the soldier was equivalent to the amount he reportedly turned down.

Dangana described the soldier's conduct as worthy of recognition and urged other personnel serving under Operation Enduring Peace to follow his example.

He also reaffirmed the military's commitment to encouraging accountability, ethical behaviour and professionalism among its officers and soldiers, stressing that personnel must continue to carry out their constitutional duties with honesty and dedication.

(Source: Vanguard Newspapers)

#Tonbo #TONBO #TonboImaging

Tonbo Imaging India Limited Q2 & H1 FY27 Concall Highlights:

👉Q2 & H1 FY27 & Future Outlook :
▫️H1 FY27 revenue ~₹219 Cr vs ~₹77 Cr in H1 FY26; Q2 revenue ₹183 Cr vs Q1 ₹36 Cr
💠Order inflow in H1 ~₹188 Cr
💠Q1 was delayed by order receipt and execution

▫️H1 FY27 profitability: gross profit ~₹75 Cr vs ~₹40 Cr in H1 FY26 (~87% higher), gross margin 34.62%
💠EBITDA ₹31.15 Cr (14.2% margin) vs ₹11.75 Cr in H1 FY26
💠PAT ₹5.8 Cr (2.61% margin)
💠Gross margin lower than FY26's 51% due to product mix

▫️Q2 FY27: EBITDA ₹44 Cr (24.11% margin), PAT ₹23.5 Cr (12.71% margin)
💠Q1 FY27 had an EBITDA loss of ₹13 Cr and a PAT loss of ₹17.7 Cr

▫️Revenue is lumpy quarter to quarter; management wants performance judged annually (3–5 year view for a products-based defence business)
💠In FY26, H1 was 22% of revenue and H2 was 78%

▫️H2 FY27 revenue expected to be materially better than H1; no formal revenue or margin guidance given
💠Basis: ₹250 Cr order book, contracts under negotiation and pipeline that could convert in the next 2–3 months
💠Guidance restricted as the IPO was only a couple of weeks ago

▫️Margins: H2 EBITDA margin expected to be higher than H1's 14%
💠Higher export share expected in H2 plus better product mix to lift gross margin
💠Employee cost is the largest cost below gross margin and largely fixed quarter to quarter, so it falls as a % of revenue at higher revenue

▫️Revenue mix: tactical ~70–80% of business today; platforms expected to take a larger share over time
💠H1 FY27 revenue: tactical ₹1,229 Mn, platform ₹941 Mn
💠Exports ~35% of H1 revenue, domestic ~65%

▫️R&D spend (excluding HPM): ~₹16 Cr in H1, of which ~₹3 Cr through P&L and the rest capitalised
💠Same trend expected in H2; FY27 total ~₹30 Cr, of which ~₹25 Cr capitalised
💠Capitalisation starts once blue-sky research is complete and customer intent is in writing (LOIs); klystron-level technology development is expensed, HPM product development is capitalised

▫️Management's stance: non-linear growth possible at some point from continued R&D investment; timelines for platform opportunities are hard to predict

👉Order book / projects and pipeline:
▫️Confirmed order book ₹2,498 Mn (~₹250 Cr) as of 30 Sep 2026; further ~₹408 Cr contracts under negotiation
💠Domestic ₹1,822 Mn (~73%), export ₹676 Mn
💠Platform ₹2,053 Mn (82% of order book), tactical ₹445 Mn
💠Contracts under negotiation: ~₹250 Cr tactical, ~₹150 Cr platform

▫️Execution timelines:
💠Tactical: delivery in 3–6 months from order; orders received by December can convert in 3–4 months as common subsystems are held in inventory
💠Platform: 6–18 months; part of the order book will execute in FY28
💠Contracts under negotiation: portion expected to be executed in FY27 if concluded by December, remainder next year

▫️Orders expected from short-term pipeline (next 2–3 months) and 9–12 month medium term, mainly OCPP and Ministry of Defence procurement
💠Expected to execute ~₹100–200 Cr this year from new orders; anything above that becomes the opening order book for next year

▫️Tactical systems — India demand:
💠Stated requirement ~80,000 thermal weapon sights and handheld thermal imagers plus ~27,000 image intensifier sights; only part of the Indian Army's overall requirement
💠Deck breakup: 75,000 thermal weapon sights, 5,000 handheld thermal imagers, 27,000 image-intensified sights, 56 laser target designators; indicative price ₹3–10 lakh per unit for weapon sights
💠Procurement activity expected over the next 6–18 months; OCPP orders timeline not more than 12 months, capital procurement takes longer (RFIs ongoing, RFPs expected, trials 1–1.5 years)
💠Mix of OCPP and capital procurement within the 80,000 units

▫️Tactical systems — international: ~10,000 thermal weapon sights and monoculars in near-term opportunities

▫️Platform systems:
💠Indicative price ₹25 lakh–₹5 Cr
💠Arjun Mk1A remote control weapon station EO systems supplied, exported to partners in several countries; thermal imager upgrades on Konkurs anti-tank missile launchers (BMPs and ground launchers)
💠MPATGM seeker / command launch unit and loitering munition seekers are field tested, past prototype stage; production orders awaited; deck cites India MPATGM seeker/CLU shortfall of 68,000 systems
💠Lightweight gimbals for loitering munitions and reconnaissance aircraft: pilot integrations under way with partners in India and overseas
💠Naval: imported stabilised gimbals on naval vessels replaced with Tonbo systems
💠Counter-drone: T-Rex drone detection system developed 2+ years back, 20 systems sold internationally and a couple in India, detects objects at 40 km in the dark
💠Positioning system for HPM being developed for a Middle East customer, at a TRL higher than 4

▫️Strategic export order (Oct 2026): ~EUR 65,000 FOPM order from a European state-owned company for the EO/IR stabilised seeker, entry into an export loitering munition programme
💠Customer has an option to order up to ~EUR 13 Mn on acceptance
💠Option is part of the ~₹408 Cr contracts under negotiation, not in the ₹250 Cr order book
💠Supply subject to End User Certificate and Government of India export authorisation; deck cites EU loitering munition seeker opportunity of 5,000 units

▫️Directed energy (HPM) — status:
💠Base Strike product at TRL 4; LOIs signed for 11 units (5 for Indian Navy as minimum order quantity, 6 for a European customer)
💠First delivery not before FY29–30; product engineering and testing risk to be cleared by FY29
💠First system cost ~₹160 Cr: EXIM loan sanctioned ~₹120 Cr, iDEX ADITI grant ~₹25 Cr, ~₹15 Cr from own balance sheet
💠Hard costs ~₹120 Cr; capitalised employee expense ~₹20 Cr over the next 2.5 years, a subset of the ₹160 Cr
💠Pricing: ~₹200 Cr per system for Indian Navy, ~$25 Mn per system for international customers
💠Three platforms in development: naval (very long range, under iDEX ADITI), Army, and shorter-range airborne variant
💠Investment over 3–4 years; management calls it an option being built, not short-term revenue

▫️Directed energy — market:
💠Global DEW TAM $3.82 Bn by CY2030, CAGR ~50%
💠India DEW TAM ~$290 Mn by CY2030; Army roadmap ~90 and Navy ~40 systems

👉Q&A :
▫️India DEW market size vs ~$290 Mn:
💠Overall India market ~140 systems at ~₹200 Cr each = ~₹28,000 Cr
💠The ~$290 Mn corresponds to the FY30 number, not the overall market

▫️Gross margins by segment:
💠Domestic tactical ~40–45%
💠Domestic platform ~45–50%
💠Exports ~60–65% (tactical and platform not split)

▫️Q2 revenue from the US (₹615 Mn in H1 FY27):
💠Platform subsystems; customer not disclosed

▫️Epirus as DEW competitor:
💠Epirus restricted largely to US DoD and some Five Eyes variants; Tonbo has no such restrictions and is in discussions with Five Eyes countries and Japan
💠Rafael system is sub-1 km; Turkey also has a ~1 km system; India has nothing in the 3–5 km range; Tonbo's multibeam klystron targets 3–5 km

▫️Product development model:
💠Tonbo creates specs from customer discussions, proves them overseas, then Indian customer includes them in RFPs; not built on DRDO specs
💠Example: DRDO/Israeli-technology thermal weapon sights weigh 1.2–1.5 kg; Tonbo's sights are 400–500 g, 8-hour life, target engagement at 1 km (deck: sights under 500 g, 8+ hr, 1,500 m)

▫️Platform order book content: includes both legacy larger gimbals and newer seekers / counter-drone systems

▫️Can H1 revenue be beaten:
💠Three sources of H2 revenue: existing order book, contracts under negotiation (if concluded by December), and short-term opportunities where RFPs are out and field trials are on
💠Programmes seeded in Q1 typically convert into purchase orders in Q2 and execute in Q3–Q4

▫️Macro:
💠India: TPCR plan covers next 10 years, procurement expected to continue
💠Europe: ~$800 Bn rearmament budget over 5–10 years

▫️Exports to the US: management declined to comment

👉 Others :
▫️Balance sheet: net worth ~₹564 Cr as of 30 Sep 2026; bank borrowings ~₹169 Cr, mainly for working capital
💠One bank raised cash credit from ₹30 Cr to ₹50 Cr after quarter end; talks under way with the other two banks to raise limits
💠Working capital days H1 FY27: 454 (FY26: 517)
💠Net cash from operating activities H1 FY27: ₹(484) Mn

▫️Market share: ~30,000 thermal weapon sights deployed in India, ~20,000 of them Tonbo's (>65% share)
💠India needs to grow towards ~300,000 weapon sights; management expects share of ~50–60% in new programmes

▫️Competition in India: Bharat Electronics, Tata, Alpha in tactical systems
💠Tonbo owns IP across optics, sensor electronics, video processing and fire control electronics
💠BEL is also a customer; Arjun Mk1A RCWS electro-optic system is Tonbo's
💠No Indian competitor internationally; no competitor in India for directed energy

▫️Business model: 100% proprietary IP, 136 R&D engineers, free of ITAR, fabless with multiple ISO 9001-certified manufacturing partners
💠28,000+ systems deployed across 24+ countries; 20,000+ thermal sights in Indian service

▫️Listing: shares listed on NSE and BSE on 23 October 2026 after a ₹852 Cr offer for sale, subscribed over 135 times

text:
Why didn't more wizards use Avada Kedavra during the Battle of Hogwarts if it's so powerful, even though it's illegal?

If Hogwarts’ defenders pointed their wands at the Death Eaters and shouted Avada Kedavra, they wouldn't cause a nosebleed. The curse physically cannot be cast in self-defense.

To perform it, a witch or wizard must possess a genuine, deep-seated desire to commit murder. This psychological requirement is spelled out early in the series. When Barty Crouch Jr. (disguised as Mad-Eye Moody) introduces the Unforgivable Curses to fourth-year students, he explains that without the malice behind it, the spell is entirely useless. Similarly, Bellatrix Lestrange mocks Harry’s attempt to use the Cruciatus Curse on her, explaining that "righteous anger won't hurt me for long", to use such magic, you have to genuinely want to cause suffering. 

Beyond the psychological barrier, using the Killing Curse carries catastrophic spiritual consequences. In the Harry Potter universe, the act of murder rips the soul apart. This is the exact mechanism Voldemort uses to create his Horcruxes. The spiritual toll is so severe that Albus Dumbledore specifically asks Severus Snape to kill him to spare Draco Malfoy's soul from the mutilating effects of murder. The members of the Order of the Phoenix and Dumbledore's Army understand this dark magic and refuse to damage their own souls, even in a war.

Furthermore, Avada Kedavra is tactically unnecessary for a skilled wizard. The magical arsenal offers incredibly effective, non-lethal combat spells that are much easier to cast in the chaos of battle. Stupefy knocks an opponent unconscious instantly. Petrificus Totalus paralyzes them entirely. Expelliarmus removes their weapon. In a frenzied melee, stunning a Death Eater achieves the exact same immediate result, removing a combatant from the field, without requiring the user to summon a profound desire to end a life.

Even when the defenders did kill in battle, they relied on other magic. When Molly Weasley strikes down Bellatrix Lestrange in a blind rage, the text never states she used Avada Kedavra. The Battle of Hogwarts was fought not just to defeat Voldemort, but to reject his methods. The defenders survived the bloodiest battle of the Second Wizarding War using the exact defensive magic they were taught to rely on.

The broader historical category is an experience in which the surroundings seem charged with a presence, pressure, or movement that changes how everything feels before its source can be identified. Western writers have described this through sudden dread, bodily disturbance, sacred awe, an altered sense of place, and impressions resembling sound without ordinary hearing. Several substantial examples emerge once the search extends beyond particular syllables.

🧵

Greek sacred landscape: a place begins to alter the person within it. In Plato’s Phaedrus, written in the fourth century BCE, Socrates notices his speech becoming unusually inspired and connects that change to the place where he and Phaedrus are sitting. At 238c–d, he describes the setting as holy and anticipates being carried into divine frenzy. The Greek expression nympholēptos means being seized by the nymphs. The useful connection is the relationship between environment and inward change: the place acquires an agency that Socrates experiences through what is happening to his own speech and consciousness. This is a philosophical dialogue’s depiction of inspiration arising within a charged setting. 

https://t.co/P5Pdy2AqHx⁠

Roman sacred dread: a presence is felt while its identity remains uncertain. In Virgil’s Aeneid, VIII.349–354, composed in the first century BCE, Evander describes a wooded hill whose sanctity makes people tremble. He identifies it as a divine dwelling while acknowledging uncertainty about which god inhabits it. The sequence matters: the place produces awe before the presence receives a settled identity. The experience has already acquired force even though its explanation remains incomplete. This is a particularly close ancient literary example of an atmosphere carrying significance that exceeds what anyone can point to or name. 

https://t.co/aO0ecGVfOq⁠

Seneca: the whole arrangement of a place produces the conviction of presence. In Moral Letters, 41.3, from the first century CE, Seneca describes entering a grove of exceptionally tall, ancient trees. Their height, the enclosure of interwoven branches, the seclusion, and the continuous shadow together generate a conviction that a divine power is present. He extends the discussion to deep natural caverns, river sources, and dark waters. His description is especially useful because the effect belongs to the encounter with the entire setting. No individual tree supplies the complete meaning; the environment is experienced as a whole, and that experience changes the observer’s orientation toward it. 

https://t.co/trS1ziBuHv⁠

Greek panic: an initially uncertain disturbance becomes a shared perceptual world. Pausanias, writing in the second century CE, recounts a night of terror during the Gallic retreat from Delphi in 279 BCE. In Description of Greece, 10.23.7–8, a few men initially imagine approaching horses and enemies; the disturbance then spreads through the army. The men cease to recognize familiar voices, bodies, and equipment, treating their own companions as enemies. Pausanias associates such causeless terror with Pan. This account offers more than a name for an oppressive atmosphere: it describes a progression in which apprehension changes perception, altered perception produces action, and the resulting action supplies further reasons for terror. Within the narrative, the surrounding world becomes hostile through the participants’ mutually reinforcing reactions. 

https://t.co/gCpqmq3zpB⁠

text:
Writers who used syllables to represent an inwardly experienced resonance, and others who explicitly described a “sound” perceived without ordinary hearing. The clearest examples are below. They include fiction, accounts of spiritual experience, and contemplative teachings.

🧵** a lot of stuff from India in this one, and that makes sense**

“HU” — Hazrat Inayat Khan, The Mysticism of Sound, “Abstract Sound,” early twentieth century.

Khan describes a presence filling space whose vibrations are, in his account, “too fine to be either audible or visible to the material ears or eyes.” He says it is experienced inwardly and describes its culmination as Hu. His account places it within and around the person, giving it both an inward and an encompassing character. This is a direct example of an author assigning a written syllable to what he understands as a pervasive, ordinarily inaudible spiritual resonance. 

https://t.co/NYznYBQvPc⁠

A humming or gong-like resonance perceived without the ears — Algernon Blackwood, The Willows, 1907.

Blackwood supplies an unusually explicit description. A character says: “I don’t think a gramophone would show any record of that. The sound doesn’t come to me by the ears at all.” He describes the vibrations as reaching him through another manner of perception and seeming to be within him. The experience belongs to a landscape already felt as pervaded by an unfamiliar presence. Blackwood gives it an acoustic comparison—humming and a distant gong—rather than a spelling such as “UUU.” This is fictional testimony, but the distinction between ordinary sound and the experience being represented is unmistakably present in the text. 

https://t.co/6pWXW6vACR⁠

“CHINI” and “CHINI-CHINI” — Haṃsa Upaniṣad, in K. Narayanasvami Aiyar’s Thirty Minor Upanishads.

This text describes stages of inwardly apprehended nāda, or spiritual sound. It explicitly gives the first two as chini and chini-chini, then compares subsequent experiences to bells, a conch, stringed instruments, a flute, drums, and thunder. The syllables describe what the practitioner is said to experience after contemplative practice; they are distinct from the mantra discussed earlier in the passage. This is a particularly clear example of a text attempting to render an inner experience through phonetic notation. Its setting is individual contemplation rather than an atmosphere shared across a city. 

https://t.co/I7bLdxXjcv⁠

“TOM,” explicitly spelled “T-O-M” — Ramakrishna, conversation recorded under October 26, 1884, in The Gospel of Sri Ramakrishna.

Ramakrishna uses tom, the resonance of a gong, to communicate his experience of manifestation and dissolution within an unlimited consciousness. He describes waves arising from an ocean and returning into it, then states: “I have clearly perceived all these things.” Here the written syllable is an explanatory analogy for a reported spiritual perception: its onset, expansion, and subsiding convey a process he says he experienced. It is more precise to call this a sonic representation of his experience than a claim that an external gong was sounding. 

https://t.co/4ETRvt8ZcT⁠

“BOUM,” “BOU-OUM,” and “OU-BOUM” — E. M. Forster, A Passage to India, 1924, Chapter XIV.

Forster writes all three forms as approximations of the Marabar caves’ echo. The experience begins with an actual echo, then acquires a pervasive psychological significance for Mrs. Moore: distinctions among words, values, and religious meanings collapse into the same boum. After leaving the cave, she experiences its implications across her understanding of existence. This example combines an external acoustic encounter with an inward continuation that changes the character of the world as she experiences it. The written syllable becomes the recurring expression of that altered condition. 

https://t.co/wWnV2eYW80⁠

text:
""Ooo-ooo-ooo”: Bely’s Unseen Sound and the Long History of an Atmosphere Becoming Audible

Remember the black pulse essay: https://t.co/2MPB9qXmXV

🧵

In Andrei Bely’s Petersburg, “Ooo-ooo-ooo” gives an approaching historical upheaval a presence before that presence can be adequately explained. The sound hangs over the outskirts of Moscow, Petersburg, and Saratov. A factory whistle, the wind, and a dog are considered and excluded. The narrator even questions whether “sound” is the appropriate category. Yet the experience becomes unusually distinct. Something seems to have entered the surroundings, and the surroundings now communicate a condition that no individual speaker fully possesses. Bely identifies it as the October song of 1905. 

https://t.co/ZJ6lSxFpy6⁠

The historical investigation has to follow several features together: the prolonged vowel, its recurrence, the apparent absence of a source, the impression of a collective presence, and the connection between sound and a changing world. Those features have different histories. Their intersections produce the strongest comparisons. An exact resemblance in lettering would be less revealing than a passage in which an unexplained sound reorganizes the relationship between a person and everything surrounding them.

Bely’s Russian spelling is “у,” approximately the English “oo.” Its grouping varies across appearances. At a crowded political meeting, the prolonged sound becomes the medium through which words about revolution and strikes intermittently emerge. In another scene, one person hears it while another reports hearing nothing. The motif passes between collective noise, uncertain perception, and the apparent voice of the environment. Three-part repetition is one of its forms; its persistence across these different situations supplies its larger significance. 

https://t.co/QlYPORF8py⁠

This movement matters. When a sound belongs to an identifiable gathering, an observer can say where it comes from. When the same sound appears beyond that gathering, its significance can exceed its immediate cause. The earlier scene becomes a memory through which the later scene is heard. Recurrence makes apparently separate locations feel connected. The novel gradually supplies an acoustic continuity beneath the discontinuity of individual encounters.

David Rodriguez’s study, Eulogy for Apollo: Synesthesia and Musicality in Andrei Bely’s Petersburg and James Joyce’s Ulysses, identifies this movement explicitly. It follows the ominous vowel into a passage where a distant humming becomes the rumble of a demonstration. Drawing on Ada Steinberg’s analysis, Rodriguez treats the recurring vowel as part of the novel’s musical organization: it links otherwise separated people and places through an insistent impression of anxiety and impending destruction. This is a useful critical foundation for understanding the sound as a recurring structural element. 

https://t.co/FiHr6Zo7jp⁠

The decisive question becomes how a sound acquires the apparent dimensions of a world. A person hears something local, but experiences it as evidence of a condition extending beyond the immediate scene. The sound becomes an index of what is gathering elsewhere. Once that connection has been established, a recurrence can reactivate the whole expectation without repeating its explanation.

The historical parallels begin with much older ways of making catastrophe, divine presence, and collective emotion audible.

text:
It is the attempt to subordinate economic power to democratic accountability while preserving personal liberty. It seeks a society in which major resources are governed for the public good, but where public ownership does not become an excuse for political monopoly. Planning must remain answerable to citizens; institutions must remain open to criticism; and equality must never be purchased through the destruction of conscience.

The name attached to a system matters less than its distribution of power. Who makes the decisions? Who can question them? Who benefits from them? Who suffers? What institution can correct them? These are the questions by which political ideals should be measured.

Patriotism, Nationalism, and Human Dignity

Patriotism is an attachment to a particular place, language, landscape, history, and community. It may be affectionate without being arrogant, protective without being expansionist, and loyal without being blind.

Nationalism, by contrast, transforms belonging into a competition for superiority. It asks the individual to admire symbols more than people, defend the nation’s honor more fiercely than its victims, and regard criticism as betrayal. Its deepest weakness is psychological: it offers dignity through collective vanity rather than through the moral treatment of actual human beings.

Nationalism may also be transferred to foreign regimes. A person who cannot bear to criticize the power closest to him may relocate his hopes onto a distant government and excuse its crimes in the name of historical necessity. Another form defines identity almost entirely through hatred—against a class, ethnicity, religion, nation, or political faction. In both cases, the believer is relieved of the difficult responsibility of examining his own side.

Class hierarchy deforms human dignity at every level. The poor may be compelled to conceal their true feelings, internalize deference, and regard humiliation as ordinary. The privileged may develop a cultivated blindness, treating deprivation as a statistical inconvenience rather than a human wound. A just society must therefore challenge not only unequal resources but also the habits of contempt, fear, and submission that inequality produces.

The Seizure of the Past

Whoever controls the past gains immense influence over the future. A society unable to remember cannot learn; a society forbidden to compare cannot judge; a society whose archives belong to one authority cannot distinguish history from official mythology.

Totalitarian power revises the past not merely to deceive future generations but to destabilize the minds of the living. Former allies become lifelong enemies. Failed policies are transformed into triumphs. Victims are recast as criminals. Documents vanish, photographs are altered, and personal memories are treated as suspicious whenever they conflict with the official narrative.

The purpose is to make individuals doubt themselves. If a person can be persuaded that his own memory is false, then he becomes dependent upon the institution that claims to remember on his behalf. The archive becomes an instrument of obedience, and history becomes a courtroom in which the present government is always acquitted.

A free society must therefore protect plural memory. It must preserve documents, permit historical disagreement, defend independent scholarship, and acknowledge national failures without regarding such acknowledgment as treason. A country does not become weaker because it can face its own crimes. It becomes weaker when it must lie about them.

The Responsibility of the Intellectual and the Citizen

The intellectual, writer, journalist, and scholar bear a special obligation to place truth above ideological allegiance. Thought must not become a decorative screen behind which suffering disappears. The more abstract the language, the more urgent the duty to return to the concrete human consequences of policy.

You continue to conflate the certainty of an event in God’s decree with mechanical coercion, which every historic Reformed confession explicitly rejects. Westminster Confession 3.1 directly refutes your caricature: God ordains whatsoever comes to pass, "yet so, as thereby neither is God the author of sin, nor is violence offered to the will of the creatures; nor is the liberty or contingency of second causes taken away, but rather established."

Certainty does not destroy agency. The crucifixion of Christ could not have turned out otherwise—it was fixed by God's eternal decree and prophetic word—yet Peter insists the men who nailed Him to the tree acted by "lawless hands" out of their own wicked choices (Acts 2:23, 4:27–28). If the certainty of an outcome erases choice and guilt, then Herod, Pilate, and Judas are entirely innocent robots.

Adam was created upright with true liberty and genuine capacity to obey; he did not eat under divine compulsion, but out of his own voluntary rebellion. God sovereignly decrees history through the authentic choices of moral creatures, never by puppet mastery, which is why Adam—and every sinner who gladly follows in his steps—stands fully and justly accountable.

text:
Which Reactors for the Philippines?

Lots of questions out there about the different classes of nuclear power plants and how and when they could be applied in the Philippines. Allow me to share my personal opinions on their readiness for purchase and where they would fit. I’ll largely exclude any Chinese or Russian offerings for obvious reasons.

First, consider how our electric systems work and are structured. There are three major grids, only weakly interconnected. The big one is of course Luzon. As the major population and economic center of the archipelago, it has the largest demand, the most transmission wires, and the most power plants. The Visayas has its own much smaller separate grid as does Mindanao. The interconnections between this grids are of very limited capacity relative to the grid demand.

Conventional, commercial nuclear power plants have reactors cooled with water, usually normal, highly purified water and are called light water reactors (LWRs.) But in one commercial product, the Canadian CANDU, the cooling is done with “heavy water,” isotopically enriched in a rare natural isotope of hydrogen called deuterium. Heavy water is not that much different from normal water, just a lot more expensive. Economies of scale have driven these conventional reactors to ever larger sizes, with the commercial range from 1,000 MW to 1,400 MW electrical output. The CANDU comes in one size of 700 MW but it is optimized for multiple reactors in one complex so a pair are 1,400 MW too.

For Luzon, we need multiple LWRs or CANDU clusters to make a dent in the current and future demands. Some of us expect a need to build a dozen by 2050 while even the PH DoE’s modest plan calls for just four. The primary choices are the Korean APR1400 or the American AP1000 but the French offer one like they sold Finland but these tend to be expensive. The Russians are having sales success with their VVER. Bangladesh, (Bangladesh!!!) has just began operation of their VVERs and Egypt is building a pair too.

A newer development that is in the news a lot are “small modular reactors” or SMRs. These are either single reactors of about 300 MW in size or a “pack” of smaller individual reactors interconnected and operating as a group of 250 MW for six or 460 MW for a dozen.

General Electric-Hitachi (GEH) has sold three to the Ontario Power Generation (OPG) in Canada (now under construction) and two to the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) in the US. Other than being smaller than a conventional LWR, and placed in an underground silo, it is very conventional with little technological risk. Its primary competitor so far is the NuScale design. That company wants to build a small reactor package in a factory and plug the “module” into an on-site building. The reactors are like conventional light water reactors in principle only much smaller. No one has bought one yet. There are others of more exotic designs like the Natrium reactor cooled with molten sodium and funded by Bill Gates but again, no buyers.

The issue with SMRs is that there are serious doubts they will ultimately make electricity at competitive prices. The history of nuclear power has long shown that “bigger is cheaper” and it will take a successful demonstration to break that trend. This will take a few more years before we should buy, first to complete construction then to operate.

If SMRs do prove out technically and financially, there could be opportunities for a decision in five or six years in the Visayas, say on Cebu or Bohol, with transmission connections to the large loads of the Cebu metropolitan area that might work. One idea was for a couple to serve Davao City too although a pair of 1,000 MW reactors might make more sense there and current politics are unfavorable.

Lastly, there’s microreactors, land-based, less than 50 MW each. A packaged 5 MW unit might fit on the isolated islands otherwise not connected to the grid (SPUGs) but the economics are unappealing compared to the existing diesel generators. Most of the SPUGs are going away anyway due to the DoE’s efforts.

The US is spending a lot of development money on microreactors but the intended application is for military bases. This part of a greater American “Fortress” plan to make all the major military bases in the US independent of the civilian infrastructure for at least 90 days. They will be “Mil-Spec” to meet military standards and so cost is not a primary consideration. They might find niches in some civilian applications like remote mining or drilling where the logistics cost for diesel fuel would be high.

The US hasn’t mentioned export yet but if microreactors work for US bases they would also work on the nine EDCA joint bases or at Subic Bay. Whether the Department of National Defense (DND) is interested or would accept them as part of a military assistance package is not yet clear.

Summary: Large conventional reactors for the immediate need on Luzon. SMRs in the Visayas and Mindanao after a few years if and when they prove themselves. Microreactors if the US decides to give them to DND.

(All opinions are my own. Next PH nuke posting will be on PH reactor siting, out this weekend.)
Joseph Somsel
BSNE, MBA

text:
At this point, Florida may need to seriously reconsider its continued participation in the United States. Not because Florida has lost its mind, but because an alarming number of other states apparently have.

For years, Texans joked about seceding from the Union. I always thought that if Florida ever decided to establish an independent republic, Texas would be its natural partner. 

Together, the two states would possess an extraordinary economic foundation, more than 55 million residents, world-class universities, major international ports, thriving industries, and something increasingly difficult to find elsewhere in America: an appreciation for the policies that actually produce prosperity.

Unfortunately, Texas has apparently disqualified itself from admission.

Consider the sheer absurdity of what happened Tuesday. Texas spent decades building a reputation as a destination for businesses, investment, and Americans fleeing the consequences of failed economic policies elsewhere. No individual income tax. Relatively business-friendly regulation. 

An expanding economy. Millions of people moving there because it offered opportunities increasingly unavailable in the states they abandoned.

And how did Texas reward that success? By throwing out Greg Abbott and electing Democrats to every statewide office on the ballot.

Apparently, prosperity had become intolerable.

The new governor, Gina Hinojosa, campaigned on distributing $1,500 to every Texas household by raiding the state’s rainy day fund. Her so-called “corruption tax refund” would cost approximately $17 billion, consuming roughly two-thirds of the fund’s existing reserves. 

Think about the intellectual bankruptcy of that proposal. Texas accumulated substantial financial reserves to protect its citizens against economic emergencies and natural disasters, and the incoming governor’s political innovation is to spend most of them handing out checks. 

What kind of fiscal responsibility is that? It is fiscal recklessness on a breathtaking scale.

Nothing says responsible government quite like buying political affection with the emergency savings account.

But the larger problem extends beyond Texas. Americans have developed the peculiar habit of fleeing states burdened by the policies they voted for, relocating to states that prospered under different policies, and then attempting to recreate the very conditions they escaped.

It is the political equivalent of escaping a sinking ship, boarding a seaworthy vessel, and immediately demanding that the new captain drill the same holes in its hull.

Florida cannot afford to become the next casualty of this spectacular failure of reasoning. People are welcome to appreciate Florida’s economy, universities, opportunities, and quality of life. But perhaps they should first consider why those things attracted them before demanding that Florida abandon the policies that helped produce them.

So, given Tuesday’s results, I propose that Florida begin considering its own republic. Texas would previously have received an enthusiastic invitation. Unfortunately, after this election, its application must be rejected for demonstrated deficiencies in political judgment.

Florida may be the last remaining candidate for a republic governed by adults.

And if the rest of the country insists on conducting a national experiment in political self-destruction, Florida ought to have the courtesy of being allowed to decline participation.
