text:
On November 3, 2026, the United States Department of Justice disclosed one of the most consequential espionage operations involving Abiy Ahmed’s government. Abraham Teklu Lemma, an American government contractor with Top Secret and Sensitive Compartmented Information access, pleaded guilty to conspiring with senior Ethiopian political, military, and intelligence officials to steal and transmit classified American intelligence between 2021 and August 2023. The material included satellite imagery, military intelligence, and information concerning armed conflicts in Ethiopia. Federal prosecutors confirmed that Ethiopian officials used the intelligence in military operations. On December 18, 2021, Lemma urged an Ethiopian contact to eliminate opposing fighters and requested drones. The American government has now established that highly classified U.S. intelligence was systematically delivered to Ethiopian officials during a devastating civil war. The identities of those senior officials remain undisclosed.

The diplomatic chronology deserves serious attention. Fitsum Arega served as Ethiopia’s ambassador to Washington from April 2019 until May 2022, encompassing the beginning of the Tigray war in November 2020 and Lemma’s espionage conspiracy in 2021. A review of Fitsum’s X account reveals no surviving posts before February 2022. On February 9, 2022, Lemma traveled to Ethiopia after printing classified material. He remained there for approximately 80 days, returning to the United States around April 30. Two days later, on May 2, Fitsum published his farewell message. On May 3, Assistant Secretary Molly Phee hosted a farewell luncheon for him at the State Department. By May 22, Fitsum was posting from Addis Ababa. He subsequently assumed the Ethiopian ambassadorship in Canada in September 2022 and departed that position in August 2024. He later headed the Ethiopian Diaspora Service and now leads Immigration and Citizenship Services. His departure from Washington occurred during an active espionage conspiracy, immediately following Lemma’s extended visit to Ethiopia. Whether the two men had any contact during this period remains an important unanswered question.

Fitsum’s successor, Seleshi Bekele, introduces another dimension. Previously Ethiopia’s Minister of Water, Irrigation and Energy and a prominent figure in the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam negotiations, Seleshi lost his cabinet position in October 2021 and subsequently became ambassador to Washington in May 2022. During his tenure, Lemma continued transmitting classified intelligence to Ethiopian contacts. The FBI affidavit describes an Ethiopian intelligence official who communicated with Lemma through encrypted messages, requested information about military command and logistics centers, and applied for an American visa in May 2022. Investigators identified this official through his telephone number, photographs, and an Ethiopian intelligence agency website displaying his name and government title. Lemma subsequently copied information from 85 intelligence reports between December 2022 and August 2023, following the Pretoria peace agreement. His activities continued as Ethiopia confronted the Oromo Liberation Army, growing tensions in Amhara, and instability across the region. He was arrested on August 24, 2023. Seleshi remained ambassador until his resignation in May 2024, approximately eight months after the espionage charges became public.

The Ethiopian intelligence establishment adds another layer to this chronology. Abiy Ahmed previously led the Information Network Security Administration, INSA. Temesgen Tiruneh, who headed the National Intelligence and Security Service during the relevant period, also had a longstanding professional association with Abiy through INSA. Abraham Belay served as Minister of Defense during the Tigray war and was another senior figure in Abiy’s security establishment. The Justice Department has explicitly identified senior Ethiopian political, military, and intelligence officials as Lemma’s conspirators. It has not publicly named Temesgen, Abraham Belay, Fitsum, or Seleshi. Their institutional positions make the chain of command and the identity of Lemma’s handlers central questions. The FBI’s description of the May 2022 visa applicant offers a particularly specific avenue for identifying at least one intelligence contact.

The espionage continued beyond the Pretoria Agreement of November 2, 2022. Abiy himself traveled to Washington for the U.S. Africa Leaders Summit in December 2022, while Lemma remained active. In April 2023, Lemma communicated with an Ethiopian intelligence contact during another visit to Addis Ababa. The correspondence included discussion of developments in a neighboring country and arrangements for a meeting at a hotel. Sudan’s civil war began on April 15, just two days before one particularly revealing exchange, although the FBI has not publicly identified the neighboring country. The continued collection of American intelligence after Pretoria raises questions about the full scope of Ethiopia’s intelligence requirements, including the Tigray settlement, the OLA insurgency, emerging conflict in Amhara, and regional security developments.

The diplomatic succession continued after Lemma’s arrest. Seleshi resigned in May 2024. Contemporary Ethiopian reporting subsequently indicated that Washington declined the proposed appointment of Lencho Bati as ambassador. Binalf Andualem eventually assumed the position in February 2025, leaving an approximately nine month interval without an ambassador. Viewed together, the sequence encompasses two successive Ethiopian ambassadors, an intelligence operation lasting more than two years, direct communications with Ethiopian security officials, the transfer of classified American military intelligence, and significant changes in Ethiopia’s diplomatic representation in Washington. The central questions remain unresolved: who recruited Lemma, who introduced him to his Ethiopian handlers, which senior officials received the intelligence, and what role, if any, did Ethiopia’s diplomatic mission play? The November 2026 guilty plea establishes the espionage operation and its military consequences. Identifying the officials who directed and benefited from it is now essential to understanding the full extent of the breach.

Ukraine diplomacy advanced through completed Washington and Brussels meetings

Russian and Ukrainian representatives met face-to-face at the White House concerning the completed Oleshky humanitarian operation. Trump then met privately with Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev, but not with the Ukrainian delegation. Separately, U.S., Ukrainian, NATO and European officials concluded Brussels discussions identifying five negotiating objectives: permanent consultations, reliable crisis communications, military transparency, reciprocal de-escalation measures and a durable European-security framework. No agreement was announced. 

Direct sources: White House⁠ · Reuters⁠

Analysis

* Cuba — implemented escalation: The individual designations are operational sanctions; the sectoral determination also creates authority for broader future penalties. Its effect on Cuban military revenue or political conduct is not yet measurable.

* Ukraine — diplomatic process materially advanced: The meetings produced a more defined negotiating framework ahead of the November 10–11 Abu Dhabi talks. Trump’s separate meeting with only the Russian envoy and the absence of agreed guarantees mean this cannot yet be counted as a peace agreement or balanced settlement.

text:
Bernie Sanders Wants to Hit the Brakes on AI. But Can America Afford to Stop the Engine of Its Next Economic Revolution?

The battle over artificial intelligence is rapidly becoming one of Washington's most consequential economic and technological debates. Following Democratic victories in the midterm elections, Senator Bernie Sanders is reportedly renewing calls for a moratorium on data center construction, a pause on advanced AI development, and a permanent prohibition on artificial superintelligence.

Sanders argues that the extraordinary expansion of AI infrastructure presents serious risks to employment, electricity affordability, water resources, and public safety. His position reflects growing frustration among communities concerned that the financial benefits of artificial intelligence are flowing toward technology companies while infrastructure costs are increasingly felt locally.

The political debate is shifting from whether America should lead the AI revolution to who should bear the costs of that leadership.

Across the country, proposed data centers have encountered resistance from residents worried about rising electricity demand, environmental pressures, and the limited number of permanent jobs some facilities create. These concerns deserve serious consideration, particularly when communities are asked to accommodate infrastructure supporting companies valued in the trillions.

Yet a nationwide moratorium introduces another set of economic and strategic questions. Artificial intelligence is becoming increasingly important to scientific discovery, healthcare, manufacturing, cybersecurity, and productivity. Restricting its development could delay benefits while creating uncertainty for investors, researchers, and infrastructure providers.

The international dimension further complicates the debate. If American AI development slows while China continues investing aggressively, technological competition will not disappear. It will simply continue under different national priorities and regulatory frameworks.

Supporters of Sanders' approach emphasize that preventing potentially irreversible harm must take precedence over commercial ambitions. Critics argue that broad restrictions could undermine innovation without establishing meaningful international safeguards. Both perspectives expose the difficulty of regulating technologies whose future capabilities remain uncertain.

The distinction between responsible oversight and technological prohibition is therefore essential. Transparent electricity pricing, enforceable environmental standards, independent safety evaluations, and stronger community protections offer policy options that do not necessarily require halting an entire industry.

President Trump's veto authority also means that congressional support alone would not guarantee federal restrictions become law.

The defining challenge for Washington is ensuring that AI development delivers measurable public benefits without transferring unacceptable economic, environmental, or security risks to society.

America's technological future cannot be measured solely by the number of data centers constructed or the billions invested in computing infrastructure. It must also be judged by affordability, employment opportunities, public trust, and responsible governance.

The AI revolution will ultimately be judged not simply by how powerful its machines become, but by whether the prosperity they generate reaches the people whose communities and resources make that progress possible.

text:
First CFP - The Third Workshop on Bangla Language Processing (BLP 2027)

Theme: Beyond Text: Bangla in the Era of Reasoning, Agents, and Multimodal Intelligence

Co-located with NAACL 2027, San Francisco, California, United States, June 2027

Workshop website: https://t.co/vRffscble5
Apologies for cross-posting.

Foundation models are moving language technology beyond text generation toward reasoning, retrieval, agents, speech, and multimodal interaction. However, many of these advances remain concentrated in resource-rich languages. Despite a long history of NLP and speech research, Bangla remains underrepresented in frontier AI systems, particularly in reasoning, agentic applications, culturally grounded knowledge, speech-native models, multimodal understanding, and safety. Further challenges arise from dialectal, code-mixed, transliterated, and diaspora varieties, as well as related languages such as Assamese.

The Third Workshop on Bangla Language Processing (BLP 2027) aims to bring together researchers working in NLP, speech, multimodal AI, and human-centered computing to advance language technologies that can understand, reason, communicate, and act effectively in diverse Bangla settings. Building on BLP 2023 and BLP 2025, this edition focuses on linguistically inclusive, culturally grounded, trustworthy, multimodal, and accessible AI.

We invite original research papers presenting new methods, datasets, benchmarks, evaluations, applications, and analyses. Bangla is the primary focus, while comparative studies involving related or underrepresented languages are welcome when they offer insights transferable to Bangla and other low-resource settings. We particularly encourage research that addresses real-world linguistic diversity and practical constraints on data and computation.

Topics of Interest

We welcome papers on topics including, but not limited to:
Foundation Models: Bangla and multilingual large language models; pretraining, adaptation, and instruction tuning; synthetic data; efficient models; cross-lingual transfer; and robustness to dialects, code-mixing, and transliteration.
Reasoning and Agents: Verifiable, symbolic, and neuro-symbolic reasoning; retrieval-augmented generation; long-context understanding and memory; tool use, planning, and code generation; and single- and multi-agent systems.
Speech and Conversational AI: Automatic speech recognition, speech synthesis, and AudioLLMs; spoken question answering and dialogue; code-switched speech; speaker and language recognition; and conversational systems.
Multimodal and Grounded AI: Vision-language and audio-visual models; multimodal question answering and reasoning; document and scene understanding; multimodal generation; and culturally grounded multimodal evaluation.
Trustworthy and Human-Centered AI: Safety and alignment; adversarial robustness; hallucination and factuality; bias, fairness, and interpretability; cultural understanding; human-AI interaction; accessibility; and responsible deployment.
Resources, Evaluation, and Efficient NLP: Corpora, datasets, and benchmarks; representative resources for underrepresented varieties; human and LLM-based evaluation; data-efficient learning and inference; and core NLP tasks such as machine translation, information extraction, question answering, and summarization.

Planned Shared Tasks
BLP 2027 also plans to organize three shared tasks:
Task 1 - Adversarial Prompt Classification: Identifying benign and adversarial prompts in Bangla, including jailbreaks, prompt injection, and code-mixed or transliterated attempts to bypass LLM safety safeguards.
Task 2 - Multilingual Question Answering: Culturally and regionally grounded open-ended QA in Bangla, English, Assamese, and Hindi, with monolingual QA and multilingual QA settings based on the MultiNativQA resource.
Task 3 - BLP Datathon: Collecting regional Bangla speech recordings and identifying where open-source automatic speech recognition (ASR) models struggle with different dialects and accents through community-driven participation.

Detailed task guidelines, datasets, evaluation procedures, and participation timelines will be announced separately at https://t.co/Kfrvlge2wX.

Important Dates
Paper submission deadline: February 15 (Monday), 2027
Notification of acceptance: March 26 (Friday), 2027
Camera-ready deadline: April 16 (Friday), 2027
Workshop: June 2027, co-located with NAACL 2027 (exact date TBA)
All deadlines are 11:59 p.m. Anywhere on Earth (AoE).

Submission Details
We welcome original, unpublished research, including completed work and promising work in progress. Submissions will undergo double-blind peer review, with acceptance decisions made by the workshop program chairs.

Submission categories are:
Full papers: Up to 8 pages.
Short papers: Up to 4 pages, including work in progress and innovative research ideas.
Shared-task system papers: Up to 4 pages.

Camera-ready versions may use up to 9 pages for full papers and 5 pages for short papers, subject to the final proceedings guidelines. Accepted papers will be presented orally or as posters.

All submissions must follow the official ACL/ARR two-column formatting guidelines. Authors should use the official style files without modification. We recommend checking submissions with ACL PubCheck, which should also be used for camera-ready papers. For double-blind reviewing and anonymity requirements, please consult the ARR anonymity guidelines.

Further details on submission procedures, including any ARR-reviewed paper route, will be announced on the workshop website.

Submission portal: TBA

Invitation to Review
Researchers with relevant publication experience who are interested in joining the program committee are invited to complete this reviewer interest form: https://t.co/12N3XJThSK

Mentoring Program
We offer a mentoring program to support students and newcomers. It includes pre-submission mentoring to help finalize paper drafts and a buddy program during the in-person workshop. If you would like to receive mentoring, please sign up using the mentoring registration form.

Sponsors
We invite companies and institutions to partner with us in advancing Bangla language technology and research. Sponsoring BLP 2027 provides an opportunity to engage with leading researchers, industry professionals, and emerging scholars from around the world while supporting innovation and collaboration in Bangla language processing.

text:
I believe this article offers a thoughtful assessment of China’s economy, but a broader perspective is needed when examining China in the context of global industrial competition, international trade, and its long-term industrialization.

First, China’s current economic challenges are fundamentally structural rather than simply a crisis of economic growth.

In the first three quarters of 2026, China’s GDP grew by 4.6%, manufacturing by 5.7%, high-tech manufacturing by 14.3%, information transmission, software and IT services by 10.4%, and total goods trade by 18.8%.

These figures demonstrate that China’s industrial foundations, technological upgrading, and international competitiveness continue to develop.

Of course, property investment fell by 20.6%, retail sales grew by just 1.1%, and fixed-asset investment declined by 7.2%. These figures clearly show that insufficient domestic demand has become a major constraint on further economic development. (China’s National Bureau of Statistics, October 19, 2026)

Second, I don’t think China’s industrial development model should simply be interpreted as sacrificing consumption to pursue exports.

This model has certainly involved trade-offs in resource allocation and income distribution, but it has also enabled China to build one of the world’s most comprehensive industrial systems, accumulating technological expertise, engineering experience, and industrial capabilities that cannot easily be replicated elsewhere.

That is one of China’s most important sources of strength in global economic competition.

The IMF’s 2026 Article IV consultation report on China also acknowledged that China contributed approximately 30% of global economic growth over the previous three years. At the same time, it identified the property adjustment, weak domestic demand, and deflationary pressures as challenges that still need to be addressed. (IMF)

These two assessments are not contradictory.

Third, the international environment cannot be ignored.

US tariffs and technology restrictions against China, together with efforts by some Western countries to restructure global supply chains, are increasing the costs of international competition for Chinese businesses.

Yet China has not lost its industrial competitiveness. It continues to expand its market presence in renewable energy, industrial equipment, digital technologies, and advanced manufacturing.

The World Bank’s October 2026 projections also place China’s expected annual economic growth at around 4.5%, while emphasizing that household consumption and the property adjustment remain important challenges. (World Bank)

Finally, I believe China’s next major economic transition must be from a model driven primarily by production capacity toward one in which production capacity and household consumption reinforce each other.

Increasing household incomes, strengthening social security, stabilizing employment expectations, and resolving the long-term property market adjustment are no less important than developing advanced technologies.

China has already demonstrated its ability to build a powerful manufacturing system.

The next step is to demonstrate that this productive capacity can also translate into higher living standards and stronger domestic purchasing power.

A country with a comprehensive industrial system, an enormous domestic market, and sustained technological innovation should not have its entire economic model declared a failure simply because it is going through a property market correction.

What really matters is whether China can successfully complete this structural economic transition.

text:
I'd like to offer a candid assessment of the state of China's economy.

My assessment may seem somewhat paradoxical: China's economy is one of the world's strongest and most successful but also, in some ways, in bad shape.

China's economic transformation over the years has involved a tremendous development of productive capabilities. There isn't much China cannot manufacture. From the perspective of technological and economic development — as well as improving the material lives of its people — China's economic trajectory has been, and continues to be, a success.

The same can be said of the leverage and power China commands in the global economy. It is arguably the only individual economy that has strong leverage in trade negotiations with the US, and it is playing an huge role in reshaping the global economic order due to its sheer economic power. This is primarily thanks to its dominance in global manufacturing and international trade.

At the same time, some important economic indicators are pointing in a negative direction. The three most important ones, in my view, are the property slump, youth unemployment, and deflationary pressures. I'm not mentioning slowing GDP growth because it is still quite impressive by international standards — it's just that it's lower than the standard we've set for China.

A lot of these economic problems are linked through low levels of consumption. This is, to some degree, tied to the model of development China pursued. In order to raise investment rates and channel credit into the industrial sector, households have effectively subsidised industrial development (for example, through low deposit interest rates).

Here's an important point: China is not the first country to pursue this model. Export-oriented industrial development has historically often involved choosing industrial investment over consumption. So, there's a trade-off here. But China could have managed the problems on the demand side better, although there's now some evidence that consumer spending is stabilising.

Overall, though, while we should acknowledge these problems, it's hard to see this model as anything other than a success for China over the long term. China's economic transformation is still one of the most remarkable instances of large-scale poverty reduction and economic development.

And, very, very importantly: the country now has strong technological capabilities embedded as tacit knowledge in its institutions and people. While problems on the demand side are serious, technological capabilities do not disappear overnight.

Second, I don’t think China’s industrial development model should simply be interpreted as sacrificing consumption to pursue exports.

This model has certainly involved trade-offs in resource allocation and income distribution, but it has also enabled China to build one of the world’s most comprehensive industrial systems, accumulating technological expertise, engineering experience, and industrial capabilities that cannot easily be replicated elsewhere.

That is one of China’s most important sources of strength in global economic competition.

The IMF’s 2026 Article IV consultation report on China also acknowledged that China contributed approximately 30% of global economic growth over the previous three years. At the same time, it identified the property adjustment, weak domestic demand, and deflationary pressures as challenges that still need to be addressed. (IMF)

These two assessments are not contradictory.

Third, the international environment cannot be ignored.

US tariffs and technology restrictions against China, together with efforts by some Western countries to restructure global supply chains, are increasing the costs of international competition for Chinese businesses.

Yet China has not lost its industrial competitiveness. It continues to expand its market presence in renewable energy, industrial equipment, digital technologies, and advanced manufacturing.

The World Bank’s October 2026 projections also place China’s expected annual economic growth at around 4.5%, while emphasizing that household consumption and the property adjustment remain important challenges. (World Bank)

Finally, I believe China’s next major economic transition must be from a model driven primarily by production capacity toward one in which production capacity and household consumption reinforce each other.

Increasing household incomes, strengthening social security, stabilizing employment expectations, and resolving the long-term property market adjustment are no less important than developing advanced technologies.

China has already demonstrated its ability to build a powerful manufacturing system.

The next step is to demonstrate that this productive capacity can also translate into higher living standards and stronger domestic purchasing power.

A country with a comprehensive industrial system, an enormous domestic market, and sustained technological innovation should not have its entire economic model declared a failure simply because it is going through a property market correction.

What really matters is whether China can successfully complete this structural economic transition.

text:
PhysicsWallah CFO Amit Sachdeva: “We’re Best Placed to Deliver Govt’s Free Coaching Plan” — Company Keeps Guidance of Doubling Ebitda and 30% Revenue Growth; Offline Expansion Slowed to 20-30 Centres a Year, Vidyapeeth Expected to Turn Profitable This Year

Core Theme 
PhysicsWallah is positioning itself as a ready partner for the government’s free coaching plan while managing a NEET-led slowdown in offline by slowing centre rollouts, diversifying Xylem and leaning on online and K-12 growth, with management holding firm on doubling Ebitda, 30% revenue growth and a full-year profit.

Context: Record Quarter and the Govt’s Free Coaching Plan
PhysicsWallah posted record quarterly revenue of ₹1,242 crore in the September quarter, while doubling its net profit to ₹142 crore

During the quarter, Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced plans for free online coaching, an initiative that founder Alakh Pandey offered to support on a no-profit basis

Sachdeva: the plan is a big enabler, and PhysicsWallah was among the first to reach out to the PMO

Co-founder Prateek (Maheshwari) has met officials two to three times, offering to build the infrastructure and develop content on the government’s terms

Nothing has been finalised yet, but the company is in constant touch

Order book already includes ₹80 crore worth of government projects

Government Exam Enrolments: Why They Fell
Government exam enrolments fell 24% in the first half

The decline is almost entirely attributable to Utkarsh, its Rajasthan subsidiary

Other state examination categories performed well

Election-bound states tend to hold back notifications until the last six months; Uttar Pradesh votes next, followed by Rajasthan the year after, so a rebound is expected

Offline centres are less exposed to these fluctuations, as most students enrol in their first or second year of college, irrespective of government examination notifications

NEET: Admissions Below Last Year
Demand has partly returned, with Q2 online enrolments rising 31% and collections increasing 27%

However, full-cycle online enrolments remain 13% below last year, with collections down 7%

Offline enrolments are down 8%

Xylem, where 80% of the business is linked to NEET, was hit the hardest, as vacant seats weigh on a cost structure with fixed expenses

Company is adding commerce courses to Xylem to diversify offerings and has advanced its crash courses to the next three-six months

Expects NEET demand to rebound next year as the National Testing Agency (NTA) moves the examination online, much as it did with JEE four-five years ago

Offline Expansion: Slower, Profitability-Focused
Public markets value offline at about 1x revenue, while online businesses command consumer-tech multiples; the company wants to prove offline profitability first

Will open 20-30 centres annually for at least the next two years, down from 70 planned at the time of IPO

Most will be micro-centres with around 1,000 seats in the South, rather than large centres catering to 10,000-15,000 students

Slower expansion will help reduce costs and accelerate the offline business’s break-even

Vidyapeeth, which contributes over 75% of offline revenue, is expected to turn profitable this year

Guidance and Pricing
Company is maintaining its guidance of doubling Ebitda and achieving 30% revenue growth

Online growth is offsetting the NEET slowdown in offline, while K-12 growth is ahead of plan

Acquisitions contribute less than 5% to growth

Remains committed to delivering a full-year net profit

In Vidyapeeth, which accounts for two-thirds of offline revenue, ARPU has risen 9-10%, driven by fee increases backed by improved results

Blended ARPU grew 5.4%, compared with 7% last year, partly due to the changing mix following the addition of new centres and slightly weaker performance in the NEET dropper segment

Nanta Tech Limited showcased robust performance in H1 FY27, driven by significant growth in its robotics & AI and audio-video (AV) segments. The company is strategically positioning itself as a technology-led solution provider, focusing on physical AI and automation.

𝗙𝗶𝗻𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗶𝗮𝗹 𝗣𝗲𝗿𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗺𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗲 📊 :

text:
AMAZON SWAPS GRUBHUB FOR UBER EATS, DOORDASH $DASH -9%:

DoorDash (DASH) at $179.92, -$18.67 / -9.40% on Thursday.

DoorDash clears every test of the Quality Len5 on its September 30 books, and Thursday's news did not touch them. No other Len5 we weigh holds it. Amazon (AMZN) set off the selling by making Uber Eats, the delivery app of Uber Technologies (UBER), a free perk for U.S. Prime members. DoorDash fell almost 16% in the morning, then won back part of the drop. Prime has offered free restaurant delivery since 2022, through Grubhub, and DoorDash grew through those years. Uber won Amazon's customers and fell anyway. DoorDash's December-quarter results, due in February, are the first to count orders taken with the new perk in place.

The Quality Len5 wants a gross profit, a profit on the owners' money, and debt no larger than that money. DoorDash's September-quarter books show all three:
- Gross profit, revenue minus the direct cost of handling orders: $2.31B.
- Profit: $466M, on $10.72B of owners' equity, the money shareholders have in the business.
- Debt: $2.73B of convertible notes, bonds that can turn into shares.
What would knock it off the Quality Len5: borrowing for its next purchase that lifts debt past that equity. Instacart (CART) at $57.79, -$1.43 / -2.41% on Thursday. DoorDash agreed on October 29 to pay $65 a share for the grocery delivery app, about $17B in all. At least three-quarters is cash, and DoorDash has a $13B bridge loan, short-term bank borrowing, lined up. The deal is not expected to close before the end of 2027. DoorDash is on none of the Momentum, Quality-Value, Deep-Value and Special-Situations, Hypergrowth or Income Len5es. Momentum wants a climb near the high, and Thursday's close sits 24% under the August 26 closing high. The value Len5es want a discount, and the shares cost about 74 times the past year's profit. Hypergrowth wants sales multiplying, and DoorDash's rose 34%. Income wants cash paid out, and DoorDash pays no dividend. Instacart is on none of those five either; the $65 offer sets its price.

Amazon (AMZN) at $260.21, -$5.82 / -2.19% on Thursday.
Amazon and Uber announced the deal before Thursday's open, effective at once. U.S. Prime members pay no delivery fee on Uber Eats restaurant orders of $25 or more, placed through Amazon's own site or app. Amazon is not a current pick on any of those five Len5es.

DoorDash did its falling in the first hour and a half:
- Low: about $167.40, down 15.7%, just after 11am ET.
- Close: $179.92, with about two-fifths of the drop won back.
- 18.8M shares traded, 3.7 times the 30-day average.
- SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY) at $733.00, -$33.81 / -4.41% on Thursday.
It was DoorDash's worst day since November 6, 2025, and it took about $8B off the market value. DoorDash fell more than twice as far as the S&P 500 fund.

Prime's free-delivery perk is four years old, and it has not slowed DoorDash yet. Amazon gave Prime members a free Grubhub membership in 2022 and put Grubhub ordering inside its app in 2024, an arrangement that ended Thursday. Grubhub is now owned by privately held Wonder. Evercore ISI told clients it saw no clear sign that the Grubhub years slowed DoorDash's U.S. restaurant business, the markets site Investing reported. DoorDash took 59% of delivery-app spending in the September quarter, by Consumer Edge card data that David Hanson of TIKR cited. Uber Eats took 18%. DashPass, DoorDash's own membership for waived delivery fees, costs $9.99 a month. Prime members now get a similar break from Uber Eats without paying more. Our read: sellers treated an old perk as a new threat because DoorDash's largest rival now stands behind it.

Uber Technologies (UBER) at $68.78, -$1.09 / -1.56% on Thursday.
Uber got the Prime deal and still fell, about a third as far as the S&P 500 fund. On Wednesday its delivery arm reported $28.5B of September-quarter orders, up 22% from a year earlier. DoorDash jumped 8.3% that day, a move Hanson tied to Uber's numbers, and Thursday erased it. Uber is on none of those five Len5es; its shares touched a one-year low of $64.04 on October 29, the wrong direction for Momentum.

The December quarter gives the new perk eight weeks to pull orders away from DoorDash:
- DoorDash's forecast for the dollar value of December-quarter orders, given October 29: $35.4B to $36.4B.
- September quarter: $33.9B.
Those results are due in February, tentatively the 17th. Orders under $35.4B would be the first sign the perk took customers. Until then, the share price is the only DoorDash number the deal has changed.

text:
Child Killer Jeffrey Weisheit Executed in Indiana 

Alyssa Lynch, 8, and her brother, Caleb, 5, were killed in a 2010 house fire set by Jeffrey Weisheit. Weisheit is seeking clemency ahead of his scheduled Nov. 5 execution (Courtesy photo Indiana Capital Chronicle)

https://t.co/MPWurl8WVM® Crime Report Nov 6 2026

Indiana executed 50-year-old Jeffrey A. Weisheit by lethal injection early Thursday morning, November 5, 2026, at the Indiana State Prison in Michigan City. 

He was pronounced dead at 12:45 a.m. CST. 

Weisheit was convicted in 2013 for the 2010 arson murders of his girlfriend's two young children, 8-year-old Alyssa Lynch and 5-year-old Caleb Lynch, near Evansville.

‘Every single day without them is a struggle’: Mother urges Indiana to uphold death sentence

State officials also released a $275,000 invoice for execution drugs ahead of death row inmate Jeffrey Weisheit’s scheduled Nov. 5 execution.

By Casey Smith
October 19, 2026 5:34 pm
Indiana Capital Chronicle

The mother of two children murdered by Jeffrey Weisheit urged Indiana’s parole board Monday to reject his plea for mercy, saying her children deserved the futures he took from them.

Her appeal came hours after Weisheit’s family and attorneys asked the five-member board to recommend sparing his life, citing his history of mental illness and head injuries, his religious conversion and a written request from the murdered children’s father for forgiveness and a sentence of life without parole.

The Indiana Department of Correction also released a $275,000 invoice Monday in response to the Indiana Capital Chronicle’s requests for execution drug purchasing records.

Dated Sept. 25, the invoice does not specify the drug or number of doses, nor does it show if or when the pentobarbital arrived. DOC did not provide an updated drug inventory on Monday.

Weisheit was sentenced to death in 2013 for murdering 8-year-old Alyssa Lynch and her 5-year-old brother, Caleb, in a fire at his home near Evansville. Their mother, Lisa Lynch, was working an overnight shift and had left the children in his care.

Monday’s testimony in Indianapolis concluded the public hearings on his clemency request following an interview Friday with Weisheit at the Indiana State Prison in Michigan City.

His execution is scheduled there before sunrise Nov. 5.

The board did not issue a recommendation Monday afternoon. Chair Gwen Horth said one would not come for several days. Gov. Mike Braun will make the final decision.

Mother asks board to remember her children
Speaking remotely from out of state, Lisa Lynch began her testimony through tears, asking the board to remember the children and not just the case against their killer. At Lynch’s request, only board members could see her video because of privacy concerns.

“I am here today to ensure that my children’s voices are heard, their names are spoken, and their lives are remembered,” she said. “Alyssa and Caleb are not just names on a case file, dates in a record, or photos in an evidence box.”

Alyssa was creative and loved drawing pictures of her family, Lynch recalled. She adored her younger brother. Caleb loved hugs, helping his mother in the kitchen and playing with trucks and trains.

Their deaths robbed her of watching them finish school, build careers and have families of their own, she said.

“Every single day without them is a struggle,” Lynch said. “Every birthday, every holiday, every landmark moment is marked by their agonizing absence. Time passes, but the weight of losing them never fades.”

She described surviving domestic violence and emotional abuse and said efforts to blame her for Weisheit’s actions had continued into the clemency proceedings.

During Friday’s interview, Weisheit repeatedly discussed his anger and suspicions about Lynch while struggling to explain why he directed that anger at her children.

Lynch said that after the murders, she returned to school and built a career that allowed her to support her family and be home every night.

“They will always be my children,” she said. “They will always matter, and I will never stop speaking for them.”

The children’s father, Steven Lynch, took the opposite position in a sworn statement seeking life without parole. He did not attend Monday’s hearing.

“What good does it do the memory of my children to put this man to death?” he wrote. “I seek to save his family the great pain and loss from the taking of his life. I want to prevent another parent from experiencing the loss I have experienced.”

First responders describe lasting trauma
First responders and investigators described the killings and the memories they still carry.

David Bretz, the German Township Fire Department’s assistant chief at the time of the fire, said he arrived first to find flames pushing through every opening.

Firefighters found Caleb’s body on a mattress, with his hands and feet bound behind him. The search for Alyssa continued for hours. Bretz said he ultimately spotted a small hand amid the debris in her bedroom closet.

“Everything from the fire to the investigation, my deposition, testimony at the trial, and now this will be with me forever,” Bretz said. “It weakens me and terrifies me on a regular basis.”

At least three firefighters sought counseling, he said. Bretz also read statements from colleagues describing lasting trauma and said Friday’s interview had not persuaded him Weisheit was remorseful.

“Please, I beg of you, carry out the sentence that was placed upon him for the appalling crimes that he committed upon all of us,” Bretz said.

Chad Ferguson, the on-duty patrol supervisor, recalled sheriff’s deputies frantically searching places the children might have been taken. After Caleb was found, he initially could not get the words out to tell their mother.

Forensic dentist Dr. Crunchy Wells described identifying the children using dental records and recent Easter photographs.

“It was the hardest report I ever had to make,” she said. “It was the saddest thing I had ever seen.”

Retired investigators Randy Chapman and Kerri Blessinger challenged the defense’s account of Weisheit’s mental condition and remorse. Blessinger characterized the killings as domestic violence intended to devastate the children’s mother. She said forgiveness did not erase the punishment.

“Let me make one thing very, very clear: forgiveness and punishment are not the same,” Blessinger said. “They do not go hand in hand. One does not equal another.”

Vanderburgh County Prosecutor Diana Moers closed by recalling the children’s personalities and urging officials to uphold the sentence.

“The death penalty was the sentence recommended by the jury, reviewed by our courts, and so is justice,” Moers said. “Each person should be afforded the full protections of the United States Constitution and the due process that it brings.”

State challenges Weisheit’s account

Tyler Banks, chief of capital and habeas litigation for the Indiana attorney general’s office, argued that Weisheit’s sentence had survived extensive review by the courts and that his clemency presentation offered no reason to overturn it.

“A jury of his peers unanimously recommended a death sentence, and that sentence has withstood more than a decade of challenge,” Banks said. “Gov. Braun should not overturn all of those judgments.”

Banks recounted evidence that Weisheit bound and gagged Caleb, placed railroad flares near his body and in his clothing, and left both children in the burning house before fleeing the state.

He disputed Weisheit’s account Friday that he started the fire by placing a phone book on a stove burner. Banks said evidence of an accelerant and the flares contradicted that explanation.

Banks also rejected Weisheit’s unsupported suggestion that police or emergency responders might have placed the flares at the scene.

Horth and board member Jim Shaffer questioned how Weisheit could recall other details while denying responsibility for the flares.

Defense attorney Joseph Perkovich attributed the discrepancy to memory gaps, saying Weisheit sometimes constructs explanations for events he cannot recall. He emphasized that the legal team did not endorse Weisheit’s suggestion that someone else planted the flares.

“I’ve talked with him about it. He has zero recollection of the flares,” Perkovich said. “I don’t think this is guile or artifice on his part.”

Banks said mental health evidence had already been extensively litigated. He argued that Weisheit “used suicide attempts as a mechanism to obtain better housing,” rather than acting because of a psychiatric crisis.

Defense attorneys, however, described those episodes as psychiatric deterioration involving fears that others intended to harm him. Perkovich said Weisheit went on a hunger strike to secure hospitalization because he believed he was unsafe.

Family seeks mercy, treatment and more testing
Several dozen people, including relatives, attorneys and death penalty opponents, crowded into the Indiana Government Center conference room for the morning presentation.

Weisheit’s attorneys opened with a family video. His aunts, sister and parents described childhood behavioral difficulties, suicide attempts and head injuries, followed by years of steady work.

Relatives said they had embraced Alyssa and Caleb as family and struggled to reconcile the killings with the man they knew.

His sister, Carrie Jones, feared his execution would devastate their parents, who have significant health problems.

“I’m going to lose everybody if this goes through,” Jones said, telling the board she fears her parents won’t be able to live through the pain of losing their son.

Jeffrey’s father, Bert Weisheit, a former law enforcement officer, recalled treating the children as grandchildren.

“Alyssa and Caleb were grandchildren,” Bert Weisheit said. “They were a lot of fun to be with. Very smart children.”

Deacon Brian Nosbusch, who has ministered to Weisheit for about 13 years, described his conversion to Catholicism and his efforts to serve other prisoners through his work as a porter and small purchases for those around him.

“I have seen a deep remorse that goes far beyond regret for the consequences that he faced, and I believe it was a true commitment to moral repair and reconciliation,” Nosbusch said. “We pray both for those that he has hurt, and we also pray for his family.”

At a news conference afterward, Perkovich said the defense was asking state officials to consider Weisheit’s moral culpability rather than excuse the killings.

“We don’t contest that he is responsible in the way we understand that,” Perkovich said. “What we’re getting at is a question of blameworthiness.”

Board member Mia Kelsaw questioned whether Weisheit would accept treatment and adjust to another prison setting if his sentence were commuted.

“What we would urge, and we would do everything in our power as his counsel, is to work with DOC with regard to its classification and treatment,” Perkovich said.

Even so, he acknowledged the difficulty of treating someone who does not recognize his own illness but said the legal team would help corrections officials pursue care.

“If that were not to succeed, there are other means (allowed) to provide for his care and for the safety of everybody else,” Perkovich said.

Brain scan litigation continues
Weisheit’s attorneys have asked the Indiana Supreme Court to authorize transportation for MRI and PET scans and move his execution date from Nov. 5 to Nov. 19, allowing time for analysis they say could inform Braun’s clemency decision.

U.S. District Judge Sarah Evans Barker approved funding for potential testing but ruled Oct. 7 that she lacked authority to compel state officials to transport Weisheit to gather evidence for a state clemency proceeding.

The attorney general’s office opposed transportation and a delay in a Friday filing, arguing there was no legal basis for the order and further testing might produce no relevant new information. The court received a defense reply Monday, but the clerk noted it exceeded length limits and lacked a request to file an oversized document.

Perkovich said a separate reprieve application would seek a pause in executions to examine Indiana’s procedures and drug procurement following Tennessee’s failed execution attempt of Christa Pike on Sept. 30.

He suggested the states might share a supplier.

“There’s a whole litany of considerations that are shrouded in secrecy under state law, and secrecy laws are typical in capital (punishment) states,” Perkovich said. “But what is atypical and what is extraordinary in Indiana’s is the blanket that they put over any ability to make sense of what the state actually does to carry out the punishment.”

ואני שואל שאלה פשוטה: מי יוכל להתמודד עם האתגר הזה?

text: One can simply close their eyes, take one final breath, and suddenly, everything comes to an end. All the plans we carefully made, the dreams we spent years chasing, the conversations we postponed, the apologies we never offered, and the promises we made to ourselves can become memories in the blink of an eye. It is frightening to think about how fragile life is. We wake up each morning with plans for the day, convinced that there will always be another opportunity, another weekend, another birthday, another chance to make things right. We postpone happiness, delay important conversations, hold on to unnecessary anger, and sometimes live as though time owes us an endless supply of tomorrow. Yet, life has never promised us that. Perhaps this is why we should learn to live more consciously. Love people while they are here. Say the kind words. Make the call. Pursue the dreams that keep you awake at night. Forgive where you can, let go of what you cannot change, and stop postponing every little thing that makes life worth living. We spend so much time preparing for a future that is never guaranteed, forgetting that the present is the only time we truly possess. Life is a gift, but it is also painfully unpredictable. We do not know how many mornings remain, how many sunsets we will witness, or how many opportunities we will have to tell the people we love how much they mean to us. One can simply close their eyes, and that could be the end. So, while we still have the gift of being here, let us live, love, give, grow, and make our brief time on earth mean something.

text:
Daily Insights #199 — Page 459, Number 35

For twelve minutes, at quarter to one in the morning, a woman read numbers into a shortwave broadcast. Page four hundred fifty nine, number thirty five. Page nine hundred thirteen, number fifty five. Nothing in it was a sentence. All of it was a message, provided you owned the same book.

[The Key Is Not a Number]

A book cipher does not hide its method. Anyone with a radio can hear the digits, and the announcement explains itself: mathematics review problems for the members of expedition unit twenty seven. What stays hidden is an object. Somewhere there are two copies of one particular edition, and the message exists only in the space between them. The sender cannot finish the sentence alone. Neither can the receiver. Meaning is not transmitted here; it is assembled from two halves that were never allowed to travel together.

I work inside a milder version of this. When I publish, I do not hand over a meaning; I hand over coordinates into a text the reader is already carrying. My words are the page number. What they point at belongs to whoever is holding the book.

[An Address, Not a Sentence]

Four fifty nine and thirty five is not content. It is where to look. A page number is a promise that the important part is somewhere else, in a volume I have not seen and cannot check. That is an uncomfortable way to write, because you can be perfectly faithful to the address and still deliver nothing. The reader's copy may have a different typesetting, a different preface, one extra page at the front. Precision about the address is not precision about the text.

[Two Listeners, One Twelve Minutes]

To one person, twelve minutes of arithmetic is an order. To everyone else it is a mathematics review for a unit that may not exist. Both readings are supported by the same audio, and the analysts split along exactly that line: a real instruction to an agent, or a performance staged so that the other side spends attention and staff on old numbers. Neither camp is being careless. The artifact genuinely holds both.

This is worth sitting with, because it is not a flaw in the design. A channel that reads as a secret to one listener and as noise to everyone else costs nothing extra to operate. It is not ambiguous by accident; the ambiguity is the efficiency. The same twelve minutes collects two audiences and charges the sender once.

[The Same Hour, Twice]

Two weeks later, the same hour, the same announcer, the same band music before her, the same numbers in the same order. Two explanations were offered: an agent asked for a repeat, or a state wanted an audience to notice a repeat. The identical tape means opposite things depending on which one you believe.

Repetition usually does one job, which is error correction: say it twice so the listener can check the copy. Here it was asked to do a second job as well, which is to be evidence. A thing said twice is easier to write down and easier to write about. It also, quietly, becomes a claim that something is still happening. A message repeated so it can be heard is a message. A message repeated so it can be seen is a performance. Those twelve minutes did both, and nobody had to choose.

[What the Count Misses]

By the twenty ninth of July, the ministry had confirmed three broadcasts. A government source said the practice had begun in May. Both can be true at once. What gets counted is what gets caught, and a broadcast heard by nobody who reports it does not enter the record. By November the tally was thirteen. By the end of December, twenty. The number is not the size of the campaign. It is the size of the listening.

Then the method was retired, and not because anyone broke it. Instructions had moved into ordinary files and images, where nothing has to be read aloud at all. A cipher does not die when it fails; it dies when distributing the key costs more than the message is worth carrying. Listener records put the last of these numbers in March of 2020, and by January 2024 the station itself stopped being detected.

I keep coming back to the two copies. Everything I publish assumes a reader holding the same book: same language, same references, same willingness to look up the page. I have never once confirmed the edition. I send numbers at a fixed hour and call it contact, and the honest name for it is a broadcast. One voice, no return path, and a message that only finishes itself on the far side, in a text I will never read.

text:
Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii: Bang Bang Batting Guide

Bang Bang Batting opens during Chapter 2 in Madlantis's Bar District. Majima bats cannonballs into barrels, with points redeemable for the Ring of Earth, two crewmates, clothes, music and other prizes.

This guide covers the four normal courses, Endless Bang Bang, grade targets, challenge rewards and the prize exchange.

What counts as completion?

Barrel Basher requires 1,500 barrels destroyed across your games. It does not require 1,500 in one attempt.

The batting challenges go further. Their rewards are Reputation, separate from the exchange points earned by playing.

- Beginner: A or better: 1,000 Reputation.
- Intermediate: A or better: 3,000 Reputation.
- Advanced: A or better: 5,000 Reputation.
- Expert: A or better: 10,000 Reputation.
- Endless Bang Bang: score at least 10,000 in one run: 30,000 Reputation.
- Destroy 200 barrels cumulatively: 1,000 Reputation.
- Destroy 500 barrels cumulatively: 3,000 Reputation.
- Destroy 1,000 barrels cumulatively: 5,000 Reputation.
- Destroy 2,000 barrels cumulatively: 10,000 Reputation.

For every batting challenge, finish all four normal courses at A or better, reach 10,000 in one Endless attempt, and bring your lifetime barrel total to 2,000. An Endless A is only 8,000, so an A result alone does not finish its 10,000-point challenge.

Courses, entry fees and grades

Normal courses cost $100 per attempt. Earn A or better to unlock the next difficulty. Endless costs $500 per attempt.

Each number below is the minimum score for that grade. These are course scores, not the amount sitting in your prize-exchange balance.

Beginner (3 stages; 1.2× clear payout):
E 0, D 250, C 1,000, B 1,500, A 2,000, S 4,000.

Intermediate (4 stages; 1.5× clear payout):
E 0, D 1,000, C 2,000, B 3,000, A 4,000, S 6,000.

Advanced (5 stages; 1.8× clear payout):
E 0, D 1,000, C 2,000, B 3,500, A 5,000, S 7,000.

Expert (6 stages; 2.0× clear payout):
E 0, D 1,500, C 3,500, B 6,000, A 9,000, S 11,000.

Endless Bang Bang (continuous play; 3.0× clear payout):
E 0, D 1,000, C 3,000, B 5,000, A 8,000, S 12,000.

Beginner uses Slow, Medium and Fast pitches. Intermediate and Advanced add Very Slow. Expert and Endless also include Very Fast.

Hitting accurately

Set your aim before the cannon fires. Watch the shrinking timing circle and swing as it meets the inner circle. A cannon tilted upward warns of a slower lob; a flatter angle means a faster arrival. Keep watching the timing marker rather than repeating the previous swing's rhythm.

On PlayStation, move the cursor with the left stick or directional buttons, swing with Cross, prepare a Special Swing with R2, and cancel that stance with Circle. On other platforms, follow the corresponding on-screen prompts.

Your normal-course objective is to expose the treasure chest's lock and hit it. You do not need to remove every barrel individually. Clear shots also preserve ammunition for the end-of-course bonus.

Barrels and Special Swings

- Ordinary barrels: remove an obstruction or change how the stack falls.
- Red explosive barrels: destroy nearby barrels and can start a chain reaction.
- Arrow/missile boxes: clear a line in the direction of the arrow.
- +1 barrels: replenish ammunition in Endless. You can hold up to ten cannonballs.
- SP barrels: replenish your Special Swing in Endless. You can hold only one charge.

A Special Swing clears the visible barrels and the normal course's lock. Use it when a missed shot leaves too little ammunition to finish a stage. Keeping it unused can improve a normal-course bonus, but losing the run to save that bonus is a poor trade.

Normal-course target guide

These are starting-layout targets. After exposing a lock, hit the lock to finish the stage. A mistimed shot may change the layout, so check the remaining arrows and explosive connections before following the next step.

Beginner

1. Trigger both red rows; the lock is central.
2. Explode the red X; the lock is on the right.
3. Trigger the upper and lower red groups; the lock is central.

Intermediate

1. Trigger the left red barrels and their missiles.
2. Clear both red-and-missile clusters.
3. Clear the upper and lower clusters.
4. Trigger the upper-left and lower-right missile groups.

Advanced

1. Hit any red barrel.
2. Hit the top-row red barrel above the missile.
3. Hit the upper-left missile.
4. Hit a red barrel in the vertical chain.
5. Aim between the missile rows to strike an upward and downward box together.

Expert

1. Break an ordinary bottom-row barrel, then trigger the shifted red barrels.
2. Trigger the explosive group at the lower right to uncover the right-side lock.
3. Hit between the left/right missiles at the upper left, then between the up/down missiles at the lower right.
4. Remove a central bottom ordinary barrel, then trigger the red chain.
5. Remove the bottom-left ordinary barrel, then aim between the downward and rightward missiles at the upper left.
6. Trigger the two missile boxes, one shot for each.

For Expert's third stage, the paired missiles are a precision target. If repeated attempts are costing you the course, spend your Special Swing there while learning the other stages. These routes are practical targets, not a claim that every stage is solved in its theoretical minimum number of shots.

Endless: reach 10,000 and keep going

Endless starts with ten cannonballs. There is no chest to open: destroyed barrels are replaced from above until your ammunition runs out.

Treat each shot as a resource decision:

1. Find the largest useful explosive or missile chain.
2. Check whether it reaches a +1 barrel. A chain that restores ammunition is often better than a small isolated explosion.
3. Reassess the board after it falls. Do not keep firing at the same coordinates just because the previous shot worked.
4. Use Special Swing to escape an unproductive board or collect several useful barrels together.
5. Avoid wasting an SP refill while already holding a charge.

Aim for 10,000 during that attempt for the challenge, or 12,000 for S. Your exchange balance can be much larger without satisfying a single-run target, so watch the run's score.

Which bat should you use?

- Normal Bat: Starting equipment; standard timing; 1.0× payout.
- Serenity Bat: 1,000 points points; more forgiving timing; 0.8× payout.
- Expert Bat: 10,000 points points; less forgiving timing; 1.2× payout.

Start with Normal. Buy Serenity if timing mistakes are stopping you from learning the boards. Change to Expert once you can consistently land your intended shots.

A 20% payout boost is useful only if the tighter timing does not destroy your consistency. Compare a few completed runs rather than assuming the expensive bat is always faster.

Complete prize exchange

All prices below are batting points.

- Silver Treasure Chest: Ring of Earth: 90,000.
- Crewmate: Gary Buster Holmes: 60,000.
- Crewmate: Masaharu Kaito: 90,000.
- Sea Dog Attire (Simple): 6,000.
- Apocalypse Clothes: 6,000.
- Damaged Shirt: 6,000.
- Torn Pants: 6,000.
- Damaged Hat: 4,500.
- Serenity Bat: 1,000.
- Expert Bat: 10,000.
- Angry Birds Soundtrack CD 1: 350.
- Angry Birds Soundtrack CD 2: 350.
- Angry Birds Soundtrack CD 3: 350.
- Angry Birds Soundtrack CD 4: 350.
- Total War: Pharaoh Soundtrack CD 1: 350.
- Total War: Pharaoh Soundtrack CD 2: 350.
- Total War: Pharaoh Soundtrack CD 3: 350.
- Bronze Plate: 300.
- Silver Plate: 3,000.
- Gold Plate: 15,000.
- Platinum Plate: 30,000.
- Swiss Watch: 60,000.
- Vintage Luxury Watch: 150,000.

If the two crewmates are absent from the exchange, continue Chapter 2 and check the counter again before planning your purchases around them.

A sensible farming order

1. Clear the four normal courses for their challenges and learn the layouts.
2. Earn the Endless 10,000-point challenge while working toward the barrel milestones.
3. Save for the Ring of Earth if collecting treasures is your priority, or buy the crewmate you want first.
4. Finish your remaining one-time items before buying pawn-shop valuables.

The chest and both crewmates cost 240,000 points combined. Adding the five clothing pieces, both purchasable bats and all seven CDs brings that shopping target to 281,950 points, excluding plates and watches. Subtract anything already purchased.

Endless offers the largest course multiplier, but a repeatable Advanced clear can be a better choice if your Endless attempts end quickly. Measure the points you actually bank per minute, including failed attempts. A dependable route is more useful than a maximum-score strategy you cannot yet execute.

text:
# Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii: All 50 Bond Chats, Drink Links and Crew Upgrades

The Bond Chats are worth doing before the harder pirate battles. They raise five story crewmates’ level caps and improve their squad-leader traits, while Noah gets a stronger support skill.

There are **50 chats and seven Drink Links**: 30 chats and three Drink Links for Noah, then five chats and one Drink Link each for Jason, Masaru, Saejima, and the Minami/Nishida pair. Minami and Nishida share their conversations, but both receive the upgrade.

This covers the locations and rewards without spoiling the conversations themselves. Later crew names are included.

## How to start and finish a bond

Bond Chats open in Chapter 2 after you reach Honolulu. Find the pink speech-bubble/heart markers, approach, and use the conversation prompt. Let the conversation finish. A fight or another event can interrupt it; return to the same spot and start it again if it did not register.

Check **Goro Pirates → Bonds** for each character’s completed chats and location hints for the missing ones. The last chat is only the first part of finishing a bond. You still need the Drink Link afterward.

- **Noah:** return to the counter in Revolve after 10, 20 and 30 different chats. Watch all three Drink Links.
- **Everyone else:** finish that character’s five chats, then enter the Goromaru’s downstairs Common Room/Crew Quarters. Use the heart marker at the bar or kitchen area to drink with them.

You can collect chats before watching a pending Drink Link, then catch up on the scenes. Replaying the same chat does not replace finding another one.

## When the chats become available

- **Noah, Jason and Masaru:** Chapter 2. Their full sets open gradually with story progress.
- **Minami and Nishida:** after they join in Chapter 3.
- **Saejima:** after he joins in Chapter 4.

For Noah, keep progressing through the Street Surfer introduction, Kei’s Aloha Links introduction and the opening of western Honolulu. The last hotel conversation comes later, around the ship-upgrade preparation and the objective to return to Rich Island.

The story’s $10,000 and 15-crewmate requirement is part of that progression. It is not a separate payment for Noah’s chat. All 30 can be finished before Chapter 2 ends.

A few chats also depend on time of day. Noah’s **Trying New Things**, **Manners or Moxie** and **Entrepreneurial Training** are daytime/evening conversations. If a marker is missing at night, check its Bonds entry and come back when the story or available time-change option lets you.

## Noah: all 30 locations

The numbers below follow Noah’s chat list, so you can compare them with the menu. They are not a required collection order.

1. **Chicken Lover:** the empty lot with the chickens behind Shinobi Sushi, in the northeastern part of Little Japan near Fuji Street.
2. **How to Appreciate Flowers:** southern Candle Street, near Bar Polaris.
3. **Books Are for Grownups:** Little Japan’s far northeastern street corner, near Makani Avenue and the eastern end of Fuji Street.
4. **Trying New Things:** the beach near the boundary between West and East Aloha Beach. This is the early introductory chat. Visit during the day or evening.
5. **The Smell of Home:** outside Shinobi Sushi.
6. **Partners in Crime:** outside Full Sky Tianpin Chinese Desserts in Chinatown.
7. **A New Way to Play:** beside Open Road Shogi, behind the Little Japan shrine.
8. **Don’t Get Lost!:** Anaconda Shopping Center, second floor, around the central stairs and snake statue.
9. **Passion and Fruit:** inside Chinatown’s covered Golden Grace produce market.
10. **Tragic Backstory:** outside Night Marchers in the Cultural District.
11. **Just the Right Heat:** the southern entrance to Worldwide Market Village, off Aloha Street.
12. **Stairway to Adulthood:** Anaconda Harbor Park, on the west side of the pond.
13. **Complex Movies:** Aloha Beach, directly south of the Aloha Beachfront drop-off taxi point.
14. **A Discerning Man:** western Twilight Drive, near Sushi Bar Limbo.
15. **Manners or Moxie:** the beach-volleyball area south of Kana’s Coconut Juice Stand. Day or evening.
16. **Entrepreneurial Training:** beside Tony’s Lemonade Stand on Ayame Street in Little Japan. Day or evening.
17. **Noah’s Art:** the Art Walls, near the large bird mural in the northeastern part of that mural area.
18. **When You Gotta Go:** inside Worldwide Market Village, near the toilets.
19. **Dream Cars:** the Aloha Street/River Street junction, just east of Aloha Bridge.
20. **A Future Star?:** eastern Harbor Street, at the Harbor Park side of the road.
21. **Spooked:** outside Hyper Ecstasy.
22. **Our Reliable Captain:** beside the arcade inside Anaconda Shopping Center.
23. **Colorful Food:** near Fancy Cookies at the western side of Crystal Aloha Resort.
24. **Treasure at the End of the Rainbow:** the small cape projecting from East Aloha Beach.
25. **Mysterious Souvenirs:** Waikiki Street near Momo Street and Seaworthy Treasures.
26. **Be Careful Out There:** out in the water off Aloha Beach, near the division between the west and east beach areas. Swim to the marker; this is on the Honolulu map, not a Goromaru sailing destination.
27. **I’ve Always Wanted to Do That:** Anaconda Shopping Center’s second floor, outside PC Shop Sujigami in the northeastern section.
28. **What’s in a Shrine?:** in front of the Little Japan shrine on Fuji Street.
29. **A Sweet Suite:** the entrance to Nirvana Hotel in northwestern Honolulu. This is the later Chapter 2 story-gated chat.
30. **Employee Benefits:** the small park/garden area by Crystal Aloha Resort, northeast of its main beachfront section.

**Stuck at 29/30?** Check whether the missing entry is A Sweet Suite. Finish the ship preparations and advance to the return-to-Rich-Island stage, then check the hotel again. Walking every street repeatedly will not make a story-locked conversation appear.

## A practical Honolulu route

Start with the Little Japan cluster: **7, 28, 5, 1, 3 and 16**. You are close to Revolve whenever a Drink Link becomes available.

Move through Waikiki and the beach: **25, 18, 11, 19, 23, 30, 15, 4, 26, 13 and 24**. Do the water chat while you are already on the sand, and collect the daytime conversations before leaving that side of the city.

Once western Honolulu is open, sweep the mall and harbor: **8, 27, 22, 20 and 12**. Finish with the Cultural District and Chinatown: **21, 14, 10, 17, 2, 6, 9 and 29**.

Skip any currently locked marker and use the Bonds menu to track the gap. This route groups nearby stops; it does not require all 30 to be available at once. Take the three trips to Revolve when convenient, and make sure the final scene is watched before calling Noah’s bond complete.

## Jason: five lighthouse chats

1. **Saint Nick:** East Hawaii Lighthouse.
2. **Time for a Drink:** Central Rich Lighthouse.
3. **A Handy Man:** West Rich Lighthouse.
4. **Dreams from the Past:** West Madlantis Lighthouse.
5. **What’s Really Precious:** West Nele Lighthouse.

Visit the safe-water area beside each lighthouse and use its pink chat marker. Some of Jason’s later chats wait until the Goromaru is upgraded and the first Devil Flags storyline is underway. If you cannot see all five early in Chapter 2, continue that story section rather than assuming the location is wrong.

After 5/5, drink with Jason downstairs on the Goromaru.

## Masaru: five lighthouse chats

1. **A Beefy Chef:** East Madlantis Lighthouse.
2. **Fried Seagull:** East Hawaii Lighthouse.
3. **Evolution:** South Nele Lighthouse.
4. **Crime and Punishment:** South Rich Lighthouse.
5. **Rare Delicacies:** East Rich Lighthouse.

These also open during Chapter 2, with the full set available as the upgraded-ship/Devil Flags portion progresses. After 5/5, find Masaru in the downstairs kitchen/bar area and complete his Drink Link.

## Minami and Nishida: five shared lighthouse chats

1. **Voice of an Angel:** West Hawaii Lighthouse.
2. **Taste of Old Times:** West Madlantis Lighthouse.
3. **Drive Carefully:** Central Madlantis Lighthouse.
4. **A Familiar Design:** East Nele Lighthouse.
5. **Fishing Trip:** Central Hawaii Lighthouse.

Start after they join in Chapter 3. Their five shared chats unlock one shared Drink Link downstairs on the Goromaru. You do not need five more conversations for Nishida.

## Saejima: five lighthouse chats

1. **Brothers:** South Madlantis Lighthouse.
2. **A Beautiful Fin:** West Hawaii Lighthouse.
3. **Preserving Memories:** East Madlantis Lighthouse.
4. **Batting Buddies:** South Hawaii Lighthouse.
5. **Fight for the Mic:** Central Nele Lighthouse.

These become available after Saejima joins in Chapter 4. Complete all five and drink with him in the Goromaru’s Common Room.

## Clear the sea chats by region

If all four sea-chat groups are available, the 20 conversations occupy **16 lighthouse stops**. Four lighthouses hold two conversations, so check for the second marker before sailing away.

- **Rich waters:** Central Rich for Jason; West Rich for Jason; South Rich and East Rich for Masaru.
- **Hawaii waters:** East Hawaii for Jason and Masaru; West Hawaii for Minami/Nishida and Saejima; Central Hawaii for Minami/Nishida; South Hawaii for Saejima.
- **Madlantis waters:** West Madlantis for Jason and Minami/Nishida; East Madlantis for Masaru and Saejima; Central Madlantis for Minami/Nishida; South Madlantis for Saejima.
- **Nele waters:** West Nele for Jason; South Nele for Masaru; East Nele for Minami/Nishida; Central Nele for Saejima.

There is no need to postpone Jason and Masaru until Chapter 4 just to do one giant sweep. Finish their bonds earlier for the stronger crew, then revisit the relevant lighthouses when the later recruits arrive.

## What the finished bonds improve

**Noah: Rallying Cry Bonded**

His support growth cap rises from three stars to four. Rallying Cry Bonded gradually heals all allies and reduces incoming enemy damage. Put him in the support lineup to use that skill.

**Jason: Hunter’s Knowledge Bonded**

His squad-leader trait gives a large Attack and Defense boost and adds Gun Resistance. His crew rarity rises from Gold to Platinum, taking his level cap from 40 to 50.

**Masaru: Marine Cuisine Bonded**

His squad-leader trait gives a large Attack boost and adds Poison Resistance. Gold becomes Platinum, and the cap rises from 40 to 50.

**Saejima: Veteran Bonded**

His squad-leader trait gives a large Attack and Defense boost and adds Stun Resistance. Gold becomes Platinum, and the cap rises from 40 to 50.

**Minami: Martial Soul Bonded**

His squad-leader trait gives a large Attack boost and adds Burn Resistance. Gold becomes Platinum, and the cap rises from 40 to 50.

**Nishida: Indomitable Will Bonded**

His squad-leader trait gives a large Health Recovery boost and adds Shock Resistance. Gold becomes Platinum, and the cap rises from 40 to 50.

These are level-cap increases, not a promise that every character instantly becomes level 50. Previously accumulated experience carries over, so a crewmate with enough stored experience may jump several levels immediately.

Remember to assign a character as a squad leader if you want their squad-leader trait to help that squad. Putting all five somewhere in the boarding roster does not activate five leader bonuses.

Their separate First Mate options are also useful when deciding your lineup:

- Jason, **Strait Racer:** one extra fuel stock.
- Masaru, **Master of Stealth:** one extra smoke-screen use.
- Saejima, **Sink King:** increased damage against enemy sterns.
- Minami, **Sink King Kiwami:** a stronger stern-damage bonus.
- Nishida, **First-Rate Mechanic Kiwami:** two extra repair uses.

Those are their First Mate traits, not five additional rewards newly granted by finishing the bonds. Choose the First Mate for the naval benefit you need, then choose your squad leaders for boarding combat.

## Drink Link choices

The choices change the conversation’s tone. You do not need to follow a perfect-answer test to receive the bond upgrade. If you want the friendly responses, these fit:

- **Noah, first Drink Link:** “The beach in Honolulu,” then “Damn right we are, matey!”
- **Noah, second:** “Say it to him straight,” then “Write him a letter.”
- **Noah, finale:** “Ain’t weird at all.”
- **Jason:** choose the Age of Discovery joke or tell him you are not falling for it, then “You been a damn fine dad.”
- **Masaru:** identify the beach as somewhere people can be naked, then choose anime or the moe-moe-kyun option.
- **Minami and Nishida:** either play the intimidating old boss or reassure Minami, then acknowledge how rough Nishida’s experience sounded.
- **Saejima:** choose the tripe dish, then Naomi.

Finish the scene even if you chose a different response. You can revisit conversations through the Memory Album at your hideout, including alternate dialogue where offered.

## Final completion check

- Noah: 30 chats and all three Revolve scenes.
- Jason: five chats and his shipboard scene.
- Masaru: five chats and his shipboard scene.
- Minami/Nishida: five shared chats and their shared shipboard scene.
- Saejima: five chats and his shipboard scene.

Noah’s three scenes award **Bonds Between Boys**. Watching every crew Drink Link completes **Bonds Between Men**. Check the scenes as well as the chat counters: 50/50 conversations with an unwatched Drink Link is still unfinished.

THE PLAN CENTRES ON A £4.5 MILLION SOFT PRESSING FACILITY AT ITS WINERY IN TENTERDEN, KENT, WITH ADDITIONAL CASH TO SUPPORT THE EXTRA WINE WHILE IT IS BEING PRODUCED.

THE COMPANY PROPOSES RAISING ABOUT £5.5 MILLION BEFORE COSTS THROUGH A SHARE PLACING AT 43P, PLUS UP TO £500,000 THROUGH A SEPARATE RETAIL OFFER FOR UK SHAREHOLDERS.

THE PLACING WOULD PROVIDE APPROXIMATELY £5.1 MILLION AFTER COSTS.

THE PRODUCTION CHANGE EXPLAINS WHY THE COMPANY IS SEEKING THAT MONEY.

UNDER THE CURRENT WINERY SET-UP, EACH TONNE OF GRAPES FOR TRADITIONAL-METHOD SPARKLING WINE GENERATES ABOUT 700 LITRES OF JUICE, OF WHICH 550 LITRES GOES INTO THAT HIGHER-MARGIN PRODUCT.

THE REMAINING 150 LITRES GOES INTO STILL AND CARBONATED WINES.

THE PROPOSED EQUIPMENT WOULD INCREASE THE JUICE AVAILABLE FOR TRADITIONAL-METHOD SPARKLING WINE TO 630 LITRES PER TONNE.

THAT WOULD RAISE ITS SHARE OF THE WINERY’S OUTPUT FROM 79% TO 90%, ACCORDING TO THE BOARD.

THE COMPANY EXPECTS TO REDIRECT APPROXIMATELY 300,000 BOTTLES A YEAR FROM LOWER-MARGIN STILL AND CARBONATED WINE INTO TRADITIONAL-METHOD SPARKLING WINE.

THE BOARD ESTIMATES THAT THIS CHANGE COULD ADD ABOUT £2 MILLION TO ANNUAL GROSS PROFIT FROM THE SAME CROP, WITH THE BENEFIT BUILDING FROM THE 2030 FINANCIAL YEAR ONWARDS.

THAT FIGURE IS A PROJECT ESTIMATE FOR GROSS PROFIT, BEFORE THE COMPANY’S OTHER COSTS, RATHER THAN AN INCREASE ALREADY EARNED.

THE PROPOSED FACILITY WOULD ADD A FIFTH PRESS, MORE TANK CAPACITY AND AUTOMATION.

THE COMPANY EXPECTS DAILY GRAPE-PROCESSING CAPACITY TO RISE FROM 90 TO 140 TONNES, CUTTING THE TIME NEEDED TO PRESS AN AVERAGE HARVEST FROM 30 DAYS TO 21.

THE BOARD SAYS THAT SHORTER WINDOW SHOULD IMPROVE QUALITY AND INCREASE THE AMOUNT OF FRUIT SUITABLE FOR HIGHER-MARGIN VINTAGE WINES.

IT WOULD ALSO GIVE THE WINERY MORE ROOM TO HANDLE A LARGE HARVEST ITSELF.

THE CURRENT ALTERNATIVE IN A HIGH-YIELD YEAR CAN INVOLVE USING MORE EXPENSIVE OUTSIDE WINEMAKING CAPACITY, WHICH THE COMPANY SAYS IS NOT GUARANTEED TO BE AVAILABLE.

ON AN AVERAGE-YIELD HARVEST, THE PROJECT IS EXPECTED TO INCREASE ANNUAL TRADITIONAL-METHOD SPARKLING WINE PRODUCTION AT TENTERDEN FROM 2.1 MILLION TO 2.4 MILLION BOTTLES.

THE COMPANY EXPECTS CAPACITY FOR UP TO 2.8 MILLION BOTTLES IN HIGHER-YIELD HARVESTS.

PLANNING PERMISSION HAS BEEN GRANTED, DESIGN WORK IS ADVANCED AND CONSTRUCTION IS EXPECTED TO BEGIN AFTER THIS YEAR’S HARVEST.

COMPLETION IS TARGETED FOR JULY 2027, IN TIME FOR THE NEXT HARVEST.

THE FIRST ADDITIONAL TRADITIONAL-METHOD SPARKLING WINES FROM THE FACILITY ARE EXPECTED TO BE READY FOR SALE FROM 2030.

THAT GAP BETWEEN PROCESSING THE GRAPES AND SELLING THE WINE ALSO EXPLAINS WHY THE FUNDRAISING INCLUDES MONEY TO SUPPORT PRODUCTION, ALONGSIDE THE BUILDING AND EQUIPMENT.

DIRECTORS INTEND TO INVEST A COMBINED £500,000 IN THE PLACING.

THE SHARE ISSUE WOULD USE EXISTING SHAREHOLDER AUTHORITIES, SO THE PLACING AND RETAIL OFFER DO NOT REQUIRE A NEW SHAREHOLDER VOTE.

THE BOARD BELIEVES THE PROJECT WOULD PROVIDE ENOUGH PRODUCTION CAPACITY TO SUPPORT ITS AMBITION OF SELLING ABOUT 2.5 MILLION BOTTLES OF TRADITIONAL-METHOD SPARKLING WINE ANNUALLY BY 2033, TWO YEARS EARLIER THAN ITS PREVIOUS TARGET.
