text:
今天又在加密书屋群里聊及美利坚全盘翻蓝以后的 Clarity Act。

1/我觉得之前 Clarity Act 在众议院以超多数票通过，绝对足以说明至少短期内 Clarity 中承诺的那些基础保障是两党共识。
参议院没过是党争问题，不是共识破灭。

这点最重要的表现是 Robinhood 的 Layer 2。
Robinhood 的政策法律团队一定认为，现在去发一个打着去中心化名号的 Layer 2，可以让他们做一些之前法律限制无法做的事情，可以让他们赚一些之前无法赚的钱，能享受一些他们之前如果做了就会被追责的法律豁免。
这个传统金融套个去中心化区块链的壳子做监管套利的趋势，绝对还没有力竭。

2/民主党手握两院，川普系最值得攻击的点必然包含 Trump memecoin 和 World Liberty Financial 这俩。
这俩不被咬两年不太可能，期间也必定波及其他的加密项目。

3/Vitalik 24 年大选前撰文说反对根据 pro-Crypto 与否来投票。川普牛是我们行业走的弯路，一定要还债的。
群友说得更好：川普实际上表现出了加密市场最烂的一部分，而且他表示这套我玩得比你们好——不就是喊单拉盘么，球长也可以亲自做。
https://t.co/37q9jgQhkZ

4/我们整个行业本质上都高度寄生于监管套利这个核心概念上。
但监管套利的基础是民族国家对金融或者对所有可监管世界都越来越家长化，而这个家长化的尺度一定是会矫枉过正的。
监管套利是否可持续这个问题背后其实是现在的监管有没有超越正常合理范围，有没有监管造成的磨损比诈骗造成的磨损更大等等。
我自己作为右派，当然觉得监管造成的后果已经事实上更鼓励所有人都做巨婴，但显然我这个观点不是共识。
群友追问：如果接下来监管不让你套利呢？

5/反过来说，Airbnb 和 Uber 本质上也是监管套利。
且无论是因为当时的环境整体宽松，还是传统旅店业、出租车业已经烂透到不改不行，后面确实都变成监管退，而 Airbnb、Uber 进。
回到我们一开始话题的由头，Clarity Act 在众议院通过，本质上也是美国明确有加密货币行业进、而监管退的苗头。

6/21 世纪是家长式政府的世纪。
纽约或伦敦或任何中心化的金融体系本质上一直都在用效率换安全、用公民主体性换安全。而这个几乎一直是单向的流动，一直在让渡更多的效率和主体性。
经过 30 年的让渡，有没有让渡到一个夸张、离谱、矫枉过正的程度？

如果有，则加密行业现在做的向监管要空间、搞主权个人的无许可金融就是拨乱反正；
如果没有，这 Clarity Act 当时表现出来的共识就会在短期内崩溃。

这段讨论的部分背景详见：https://t.co/iZAqHSw4Lq

7/还有一个东西在显著复杂化问题的情况：AI 时代大规模的 Cyber security 攻击。
目前听说某个韩国加密交易所已经准备改为 T+1 提现了，连加密行业本身都在主动尝试让渡更多自主性和效率去换安全。
所以这种共识应该就很脆弱，甚至完全可以消散倒流。
所以要挑战臃肿、低效、僵化、腐朽的传统金融，则至少我们要不断证明，我们的行业足以提供以一个值得信任的、总体上美好的 counter offer。

Since I already had an apartment of my own, I decided to hold on to the property as an investment while I figured out my next move.

All I asked was that he look after the property and pay the utility bills.

He was incredibly thankful. He even promised he would never do anything that might make me regret helping him.

For the first few months, things appeared to be fine. Every so often, he sent me photos of the house and told me everything was being kept in good shape.

text:
DA assures El Niño measures despite Q3 output drop

MANILA – The Department of Agriculture (DA) on Friday assured that it has measures in place to cushion the impact of extreme weather, following a 5 percent decline in agriculture and fisheries production in the third quarter. 

Both “rising input costs and unfavorable weather situations” are seen as factors behind the overall output drop, valued at PHP389.42 billion in July to September, according to the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) report. 

In a statement, DA Secretary Francisco Tiu Laurel Jr. said the administration has already prepared funds and intervention to ensure recovery from the looming effect of very strong El Niño. 

“We have mapped out a PHP62-billion El Niño response plan that will leverage new technologies, innovations, targeted interventions, and collaboration with various government agencies to mitigate the impact of the climate risk on agriculture,” he said. 

For his part, DA Undersecretary and Rice Industry Development Program overseer Christopher Morales underscored the need to allocate investments in water management infrastructure. 

“Water management infrastructure will not only help us cope with droughts but also allow us to store excess water during La Niña episodes,” he said. 

These include water impounding dams and solar-powered irrigation systems.

Tiu Laurel, meanwhile, said that subsectors which performed stronger during the third quarter, particularly livestock and poultry, offer a “foundation for recovery” as the country braces for the peak impact of a very strong El Niño. 

According to the PSA, the livestock and poultry sectors accounted for almost 37 percent of the overall agrifishery output, which countered weakened crop and fishery production. 

Poultry was the strongest performer, which expanded 4.9 percent and valued at PHP79.67 billion; while livestock production rose by 1.1 percent, valued at PHP61.17 billion. 

To sustain these gains, the agency said it is important to ensure that interventions will help support domestic food supply, protect farmers’ income, and keep staple food at affordable prices despite weather disruptions. 

“And the DA will not do this alone. This El Niño plan will be carried through a whole-of-government approach,” Tiu Laurel said.

Crops, which include corn and palay (unhusked rice), meanwhile, accounted for 51 percent of total agricultural and fisheries production. 

Palay and corn output both plunged by 18 percent and 17 percent, respectively. 

Rice production dropped to 3.08 million metric tons (MT), while corn output declined to 2 million MT, with adjustments on cropping intentions due to spiking fertilizer prices and high input costs, alongside the effect of flooding following the effects of the southwest monsoon. (PNA/Stephanie Sevillano)

=====

The Department of Agriculture on Friday (Nov. 6, 2026) assured that it has measures in place to cushion the impact of extreme weather, following a decline in agriculture and fisheries production during the third quarter. The .38 Casull is a rare, high-velocity proprietary handgun cartridge developed by Dick Casull (of .454 Casull fame) around 1998. It was designed primarily for a custom 1911-pattern semi-automatic pistol, the Casull Arms CA-3800, rather than as a mainstream commercial round. 

Design and Origins
It is a rimless bottleneck cartridge. The parent case is the .45 Winchester Magnum (necked down for .38/.357-diameter bullets); it draws on the earlier .38-45 Clerke wildcat concept from the 1960s. Key dimensions include a bullet diameter of approximately .356 in (9.04 mm) and a case length of 23.70 mm (about 0.933 in). The design supports centerfire primers and was engineered for reliable feeding and extraction in a semi-auto.

Factory loads from Casull Arms included:
124-grain (often ZTP-JHP or similar) at roughly 1,800 fps
147-grain (XTP-JHP style) at roughly 1,650 fps

The CA-3800 PistolThis was a hand-built, 1911-style single-action semi-auto with a 6-inch match barrel, heavy slide, strong recoil spring (around 13 kg / ~28–30 lb), adjustable sights, checkered exotic wood grips, and a capacity of about 8+1. Empty weight was around 40 oz. Some examples were dual-caliber or offered with a .45 ACP barrel option. Production ran roughly 2000–2005 under Casull Arms (Afton, Wyoming) and totaled only a small number—estimates range from under 100 to around 200 units before it stopped due to regulatory issues. The guns are highly collectible; examples (sometimes from notable collections) have sold in the $4,000–$5,000+ range.

Operators can outspend the opposition and still lose when people get a say, and I'd rather see that than another bonus pitch. Trust is the one thing they keep failing to buy.

1 - Gambling companies put $23 million behind a Nebraska online sports betting measure against $1 million from opponents, and voters still rejected it 55%-45%. Money talks, just not always loudly enough.

2 - TrottahCS reports that gambling team logos, stickers and names are banned at the Singapore Major without a Singapore gambling license, and claims @bcgame and @1win were given 24 hours to come up with alternatives. Nothing says sponsorship like a day-long scramble.

3 - fitzmagic13 claims that under @realDonaldTrump's new gambling tax, a bettor who wagers 100k in 2026 and breaks even would owe $10k in phantom gambling tax, and says there is bipartisan support to repeal it. Owing tax on a break-even year is a strange way to define a loss.

4 - DarrenBaileyIL lists a new 15% tax on sports betting, a new 25¢ to 50¢ tax on every online sports bet and a new 15% tax on fantasy sports in @JBPritzker's 2019-2026 tax record.

5 - GAMDOM'S CRASH HOUSE EDGE

@provablyfairorg says its investigation of @gamdom's Crash game found the house edge is up to 2.98× the advertised rate. It also says Crash is not provably fair as implemented, and it estimates about $1.58m in extra expected player losses since January. The house edge is the term that decides everything, because no bonus offsets a game that charges more than it advertises. If Provably Fair is right, "provably fair" is just a label on the lobby, and that is the worst thing a crypto casino can get wrong. Until Gamdom rebuts it, Crash there belongs off any bonus hunter's list.

6 - ROOBET'S $1100 OFFER

@BeCoolMandy says she wagered over 1 million on Lightning Plinko at @Roobet and lost roughly $50,000. She says Roobet's response was a bonus of $1100 with a 10x rollover requirement. If that is what was offered, it is not goodwill, it is a leash. A rollover on a bonus that small against a loss that size hands back a sliver and keeps the player betting. Any bonus hunter has seen this move, and the right response is to read the rollover first and take the money never.

Tria gives people a way to spend crypto from a self-custodial account. The app can make money from card memberships and trading. The question for TRIA holders is how much of that business creates demand for the token.

NO.1 WHAT IS TRIA?

TRIA is the token behind Tria, a self-custodial finance app for spending, trading, and earning with crypto.

Think of someone holding stablecoins who wants to pay for dinner. Tria’s card gives them a way to spend through a familiar checkout. BestPath, Tria’s routing system, is designed to handle the steps needed to move or convert assets across chains.

NO.2 WHY PEOPLE CARE

Crypto spending is awkward when your balance sits on the wrong chain or in the wrong asset. Tria aims to handle those conversions behind the scenes while letting users keep custody of their funds.

The real test comes after the first card purchase. If conversion costs are low and payments work reliably, users have a reason to make Tria their everyday card. If they only use it for rewards, that spending may disappear when incentives drop.

NO.3 THE NARRATIVE

Tria’s bet is that card spending brings people into the app, and some of them stay to trade, earn, or book travel.

Its whitepaper reports $100M+ in transaction volume and $2.5M+ in revenue over four months of closed beta. Those are company-reported beta figures. I’d want to see recent monthly card spend from returning users and how much revenue remains after rewards.

NO.4 THE EDGE

BestPath gives Tria a second route to market. Tria can use the routing system in its own app and offer it to other products through its SDK.

If outside apps pay to use it, Tria can earn from transactions even when the customer never opens the Tria app. The whitepaper describes routing fees and SDK licensing as revenue streams. How much third-party traffic they generate is what I’d watch.

NO.5 KEY METRICS

Approximate November 6 snapshot

Price: $0.00249
Market cap: $5.38M
Circulating supply: 2.16B TRIA, or 21.6% of max supply
Maximum supply: 10B TRIA
FDV: $24.93M
24-hour token trading volume: $2.34M
Perpetual futures open interest: $13.44M

Perps open interest was roughly 2.5× the circulating market cap. That measures open derivatives positions. Card spending is a separate measure of product usage.

NO.6 TOKENOMICS

The community allocation is 41.04% of supply. Tria says users accrue rewards through spending, trading, earning, staking, and ecosystem programs.

That gives users ways to earn TRIA. The other side of the equation is what makes users or integrators buy it. Card memberships and routing fees can bring in business revenue. I couldn’t verify how much of that revenue creates recurring demand for TRIA.

NO.7 UNLOCKS & RISKS

Tria’s August update pushed the first unlock for core contributors and investors to February 2028, with an exception for Legion round investors. It also brought forward 336.9M TRIA in community releases into August through October 2026. That shifted the timing within the existing allocation.

https://t.co/knrdP1BrTR lists 90.2M TRIA for December 3, but the Foundation says it moved releases from the 3rd to a month-end schedule. I’d treat the tracker’s date and amount as unconfirmed under the revised schedule. The more immediate risk is that rewards enter circulation faster than users find reasons to hold the token.

NO.8 BULL vs BEAR

BULL: Cardholders keep spending after incentives ease, outside apps pay to use BestPath, and more of that activity creates measurable TRIA demand.

BEAR: Card usage follows rewards, routing revenue remains small, and recipients sell TRIA faster than new buyers come in.

The deciding metric is how much repeat customer activity creates demand for TRIA after accounting for rewards.

NO.9 VERDICT

My scorecard

Product & Adoption: 7/10
Token Economics: 4/10
Growth Potential: 7/10
Risk Profile: 3/10 — higher means safer
Overall Grade: C

At ~$25M FDV, I’d want several months of repeat card spending and a measurable link between routing activity and token demand before calling TRIA cheap.

If card spend doubles, who actually needs to buy more TRIA?

Cap brings underwritten credit on-chain. The protocol has roughly $180M in TVL, while CAP trades at a $1.08B fully diluted valuation. The question is what credit growth does for the token.

NO.1 WHAT IS CAP?

CAP is the token of Cap, an Ethereum credit protocol built around cUSD and its yield-bearing version, stcUSD. Think of a business borrowing dollars with a third party pledging collateral to back the loan. The borrower gets funding, and the underwriter earns a premium for taking the risk.

NO.2 WHY PEOPLE CARE

A business can borrow without posting its own crypto collateral if an underwriter is willing to guarantee the loan. For stcUSD holders, the quality of that guarantee matters. The yield depends on borrowers paying and the collateral being sufficient if they don’t.

NO.3 THE NARRATIVE

Cap reported onboarding 30 borrowers and 22 underwriters as of July 2026. That shows the protocol has recruited both sides of the market. The stronger signal would be repeat borrowing and renewals at rates that still make sense for underwriters.

NO.4 THE EDGE

Underwriters can pledge assets such as ETH, BTC, or tokenized real-world assets to back specific borrowers. That gives Cap a way to offer credit to businesses that don’t want to lock up their own assets for every loan.

NO.5 KEY METRICS

Approximate November 6 snapshot:

Price: $0.108
Circulating supply: 1.56B CAP, or 15.6% of max supply
Market cap: ~$168M
Max supply: 10B CAP
FDV: ~$1.08B
TVL: ~$180M, down 38% over 30 days
30-day fees / tracked protocol revenue: ~$413K / ~$194

NO.6 TOKENOMICS

Users stake cUSD to receive stcUSD. CAP is a separate token, with 47.37% allocated to the ecosystem and community and 40% to the team and private investors combined. I’d want to see a measurable link between loan activity and recurring CAP demand.

NO.7 UNLOCKS & RISKS

TokenRadar models a June 26, 2027 cliff of ~1.08B CAP, equivalent to ~69% of today’s float. About 1B CAP of that figure is estimated, so the exact release needs confirmation. The credit risk is that a borrower defaults while the underwriter’s collateral is falling in value.

NO.8 BULL vs BEAR

BULL: Borrowers renew, underwriters earn enough to keep backing loans, and credit growth creates a recurring use for CAP.

BEAR: Depositors earn stcUSD yield while demand for CAP stays thin and vesting expands the float.

NO.9 VERDICT

Product & Adoption 7/10 · Token Economics 3/10 · Growth Potential 7/10 · Risk Profile 3/10

Overall Grade C

At ~$1.08B FDV, I’d want evidence that repeat borrowing creates demand for CAP before getting bullish.

If Cap doubles its loan book, who needs to buy more CAP?

filecoin:native  — FILECOIN
⠀
A $680 MILLION cryptocurrency.
⠀
A decentralized storage network built to compete with centralized cloud infrastructure.
⠀
A $1.57 BILLION fully diluted valuation.
⠀
And a token trading nearly 99.7% below its all-time high.
⠀
But here's the contradiction.
⠀
Filecoin has spent years building decentralized storage infrastructure.
⠀
Its technology can verify that storage providers are maintaining data.
⠀
Yet independent on-chain research raises serious questions about how much customers are actually paying for storage.
⠀
Is filecoin:native one of crypto's most overlooked infrastructure investments?
⠀
Or is the market correctly discounting weak commercial demand and continuing token issuance?
⠀
Let's examine the numbers. 👇
⠀
01 | WHAT IS FILECOIN?
⠀
Filecoin is a decentralized storage network designed to create an open marketplace for storing data.
⠀
Instead of relying exclusively on centralized cloud providers, users can purchase storage from independent providers.
⠀
Its infrastructure includes:
⠀
• Decentralized storage markets
• Proof-of-Replication
• Proof-of-Spacetime
• Filecoin Virtual Machine
• Storage provider collateral
• FIL-denominated network economics
• Filecoin Onchain Cloud
⠀
The objective is to create verifiable, permissionless storage infrastructure.
⠀
But building storage capacity and selling storage to paying customers are two different achievements.
⠀
02 | WHERE DOES DEMAND COME FROM?
⠀
FIL has several direct utility mechanisms.
⠀
STORAGE PAYMENTS — Customers can pay for storage services.
⠀
COLLATERAL — Storage providers pledge FIL to participate in network operations.
⠀
TRANSACTION FEES — FIL pays for blockchain execution.
⠀
TOKEN BURNS — Certain network fees and penalties remove FIL from circulation.
⠀
SPECULATION — Investors buy FIL based on expectations for decentralized storage adoption.
⠀
Unlike governance-only tokens, FIL has direct infrastructure utility.
⠀
But here's the important distinction.
⠀
A storage provider locking FIL as collateral isn't equivalent to a customer paying for storage.
⠀
And subsidized storage activity isn't proof of sustainable commercial demand.
⠀
03 | THE BIG NARRATIVE
⠀
Three narratives define Filecoin.
⠀
DECENTRALIZED STORAGE
⠀
Reducing dependence on centralized infrastructure providers.
⠀
AI & DATA INFRASTRUCTURE
⠀
Providing verifiable storage for datasets, applications, and emerging AI workloads.
⠀
DECENTRALIZED PHYSICAL INFRASTRUCTURE
⠀
Using independent operators to supply storage capacity.
⠀
The addressable market is substantial.
⠀
Data storage is essential to the digital economy.
⠀
But a large global cloud market doesn't automatically translate into Filecoin revenue.
⠀
Customers still need competitive pricing, reliable retrieval, strong performance, and simple integration.
⠀
04 | THE COMPETITIVE ADVANTAGE
⠀
Filecoin has several technical strengths.
⠀
• Cryptographic storage verification
• Decentralized provider infrastructure
• Programmable smart contracts
• Storage-backed collateral mechanisms
• An established developer ecosystem
• Integration with IPFS-related tooling
• Infrastructure designed for verifiable data storage
⠀
Against $AR, Filecoin uses a different storage marketplace and economic architecture.
⠀
Against traditional cloud providers, it emphasizes decentralized verification and permissionless participation.
⠀
But the competitive disadvantages are meaningful.
⠀
Centralized cloud platforms offer mature tooling, integrated services, and established customer relationships.
⠀
Decentralized storage must prove that its benefits justify operational complexity.
⠀
Technology alone isn't a competitive moat.
⠀
05 | THE NUMBERS THAT MATTER
⠀
November 6, 2026 snapshot:
⠀

FILECOIN NETWORK:

These numbers reveal an important distinction.
⠀
Filecoin is primarily a storage network.
⠀
Its DeFi TVL doesn't measure its total storage capacity or storage usage.
⠀
But its limited financial activity highlights how small its on-chain DeFi economy remains.
⠀
The most important metrics are paid storage deals, customer retention, storage utilization, and recurring payments.
⠀
06 | THE TOKENOMICS QUESTION
⠀
FIL uses a more complex monetary model than fixed-supply cryptocurrencies.
⠀
Its economics include:
⠀
• Block rewards for storage providers
• Storage provider collateral requirements
• Vesting and release schedules
• Network transaction fees
• Token burns
• Penalties for certain provider failures
⠀
New issuance rewards network participation.
⠀
Collateral can temporarily restrict liquid supply.
⠀
And burns permanently remove tokens.
⠀
But here's the distinction.
⠀
Collateral locking isn't permanent supply destruction.
⠀
And token burns don't automatically offset new issuance.
⠀
The relevant equation is:
⠀
Net Supply Change = New Issuance − Token Burns
⠀
Investors must also distinguish circulating supply from total supply.
⠀
FIL's approximately $1.57 billion FDV is a provider-reported valuation based on its supply methodology, not a fixed maximum-supply guarantee.
⠀
07 | THE PAID STORAGE PROBLEM
⠀
This is Filecoin's most important fundamental challenge.
⠀
An October 2026 investigation by Bitquery examined historical storage activity.
⠀
Its findings included:
⠀
Storage Providers Proving Data:
⠀
4,044 in September 2022
⠀
517 in August 2026
⠀
That's an approximately 87% decline.
⠀
New Storage Deals:
⠀
4.75M in June 2023
⠀
153,675 in August 2026
⠀
That's an approximately 97% decline.
⠀
The investigation also reported that only 21,781 of approximately 17.97 million legacy deal settlements examined carried any payment.
⠀
These figures challenge the assumption that large historical storage activity necessarily represented paying customer demand.
⠀
But the investigation has limitations.
⠀
It covers specific on-chain payment mechanisms and historical periods.
⠀
It doesn't establish that every off-chain commercial arrangement generated zero revenue.
⠀
Still, the evidence raises a serious question.
⠀
How much of Filecoin's storage activity is supported by customers willing to pay sustainable market prices?
⠀
08 | THE 2026 STRATEGY SHIFT
⠀
Filecoin's own 2026 network strategy recognizes the need to prioritize demand.
⠀
The ecosystem is shifting its emphasis away from simply expanding storage supply.
⠀
The new priorities include:
⠀
• Increasing paid on-chain storage deals
• Improving network economics
• Growing commercial storage demand
• Expanding Filecoin Onchain Cloud
• Strengthening the relationship between usage and revenue
⠀
This is strategically important.
⠀
A storage network doesn't become commercially successful simply by accumulating capacity.
⠀
It needs paying customers.
⠀
And those customers must generate enough economic activity to support the network over time.
⠀
The direction is sensible.
⠀
Execution remains the unresolved question.
⠀
09 | THE REVENUE & BURN QUESTION
⠀
This is where the investment thesis becomes difficult.
⠀
Recent network fees are approximately $1,200 per day.
⠀
Annualizing that figure produces roughly $440,000.
⠀
Against a $680 million market capitalization, the direct fee base is small.
⠀
But transaction fees aren't equivalent to total storage-market revenue.
⠀
Filecoin can support storage payments through mechanisms not fully represented by ordinary chain fees.
⠀
That distinction matters.
⠀
The stronger concern comes from the independent storage-payment investigation.
⠀
Bitquery reported that Filecoin Onchain Cloud's warm-storage payments totaled approximately $1,676 from November 2025 through August 2026.
⠀
That figure covers the investigated payment mechanism and period, not every possible Filecoin commercial relationship.
⠀
The same investigation reported approximately 2 million FIL burned between September 2025 and August 2026.
⠀
Most of that burning was attributed to provider fees and penalties rather than ordinary user transaction gas.
⠀
That matters because burns driven by penalties aren't the same economic signal as burns driven by growing customer demand.
⠀
The strongest bullish evidence would be rising recurring storage payments alongside sustainable network economics.
⠀
10 | THE FINAL VERDICT
⠀
Filecoin has built meaningful decentralized storage infrastructure.
⠀
Its strengths include:
⠀
• Established storage verification technology
• Direct FIL utility
• Independent storage providers
• Smart contract functionality
• An existing developer ecosystem
• Exposure to AI and data infrastructure
• A strategic shift toward paid demand
⠀
But the risks remain substantial.
⠀
THE BULL CASE:
⠀
Paid storage adoption accelerates.
⠀
Filecoin Onchain Cloud attracts recurring customers.
⠀
Storage utilization improves.
⠀
Commercial revenue increases.
⠀
FIL demand strengthens.
⠀
And network economics improve relative to issuance.
⠀
THE BEAR CASE:
⠀
Paid storage adoption remains weak.
⠀
Providers continue leaving the network.
⠀
Centralized competitors retain their advantages.
⠀
New issuance pressures liquid supply.
⠀
Storage activity remains dependent on incentives.
⠀
And FIL continues trading primarily on infrastructure narratives rather than commercial results.
⠀
What would strengthen my conviction?
⠀
• Verified paid storage revenue
• Sustained growth in paying customers
• Improving provider economics
• Higher organic storage utilization
• Transparent FIL issuance and burns
• Stronger recurring Onchain Cloud payments
• Evidence of competitive storage performance
⠀
THE BOTTOM LINE
⠀
filecoin:native is one of crypto's clearest examples of the difference between infrastructure capacity and commercial adoption.
⠀
Approximately $680 million in market capitalization.
⠀
A decentralized storage network with years of development.
⠀
And a token trading nearly 99.7% below its historical peak.
⠀
But here's the contradiction.
⠀
Filecoin has built the infrastructure to support decentralized storage.
⠀
Yet recent independent research raises serious questions about the scale of genuine paid demand.
⠀
The next major catalyst isn't simply another AI partnership or storage-capacity milestone.
⠀
It's evidence that customers are paying meaningful, recurring amounts to use the network.
⠀
Infrastructure creates capacity.
⠀
Customers create revenue.
⠀
And sustainable demand determines whether the token economics work.
⠀
Bookmark this analysis before the next DePIN rotation.
⠀

⠀
filecoin:native, $AR, or ethereum:0xb64ef51c888972c908cfacf59b47c1afbc0ab8ac?
⠀

⠀

WORLD NEWS — 6 NOVEMBER

Paraguay’s president resigns, Washington’s post-election battle takes shape, OpenAI responds to the data-centre backlash, social-media giants sue California and a British celebrity is convicted.

The verified 24-hour brief 🧵

2/11 🇵🇾 PARAGUAY

President Santiago Peña resigned after digital lender ueno collapsed, freezing millions of accounts and triggering an impeachment push.

Peña denies allegations of conflicts of interest and says he will defend himself before the Senate.

3/11 Ueno served around 3 million customers and administered about $850m linked to public institutions and pensions.

The central bank intervened over solvency failures; its chief resigned and eight bank executives face arrest warrants. Customers are still awaiting access to funds.

4/11 🇺🇸 POST-MIDTERM WASHINGTON

Democrats won Congress but President Trump retains his veto and extensive executive authority. Their strongest immediate tools will include blocking nominees, launching investigations and challenging funding for the Iran war.

Gridlock remains likely.

5/11 US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth vowed to resist impeachment efforts and remain at the Pentagon.

Democrats plan investigations into his leadership and the Iran war. Republican Thomas Massie also said he would reintroduce impeachment articles. No vote has occurred.

6/11 🇬🇧 ROYAL DIPLOMACY

A senior royal aide said Britain increasingly deploys King Charles in politically sensitive diplomacy.

During his Caribbean tour, Charles expressed sorrow over slavery but did not offer an apology or reparations, in line with government policy.

7/11 🤖 AI ACCELERATING AI

An independent METR study estimated Anthropic’s models have improved on benchmark tasks around 1.9× faster since October 2025, partly because AI is helping researchers develop successors.

METR stressed that the estimate is highly uncertain.

8/11 🏗️ OPENAI’S DATA-CENTRE RESPONSE

Following voter resistance to new data centres, OpenAI promised more community consultation and transparency over energy, water and noise.

It also says its facilities should cover their own energy and infrastructure costs.

9/11 📱 CHILDREN AND SOCIAL MEDIA

Google, Meta and TikTok sued to block a new California law intended to reduce addictive social-media features for under-16s.

The companies are challenging the law; a court has not yet decided whether it is valid.

10/11 📉 AI MARKET SELLOFF

The Nasdaq fell 5.5% as investors feared tougher AI regulation and slower data-centre construction. Roughly $3tn was erased from S&P 500 companies, while major Asian technology markets also dropped sharply.

This is a market reaction—not an AI-policy ruling.

11/11 ⚖️ RUSSELL BRAND

A London jury convicted the comedian of one rape and three sexual assaults. It acquitted him of three other charges.

Brand denied non-consensual sex. He was remanded in custody and will be sentenced Monday; two additional allegations remain under investigation.

text:
Day 13 of reading a @paulg  essay every single day (13/235) ​

Today, I read "The Right Kind of Stubborn" and "Haters".
I read two today because I was not able to make time to read yesterday.

The reason I chose these essays is that the titles caught my eyes after filming a documentary all day today about @boardyai.

The first word that came to my mind right after interviewing @andrewdsouza was 'A good listener'.

I was able to see this from the morning standup.
Many ideas popped up during the meeting, and Andrew listened carefully to all of them.

Andrew asked a few questions. It seems like a refutation at the beginning, but it turned out to be a fair dispute.

In his essay, PG said: "I can't think of anyone more determined than the Collison brothers (from @stripe), and when you point out a problem to them, they not only listen, but listen with an almost predatory intensity."

I saw this in Andrew today. He was one of the best listeners I've ever seen.

When I visit a startup for an interview, I can tell what the employees think of the founder by their attitude.
This is a common pattern in unicorn startups — they treat their founder like "Boss". They take care of small details like water, straws, etc. Their employees try their best to make every moment perfect for their boss.

Shame on me, but before the filming, I thought @boardyai might have a similar atmosphere because @andrewdsouza built a multi-billion dollar company before starting Boardy. (There were 300+ people working in there)

I spent all day today in @hf0 with @boardyai , but I was not able to see any moment like that. Boardy people do not hesitate to bring new ideas in front of everyone including Andrew. To be honest, it was like looking at university students who're preparing the final project. (but with way more talented people)

There's a famous proverb in Korea. "Rice plants tend to bow their heads as they grow ripe." It's very simple. But that does not mean it's easy.

text:
OKLO $OKLO — I BOUGHT AT $7 IN 2024. AFTER THE SHARP CORRECTION, MY LONG-TERM BULLISH THESIS REMAINS INTACT.
I first invested in Oklo around $7 in 2024 and held through its extraordinary rally.
On October 24, I revisited the investment case after the stock had fallen back towards $26.
Now, ahead of Q3 earnings, I'm asking a more important question.
Has the underlying business made enough progress to justify my continued conviction?
For me, the answer depends on commercial execution, not short-term share-price movements.
I remain bullish on the long-term opportunity, but I also recognise that Oklo is still a development-stage nuclear company with substantial execution risks.
1. AI'S POWER PROBLEM ISN'T GOING AWAY
Hyperscalers are committing enormous amounts of capital to data centres, GPUs, networking and AI infrastructure.
But none of that infrastructure operates without reliable electricity.
As AI workloads expand, access to dependable, round-the-clock power becomes increasingly valuable.
That's where I see Oklo's opportunity.
Its Aurora reactor technology is designed to provide nuclear electricity to customers with significant power requirements.
Unlike intermittent generation, nuclear power can potentially provide continuous output, making it attractive for data centres and industrial customers.
But nuclear won't automatically be the cheapest or fastest solution. Natural gas, renewables paired with storage and existing nuclear generation remain important competitors.
The opportunity for Oklo is to demonstrate that advanced nuclear can deliver reliable electricity at commercially attractive prices.
2. THE BUSINESS MODEL COULD CREATE LONG-TERM RECURRING REVENUE
What interests me about Oklo isn't simply its reactor technology.
It's the company's ambition to build, own and operate power plants, selling electricity through long-term commercial arrangements.
If successful, that could create recurring revenue over the operating lives of its facilities.
But the economics are very different from selling equipment.
Oklo would need to fund development, licensing, construction and commissioning before meaningful electricity revenue begins.
That makes construction costs, financing, electricity pricing and plant utilisation critical.
A long-term power agreement is valuable, but it doesn't automatically guarantee attractive returns.
3. NUCLEAR FUEL COULD BECOME A STRATEGIC ADVANTAGE
I also see potential in Oklo's efforts to develop nuclear fuel capabilities and secure access to the supplies required for commercial deployment.
Advanced nuclear technology depends on more than reactor design.
Fuel availability, manufacturing capacity, regulatory approvals and a reliable supply chain all matter.
If Oklo can establish a dependable fuel strategy, it could reduce a significant deployment constraint and strengthen its competitive position.
But fuel recycling and supply-chain development remain technically complex, capital-intensive and subject to regulatory requirements.
The advantage still needs to be demonstrated commercially.
4. TECHNICAL PROGRESS IS ENCOURAGING. COMMERCIAL EXECUTION IS THE REAL TEST.
Oklo's Groves test reactor achieved first criticality in August 2026, an important technical milestone.
That progress supports the company's broader nuclear development ambitions.
But I distinguish technical milestones from commercial readiness.
Operating a test reactor is not the same as licensing, constructing and operating a commercial Aurora powerhouse.
For me, the next stage is about converting technical progress into regulatory approvals, construction milestones and eventually electricity sales.
That's where the investment thesis will increasingly be tested.
5. THE BALANCE SHEET PROVIDES FLEXIBILITY, BUT CAPITAL DISCIPLINE MATTERS
Oklo entered this reporting period with substantial financial resources.
At the end of Q2, the company reported approximately $3B in cash and marketable securities.
But the spending requirements are significant.
🔹 Q2 operating cash outflow: $65.5M
🔹 Q2 capital expenditure: $126.9M
🔹 FY2026 planned capital expenditure: $400M–$500M
That financial position provides flexibility to pursue development, fuel infrastructure and commercial expansion.
But I don't view the cash balance as proof that future financing won't be necessary.
The critical questions are how much each commercial project will cost, how quickly it can begin generating revenue and what returns Oklo can earn on the capital deployed.
A strong balance sheet creates an opportunity to execute. It doesn't guarantee successful commercialisation.
6. VALUATION AND MARKET SENTIMENT
There's another reason I'm approaching today's report with discipline.
Oklo's shares have experienced a substantial correction, while options activity suggests investors are positioning for considerable volatility.
The November 5 options data showed a put/call ratio of approximately 0.81 against a typical 0.64, with implied volatility above 100%.
That reflects elevated uncertainty. It doesn't predict the direction of the next move.
The sharp share-price decline has made me revisit the valuation, but I'm not treating the correction alone as a buying signal.
With Oklo still largely pre-commercial, traditional earnings and revenue multiples offer limited insight into its long-term potential.
I think a more useful approach is to assess future power generation capacity, achievable electricity pricing, construction costs, financing requirements and eventual free cash flow.
I'm bullish on the business opportunity, but that doesn't mean the stock is attractive at every valuation.
THE BEAR CASE — WHAT COULD GO WRONG?
There are genuine risks that investors shouldn't underestimate.
🔹 Regulatory approvals could take longer than expected.
🔹 Commercial reactor deployment could face construction delays and cost overruns.
🔹 Nuclear fuel availability could constrain expansion.
🔹 Additional financing could dilute shareholders or increase financial risk.
🔹 Competition from established nuclear operators, natural gas and other power technologies could pressure project economics.
🔹 Long-term customer interest may not translate into binding, financeable contracts.
🔹 Valuation could remain under pressure even as the company achieves development milestones.
These aren't minor risks.
Oklo's investment case depends heavily on future execution, and meaningful commercial electricity revenue remains ahead of it.
WHAT I'M WATCHING IN TODAY'S Q3 REPORT
🔹 Aurora deployment: Regulatory progress and realistic commercial operating timelines.
🔹 Construction readiness: Engineering, manufacturing, site preparation and supplier milestones.
🔹 Customer agreements: Progress converting commercial interest into binding, financeable power arrangements.
🔹 Nuclear fuel: Availability, recycling initiatives and supply-chain development.
🔹 Cash position: Updated liquidity, spending requirements and potential financing needs.
🔹 Project economics: Any clearer indication of construction costs, power pricing and expected returns.
For me, these disclosures will matter more than whether quarterly EPS beats or misses expectations.
MY TAKE
I remain bullish on Oklo because I believe reliable power will become an increasingly valuable part of the AI infrastructure investment cycle.
But the opportunity extends beyond AI. Industrial electrification, grid reliability and long-term energy security could also support demand for dependable electricity.
What makes Oklo interesting is its potential to participate in that demand through a long-duration electricity generation business.
What makes it risky is the amount of capital, time and execution required to get there.
I don't expect a development-stage nuclear company to be judged like an established utility.
But I do expect management to demonstrate measurable progress towards commercialisation.
My investment framework remains straightforward:
Capital → Nuclear development → Regulatory approval → Construction → Power generation → Revenue → Free cash flow → ROIC
Every stage matters.
The company that develops promising technology isn't necessarily the company that generates the best shareholder returns.
And the strongest long-term opportunity doesn't automatically justify any valuation today.
I bought Oklo at $7 because I believed in the long-term opportunity. I remain bullish today, but conviction alone isn't enough.
The next phase is about proving that Oklo can turn its technology, financial resources and commercial ambitions into operating nuclear assets that generate sustainable cash returns.
That's what I'll be looking for in today's Q3 earnings report.

The 30% Nobody Calls Too Risky

One of the biggest challenges for asset managers and financial advisers today is building portfolios that match their clients’ risk profiles when cash and bonds no longer offer the protection they once did.

Some have given up on differentiated risk profiles altogether and gone 100% into equities. But how many clients would choose that allocation if they knew exactly what they were getting?

Nearly 30% of the MSCI World Index is in technology stocks, and semiconductors account for more than a third of that exposure. There’s no shortage of charts showing how large tech has become in the index. Yet most investors stay put, whether they invest through index funds or active managers.

Here’s a comparison clients rarely see: over the period measured, semiconductor stocks were more volatile than bitcoin.

Bitcoin is routinely kept out of strategic portfolios because it’s considered ‘too risky’. How often do you hear the same objection to the semiconductor exposure clients already have through a global equity fund?

Why the double standard?

Tech already drives a large part of the return of an equity-heavy portfolio, so adding more of it does little for diversification. Bitcoin’s correlation with equities, meanwhile, is lower than many investors assume. An asset can be volatile on its own and still play a role in a diversified portfolio. What matters is how much you own and how it behaves alongside everything else.

You can build multi-asset portfolios without relying on cash and bonds and still cater to different risk profiles. That starts with looking beyond the usual building blocks and asking what each investment actually contributes to the portfolio.

text:
Similar Words. Different Tech. #05

Preconfirmation vs. Settlement vs. Finality

Imagine swapping ETH for USDC on an Ethereum rollup. Your wallet shows "Transaction Confirmed" almost instantly.

But the transaction hasn't necessarily settled on Ethereum, let alone reached finality.

So when is a transaction really complete?

1️⃣ Preconfirmation - An Early Commitment

A preconfirmation (preconf) is a commitment from an operator that a transaction will be included or executed under specified conditions.

Depending on the design, it can provide:

• Inclusion assurance: A promise to include your transaction.
• Execution assurance: A commitment to a specific execution result.
• Economic accountability: Collateral or penalties if the operator breaks its commitment.

Preconfirmations allow applications to offer faster feedback without waiting for Ethereum settlement.

But a preconfirmation is not an irreversible onchain result.

2️⃣ Settlement - Establishing the Accepted State

Settlement is where a rollup's execution results are recorded and accepted through its settlement mechanism on Ethereum.

A rollup typically posts transaction data and state commitments to L1, where its rules determine which state transitions are valid.

For example, after your ETH-to-USDC swap executes on L2, the resulting state needs to be established through the rollup's Ethereum settlement process.

Importantly, submitting a batch to Ethereum does not automatically mean the rollup state has completed settlement or reached finality.

3️⃣ Finality - Making the Accepted History Irreversible

Finality answers a different question: Can the accepted transaction history still be reversed?

Ethereum finalizes checkpoints through its proof-of-stake consensus.

Once a block is finalized, reversing it would require a serious violation of Ethereum's consensus security assumptions.

Ethereum consensus finality typically takes minutes, not milliseconds.

And for rollups, finalized L1 data and finalized L2 state are not always the same thing. The rollup's proof and settlement rules also matter.

text:
$IONQ lays out its path to profitability

Earlier today, Inder Singh, COO and CFO of IonQ, explained why IonQ raised $2B at a premium: long-term capital to keep investing in R&D and talent. The same Q3 2026 call answers the next question, how that investment fits with profitability.

In his prepared remarks, Inder put Q3 adjusted EBITDA (operating profit before non-cash costs like stock-based pay) at negative $133.6 million, reflecting integration costs concentrated in the quarter. He expects Q4 to improve, said the S&P Global Capital IQ consensus of negative $127 million doesn't seem unreasonable to IonQ, and tied that improvement to IonQ's commitment to profitability and to integrating the companies it acquired.

Craig Ellis, Senior Managing Director and Director of Research at B. Riley Securities, picked up on those comments, noting that a back office emphasis next year makes a lot of sense. (0:47)

Inder answered that he never thought IonQ would be talking about $1.2 billion in RPO (contracts signed but not yet booked as revenue), which opens room to expand margins. He described the path to profitability as what any responsible company would do, now that IonQ is reaching scale, without damaging its hyper-growth trajectory. The discipline covers costs and capital allocation with Niccolo and the leadership team: where to put the incremental dollar for growth, and the return on that growth. In his words, "I think we're now of scale." (0:57)

Niccolo de Masi, Chairman and CEO of IonQ, said that as what IonQ believes is the largest player in its sector, it will keep powering the technical roadmap in parallel with financial milestones. For him, integration also covers that roadmap and IonQ's ability to sell it, so customers drive multiples of revenue per engagement, opening "exponential gross margin and profitability opportunities." (1:39)

He closed the call expecting shared technology, manufacturing and customer relationships to strengthen each part of the business and become drivers of growth and long-term shareholder value. "IonQ is building the quantum ecosystem," he said, with a scale that supports "structural profitability" expected in the coming years. (2:17)

From the prepared remarks to the last sentence of the call, profitability came back at every stage: in the numbers, in an analyst's question, in the answers of both IonQ leaders.

text:
$IONQ : why raise $2B at a premium?

On the Q3 2026 earnings call (5 Nov 2026), Liam Pharr, Equity Research Analyst at Bank of America, speaking for Vivek Arya, the bank's research analyst who covers IonQ, asked why raise now, and for what, with Superion 256 ramping in the first half of 2027. In October IonQ raised $2 billion at a premium to its share price: the investors who bought the new shares paid more than the market price at the time.

Inder Singh, COO and CFO of IonQ, answered that IonQ needs the ability to invest for the long term, in R&D and in what he called the best talent on the planet, to keep its innovation edge. IonQ introduces a new generation of quantum computer every year, each one exponentially more powerful than the last. That takes visibility on five years of R&D and more, and the ability to keep investing without blinking.

Given how volatile the stock market has been, he said he was pleased the raise was done when it was, and at a premium. He tied it to the next chapter rather than to Superion 256: a company at half a billion dollars in revenue today heading to a billion and beyond, with a fortress balance sheet.

His conclusion: long-term capital, raised for no particular need, which he believes gives IonQ some years of runway and keeps it setting the pace for the industry.

In a certain village, there lived a poor woman. She possessed no material wealth, yet she held a profound, life-deep devotion for the Divine Mother (Amma). Every single day, she would visit the temple and offer her heartfelt salutations. Once, a grand festival took place in the village, during which the wealthy residents offered gold ornaments and silk garments to the Divine Mother.
Saddened by the fact that she had nothing of value to offer, the poor woman found a fragment of an old, broken clay bangle among some discarded items. Unseen by anyone, she placed it at the feet of the Divine Mother and, with tears in her eyes, prayed silently, "Mother, this is the only wealth I have to offer."
That night, the Divine Mother appeared in the priest’s dream and said, "Of all the offerings made by my devotees during today’s festival, the piece of a clay bangle given by that poor woman is the most precious to me. This is because she offered it with a pure heart, having completely cast aside her ego."
Spiritual Truth: What the Divine seeks is not the display of our possessions or worldly riches; rather, it is a pure heart and sincere, untainted devotion. When the mind is pure, the grace of the Divine Mother is always present.

In a certain village, there lived a poor woman. She possessed no material wealth, yet she held a profound, life-deep devotion for the Divine Mother (Amma). Every single day, she would visit the temple and offer her heartfelt salutations. Once, a grand festival took place in the village, during which the wealthy residents offered gold ornaments and silk garments to the Divine Mother.
Saddened by the fact that she had nothing of value to offer, the poor woman found a fragment of an old, broken clay bangle among some discarded items. Unseen by anyone, she placed it at the feet of the Divine Mother and, with tears in her eyes, prayed silently, "Mother, this is the only wealth I have to offer."
That night, the Divine Mother appeared in the priest’s dream and said, "Of all the offerings made by my devotees during today’s festival, the piece of a clay bangle given by that poor woman is the most precious to me. This is because she offered it with a pure heart, having completely cast aside her ego."
Spiritual Truth: What the Divine seeks is not the display of our possessions or worldly riches; rather, it is a pure heart and sincere, untainted devotion. When the mind is pure, the grace of the Divine Mother is always present.

text:
THE SACRED LANGUAGE OF DESIRE
PART II — THE ALLIANCE, THE COSMOS AND THE LAST WORD
An ode inspired by the wisdom of Thoth

Thoth observed that not every alliance must be written in the language of warfare. Some partnerships are won through intelligence, some through patience, and some through knowing when to speak and when silence carries greater authority.

Let their union be less Bonnie and Clyde and more the calculated nerve of Ray Donovan beside the strategic brilliance of Olivia Pope. Not fugitives from responsibility, but two minds capable of reading a room, weighing a choice and moving with purpose. One need not rule the other. Their strength is found in cooperation.

Two independent minds may share one direction without surrendering their individuality. They need not compete for attention, test affection through jealousy, or turn every disagreement into a battlefield. Let humour be their private language, passion their fire, honesty their compass and trust the ground beneath their feet.

They can play the game of life together: exchange glances across a crowded room, trade clever words, laugh at the world's foolishness, plan their next adventure and keep a little mystery alive. Yet the game must never be played with each other's dignity.

Then Thoth lifted his stylus and inscribed a new season upon the celestial tablet. A new dimension opened beyond the familiar horizon. The old constellations became new directions. The Falcon rose above the ordinary boundaries of the sky, and the heavens unfolded like a map of possibility.

They travelled through the Cosmic New Dimension, above the imagined gates of Nibiru Heaven, beneath the watch of distant stars. These were not promises made by the heavens, but images for the wonder two people may discover when they choose to journey side by side.

The stars did not promise an easy road. They offered only a vastness in which to discover what two willing hearts could create. For affection is not proven by grand declarations alone. It is revealed in ordinary hours: remembering, showing up, speaking truth, making room, apologising when wrong and choosing care even when excitement has quietened.

And Thoth wrote the final instruction:

Do not confuse desire with devotion. Do not confuse possession with protection. Do not confuse reputation with character. Do not mistake independence for an absence of tenderness. Let the man be courageous enough to be honest; let the woman be confident enough to declare her worth. Let both be free to choose, and responsible for the choices they make.

A beautiful face may awaken desire. A clever mind may sustain fascination. Shared laughter may kindle affection. But mutual respect gives that affection its foundation.

For the tongue can build a temple or bring it down. Words may invite two hearts closer, but actions must keep faith with what was spoken. Let the language between them be clear, playful, courageous and kind.

And when two people understand this mystery, their love becomes more than an encounter. It becomes a living inscription, written not only in poetry but in daily conduct.

Thus spoke the wisdom of Thoth:

The greatest art of attraction is not to make another fall, but to give two souls a reason to rise together. What is written in deception fades with time; what is written in truth may outlive the hands that wrote it.

Let their promises hold firm. Let both remain true in love.

Amazing how @deepigoyal is positioning himself as the misunderstood genius, a visionary so far ahead of his time that the scientific community apparently just isn’t capable of understanding him. Quite the martyrdom campaign!

Except there’s a small problem. Science doesn’t care how rich you are, how much you’ve invested or how convinced you are of your own brilliance.

When doctors question whether a sensor sitting over a superficial artery can reliably measure blood flow inside the brain, the answer isn’t “I’ve spent $30 million”, “I’ve left my CEO job” or “we offer a 14-day refund”.

None of that establishes scientific validity. A refund policy isn’t peer review. A cap table isn’t clinical evidence. And personal conviction is certainly not a substitute for independent scientific scrutiny.

Temple is already accepting ₹85,000 pre-orders while its more ambitious claims remain contested and its research awaits peer review. Now Goyal says it’s merely a wellness tracker, not a clinically validated medical device. Then why build an entire narrative around brain health, cerebral blood flow and ageing?

And where are our regulators in all this? Who determines when a wellness product’s physiological claims warrant greater scrutiny?

What bothers me most is this growing techbro culture where questioning a billionaire’s claims is treated as hostility towards innovation. Doctors asking for evidence are not attacking science. They are doing precisely what science demands.

You don’t become a Galileo simply because qualified people disagree with you.

And you certainly don’t establish a scientific breakthrough through an expensive PR campaign and a persecution complex.

If you want the credibility of science, you must also accept the inconvenience of being questioned.

text:
The New Testament does not say to respect other people’s religions or be hospitable to their beliefs. It says the opposite.

1 Corinthians 10:27-28 is the passage being twisted. Paul writes: if an unbeliever invites you and you want to go, eat whatever is set before you without asking questions for conscience’ sake. But if someone says “this was offered in sacrifice,” do not eat it, for the sake of the one who informed you and for conscience’ sake.

That is practical advice about food and not causing unnecessary offense or appearing to endorse idolatry when it is made an issue. It is not a command to respect the religion itself. Earlier in the same chapter Paul says flee from idolatry, and that what pagans sacrifice they sacrifice to demons, not to God (1 Cor 10:14, 20). An idol is nothing, and there is no God but one (1 Cor 8:4).

Hospitality in the New Testament means kindness to people (Romans 12:13; Hebrews 13:2; 1 Peter 4:9), not affirmation of false gods or doctrines. Accepting a meal invitation from an unbeliever can be an opportunity for witness, but it does not require treating their religion as valid. Jesus and the apostles repeatedly rejected idols and called people to turn from them to the living God (Acts 14:15; 17:29-30; 1 Thess 1:9; 1 John 5:21).

The exclusive claims stand: Jesus is the only way (John 14:6). There is salvation in no one else (Acts 4:12). There is no agreement between the temple of God and idols (2 Cor 6:16). Treating people with basic kindness while rejecting their false religion is biblical. Affirming the religion is not.

“Crucial,” basic tracking completed on 13 September 1986 at Prince’s Galpin Boulevard home studio in Chanhassen, Minnesota (lyrics almost entirely rewritten two days later), arrives at a fracture. Days after the Parade Tour ended in Japan and weeks before he disbanded The Revolution, Prince returned to solitary one-man recording. Written for the abandoned musical The Dawn and later noted by Prince himself as intended for Sign o’ the Times before replacement by “Adore,” the ballad is a demand for absolute totality rather than romantic comfort. 

He begins as captive: “Baby, you got to be from a different world / Because just one look from you could make an army surrender / Baby, you have got to rescue me / A prisoner in love with the opposite gender.” Martial surrender inverted into erotic need is pure Prince—power and vulnerability fused. The multi-instrumentalist who played every part himself now needs rescue. This mirrors 1986: reclaiming creative control by dissolving the band, yet seeking a connection intense enough to fill the isolation that followed.

The pre-chorus rejects ranking: “I ain’t saying you’re better, baby / But I ain’t saying you are not / I ain’t saying anything until you stop.” Only after she ceases holding back will he speak. Then the offer: “Because, baby, I will be your jack of all trades / A mind and body well-made.” He projects his studio identity onto the relationship. Love must match his musicianship—crucial, “everything from A to Z,” “you’ve got to show me everything.”

“Old Man River knocking at your door” insists they “let more than our feelings show.” The ancient, unstoppable force externalizes the demand for full exposure: “Tonight, don’t hold nothing back… I’ll give you mine if you give me yours.” Sexual and spiritual merge, as they always did for Prince. In a life of intense, often controlling relationships and the recurring search for an ideal other (the dawn he kept invoking), the lyrics expose a fear that partial intimacy would leave him permanently imprisoned—rescued only by reciprocal, total surrender. Later sax (Eric Leeds, November 1986) and orchestral overdubs (Clare Fischer, January 1987) enlarge the lush insistence, but the core remains that solitary September tracking. 

Why this art
Gustav Klimt’s The Kiss (1907–1908) locks two lovers in a golden, patterned embrace at the edge of a flowered meadow. Bodies merge into one ornamental whole; geometric rectangles and circular floral motifs interlock until individual outlines dissolve. It visualizes the demand that love be crucial “from A to Z”—nothing left outside the union. One figure’s protective lean and the other’s closed-eyed acceptance echo the prisoner/rescuer dynamic and mutual total showing. In Klimt’s gold, as in Prince’s falsetto and guitar lines, the ordinary becomes transcendent through absolute surrender.

text:
Diwali is celebrated across five auspicious days, each carrying its own spiritual legend, traditions, and significance:

Day 1 — Dhanteras (Dhanatrayodashi): Marks the birth of Lord Dhanvantari, the god of Ayurveda and healing, during the cosmic churning of the ocean. Families thoroughly clean their homes, light lamps for Yama (the god of death) to ward off untimely illness, and purchase gold, silver, or new kitchen utensils to invite health and prosperity.
Day 2 — Naraka Chaturdashi (Choti Diwali): Commemorates the victory of Lord Krishna, Goddess Kali, or Satyabhama over the demon king Narakasura, symbolizing the removal of evil and spiritual laziness. Devotees wake before sunrise for an Abhyanga Snan (ritual oil and herbal bath) and decorate doorways with vibrant rangoli and rows of clay diyas.
Day 3 — Lakshmi Puja (Main Diwali): The climax of the festival, celebrating Lord Rama's return to Ayodhya with Sita and Lakshmana (Assisted by Lord Hanuman) after 14 years of exile, as well as the worship of Goddess Lakshmi. Homes are illuminated inside and out on the darkest new moon night (Amavasya) to welcome wealth, peace, and the triumph of light over darkness.
Day 4 — Govardhan Puja (Annakut / Padwa): Honors Lord Krishna lifting the Govardhan Hill on his little finger to shelter villagers from Lord Indra's torrential rains. Devotees prepare a grand mountain of vegetarian food offerings (Annakut) in gratitude to nature; in many regions, it also marks the New Year and celebrates the marital bond between husband and wife.
Day 5 — Bhai Dooj (Bhau Beej / Yama Dwitiya): Celebrates the bond between brothers and sisters, inspired by the legend of Yama visiting his sister Yamuna, who welcomed him with a tilak and a feast. Sisters apply a protective tilak to their brothers' foreheads and pray for their long life, while brothers offer gifts and vows of lifelong support. Happy Danteras

text:
The defining feature of this window is not a model — it is a warehouse inventory dump. Twenty-five entries, nearly all of them re-hosts and LoRA adapters posted to Modelers, the Ascend-adjacent hub that has quietly become the default landing page for anything meant to run on Axera or Huawei silicon. No frontier results, no lab launches, no funding theatrics. If you build for edge hardware, there is real plumbing in here. If you do not, this is thirty seconds of your life.

The most useful artifact is Alibaba's SenseVoice ported to Axera's low-power NPUs — the multilingual recognizer, emotion and audio-event tagging included, packaged to run fully offline on-device instead of behind an API. It is joined by a second listing, SenseVoice_AgenticRAG, which wraps the same ASR engine in an on-device retrieve-and-answer loop. Neither is a research result. Both are deployment artifacts, which is precisely why they matter more than another unaudited benchmark table: offline speech that stays on cheap silicon is a product decision, not a leaderboard entry.

The re-host parade continues with AXERA-TECH's republication of two Hugging Face small models — SmolLM2-360M-Instruct and SmolLM3-3B. The 360M build's 8,192-token context is the interesting bit at that parameter count; the 3B keeps its switchable think/no-think mode and 64k window upstream. Note what is not claimed anywhere: no fine-tune, no new evals, no Axera-specific numbers. The story is the funnel. Western open weights are being piped into the Chinese edge stack faster than anyone bothers to write a launch post, and the repos are the announcement.

AMD's entry is the one with a genuinely different audience: a 4-bit AWQ build of Llama 3.1 8B packaged for DirectML, meaning local inference on a Ryzen AI laptop or Radeon GPU without CUDA and without a cloud key. Reasonable, unglamorous, useful. Less reasonable is the fact that the same window carries a second AMD artifact — a TorchAO 4-bit checkpoint of the identical model — plus an NPU-serving W8A8 build. Three quantizations of one 8B model is not a roadmap. It is a search.

The rest of the audio and dataset tier is thin but coherent. Axera lands a Sherpa-ONNX keyword-spotting package for cloud-free wake words and a SileroVAD port weighing in around 2MB for always-on voice activity detection — the unglamorous plumbing every voice product actually needs. A tiny multilingual Aya shows up in GGUF with the summary itself hedging about fine print, which is never a good sign. And the OpenThoughts3 science slice, roughly 100k step-by-step reasoning traces under Apache-2.0, is listed twice in this window under two IDs; the dataset is training data, not a model, and the duplicate listing is exactly the kind of catalog sprawl that makes this hub hard to read.

Then there is the LoRA avalanche: eleven of the twenty-five entries are FLUX.1 style adapters, most of them from the Canopus line — anime, face realism, ASCII typography, UltraRealism 2.0, pencil sketch, two separate Pixar-look adapters, an SDXL-class realism model, a Red Dead-inspired minimalize style, Snoopy, a photo-shoot mini, and a fashion-design model for apparel mockups. Each summary insists it "solves a specific creative gap." A LoRA is a file, not a launch, and a hub that surfaces eleven of them in a single overnight window is telling you more about supply than about demand.

The pattern worth carrying forward: the edge stack is consolidating around a handful of distribution points, and the interesting work is packaging — quantization, NPU ports, offline loops — not capability. Nobody in this batch shipped a better model. Several people shipped a model more people can actually run. That is the less quotable half of progress, and this week it is the only half on offer.

💔 On January 11, 2023, six-year-old Elina Fedorenko died in Avdiivka, a frontline town in the Donetsk region. The girl's condition deteriorated during the night. According to preliminary reports, the cause of little Elina's death was a heart attack. That night, Russian troops shelled Avdiivka eight times with artillery and Grad rockets.

"In the evening, her hands and feet started to go numb... She died during the night..." said Vitaliy Barabash, head of the Avdiivka military-civilian administration.

Volunteer Vlad Makhovsky said that due to the Russian shelling, Elina lived in a basement with her grandmother and grandfather. According to the Avdiivka military-civilian administration, her father, Stanislav, had died, and her mother was abroad.

Vladislav Makhovsky met Elina when he was bringing aid to the city.

"She was six years old... The first time I saw her, she was in the basement with her grandmother and grandfather. Her words, in that basement, were: 'I'm scared'," Vlad said.

The volunteer offered Elina's grandparents to evacuate the city with her to a safer region. However, they refused. Despite the constant shelling of Avdiivka, the girl remained there with her relatives. Meanwhile, most of the population had left the city. As of the beginning of 2023, there were 2,500 residents left in Avdiivka.

In September 2022, when Vlad visited Avdiivka again, it was Elina's birthday. The volunteer brought the girl a cake and a gift. However, Elina's grandparents, according to the volunteer, refused to let him meet her.

"The pain, the terrible pain, a child I saw a few times, but who touched my heart, a little girl with big, trusting eyes..." Vlad said.

text:
Good morning from Virginia. 🇺🇸

On the sixth of November, 1860, the American people cast their ballots in a presidential election that would decide not merely who occupied the White House, but whether the Union forged by Washington and Madison could survive the sectional passions that had been rising for a generation. Abraham Lincoln of Illinois, the rail-splitter turned lawyer and the first candidate of the young Republican Party, carried the day with 180 electoral votes out of 303. He took roughly 1.866 million popular votes—39.8 percent of the total—yet his name did not appear on the ballot in ten Southern states. The opposition, once the dominant force in American politics, had shattered into three contending factions, and the arithmetic of the Electoral College delivered the presidency to a man the Deep South had already resolved to treat as an existential threat.

The Democratic Party that had controlled the White House for most of the previous thirty years could not hold itself together. At Charleston and then at Baltimore the convention split. Stephen A. Douglas, the “Little Giant” of Illinois who had championed popular sovereignty in the Kansas-Nebraska Act, became the nominee of the Northern Democrats and ran with Herschel V. Johnson. John C. Breckinridge of Kentucky, the sitting vice president and the choice of the Southern rights men, stood on a platform demanding federal protection for slavery in the territories; his running mate was Joseph Lane of Oregon. A fourth ticket, the Constitutional Union Party, offered John Bell of Tennessee and Edward Everett of Massachusetts under the simple banner of “the Constitution, the Union, and the enforcement of the laws.” Douglas finished second in the popular vote yet won only Missouri and part of New Jersey—12 electoral votes. Breckinridge swept the cotton states and took 72 electors. Bell carried the border states of Virginia, Kentucky, and Tennessee and gathered 39. Lincoln swept the free states of the North and West and nothing else.

The campaign itself had been fought largely in the North. Lincoln stayed home in Springfield, speaking little, while Douglas raced across the country in a desperate effort to hold the Union together. In the South, Republican electors were not even permitted in many places; Lincoln’s support there was negligible or nonexistent. When the returns confirmed his victory, the reaction was immediate and uncompromising. South Carolina’s legislature called a convention; on December 20 the state adopted an ordinance of secession. Mississippi, Florida, Alabama, Georgia, Louisiana, and Texas followed in rapid succession before Lincoln was inaugurated. The long compromise era—Missouri, 1850, Kansas-Nebraska—had ended. A minority president, chosen by a sectional party that had made opposition to the expansion of slavery its central principle, now faced a dissolving Union.

The election of 1860 did not invent the crisis; it revealed that the crisis could no longer be postponed. Four candidates, four visions of the American future, and one electoral verdict that the Southern states refused to accept. The war that followed would decide by force of arms what the ballot box of 1860 could not settle.

He has been banned enough already starting with Doc/Ham starting AJAX ahead of him after being heavily recruited to Milwaukee to start after a 17ppg stint in Toronto over 3.5 when he had other TPMLE offers available where he would have had significant PT.

And then after the trade for Kuzma instead of taking Prince out of starting lineup Ham ensured that he started ahead of GTJ at SG out of position.

It was only after fans lobbied significantly that GTJ started in the league playoffs and he had 2 33+ point games and did not disappoint. Clearly the second best player after Giannis on the team while others looked totally out of place. Still had a very efficient season shooting 41.6% from 3 and a TS% of 59.1% for the season and over 50% from the floor overall vs Indy.

Last year he started well despite seeing his usage decline under Doc and a team with no true PG. Was averaging over 50% from corner 3s a third into the season. Shot 38.2% and 40% in November and December respectively. And 42.9% and 37.9% in February and March respectively. By the turn they of the year his usage however had decreased considerably to a career low. He rarely had the ball in his hands working off a P’N roll for his patented pull up one or two dribble 2s with the defender on his back hip.

Meanwhile AJG started every single game despite shooting 35% in December and March and having a very inconsistent season shooting overall. Despite this he played 30 minutes a game second only to Rollins on the team and barely averaged 10ppg less than GTJ averaged the year before as part of the second unit getting 25 minutes.

He is a career 39% 3 point shooter, was among league leaders in steals and deflections in the past and can’t get any burn despite AJG’s inconsistent shooting this year. 1-5, 0–1, 1-6 sandwiched in between two good games in his last 5. GTJ would’ve been benched if he had a stretch like that. Obvious double standard. A player in his prime coming to Milwaukee as a career 15ppg player has effectively been banned last season and the start of this season after seeing less time than was promised him in ‘24-‘25, despite still having an efficient season. I think that’s punishment enough. 

He deserves to be part of the Herro Rollins rotation with Burries earning his minutes and AJG getting 20 minutes if that. text:
The Market That Never Sleeps

Picture a trading desk at 2 a.m. in Seoul. Samsung and SK Hynix shares are still moving in Korea's post-market session, while a developer in New York wonders what the price right now really is.

That gap between when markets move and when your data catches up is the problem Pyth spent October working on.

 A month that kept growing

Pyth closed October with $13.67M in annualized paid subscription run-rate, up 18.9% from September's $11.49M. People were showing up too: 124,705 visitors to Pyth Terminal and 4,451 signups, up 37% in a month. Nearly 30% of new revenue came through self-serve checkout, and 332 paying accounts now rely on the data.

## The curve that learned to move

Treasury yields usually arrive as a slow, once-a-day snapshot. In October, Pyth Indices introduced a live constant-maturity U.S. Treasury curve: 14 feeds across seven maturities, from 2 to 30 years. Each maturity carries a par yield and a discount factor, published through European and U.S. market hours.

The curve now moves with the session, and builders no longer have to chase individual bonds through every auction. Alongside it, the Indices catalog grew from 50 to 77 stable feeds, adding AMD, Alibaba, SPY, QQQ, a diesel index and more.

When the reader is a machine

The quiet shift this month is who consumes market data. With Pyth Pro MCP Server 1.1, AI agents can discover feeds, check what their plan covers, and pull historical prices inside their own research workflow.

Exa, the agentic search company, is testing exactly that: Exa researches a company or event, and Pyth supplies the market data behind the story. It's early, but it hints at where this is going.

 The story behind the price

A price alone rarely explains itself. So Pyth's Data Marketplace now offers corporate-action data for supported U.S. equities, covering dividends and stock splits with dates, amounts and ratios. When a price jumps, builders can see the event that caused it, or prepare for it before it lands.

Out in the open

At WFIC 2026, Michael James of Douro Labs joined a panel with voices from Nasdaq, Cboe, OTC Markets Group and TraditionData, moderated by Morgan Stanley. Their shared conclusion: longer trading days take more than open venues. Data, liquidity and risk systems all have to keep up. Pyth's billboards in Miami, New York, London and Copenhagen carried the same message.

 The next chapter

October read like one story told through many products: Terminal, Pro, Indices and Marketplace, all aimed at the "price of everything" layer for markets that never close.

She entered me from the back and sent me into a state of unmitigated bliss with her ceaseless pounding. The fleeting feeling in my head gave way to a pulsing in my midsection. I arched my back in a battle wit the newfound sensation, until, in a moment of clarity, I released what was left in my tank. As she thrust into me, spurts of cum rained in a zigzag pattern across her bedsheets.

“You little fucking slut!” she exclaimed, as she smacked me on one cheek.

Her verbal diatribe continued along with repeated rakes across the ass I had so eagerly and innocently offered her in the beginning of the night. Her strokes increased in ferocity, as the bedsprings croaked under the onslaught. Then, she pulled out. I stared ahead expectantly for several seconds before I felt a shower of warm liquid drench my backside, which began to slowly trickle into my crack. I put my face down into the mattress and let her revel in satisfaction as she tugged the last remaining drops out of the hose pointed at my rear. When I sensed she was done, I turned to face Lisa. Facing each other on our knees, on the mattress, we embraced again and kissed passionately. Lisa got up, scrounged up a towel and helped to clean me off. Feeling the urgency of the oncoming morning, I gathered up my clothes.

“I have to go,” I said. “But, let’s do this again.”

“I would love that,” she replied.

We dressed together, I in my street clothes, and her in a silk robe that left little to the imagination. I knew I had to leave before I started getting turned on again, so, in reverse order of operation, she walked me back through the bungalow, out through the gate, and to the convertible. We embraced and kissed once more.

“Text me,” she said.

“You can count on it,” I said as I entered the vehicle.

I drove away, into the encroaching light of day, with perhaps a few hours to catch some sleep and to think of an excuse that would satisfy everyone waiting back at the cottage.
