Royal Caribbean's Royal Suite Class: The Pinnacle of Family Cruising

For travelers seeking a luxury experience without leaving the excitement of a mega-ship behind, Royal Caribbean's Royal Suite Class represents one of the most compelling premium products in contemporary cruising. Combining spacious accommodations, exclusive dining, personalized service, and VIP privileges, Royal Suite Class transforms a traditional cruise vacation into something much closer to a luxury resort experience at sea. Royal Caribbean divides the program into three tiers: Sea Class, Sky Class, and Star Class.

What Is Royal Suite Class?

Royal Suite Class is Royal Caribbean's premium suite program, offering elevated accommodations, exclusive venues, and varying levels of personalized service. The concept is designed for guests who desire more space, privacy, and convenience than standard staterooms can provide. The program is available on selected Oasis Class, Quantum Class, and Icon Class vessels.

Royal Suite Class Tiers Compared
Sea Class
Best for:

Families wanting extra space and suite accommodations without paying luxury-level prices.

Typical Suites
Junior Suites
Sunset Junior Suites
Select entry-level suite categories
Included Benefits
Priority boarding
Dedicated check-in area
Dinner access to Coastal Kitchen (subject to availability)
Premium bath amenities
Espresso machine
Luxury bedding and robes
Advantages

Sea Class delivers larger accommodations and some suite privileges while remaining significantly less expensive than higher tiers.

Limitations

No suite lounge access, concierge service, Royal Genie, included internet, or complimentary specialty dining.

Sky Class
Best for:

Families seeking a premium vacation experience with VIP treatment but not necessarily all-inclusive luxury.

Typical Suites
Grand Suites
Owner's Suites
Crown Loft Suites
Some AquaTheater Suites
One-bedroom and two-bedroom suite categories
Additional Benefits over Sea Class
Concierge service
Full Coastal Kitchen access
Suite Lounge access
Priority dining reservations
Priority embarkation and departure
Reserved entertainment seating
VOOM internet package
Access to exclusive suite sun decks on qualifying ships
Advantages

The sweet spot of the program. Many experienced cruisers consider Sky Class the best value because it combines exceptional suite accommodations with meaningful VIP perks.

Star Class
Best for:

Families wanting a nearly all-inclusive luxury experience and personalized service.

Typical Suites
Ultimate Family Suite
Royal Loft Suite
Owner's Loft Suite
Four-Bedroom Villa Suite
Ultimate Townhouse
Grand Panoramic Suites
Other flagship suite categories depending on ship
Signature Benefits
Royal Genie personal concierge
Complimentary specialty dining at most venues
Included beverage packages
Included gratuities
Included internet
Priority access throughout the ship
Customized onboard experiences
Exclusive suite dining privileges
Royal Genie Service

The Royal Genie is often compared to a luxury hotel butler. Guests can have dining reservations arranged, private celebrations coordinated, preferred seating secured, and much of the daily planning handled for them. This service is exclusive to Star Class.

Ships Featuring Royal Suite Class

Royal Suite Class is not available fleet-wide. Royal Caribbean currently offers it on the following ships:

Icon Class
Icon of the Seas
Star of the Seas
Legend of the Seas
Hero of the Seas
Oasis Class
Oasis of the Seas
Allure of the Seas
Harmony of the Seas
Symphony of the Seas
Wonder of the Seas
Utopia of the Seas
Quantum Class
Quantum of the Seas
Anthem of the Seas
Ovation of the Seas
Odyssey of the Seas
Spectrum of the Seas

These ships feature dedicated suite-only venues such as the Suite Lounge, Coastal Kitchen, and various suite sundecks.

Approximate Cost for a Family of Four
7-Day Caribbean Cruise

Pricing varies significantly based on season, departure port, ship, and suite type. The following reflects typical booking ranges seen on newer Oasis, Quantum, and Icon-class ships.

Royal Suite Class Tier Typical Suite Category Family of 4 Approximate CostSea Class Junior Suite $5,500 - $9,000
Sea Class Sunset Junior Suite $6,500 - $10,000
Sky Class Grand Suite $9,000 - $15,000
Sky Class Owner's Suite $12,000 - $20,000
Star Class Crown Loft Suite $18,000 - $30,000
Star Class Royal Loft Suite $25,000 - $50,000+
Star Class Ultimate Family Suite / Ultimate Townhouse $30,000 - $80,000+

These estimates include cruise fare but may vary substantially based on demand, holiday sailings, ship age, and booking lead time.

Typical Real-World Family Budgets

Value Luxury Experience (Sea Class)

Around $7,000-$9,000 total
Best for families wanting extra space and priority boarding

Premium Family Vacation (Sky Class)

Around $11,000-$16,000 total
Excellent balance of perks and price
Most popular choice among suite guests

Ultra-Luxury Experience (Star Class)

Around $20,000-$40,000+
Comparable to staying in a luxury resort villa
Includes many expenses that other passengers must purchase separately
Which Royal Suite Class Is the Best Value?

For most families, Sky Class provides the greatest overall value. The combination of Concierge service, Coastal Kitchen access, Suite Lounge privileges, priority seating, and premium accommodations delivers a distinctly luxury experience without the substantial premium required for Star Class.

Sea Class is ideal for families primarily seeking larger accommodations, while Star Class is aimed at travelers for whom personalized service and exclusivity are more important than budget considerations.

Final Thoughts

Royal Caribbean's Royal Suite Class has become one of the most sophisticated suite programs in mainstream cruising. Whether staying in a Junior Suite on Harmony of the Seas, a Grand Suite on Wonder of the Seas, or the spectacular Ultimate Family Suite on Icon of the Seas, guests enjoy accommodations and privileges that rival many luxury cruise brands while retaining access to the largest collection of activities, entertainment venues, and family attractions at sea. For a family of four, the decision often comes down to whether the goal is extra space (Sea Class), enhanced VIP treatment (Sky Class), or a fully elevated, concierge-led luxury vacation (Star Class).

text:
Republicans lose Congress, but Trumpism is far from finished
What the Republicans’ midterm defeat means for Donald Trump, the Democrats, and Russia
Published 6 Nov, 2026 
By Maxim Suchkov, Director of the MGIMO Institute for International Studies (IIS)
https://t.co/iHA08S6xhx
The Republicans have suffered a crushing defeat in the US midterm elections, and the Democrats have every reason to celebrate, but the real significance of the result lies less in the number of seats changing hands than in what it reveals about the direction of American politics.
The warning signs were there long before polling day, given almost two years after Donald Trump’s return to the White House many Americans have seen little improvement in their daily lives. Trade wars have unsettled the economy, while the adventure in Iran has reinforced the feeling that Washington is leading the country towards another costly and unnecessary confrontation. Democrats exploited these anxieties effectively, while Trump’s coalition appeared increasingly divided and considerably less eager to defend its president than it was in 2024.
The uncertainty before the vote concerned the scale of the Republican defeat. Would the party lose the House of Representatives but cling on to the Senate, and could it preserve its advantage among state governors? In the event, the worst outcome materialized as Democrats won both chambers of Congress and, for the first time since 2010, emerged with more governorships than their rivals.
It would be easy to overstate the immediate consequences because American politics has always been capable of dramatic reversals. Even Texas, long considered a Republican fortress, has been experiencing demographic and political changes for years and nor will a Democratic Congress necessarily transform the way Trump governs. He relied heavily on executive orders when Republicans controlled Capitol Hill and is unlikely to abandon that habit now.
There will be investigations and endless talk of impeachment, and Democrats may well pursue it, but winning control of Congress isn’t the same as possessing the votes required to remove a president. Washington will find ways to keep itself busy and much of the country will carry on much as before, thus the more interesting conclusions are political rather than procedural.
First, Trump is entering the final two years of his presidency in a position weaker than that of an ordinary lame duck as he risks becoming a liability to the very Republicans who once regarded his endorsement as the surest route to office.
After losing to Joe Biden in 2020, Trump retained his influence through the image of a man persecuted by the ‘deep state’. Younger conservatives competed for his favor, while former critics, including figures such as Marco Rubio and J.D. Vance, made their peace with him. The rewards were obvious because to secure Trump’s backing was often to secure a political future.
Now that calculation looks rather different, given several candidates associated with him have been defeated, and ambitious Republicans must consider how to build careers in a post-Trump party while Trump himself remains at its center, so the contest for 2028 has acquired a complication for which there is no easy solution.
Second, the Democrats have rediscovered a political resource they badly lacked in 2024, with credible new faces. Two years ago, their inability to offer voters a more compelling alternative than Kamala Harris exposed the exhaustion of the party’s leadership, but today they can point to a younger generation of politicians, many still under 50, with the ambition and energy to compete nationally.
They’re not yet ready-made presidential candidates and they need experience in government and recognition beyond their own states, but the pool is there, and that’s already a considerable improvement.
More revealing is how these rising Democrats speak. Some have begun borrowing themes once associated almost exclusively with the right, about protecting American livelihoods, looking after problems at home rather than crusading abroad, and restoring the country’s sense of national purpose. The vocabulary has changed because the electorate has changed. Americans don’t support politicians solely for their programs, rather they also respond to the emotions those politicians awaken.
For the moment, Democrats have proved better at capturing the public mood, but whether they can translate that mood into a coherent program is quite another question.
Third, anyone expecting a simple return to pre-Trump America is likely to be disappointed. Trump’s opponents at home and abroad may interpret the Republican collapse as proof that MAGA has been defeated and the old political order can be restored, but that’s wishful thinking...link to read full article

The AI buildout got priced on delivery in a single session, while the most sensitive models shipped behind locked doors.

NASDAQ · $2.5T ERASED
The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.52% on November 5, its worst day since April 2025, closing in correction territory more than 10% below its October record. The Nasdaq 100 lost 6.4%, about $2.5 trillion, and the chip index fell 12.25%. Reuters and CNN report the selling followed midterm results investors read as a threat to data center construction, especially in Texas. Chips, memory, neoclouds and power fell together.

MICROSOFT · $70.9B QUESTIONED
Bloomberg reports Microsoft is tightening oversight of its Nebius, IREN and Nscale builds and walking away from projects it deems risky. It exited a roughly $3 billion Nscale site in England after grid power slipped into the 2030s, and declined an option to more than double its Texas agreement. IREN confirmed the provider side: deliveries slipped on Microsoft-requested design changes, with no penalties, even as it plans about $15 billion in further spending.

OPENAI · 48.5% ON EXPLOITGYM
OpenAI released GPT-6 Cyber, built on GPT-6 Astra and rated Critical for cybersecurity under its Preparedness Framework, up from High. Access runs through the API and Codex for approved Daybreak Red customers only. OpenAI reports 48.5% on ExploitGym, 81 previously unknown high-severity Firefox flaws found, and working exploits for 948 of 1,724 reproduced Linux kernel flaws. A $1 billion grant program subsidizes defenders.

ANTHROPIC · READ-ONLY MONEY
Personal Finance in Claude connects bank, card, loan and investment accounts through Plaid, in a US-only beta on paid plans. Claude reads balances, limits and two years of transactions across up to 16 banks, and moves nothing: no transfers, no investing, no investment advice. Hub chats are excluded from training, and Anthropic offers no financial products of its own.

BLOOM · 900 MW AS PRIMARY POWER
NTT DATA agreed to deploy 900 megawatts of Bloom fuel cells as primary data center power across multiple projects, with first shipments in 2027. Bloom calls it its largest international project; no value, sites or fuel were disclosed. Bloom shares fell 16.4% the same day, priced with the rest of the buildout it supplies.

THE THROUGH-LINE
Delivery timelines set the price, politics sets the timeline, and the sharpest models ship only behind identity checks and read-only limits. Local consent and grid access now trade alongside capital.

Wall Street rout spreads to Asian markets
South Korea halted trading after a massive US tech selloff sent stocks in Japan and Taiwan plunging
Published 6 Nov, 2026 (FULL)
https://t.co/qYtZMQhnbB
Asian stock markets plunged on Friday, extending a massive technology-led selloff on Wall Street that sent major indexes tumbling and forced a temporary trading halt in South Korea.
The turmoil began on Wall Street on Thursday, when a massive selloff was triggered by fears that the Democrats’ midterm election victories could derail US President Donald Trump’s ambitious AI investment drive.
The Democratic Party secured majorities in both the House of Representatives and the Senate in Tuesday’s elections, wresting control of Congress from the Republicans. Candidates campaigning against new data center development also won gubernatorial races in Texas and Georgia, two states that have long offered tax incentives to attract technology investment.
Newly elected governors in states accounting for roughly 40% of planned US data center capacity promised to halt or pause construction, Bloomberg reported on Thursday.
The shockwaves quickly reached Asia, where South Korea’s benchmark Kospi index sank as much as 8.8% in early trading, triggering an automatic 20-minute trading halt designed to curb panic selling. Japan’s Nikkei 225 plunged around 6%, while Taiwan’s Taiex dropped more than 8%.
The rout hit some of Asia’s biggest technology companies, particularly chipmakers that have benefited from the artificial intelligence boom. South Korean giants Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix suffered heavy losses, while shares of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) also fell sharply.
“It is time for correction, but we feel that there may be some overreaction to the outcome of the midterm election,” Jun Kwang-woo, chairman of the Seoul-based Institute for Global Economics, told Reuters.
The crash also wiped more than $18 billion off the combined fortunes of 22 of Asia’s richest tech tycoons, according to Bloomberg’s Billionaires Index. SoftBank founder Masayoshi Son suffered the biggest loss at $3.9 billion, while Samsung’s controlling family saw its wealth shrink by around $2.5 billion.
On Wall Street, the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite plunged 5.5%, wiping out an estimated $2 trillion in market value. The S&P 500 sank 4.4%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 3.4%, marking the steepest US market decline since the turmoil triggered by Trump’s tariffs in April 2025.
Semiconductor giants were among the hardest hit. Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) and memory chipmaker Micron plunged more than 17%, while Nvidia shed 9.3% and Broadcom lost over 10%.
The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, which tracks major US-listed chipmakers, tumbled more than 12%. The rout also swept through major technology companies including Alphabet, Microsoft, Apple, Amazon, and Meta.
The AI sector had already come under pressure in October, when an estimated $2 trillion was erased from the Nasdaq-100. Investors have grown increasingly skeptical that massive spending on AI infrastructure will generate sufficient returns.
The Trump administration has touted more than $3 trillion in technology and AI investment commitments since January 2025, although much of the pledged funding has yet to be spent.
Asian markets recovered some of their early losses on Friday but still closed sharply lower. South Korea’s Kospi finished down 6.02%, Japan’s Nikkei 225 lost 5.96%, while Taiwan’s Taiex shed 4.51%.

Daily macro brief for November 6. Pre-session regime assessment.

THE SELLOFF
Thursday the Nasdaq 100 fell 6.36 percent to 26629.81, the S&P 500 4.36 percent to 7353.73, the Russell 2000 4.45 percent to 2729.89 and the Dow 3.44 percent, or 1,833 points, to 51523.06. The trigger was the fear that the Democratic sweep brings limits on data-center construction: Texas elected a governor who campaigned on a temporary moratorium.

AI INFRASTRUCTURE
After the close IREN said more than 4 billion dollars of annualized revenue expected in 2026 is pushed to at least January at a customer's request, and its co-CEO named Microsoft. Quarterly revenue of 228 million beat the 221 million estimate. Delivery and financing timing now sit beside policy as a question for the build-out.

ASIA OVERNIGHT
The selling moved to Asia. SoftBank fell 11.6 percent, the Kospi triggered a circuit breaker, and TSMC and SK Hynix posted steep losses.

THIS MORNING
US futures rebound in tech while the Dow lags. NQ is about 1.4 percent above its 26752 settlement and ES about 0.3 percent above 7383, YM is about 0.9 percent lower and RTY is flat. SMH is up about 5 percent pre-market, Nvidia about 4.6 percent and AMD about 7.6 percent. DIA is down about 0.8 percent, with Microsoft about 1.6 percent and Apple about 0.9 percent lower.

RATES
Thursday's official close: 2-year 4.46 (-12bp), 5-year 4.59 (-10), 10-year 4.84 (-6), 30-year 5.25 (-3). A bull steepener led by the front end, with 2s10s at 38bp from 32. The Bank of England raised Bank Rate 25bp to 4.00 percent, its first hike since August 2023, in an 8-1 vote with the dissent for a larger move.

VOLATILITY
VIX closed at 28.18 from 16.61, with VIX9D at 32.66 and VIX3M at 25.55: an inverted term structure, stress concentrated at the front. VVIX closed at 134.99. Spot VIX reads about 26.5 this morning.

ENERGY
CL December settled at 90.52 on Thursday, up about 2.7 percent as Iran reported new tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, and trades near 90.6. Reuters reported an Iranian nuclear proposal sent to Washington through Qatar. Headline risk stays two-way. No weekly EIA petroleum report today.

GOLD
GC trades near 4078, about 0.9 percent below its 4113.5 settlement. It falls with the tech bounce and offers no haven bid this morning.

CALENDAR (ET)
October payrolls 8:30: estimates between 59,000 and 65,000, unemployment expected at 4.2 percent, September at 29,000. Fed Vice Chair for Supervision Bowman 12:15, consumer credit 15:00. Before the open: Moderna, Humana, Vistra, Charter, Oklo and TeraWulf.

REGIME ASSESSMENT
The regime is stressed, not repaired. Volatility is in backwardation, the front end rallied hard and the AI trade broke on policy and financing at once. This morning's chip rebound runs against Asia's close and lands before the payrolls print. A soft number extends the front-end rally; a strong one tests both the bounce and the rate path. The split between NQ and YM reads as positioning repair in tech, not a broad turn to risk.

text:
President Trump today advanced an important discussion with several European leaders about the need for a broader European security architecture that can help establish the conditions for lasting peace.

Building on his leadership and the substantive work undertaken this week in Brussels with Ukraine, NATO, and our European partners, @SEPeaceMissions and I wanted to share some of the objectives guiding our ongoing discussions.

For more than 30 years, Europe and Russia have struggled to establish a sustainable security framework. Decades of mistrust, competing security concerns, and the devastating consequences of this war make this an extraordinarily difficult challenge, but one that is essential to lasting peace.

Our objective is to develop practical arrangements that address the security concerns of all sides, reduce the risk of future conflict, and create a more stable and predictable security environment.

We are exploring five principal goals: permanent security consultations, reliable crisis communications, greater military transparency, reciprocal measures to reduce escalation risks, and an enduring framework for long-term European security and stability.

Any arrangements must fully respect the sovereignty, territorial integrity, and independent decision-making of every nation. Each country will retain authority over its own security and alliances, and no country would have a veto over another’s sovereign choices. NATO will remain central to European collective defense, and this initiative would build upon existing institutions and commitments.

We will continue consultations through the Shell Bay format with Ukraine, NATO, the EU, and our European partners, expanding engagement to ensure that all relevant perspectives and ideas are considered. We will also engage Russia as part of the peace negotiations.

Next week in Abu Dhabi, the United States will convene the first trilateral peace discussions with Ukraine and Russia since February. All parties remain intensely engaged in preparing for substantive and productive negotiations. We will consult closely with our European partners on the sidelines and, if progress is made, aim to move toward a broader multilateral format with their direct participation.

These ideas continue to evolve, and we welcome thoughtful input. Creating the right structure will be critical to ending this war and transitioning from conflict toward conditions that make possible a durable peace.

This is difficult, detailed work. There are no easy solutions. But the opportunity to help end this devastating war and build a foundation for a more peaceful, secure, and prosperous Europe for generations to come makes it a challenge well worth undertaking.

We will see how these discussions develop and continue working intensively with all parties toward President Trump’s objective of a comprehensive and lasting peace.

🔸A furious Baldwin met Saladin at Montgisard and, despite being heavily outnumbered by as much as three to one, ordered his army to charge. The result was catastrophic for Saladin. The sultan narrowly avoided being killed and escaped on a camel, forced to watch as his men were slaughtered.

🔸In this first significant engagement, Saladin learned much about his opponent. Despite his crippling illness, Baldwin was courageous, resolute, and a worthy descendant of his heroic forefathers.

The Aftermath of Montgisard!

🔸Following Baldwin’s victory at Montgisard, the relationship between the two rulers was dominated by conflict. In April 1179, Baldwin’s constable, Humphrey of Toron, was killed by Saladin’s forces while Baldwin was leading a raid into Banyas. Then, in June 1179, Baldwin suffered a crushing defeat at Marj Ayun as he attempted to halt Saladin’s attacks on Christian territory east of Sidon.

🔸These were minor engagements in the broader struggle, and the shifting fortunes of battle had little lasting impact on the region’s geography. They were, however, opportunities for each leader to test his opponent on the battlefield and inflict significant damage upon his enemy’s retinue.

The Construction of Chastelet Castle!

🔸Baldwin intended to fortify his borders lest Saladin launch another attack. He ordered the construction of a castle called Chastelet overlooking Jacob’s Ford, which lay on the border between Christian and Muslim territories. Jacob’s Ford was strategically significant and used by botèqq1h Christians and Muslims, as it sat on the main road between Acre and Damascus.

🔸Saladin considered the castle an infringement upon Muslim territory and ultimately disrespectful. This was not how one ruler ought to treat another. Saladin wanted to avoid a confrontation and attempted diplomacy, treating Baldwin courteously as a fellow ruler. Saladin initially offered Baldwin 60,000 dinars, later increasing the offer to 100,000 dinars to demolish the castle. Baldwin refused. Saladin responded by raiding the surrounding area, and in August 1179, he launched an assault on the castle itself. After five days, Saladin breached the defenses and tore them down. More than 700 soldiers and laborers were taken prisoner, and many more were killed during the Siege of Jacob’s Ford.

Baldwin was in Tiberias at the time of the attack. By the time he reached the castle with reinforcements, he was too late. His ambitious project lay in smoldering ruins.

A Truce is Made!

🔸Persistent warfare was costly and time-consuming for both sides. It was often deemed preferable to live in harmony alongside one’s enemies than to live in perpetual warfare. As much as Baldwin and Saladin fought, they also both understood the value of peace. In 1180, a two-year truce was agreed between the two rulers. For Saladin, the truce enabled him to devote his attention to campaigns in northern Syria. Baldwin, however, needed the treaty more urgently. His health had begun to deteriorate significantly, and he needed to address the pressing matter of succession.

🔸Baldwin married his sister, Sibylla, to a Poitevin knight, Guy of Lusignan, hoping that he would serve as Baldwin’s successor and military commander when the king became too ill to exercise his powers.

🔸Baldwin’s decision to marry his sister to Guy was unpopular in certain circles at court and caused division within the kingdom. A significant party of nobles refused to follow Guy. Ultimately, Baldwin proved unable to relinquish effective control to Guy. As a result, the Leper King continued to rule despite his increasingly severe physical limitations.

IRAN: THE REAL ARCHITECT OF THE FIASCO IS NOT WHO WE THINK IT IS
By @BPartisans 

In Washington, when a war turns into a disaster, politicians look for scapegoats, generals polish their medals, and the Pentagon disguises its mistakes as historic victories. But Ken Klippenstein is throwing a wrench into this neat division of roles: behind Pete Hegseth stands Admiral Brad Cooper, head of CENTCOM and a central figure in military planning against Iran.

And while the Strait of Hormuz is throwing the energy markets into turmoil, what is our great strategist doing? CENTCOM is launching “Inside CENTCOM,” a podcast featuring Cooper. Fantastic! After bombing Iran, the time has come to bombard listeners with heroic tales. If we can’t control the consequences of war, we might as well control the narrative.

For Klippenstein’s investigation reveals a damning contradiction. The military plan pursued four objectives: to destroy Iran’s air and naval forces, to neutralize its missiles and drones, and then to dismantle its production capabilities.

But two details were missing from the list: the nuclear program, despite being the central pretext for the intervention, and securing the Strait of Hormuz, a strategic waterway on which part of the world’s energy trade depends.

A war meticulously organized to destroy targets, yet whose objectives did not even explicitly include protecting the economic lifeline that the adversary could threaten. It took a hell of a lot of arrogance to confuse firepower with strategic intelligence.

Cooper could boast about his 161 destroyed ships, his sunk submarines, and his thousands of neutralized mines. What magnificent material carnage! Except that Tehran didn’t need an intact fleet to disrupt the Strait of Hormuz. A few missiles, drones, and a persistent threat were enough to make insurers and markets tremble.

Washington was collecting wrecks. Iran was capitalizing on the consequences.

And when the Americans had to return to strike secondary capabilities that had not been sufficiently neutralized, the spectacle became downright grotesque: an army capable of pulverizing installations, but whose strategy always raised the same fundamental question: what next?

Trump decided on war. Hegseth sold it with a barrage of bellicose statements. But Cooper and his command must also explain their operational choices and their anticipation of retaliation.

This is precisely the accusation raised by Klippenstein: having confused the accumulation of tactical successes with mastery of a war.

Trump wanted a historic victory. His generals offered him a tally of destruction. Iran, for its part, turned their certainties into a global energy bill. And at CENTCOM, they’re launching a podcast to recount the feat.

St Leonard of Noblac was a Frank courtier, and during a certian invasion which they were losing, the Queen suggested to Leonard that he invoke the help of God to repel the invading army. He did, and the tide of battle turned, naming Clovis victorious. Saint Remigius, bishop of Rheims then used this miracle to convert the King, Leonard, and a thousand of thier followers to Christianity. Following his conversion, St. Leonard refused the offer of a See from his grandfather, King Clovis I.

He then began a life of austerity, sanctification, and preaching. His desire to know God grew so strong that he decided to enter the monastery at Orleans. His brother, Saint Lifiard, followed his example and, leaving the King's court, built a monastery at Meun, and lived there.

However, Leonard desired further seclusion, so he withdrew into the forest of Limousin, converting many on the way, and living on herbs, wild fruits, and spring water. He built himself an oratory, leaving it only for journeys to churches. Others, recognizing his holiness, begged to live with him, and a monastery was formed. Leonard had a great compassion for prisoners, and converted many and obtaining their release.

He died of natural causes around 559. After his death, churches were dedicated to him in France, England, Belgium, Spain, Italy, Switzerland, Germany, Bohemia, Poland and other countries. Pilgrims flocked to his tomb, and in one small town in Bavaria there are records of 4,000 favors granted through Saint Leonard's intercession.

St. Petersburg’s one-time enlistment bonus fell from $43,224 in early October to $12,350 by mid-month and $4,940 by late October. Russia is also delaying military payments and cutting benefits for families of soldiers killed in Ukraine.

RECRUITMENT MONEY

The Institute for the Study of War reports that Russia’s Defense Ministry and regional authorities are cutting or delaying enlistment payments as budget deficits grow. St. Petersburg’s successive reductions show how fast a promised incentive can shrink: the late-October figure was less than one-eighth of the early-October offer.

DEATH BENEFITS

ISW also cites a Russian pro-war commentator who said on November 3 that regions had widely reduced or eliminated payments to families of dead servicemen during 2026. The cuts reach both ends of the contract: what a man is offered to join, and what his family may receive if he is killed.

Putin is keeping the war going while making recruits and bereaved families absorb more of its cost. Regional budgets are under pressure, and the Kremlin’s answer is to pare back the promises used to sustain its army.

HOW CAN THIS GOVERNMENT CONTINUE TO LET OUR VETERANS DOWN? ABSOLUTELY DISGRACEFUL! 🇬🇧

My brother joined the Army at just 17 years old. He’s now 40, having dedicated almost his entire adult life to serving his country, with just a two-year break from the Paras.

He left the Army in June after living in military accommodation in St Athan, Wales, for the past four years, and now faces the very real possibility of becoming HOMELESS!

He’s done EVERYTHING asked of him. Applied to Vale of Glamorgan Council, repeatedly chased his housing application and contacted numerous veterans’ charities. Yet nobody seems willing or able to help.

The council continues to request documentation he’s ALREADY provided, while the charities he’s approached appear only able to offer support if he’s injured or struggling with addiction.

It’s now reached the heartbreaking point where he’s genuinely considering buying a TENT just to have somewhere to sleep!

How is this acceptable? A man who has spent many years serving and protecting his country, yet when he needs help, he’s left to fend for himself.

Our veterans deserve more than empty promises and being passed from pillar to post. Where is the priority housing we’re constantly told they’re entitled to?

I’m absolutely disgusted that this is how we treat those who have served our country.

I’m now publicly calling on Vale of Glamorgan Council, local councillors Julie Lynch-Wilson and Stephen Haines, and the Minister for Veterans and People, Calvin Bailey MP, to urgently intervene.

How can someone who has dedicated the best part of his life to serving this country be left facing homelessness, with nobody taking responsibility?

My brother isn’t asking for special treatment. He’s asking for somewhere safe to live after giving so many years of his life to his country.

Does he really have to end up sleeping in a tent before someone finally takes notice and offers him the help he desperately needs?

We constantly hear politicians praising our Armed Forces and promising to support veterans. But where is that support when they actually need it?

text:
Proof that not all soulmates are lovers.

I think one of the most misunderstood relationships in Harry Potter is the one between Harry Potter and Hermione Granger. Not because they should have ended up together romantically, but because people sometimes struggle to appreciate just how profound their friendship was without attaching a romantic label to it.

Go back to the books, and you will find a relationship built on something much deeper than attraction. It was built on trust, loyalty, sacrifice and an understanding that developed over seven years of facing almost impossible circumstances together.

Consider Goblet of Fire. When Ron falls out with Harry after his name comes out of the Goblet of Fire, Hermione refuses to abandon Harry. She knows he didn’t enter himself, even when practically everyone around him seems willing to believe otherwise. She helps him prepare for the first task, teaches him the Summoning Charm and remains beside him throughout the tournament. She doesn’t need to agree with everything Harry does to recognise when he needs someone in his corner.

Then there is Order of the Phoenix. Harry is isolated, frustrated and struggling with everything that happened at the end of the previous year. Hermione repeatedly challenges his assumptions, even when he doesn’t want to listen. She is also one of the people who helps him establish Dumbledore’s Army. She doesn’t simply validate his anger; she helps him turn it into something productive. That is an important distinction. A genuine friend doesn’t always tell you what you want to hear.

And look at Deathly Hallows.

When Ron abandons the Horcrux hunt, Hermione stays with Harry. This is not some comfortable adventure where they can retreat to Hogwarts when things become difficult. They are fugitives, constantly moving, struggling to find food and shelter, and carrying the responsibility of stopping Voldemort.

Hermione has also sacrificed her own family life. Before leaving, she modifies her parents’ memories and sends them away to protect them. She has no guarantee that she will return to them. Yet she continues with the mission.

During the months in the tent, she takes care of Harry when he is injured, keeps watch, researches their next steps and continues helping him search for Horcruxes. Their situation becomes increasingly desperate, but she doesn’t abandon him.

One of the most touching moments comes after their escape from Godric’s Hollow. Harry is devastated by what he has discovered about Dumbledore and is beginning to question someone he once trusted completely. Hermione doesn’t have all the answers. She cannot magically make his disappointment disappear. But she offers him quiet comfort.

The same emotional understanding appears when they visit Godric’s Hollow. Hermione creates a wreath for Harry to place on his parents’ graves. She understands that this is something he needs, even though he never explicitly asks her to do it.

These are small gestures, but they reveal something important about their friendship: Hermione often recognises what Harry needs emotionally, even when he struggles to articulate it himself.

And Harry isn’t simply the person being protected. He trusts Hermione’s intelligence, respects her judgement and repeatedly recognises how much he depends on her. In Half-Blood Prince, when Slughorn questions Hermione’s abilities, Harry proudly tells him that one of his best friends is Muggle-born and the best witch in their year. He doesn’t see her intelligence as something to compete with. He admires it.

Even more importantly, Harry understands that Hermione has her own fears, insecurities and emotional struggles. Their friendship isn’t built on one person constantly rescuing the other. They take turns being strong for each other.

text:
Proof that not all soul mates are lovers.

Watch this video again. Not as a ship. Not as a what if. Just watch what Harry Potter and Hermione Granger actually were.

Hermione Granger stayed when everyone else left. When Ron Weasley walked out in the tent in Deathly Hallows, when it was cold, when they had no food, when they had no plan, when Harry Potter was losing his mind, she stayed. She danced with him, not because she wanted him, but because she knew he was about to break and she was the only one who could hold him together without saying a word.

Harry Potter chose her, every single time, without ever having to kiss her. He trusted her with his life, with his secrets, with his fear. He did not trust Ginny Weasley like that. He did not trust Ron Weasley like that. He trusted Hermione Granger like she was a part of him.

And here is the questionable part no one wants to admit. If a soul mate is the person who knows you when you do not know yourself, who stays when it is easier to leave, who sees you at your worst and still chooses you, then Harry Potter and Hermione Granger were soul mates. Full stop.

Not lovers. Not a couple. Not a secret romance. Soul mates.

We have been taught that if a boy and a girl are that close, they must be in love. That if they hug, if they dance, if they cry together, it must mean something romantic. But what if it means something bigger? What if it means they were family in a way romance could never touch?

Rowling gave Hermione Granger to Ron Weasley. She gave Harry Potter to Ginny Weasley. And we all accepted it because that is how stories are supposed to end. Boy gets girl. Best friend gets best friend. Neat. Clean. Safe.

But the story itself never agreed. The story kept showing us a boy and a girl who did not need to be lovers to be inseparable. A boy who would die for her without ever calling her his. A girl who would live for him without ever calling him hers.

So tell me. If soul mates do not have to be lovers, why do we get so angry when someone says Harry Potter and Hermione Granger were soul mates? Is it because we are scared that the deepest love in the story was not romantic at all? Or is it because we know it is true, and it ruins the neat ending we were given?

They were not lovers. They were more than that. And that is what makes this video hurt so much."

text:
Where you can venerate some First Class Relics:
.
Austria
Vienna
Relic: St. Longinus' Lance (lance of the Roman soldier who pierced Christ's side)
Where: Hofburg Treasure House, Vienna, Austria. The shaft of the lance is at St. Peter's Basilica, Rome.
Relic: St. Elizabeth of Hungary
Where: Convent of St. Elizabeth, Vienna, Austria. Preserved here is St. Elizabeth's skull, crowned with the crown she wore in life.
Belgium
Brussels
Relic: St. Boniface of Brussels, Bishop of Lausanne
Where: Notre Dame de la Chapelle, Brussels, Belgium
Gheel
Relic: St. Dymphna
Where: Church of St. Dymphna, Gheel (province of Antwerp), Belgium
Canada
Midland
Relic: St. Isaac Jogues, St. Jean de Brébeuf, and Companions
Where: The Martyrs' Shrine, Highway 12, Midland, Ontario, Canada
Quebec
Relic: Kateri Tekakwitha (awaiting canonization)
Where: Saint Francis-Xavier Mission Church, Kahnawake, Quebec, Canada
Relic: St. Anne
Where: Church of Ste. Anne de Beaupré, Ste. Anne de Beaupré, Montmorency county, Quebec, Canada (the majority of St. Anne's relics are in Apt, Bouches-du-Rhone, Provence, France).
Czech Republic
Prague
Relic: St. Wenceslaus, St. Vitus
Where: Cathedral of St. Vitus, Prague, Czech Republic
Relic: St. Ludmilla
Where: St. George's Basilica, Prague, Czech Republic
Note: 
Though not a shrine in honor of canonized Saints, also of note in the Czech Republic is "Sedlec Ossuary" ("Kostnice") of the Cistercian All Saints chapel in Sedlec, a suburb on the outskirts of the town of Kutna Hora, about 45 miles East of Prague. In A.D. 1278, the abbot there went on a pilgrimage to the Holy Land and brought back some soil, which he poured over the cemetery ground. Christians, then, wanted to be buried in that soil when they died, but after a time the graveyard became too crowded, especially in A.D. 1318, when 30,000 people were buried after dying from the Plague. An ossuary was built so that the older bones could be dug up and new bodies buried. A woodcarver was later hired to decorate the chapel, and he used the bones decoratively. The ossuary came to be adorned -- literally -- with the bones of around 40,000 Christians. You can see some pictures of this fascinating place at this website, and see this page for a Quicktime panoramic view of the place. (links will open in a new browser window)
Ecuador
Quito
Relic: Mother Mariana de Jesus Torres (incorrupt), and the miraculous image of Our Lady of Good Success
Where: Mother Mariana lies in a glass coffin at the cloistered Convent of the Immaculate Conception in Quito, Ecuador. The miraculous statue can be seen by the public at these times: during the novena anticipating the Feast of the Purification, from around January 24 to February 2; during the month of May; during the month of October.
Egypt
Alexandria
Relic: St. Mark, Evangelist
Where: St. Mark Church in Alexandria, Egypt. (Cenotaph in Church of San Marco Venice, Italy where his relics had been taken during the Crusades.)
England
London
Relic: The Venerable Bede
Where: Galilee Chapel, Durham Cathedral, County Durham, England
Relic: St. Edward the Confessor (incorrupt)
Where: Westminster Abbey, London, England
Relic: St. John Southworth
Where: Westminster Cathedral (Precious Blood Cathedral), London, England. St John was hanged, drawn, and quartered during the Protestant "Reformation" for celebrating the Traditional Mass. The quarters of his body and his head were recovered after the execution, reassembled and sent to the Catholic Seminary at Douai, where it was buried during the Napoleonic purges in France. The relic was re-discovered in the last century during construction work to build a new road, and is now contained within a silver effigy, dressed in red Mass Vestments and contained within a glass reliquary in the Chapel of Saint George and the English Martyrs.
Relic: St. Thomas More and St. John Fisher
Where: Church of St. Peter ad Vincula in the Tower of London (St. Thomas More's head, after it was removed, was boiled and displayed, after which it was to be thrown into the Thames River. His daughter rescued it by bribing the guard and allegedly buried it in her husband's family vault).
France
Annecy
Relic: St. Francis de Sales
Where: Church of the first Monastery of the Visitation, Annecy, France (his incorrupt heart is preserved at the Monastery of the Visitation, Treviso, Italy).
Ars
Relic: St. John Vianney (incorrupt)
Where: Basilica at Ars, France
Bordeaux
Relic: St. Simon Stock
Where: Carmelite monastery, Bordeaux, France (his skull is preserved at Aylesford, Kent, England)
Champagne
Relic: St.Helena
Where: Abbey of Hautvillers, Champagne, France (diocese of Reims). Her relics were translated here from Constantinople in A.D. 849 (Note: it is in this abbey that the pirest, Dom Pierre Perignon, invented Champagne in the 17th century. He, too, is buried here).
Lisieux
Relic: St. Thérèse of Lisieux 
Where: Chapel of the Convent of Carmel, Lisieux, France
Nevers
Relic: St. Bernadatte (incorrupt) 
Where: Convent of St. Gildard in Nevers, France
Paray-le-Monial
Relic: St. Margaret Mary Alacoque (unsure as to whether or not she is incorrupt; I've read that her relics are not incorrupt, but are kept in a figurine of her which makes her appear incorrupt)
Where: Shrine of St. Margaret Mary Alacoque, Paray-le-Monial, France
Paris
Relic: St. Genevieve
Where: Saint Etienne-Du-Mont, Paris, France
Relic: Crown of Thorns and a piece of the True Cross 
Where: Kept, starting with King St. Louis IX, at Ste. Chapelle, Paris, France (on the Ile de la Cité, near Notre Dame) -- a chapel the sainted King built just for these relics. Removed during the French Revolution and placed in the Bibliotheque Nationale. They are now at Notre Dame Cathedral in Paris (but visit Ste. Chapelle anyway! It is stunning...).
Relic: St. Catherine Labouré (incorrupt) 
Where: Chapel of the Sisters of Charity Convent, 140 Rue du Bac, Paris, France
Relic: St. Vincent de Paul (incorrupt) 
Where: Church of St. Vincent de Paul, Rue de Sevres, Paris, France (his heart is at the Chapel of the Miraculous Medal)
Seine et Marne
Relic: St. Fiacre
Where: Cathedrale de Meaux, Seine et Marne, France
Saint Denis
Relic: St. Louis IX
Where: Basilica of St. Denis, St. Denis, France (now a northern suburb of Paris). You will find here almost all the remains of French monarchs from Dagobert I on. During the French Revolution, the contents of the tombs were emptied into a mass grave, but were later recovered and put into a large ossuary inside the Basilica.
Toulouse
Relic: St. Thomas Aquinas 
Where: Basilica of St. Sernin, Toulouse, France
Vannes
Relic: St. Vincent Ferrer
Where: Cathedral of Vannes, Vannes, France
Germany
Cologne
Relic: The Three Magi
Where: Discovered in Persia, brought to Constantinople by St. Helena, transferred to Milan in the fifth century and then to the Cathedral of Cologne, Germany in A.D. 1163, where they've been ever since.
Relic: St. Ursula
Where: Ursalaplatz (Church of St. Ursula), Cologne, Germany
Relic: St. Albert the Great
Where: Komdienstraße (Church of Saint Andreas), Cologne, Germany
Eibergen
Relic: St. Hildegard von Bingen
Where: Parish church of Eibergen, Eibergen, Germany (originally buried at the graveyard of the convent of Disibodenberg. Translated to present location in A.D. 1642).
Eichstatt
Relic: St. Walburga
Where: Church of St. Walburga, Eichstätt, Bavaria, Germany. Her relics exude a healing "oil of Saints" between 12 October and 25 February, her Feast in the Benedictine Breviary.
Fulda
Relic: St. Boniface
Where: Cathedral of Fulda, Fulda, Germany
Munich
Relic: St. Mundita
Where: Peterskirche (St. Peter's Church), Rindermarkt 1 (near the Rathaus), Munich, Germany. I have no idea who this Saint it, but her skeleton is gilded, bejeweled, and kept in a glass case. Fitted with glass eyes, she seems to stare at you from the beyond...
Trier
Relic: Christ's Robe
Where: Cathedral of St. Peter, Trier, Germany. The "tunica Christi" was brought to Trier by St. Helena.
Hungary
Buda
Relic: the right hand King Saint Istvan (Stephen) (this relic is known as the "Holy Right")
Where: Saint Istvan's Basilica, Buda (the western part of Budapest)
India
Chennai
Relic: St. Thomas the Apostle
Where: Santhome Cathedral, Chennai, India
Goa
Relic: St. Francis Xavier (incorrupt)
Where: Basilica Bom Jesus, Goa, India
Ireland (Republic of Ireland and Northern Ireland)
Downpatrick
Relic: SS. Patrick, Brigid, and Columba (a.k.a. "Columcille")
Where: Cathedral of Down, Downpatrick, Northern Ireland
Dublin
Relic: St. Valentine
Where: The Carmelite Whitefriar Church, Dublin, Republic of Ireland. At least some of the greater relics of St. Valentine were retrieved from the Cemetery of St Hippolytus, on the Tiburtine Way in Rome, and given to Fr. John Spratt by Pope Gregory XVI in 1836.
Italy
Amalfi
Relic: St. Andrew, Apostle
Where: Cathedral of Amalfi, Italy
Aquila
Relic: St. Bernardine of Siena
Where: Basilica di S.Bernardino, Aquila, Abruzzo, Italy
Assisi
Relic: St. Francis of Assisi
Where: Lower Church of the Basilica of Saint Francis of Assisi, Assisi, Umbria, Italy
Relic: St. Clare of Assisi, St. Agnes of Assisi, and their mother, Blessed Ortolana
Where: Basilica of Santa Chiara, Assisi, Umbria, Italy
Bari
Relic: St. Nicholas of Myra
Where: Translated from Myra to the Church of St. Stephen in Bari, Apulia, Italy in A.D. 1087 to save them from Muslim desecration.
Bologna
Relic: St. Dominic 
Where: Church of St. Dominic, Bologna, Italy
Relic: Blessed Imelda Lambertini (incorrupt?)
Where: San Sigismondo Church near the University of Bologna, Bologna, Italy. Blessed Imelda died in ecstasy while receiving her First Holy Communion. I am uncertain how accurately the picture above represents Imelda's state of preservation; this may be a wax figure. The translation of the Latin inscription above her tomb reads:
Imelda Lambertini
A virgin of Bologna in ancient Coenobio
St. Mary Magdalene in the Valley of Peter,
Emulating the innocent angel
When, long ago, she desired most passionately 
To approach the sacred altar,
But did not reach it because of her tender youth.
Jesus Himself, overcome by her great love,
Four days before the Ides of May in the year 1333
He descending from heaven, restored her in a new miracle with the divine bread,
Embracing her as a spouse,
He filled her with so much ecstatic joy
That the bonds of her fragile body were broken
And her most innocent spirit flew away from this earth
To the eternal banquet of Christ.
Oh blessed citizen of Bologna
You whose bones protect this place with their religious power,
Watch over the chaste line of children,
And approach the celestial banquets.
Teach them to trample down the earthly delights, like you
And to always hope for immortality.
Caposele
Relic: St. Gerard Majella
Where: Caposele, Italy
Cascia
Relic: St. Rita of Cascia (incorrupt)
Where: Basilica of St Rita in Cascia, Italy
Castello
Relic: Blessed Margaret of Castello (incorrupt) 
Where: Church of St. Domenico, Castello, Italy
Lanciano
Relic: Eucharist whose accidents had turned also to Flesh in A.D. 700
Where: Church of Lagontial, Lanciano, Italy. A Basilian monk who was offeriing Mass in the church of St. Legonziano in Lanciano began to doubt the real presence of Christ under the sacred species after the consecration. At that very moment, the priest saw how the sacred host was transformed into human flesh and the wine into blood, which later coagulated. These relics are kept in the cathedral. On Nov. 18, 1970, Dr. Edoardo Linoli analyzed the remains of "miraculous flesh and blood" and concluded that it was human myocardial tissue and genuine blood, respectively.
Milan
Relic: St. Ambrose
Where: Basilica of Sant'Ambrogio, Milan, Italy (crypt open on his Feast Day)
Relic: St. Charles Borromeo
Where: Cathedral of Milan, Italy
Monoppello
Relic: St. Veronica's Veil (?)
Where: Carthusian Monastery, Monoppello, Italy. If this is the true Veil of Vernoica, the history goes like this: the veil had been kept at St. Peter's Basilica, Rome, Italy (there is a niche for it near the statue of St. Veronica there), but was removed from there when St. Peter's was being rebuilt, and taken to this monastery in A.D. 1608. There is either a copy of the veil at the Vatican today in the aforementioned niche, or the one at the Vatican is the original (all other copies of the Veil were prohibited by Pope Paul V in 1616).
Naples
Relic: St. Januarius (Genarro)
Where: Cathedral of Naples, Naples, Campania, Italy. A vial of St. Genarro's dried blood liquefies and "boils" when brought near his head 18 times a year.
Monte Cassino
Relic: St. Benedict and St. Scholastica 
Where: Abbey of Monte Cassino, on a hill overlooking Monte Cassino, Italy
Montefalco
Relic: St. Clare of Montefalco (incorrupt)
Where: Church of the Holy Cross, Montefalco, Italy
Nettuno
Relic: St. Maria Goretti
Where: Our Lady of Grace, Nettuno, Italy
Padua
Relic: St. Anthony of Padua 
Where: Basilica of St. Anthony, Padua, Italy. When St. Anthony's coffin was opened 30 years after his disposition, most of his body was found to have returned to dust but for his tongue, which remained fresh as a sign of his gift of preaching. It is this that is kept at the Basilica.
Relic: St. Luke
Where: Basilica of St. Justina in Padua, Italy
Pavia
Relic: St. Augustine
Where: San Pietro in Ciel D'Oro, in Pavia, Italy
Rieti
Relic: St. Barbara
Where: Cathedral of Rieti, Italy
Rome
Relic: Titulus Crucis, a Crucifixion nail, relic of the True Cross, two thorns from the Crown of Thorns, the greater part of the sponge used to give Christ vinegar, a piece of the cross of the good thief (St. Dismas), finger of St. Thomas the Apostle 
Where: Santa Croce in Gerusalemme (Holy Cross in Jerusalem) 12 Piazza di Santa Croce in Gerusalemme, Rome, Italy. The church, whose floor was packed with soil from the Holy Land, was consecrated about A.D. 325, in an older building that was rebuilt to house the Passion Relics brought to Rome by St. Helena, Constantine's mother. The "Titulus Crucis" is the sign that hung over Christ's Head, naming Him as "King of the Jews."
Relic: St. Agnes 
Where: Sant' Agnese fuori le mura (St Agnes Outside the Walls), 364 Via Nomentana, Rome, Italy. The church is built over St. Agnes's tomb. Her head is preserved at the Sancta Sanctorum in the area.
Relic: Many Popes, including: St. Peter; St. Leo the Great; St. Gregory the Great; St. Pius X (incorrupt). Many Saints, including St. Gregory Nazianzen. 
Where: San Pietro in Vaticano (St. Peter's Basilica, Vatican City, Italy)
Relic: St. Jerome and St. Pius V (incorrupt), part of the manger, the icon Salus Populi Romani
Where: Santa Maria Maggiora (St. Mary Major) 42 Piazza di Santa Maria Maggiore, Rome, Italy
Relic: St. Bartholomew, Apostle (?)
Where: St. Bartholomew-in-the-Island, Rome, Italy
Relic: St. Lawrence and St. Stephen 
Where: San Lorenzo fuori le Mura (St Lawrence outside the Walls, a.k.a. San Lorenzo in Campo Verano) 3 Piazzale del Verano, Rome, Italy. The church is built over the tomb of St. Lawrence. St. Stephen was brought from Constantinople by Pope Pelagius II. Another church, San Lorenzo in Panisperna, was built over the place of St. Lawrence's martyrdom, and there one can see the gridiron upon which he was put to death.
Relic: St. Paul 
Where: Some of St. Paul's relics are kept at the Basilica of St. Paul's Outside the Walls (San Paolo Fuori Le Mura). At the Church of the Decapitation (Church of San Paolo Alle Tre Fontane), built over the site he was beheaded, you can see the marble column to which St. Paul was bound, the table on which he died, and three springs that sprang up at the spot where he was killed (the springs are now operated mechanically).
Relic: SS. Cosmas and Damian
Where: Church of Saints Cosmas and Damian, Rome, Italy
Relic: Hearts of Popes Sixtus V, Urban VII, Gregory XIV, Innocent IX, Clement VIII, Leo XI, Paul V, Gregory XV, Urban VIII, Innocent X, Alexander VII, Clement IX, Clement X, Bl. Innocent XI, Alexander VIII, Innocent XII, Clement XI, Innocent XIII, Benedict XIII, Clement XII, Benedict XIV, Clement XIII, Clement XIV, Pius VII, Leo XII, Pius VIII, Gregory XVI, Bl. Pius IX (all the Popes from Sixtus V, who died in 1590, to Pius IX, with the exception of Pius VI)
Where: Santi Vincenzo e Anastasio (Church of SS. Vincent and Anastasius), in the Piazza di Trevi, Rome
Relic: Steps of Pilate's house that Christ ascended for His sentencing (moved from Jerusalem to Rome by St. Helena)
Where: Basilica of St. John Lateran, Rome, Italy. Also in this basilica is a monument to Pope Sylvester II that is said to "cry" before a Pope dies (its marble becomes moist).
Relic: St. Cecilia
Where: Basilica of St. Cecilia, Rome, Italy. St. Cecilia was originally buried in the Catacombs of St. Callixtus (Catacombe di San Callisto), but in A.D. 821, Pope Paschal I collected some of the remains of the Saints to preserve them from raiders. Her relics were lost, though, but the Pope dreamed of where could be found. Her incorrupt body was located in what is now the Crypt of St Cecilia in those Catacombs.
Relic: St. Sebastian
Where: Church of St. Sebastian, Rome, Italy. (St. Sebastian's head is at Church of the Four Crowned Martyrs -- "Santi Quattro Incoronati)
Relic: St. Monica
Where: Church of St. Augustine in Campo Marzio, Rome, Italy
Relic: St. Ignatius of Loyola and St. Robert Bellarmine
Where: Church of the Gesu, Rome, Italy
Relic: St. Catherine of Siena and Fra Angelico 
Where: Altar at the Basilica of Santa Maria Sopra Minerva, Rome, Italy (St. Catherine's head is in the Church of San Domenico, Siena, Italy)
Note: 
Also of interest in Rome are two sites rather like Kostnice in the Czech Republic (see above). The first is the Cimitero dei Capuccini, the Capuchin catacombs near Piazza Barberini. This subterranean crypt underneath the Church of Santa Maria della Concezione contains the bones of monks and others arranged in artistic designs. The second is S.Maria dell'Orazione e Morte, located at via Giulia 262. This place contains the bones of unknown people who died and had no one to bury them, and who were buried by a Confraternity that had charge of such things and offered Masses for their souls.
San Giovanni Rotondo
Relic: St. Pio of Pietrelcina (Padre Pio)
Where: Padre Pio Shrine, San Giovanni Rotondo, Italy
Turin
Relic: St. John Bosco (incorrupt), St. Dominic Savio, St. Maria Mazzarello (incorrupt)
Where: Basilica di Maria Ausiliatrice (Mary Help of Christians), Turin, Piedmont, Italy. In Valsalice, Piedomont, you can see the room where St. John Bosco died, kept exactly as it was when he went to his Heavenly reward.
Relic: The Holy Shroud
Where: Royal Chapel of the Holy Shroud, Cathedral of San Giovanni, Turin, Piedmont, Italy (since A.D. 1578)
Venice
Relic: St. Lucy
Where: Church of San Geremia Venice, Italy. Her remains, moved from Syracuse to Constantinople, were translated from Constantinople to Venice in A.D. 1204. Her head, however, may be venerated at the Cathedral of Bourges France (it was sent to Louis XII).
Relic: St. Roch
Where: Church of San Rocco, Venice, Italy.
Malta
Relic: The pillar upon which St. Paul was martyred, Wrist bone of St. Paul
Where: Church of St Paul's Shipwreck, Saint Paul Street, Valletta. The church contains ornate baroque carvings covering almost the entire surface of the church and ornate statues that are paraded through the streets on the appropriate day.
Relic: Saint George Preca, various relics including a vial of blood
Where: Where: Blata l-Bajda, close by the mother house of the M.U.S.E.U.M. (Magister Utinam Sequator Evangelium Universus Mundus) Society, a group founded by the saint to promulgate the faith in Malta and abroad.
Peru
Lima
Relic: St. Martin de Porres
Where: Convent of the Holy Rosary, Lima, Peru
Poland
Krakow
Relic: SS. Hedwig (Jadwiga) and Stanislaus
Where: Cathedral Basilica of St. Stanislaus and St. Wenceslaus. ("Wawel Cathedral"), Krakow, Poland
Spain
Agreda
Relic: Venerable Mary of Agreda (incorrupt) 
Where: Convent of the Conception, Agreda, Spain
Avila
Relic: St. Teresa of Avila (incorrupt)
Where: Convent of St. Teresa, Avila, Spain (St. Teresa's heart is in the Carmelite Convent in Alba de Tormes, Spain)
Compostela
Relic: St. James the Greater
Where: Cathedral of Santiago de Compostela, Compostela, Spain
Granada
Relic: St. John of God
Where: Iglesia de San Juan de Dios, Granada, Spain. At the Museo de S. Juan de Dios. Calle Convalescencía, you can see the room in which he died, along with some of his belongings.
Oviedo
Relic: Sudarium of Oviedo (the second linen used to cover Jesus' Face at His entombment)
Where: Cathedral of Oviedo, Oviedo, Spain
Segovia
Relic: St. John of the Cross
Where: Segovia, Spain
Sweden
Vadstena
Relic: St. Birgitta
Where: Vadstena Cloister, Vadstena, Ostergotlands Lan, Sweden
United States
Chicago, Illinois
Relic: Over 2000 relics, including some of all 12 Apostles and 24 of the 33 Doctors of the Church
Where: St. John Cantius Parish, 825 North Carpenter Street Chicago, Illinois 60622-5405, Phone: 312-243-7373
St. Marys, Kansas
Relic: Practically every Saint who's ever lived
Where: At St. Mary's Academy, there's a Relic Chapel that contains an incredible amount of first class relics (though no major tombs or shrines). The address is: St. Mary's Academy & College, 200 E. Mission Street, St. Marys, KS 66536
Louisville, Kentucky
Relic: St. Bonosa and St. Magnus
Where: At St. Martin of Tours parish church, 639 South Shelby Street, Louisville, Kentucky, 40202
Emmitsburg, Maryland
Relic: St. Elizabeth Ann Seton
Where: Seton Shrine Chapel, Emmitsburg, Frederick County, Maryland
Relic: St. Frances Cabrini 
Where: St. Frances Cabrini Shrine, 701 Fort Washington Avenue, New York City, New York
Maria Stein, Ohio
Relic: Practically every Saint who's ever lived
Where: Another Relic Chapel like that of St. Mary's Academy in Kansas (no major tombs or shrines) is the Maria Stein Center. The address is: 2291 St. Johns Road, Maria Stein, Ohio 45860, (419) 925-4532
Philadelphia, Pennsylvania
Relic: St. John Neumann
Where: National Shrine of Saint John Neumann, 1019 North Fifth Street, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania 19123
Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania
Relic: Practically every Saint who's ever lived
Where: Another Relic Chapel -- the largest in the United States -- is St. Anthony's Chapel in the Most Holy Name of Jesus parish. The address is: 1700 Harpster St., Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania (Troy Hill).

While we're doing these childishly simple explainers, no, Trump did not betray a campaign promise by starting a new war after promising no new wars. That's a false reading of a situation where Trump communicated poorly.

Trump made two potentially contradictory promises.

1) No new wars.
2) Iran will never have a nuclear weapon.

Under normal circumstances, these two promises are compatible, but Iran was pursuing a nuclear weapon. When it got close enough to a nuclear weapon to cross a red line, the two promises immediately came into conflict.

Trump could not fulfill both promises the moment Iran got close to completing a nuclear weapon. Could not. Impossible.

The two promises came into conflict and therefore had to be prioritized. Trump, like every sane person with a realistic outlook who isn't doing Russian or Iranian propaganda or something like it, correctly (practical) and rightly (moral) concluded that prioritizing (2) (Iran will never have a nuclear weapon) was the right and necessary thing to do.

Stopping Iran from getting a nuclear weapon became superordinate to starting no new wars in the very instant Iran crossed a red line on nuclear weapon production.

Every adult understands this, whether they like it or not.

The mysterious part of this whole affair is that the New Right, like all foreign propaganda on the matter, pushed a hard line that Trump betrayed his voters with a new war without ever once explaining this conflict or the necessity of resolving it the way he did (by striking Iran, twice, the second of which dragged into a more protracted conflict).

Never once.

Does that not strike you as odd?

All of the messaging on the point was that Trump lied, Trump betrayed his base, Trump betrayed his voters. All of it.

Not once did anyone on the New Right sit down and tell their mostly young and inexperienced audience, who never experienced the nuclear fears of the Cold War, that these two promises came into conflict because of Iran's actions, and Trump had to prioritize them and to take the more important road. Not once.

text:
Dear God, thank You for today.  Lord, fill me overflowing with Your love by the power and presence of Your Holy Spirit working through me.  Remove everything separating me from You and lead me in Your way everlasting.  Take me, love me, mold me, use me as a vessel of Your light to shine before men that they might be drawn to You, to abide in You.  For the benefit of others for Your glory alone Father, Your will be done on earth as it is in Heaven.  Amen and Amen 

Job 33:26

    [26] then man prays to God, and he accepts him;
        he sees his face with a shout of joy,
    and he restores to man his righteousness.

"No weapon that is formed against thee shall prosper."  Isaiah 54:17 

This day is notable in English history for two great deliverances wrought by God for us. 

On this day the plot of the Papists to destroy our Houses of Parliament was discovered, 1605.  And secondly—today is the anniversary of the landing of King William III, at Torbay, by which the hope of Popish ascendancy was quashed, and religious liberty was secured, 1688.

This day ought to be celebrated, not by the saturnalia of striplings, but by the songs of saints. 

Job 33:28

    [28] He has redeemed my soul from going down into the pit,
        and my life shall look upon the light.’

Our Puritan forefathers most devoutly made it a special time of thanksgiving. 

There is extant a record of the annual sermons preached by Matthew Henry on this day. Our Protestant feeling, and our love of liberty, should make us regard its anniversary with holy gratitude. Let our hearts and lips exclaim, "We have heard with our ears, and our fathers have told us the wondrous things which thou didst in their day, and in the old time before them." Thou hast made this nation the home of the gospel; and when the foe has risen against her, thou hast shielded her. 

Help us to offer repeated songs for repeated deliverances. 

Grant us more and more a hatred of Antichrist, and hasten on the day of her entire extinction. Till then and ever, we believe the promise, "No weapon that is formed against thee shall prosper." Should it not be laid upon the heart of every lover of the gospel of Jesus on this day to plead for the overturning of false doctrines and the extension of divine truth? 

Psalm 50:23

    [23] The one who offers thanksgiving as his sacrifice glorifies me;
        to one who orders his way rightly
        I will show the salvation of God!”

Would it not be well to search our own hearts, and turn out any of the Popish lumber of self-righteousness which may lie concealed therein?

2 Timothy 1:6-7

[6] For this reason I remind you to fan into flame the gift of God, which is in you through the laying on of my hands, [7] for God gave us a spirit not of fear but of power and love and self-control.

2 Timothy 1:13-14

[13] Follow the pattern of the sound words that you have heard from me, in the faith and love that are in Christ Jesus. [14] By the Holy Spirit who dwells within us, guard the good deposit entrusted to you.
