text:
November 4 Saint Charles, Bishop and Confessor: From The Liturgical Year of Dom Prosper Gueranger.
.
White Double.
.
Humilitas. This word already stood, crowned with gold, upon his family escutcheon, when Charles was born at the castle of Arona. It had been said of the Borromeos that they knew nothing of humility, except to bear it on their coat of arms: but the time had now come, when the mysterious device was to be justified by the most illustrious scion of that noble family; and when, at the zenith of his greatness, a Borromeo would learn to void his heart of self, in order that God might fill it. Far, however, from abjuring the high-mindedness of his race, the humble Saint was the most intrepid of them all, while his enterprises were to eclipse the noble exploits of a long line of ancestors. One more proof that humility never debases.
.
Charles was scarcely twenty-two years of age when Pius IV, his maternal uncle, called him to the difficult post of Secretary of State, shortly afterwards created him Cardinal and Archbishop of Milan, and seemed to take pleasure in heaping honors and responsibilities on his young shoulders. The late Pontiff, Paul IV, had been ill requited for placing a similar confidence in his nephews the Caraffas, who ended their days upon the scaffold. His successor, on the contrary, as the event testified, was actuated by the inspiration of the Holy Ghost, not by the dictates of flesh and blood.
Sixty years of that fatal century had already elapsed, while the evils consequent on Luther’s revolt were ever increasing, and the Church was daily threatened with some new danger. The Protestants had just imposed upon the Catholics of Germany the treaty of Passau, which completed the triumph of the fanatics, and secured to them equality and liberty. The abdication of Charles V in despair left the empire to his brother Ferdinand; while Spain, with its immense dominions in both hemispheres, fell to his son Philip II. Ferdinand I inaugurated the custom of dispensing with Rome, by crowning himself with the diadem which St. Leo III had placed upon the brow of Charlemagne; and Philip, enclosing Italy by taking Naples in the South and Milan in the North, seemed to many to be threatening the independence of Rome herself. England, reconciled for a brief period under Mary Tudor, was replunged by Elizabeth into the schism which continues to the present day. Boy kings succeeded one another on the throne of St. Louis, and the regency of Catharine de Medici involved France in the wars of religion.
.
Such was the political situation which the minister of Pius IV had to cope with, and to utilize to the best of his power for the interests of the Holy See and of the Church. Charles did not hesitate. With faith to supply for his want of experience, he understood that to the torrent of errors, which threatened to deluge the world, Rome must first of all oppose, as an embankment, that undivided truth of which she is the guardian.
.
He saw how, in contest with a heresy, which claimed the name of Reformation while it let loose every passion, the Church might take occasion from the struggle to strengthen her discipline, elevate the morals of her children, and manifest to the eyes of all her indefectible sanctity. This thought had already, under Paul III and Julius III, led to the convocation of the Council of Trent, and inspired its dogmatic definitions and reformatory decrees. But the Council, twice interrupted, had not completed its work, which was still under dispute. It had now been suspended for eight years, and the difficulties in the way of its resumption continued to increase, on account of the quarrelsome pretensions of princes. The Cardinal-nephew bent all his efforts to surmount the obstacles. He devoted day and night to the work, imbuing with his views the Sovereign Pontiff himself, inspiring with his zeal the nuncios at the various courts, vying in skill and firmness with diplomatic ministers in order to overcome the prejudices or the ill will of monarch. And when, after two years of these difficult negotiations, the Fathers of Trent gathered together once more, Charles was the providence and the tutelary angel of this august assembly. To him it owed its material organization, its political security, the complete independence of its deliberations and their thenceforward uninterrupted continuity. Himself detained at Rome, he was the intermediary between the Pope and the Council. The presiding legates soon gave him their full confidence, as is proved from the pontifical archives; to him, as to the ablest counselor and most reliable support, they daily had recourse in their solicitudes and anxieties.
.
For her (wisdom’s) sake, says the Wise Man, I shall have glory among the multitude, and honor with the ancients, though I be young … and the faces of princes shall wonder at me. They shall wait for me when I hold my peace, and they shall look upon me when I speak, and if I talk much they shall lay their hands on their mouths. Such was truly the case with St. Charles, at this critical moment of the world’s history. No wonder that divine Wisdom, to whom he listened with such docility, and who inspired him so copiously, rendered his name immortal in the memory of a grateful posterity.
.
In his Defense of the too famous Declaration, Bossuet, speaking of the Council of Trent which owed its completion to St. Charles, says that it brought the Church back to the purity of her origin, as far as the iniquity of the times would permit. And when the œcumenical sessions at the Vatican were opened, the Bishop of Poitiers, the future Cardinal Pie, spoke of “that Council of Trent, which deserved, more truly even than that of Nicæa, to be called the great Council; that Council, concerning which we may confidently assert, that since the creation of the world no assembly of men has succeeded in introducing among mankind such great perfection; that Council whereof it has been said that, as a tree of life, it has forever restored to the Church the rigor of her youth. More than three centuries have elapsed since its labors were completed, and its healing and strengthening virtue is still felt.”
.
“The Council of Trent is perpetuated in the Church by means of the Roman Congregations charged with its continual application, and with ensuring obedience to the pontifical constitutions which have followed and completed it.” Charles suggested the measures adopted for this end by Pius IV, and approved and developed by succeeding Pontiffs. He caused the Liturgical Books to be revised, and the Roman Catechism to be compiled. But first, and in all things, he was himself the living model of his renewed discipline, and thus acquired the right to exercise his zeal for or against others. Rome, initiated by him in the salutary reform, of which it was fitting she should set the first example, was in a few months completely transformed. The three churches now dedicated to St. Charles within her walls, and the numerous altars which bear his name in other sanctuaries of the holy City, are the testimony of her enduring gratitude.
.
His administration, however, and his sojourn in Rome lasted only during the six years of Pius IV’s pontificate. On the death of that Pope, in spite of the entreaties of Pius V, whose election was done chiefly to his exertions, Charles set out for Milan, which called for the presence of its Archbishop. For nigh a century, the great Lombard city had scarcely known its pastors save by name; and this abandonment had delivered it, like so many others at that period, to the wolf that catcheth and scattereth the sheep. Our Saint understood far otherwise the responsibility of the cure of souls. He gave himself entirely to this duty, without care for himself, without a thought for the judgments of men, without fear of the powerful. His maxim was: to treat of the interests of Jesus Christ in the spirit of Jesus Christ; his program, the ordinances of Trent. Charles’s episcopate was the carrying out of the great Council; its living form, the model of its practical application in the whole Church, and the proof of its efficiency, demonstrating that it sufficed for every reform, and could, of itself alone, sanctify both pastor and flock.
.
We would gladly have given more than a passing notice of these Acts of the church of Milan, which have been lovingly collected by faithful hands, and which show our Saint in so grant a light. Herein, after the six provincial councils and eleven diocesan synods over which he presided, follows the inexhaustible series of general or special mandates dictated by his zeal; pastoral letters, the most remarkable of which is the sublime Memorial written after the plague in Milan; instructions upon the holy Liturgy, upon the tenure of churches, upon preaching, upon the administration of the Sacraments, and notably the celebrated instruction to Confessors; ordinances concerning the archiepiscopal court, the chancellorship, canonical visitations; regulations for the archbishop’s domestic family, and his vicars and officials of all ranks, for the parish priests and their meetings in conference (a custom introduced by him), for the Oblates he had founded, the seminaries, schools, and confraternities; edicts and decrees; and lastly various tables, and complete forms of administrative acts, so drawn up that nothing remains but to insert names and dates. It is a true pastoral encyclopedia which, in its magnificent amplitude, would appear to be the work of a long life, yet St. Charles died at the early age of forty-six; and moreover all this was written in the midst of trials and combats sufficient to have been his sole preoccupation.
But it is time to listen to the Church’s account of him.
.
Carolus, Mediolani nobili Borromæorum familia natus, quanta futurus esset sanctitate conspicuus, divina lux super parientis matris cubiculum noctu coruscans præsignavit. A pueritia clericali militiæ adscriptus, abbatia postmodum insignitus, patrem admonuit, ne reditus in rem familiarem converterentur: quorum ipse nactus administrationem, quidquid supererat, expendebat in pauperes. Adolescens liberalibus disciplinis Papiæ operam dedit. Castitatem adeo coluit, ut impudicas etiam mulieres ad labefactandam ejus pudicitiam pluries immissas invicta constantia fugaverit. Vigesimum tertium ætatis annum agens, a Pio Quarto ejus avunculo in sacrum Cardinalium collegium cooptatus, insigni pietatis ac virtutum omnium splendore præluxit. Mox ab eodem Mediolanensis archiepiscopus creatus, in eo plurimam operam adhibuit, ut juxta sacrosanctum Tridentinum concilium, quod ejus potissimum solicitudine jam tum fuerat absolutum, ecclesiam sibi commissam componeret: atque ut depravatos plebis suæ mores reformaret, præter iteratam sæpius synodorum celebrationem, seipsum eximiæ sanctitatis præbuit exemplar. In profligandis hæreticis e partibus Rhætorum et Helvetiorum, quorum plurimos ad christianam fidem convertit, maxime laboravit.
.
Charles was born at Milan, of the noble family of Borromeo. His future pre-eminent sanctity was foreshown by a heavenly light shining at night over the room where he was born. He was enrolled in his boyhood in the ranks of the clergy, and soon provided with an Abbey; but he warned his father not to turn its revenues to private use; and as soon as its administration was entrusted to him, he spent all the surplus income on the poor. As a youth he pursued his liberal studies at Pavia. He had the greatest love for holy chastity; and several times put to flight, with the greatest firmness, some shameless women sent to tempt him. In the twenty-third year of his age, his uncle Pius IV created him Cardinal; and he adorned that dignity by his great piety and remarkable virtues. Being soon afterwards made Archbishop of Milan, he labored strenuously to carry out, in his whole diocese, the decrees of the Council of Trent, which had just been concluded mainly through his exertions. To reform the evil customs of his people he held many synods, and moreover was ever himself a perfect model of virtue. He also labored much to expel the heretics from Switzerland and the country of the Grisons, and converted many of them to the true faith.
.
Hujus viri caritas præcipue enituit, cum Uritano principatu vendito, pretium universum ad quadraginta sureorum millia, una die in pauperes erogavit. Nec minore pietate viginti millia, quæ sibi fuerant legata, distribuit. Ecclesiasticos proventus, quibus ab avunculo copiose fuerat cumulatus, dimisit, nonnullis retentis, quibus ad proprios usus et egenorum necessitates utebatur. Quo tempore pestis Mediolani grassabatur, domesticam supellectilem, ne relicto sibi lectulo, in eosdem alendos contulit, super nuda in posterum tabula discumbens; eoque morbo laborantes sedulo invisens, paterno reficiebat affectu, et Ecclesiæ sacramenta, propriis ipse manibus administrans, mirum in modum solabatur: humillimis interim precibus reconciliator accedens, publica supplicatione indicta, fune sibi ad collum alligato, nudis pedibus, etiam offendiculo crucentatis, crucem bajulans, semetipsum pro peccatis populi hostiam, offerens, divinam indignationem avertere satagebat. Ecclesisasticæ libertatis fuit acerrimus propugnator. Disciplinæ vero restituendæ sollicitus, a seditiosis, dum orationi insisteret, tormenti bellici laxata rota, igneo globulo percussus, divina virtute servatur illæsus.
.
The charity of this holy man was strikingly exhibited when he sold the principality of Oria, and in one day distributed the price, amounting to about forty thousand gold pieces, among the poor. With no less generosity he, on another occasion, distributed twenty thousand gold pieces left him as a legacy. He resigned the many ecclesiastical benefices which his uncle had bestowed upon him, except a few which he retained for his own necessities and for relieving the poor. When the plague was raging in Milan, he gave up the furniture of his house, even his bed, for the support of the poor, and thenceforward always slept on a bare board. He visited the plague-stricken with unwearied zeal, assisted them with fatherly affection, and, administering to them with his own hands the Sacraments of the Church, singularly consoled them. Meanwhile he approached to God in humble prayer as a mediator for his people; he ordered public supplications to be made, and himself walked in the processions, with a rope round his neck, his feet bare and bleeding from the stones, and carrying a cross; and thus offering himself as a victim for the sins of the people, he endeavored to turn away the anger of God. He strenuously defended the liberty of the Church, and was most zealous in restoring discipline. For this reason some seditious persons fired upon him while he was engaged in prayer, but by the divine power he was preserved unharmed.
.
Abstinentia fuit admirabili: jejunabat sæpissime, pans tantum et aqua, solis quandoque Iupinis contentus. Nocturnis vigiliis, asperrimo cilicio, assiduis flagellis corpus domabat. Humilitatis ac mansuetudinis studiosissimus fuit. Orationem ac verbi Dei prædicationem, gravissimis licet curis occupatus, numquam intermisit. Multas ecclesias, monasteria, collegia ædificavit. Plura scripsit, ad episcoporum præsertim instructionem utilissima: cujus etiam opera parochorum catechismus prodiit. Demum in solitudinem Varalli montis, ubi sculptis imaginibus Dominicæ passionis mysteria ad vivum repræsentantur, secessit: ibique, diebut aliquot voluntaria castigatione asperam, sed Christi dolorum meditationibus suavem vitam ducens, in febrim incidit. Mediolanum reversus, ingravescente morbo, cinere ac cilicio coopertus, et oculis in crucifixi imaginem defixis, migravit in cœlum, ætatis anno quadragesimo septimo, Domini vero millesimo quingentesimo octogesimo quarto, tertio nonas Novembris. Quem miraculis clarum Paulus Quintus Pontifex Maximus in Sanctorum numerum retulit.
.
His abstinence was wonderful: he very often fasted on bread and water, and sometimes took only a little pulse. He subdued his body by night-watchings, a rough hairshirt and frequent disciplines. He was a great lover of humility and meekness. Even when occupied by weighty business, he never omitted his prayer or preaching. He built many churches, monasteries and colleges. He wrote many works of great value especially for the instruction of bishops; and it was through his care that the catechism for parish priests was drawn up. At length he retired to a solitary place on Mount Varallo, where the mysteries of our Lord’s Passion are sculptured in a lifelike manner, and there after spending some days in severe bodily mortifications sweetened by meditation on Christ’s sufferings, he was seized by a fever. He returned to Milan; but the illness growing much worse, he was covered with sackcloth and ashes, and with his eyes fixed on the crucifix he passed to heaven, in the forty-seventh year of his age, on the third of the Nones of November, in the year of our Lord 1584. He was illustrated by miracles, and was enrolled among the Saints by Pope Paul V.
.
Successor of Ambrose, thou didst inherit his zeal for the house of God; thy action also was powerful in the Church; and though separated in time by a thousand years, your names are now united in one common glory. May your prayers also mingle before the throne of God for us in these times of decadence; and may your power in heaven obtain for us pastors worthy to continue, or if need be to renew, your work on earth. How obviously applicable to both of you were those words of Holy Writ: What manner of man the ruler of the city is, such also are they that dwell therein. And again: I will fill the soul of the priests with fatness; and My people shall be filled with My good things, saith the Lord.
.
Rightly didst thou say, O Charles: “Never did Israel hear a more awful threat than this: Lex peribit a sacerdote. Priests are divine instruments, upon whom depends the welfare of the world; their abundance is the riches of all, their default is the ruin of nations.”
And when, from the midst of thy priests convoked in synod, thou didst pass to the venerable assembly of seventeen bishops thy suffragens, thy language became, if possible, still more vehement: “Let us fear lest the angered Judge say to us: If you were the enlighteners of My Church, why have you closed your eyes? If you pretended to be shepherds of the flock, why have you suffered it to stray? Salt of the earth, you have lost your savor. Light of the world, they that sat in darkness and the shadow of death have never seen you shine. You were Apostles; who, then, put your apostolic firmness to the test, since you have done nothing but seek to please men? You were the mouth of the Lord, and you have made that mouth dumb. If you allege in excuse that the burden was beyond your strength, why did you make it the object of your ambitious intrigues?”
.
But by the grace of God blessing thy zeal for the amendment of both sheep and lambs, thou couldst add, O Charles: “Province of Milan, take heart again. Behold, thy fathers have come to thee, and are assembled once more for the purpose of remedying thy ills. They have no other care than to see thee bring forth the fruits of salvation; and for this end they multiply their united efforts.”
My little children, of whom I am in labor again, until Christ be formed in you. Such is the aspiration of the Bride, which will cease only in heaven: and synods, visitations, reformation, decrees concerning preaching and government and ministry were, in thy eyes, but the manifestation of this one desire of the Church, the expression of the mother’s cry as she brings forth her children.
.
Deign, O blessed Pontiff, to restore in all places the love of holy discipline, wherein the pastoral solicitude that rendered thee so glorious found the secret of its marvelous fecundity. It may be sufficient for the simple faithful merely to know that among the treasures of the Church there exists, side by side with her doctrine and Sacraments, an incomparable code, the work of ages, an object of legitimate pride to all her sons, whose divine privileges it protects. But the priest, entirely devoted to the Church, cannot serve her usefully without that profound and persevering study which will give him the understanding of her laws in detail. But clergy and laity alike must beseech God that the miseries of the times may not impede the meeting of our venerated superiors in the councils and synods prescribed at Trent, and so grandly carried out by thee, O Charles, who didst prove by experience their value for the salvation of the world. May heaven, for thy sake, hear our prayer; and then we shall be able to say with thee to the Church: “O tender mother, let thy voice cease from weeping … for there is a reward for thy work, saith the Lord; and thy sons shall return out of the land of the enemy. And I will fill the soul of the priests with fatness: and my people shall be filled with my good things.”
.
Let us offer our homage to two Martyrs, whose memory was celebrated on this day even before that of St. Charles. Vitalis the slave and Agricola his master, combating together in the glorious arena proved that social inequality counts for nothing with regard to heaven’s nobility. St. Ambrose, when sojourning at Bologna where they had suffered, discovered their bodies and celebrated their triumph. The Church, following his example, has ever associated them in one common homage.
.
2nd Collect
.
Præsta, quæsumus omnipotens Deus, ut, qui sanctorum Martyrum tuorum Vitalis et Agricolæ solemnia colimus, eorum apud te intercessionibus adjuvemur. Per Dominum.
.
Grant, we beseech Thee, Amighty God, that celebrating the festival of Thy holy martyrs, Vitalis and Agricola, we may be assisted by their intercession with Thee. Through our Lord.

text:
ALARM TO THE UNCONVERTED
Joseph Alleine, 1671

THE NATURE OF CONVERSION (PART 3 of 3)

7. The OBJECT to which we turn in conversion is—God the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit—whom the true convert takes as his all-sufficient and eternal blessedness. A man is never truly sanctified until his heart be truly set upon God above all things, as his portion and chief good. These are the natural breathings of a believer's heart: 'You are my portion.' 'My soul shall make her boast in the Lord.' 'My expectation is from him; he alone is my rock and salvation and my glory; the rock of my strength, and my refuge, is in God' (Psalm 119:57; Psalm 34:2; Psalm 62).

Would you be certain whether you are converted or not? Now let your soul and all that is within you attend. Have you taken God for your happiness? Where does the desire of your heart lie? What is the source of your greatest satisfaction? Come, then, and with Abraham lift up your eyes eastward, and westward, and northward, and southward, and look around you; what is it that you would have to make you happy? If God should give you your choice, as He did to Solomon, or should say to you, as Ahasuerus to Esther, 'What is your petition, and what is your request, and it shall be granted you?' [Esther 5:6] what would you ask? Go into the gardens of pleasure, and gather all the fragrant flowers there—would these satisfy you? Go to the treasures of mammon; suppose you may carry away as much as you desire. Go to the towers, to the trophies of honor. What do you think of being a man of renown, and having a name like the name of the great men of the earth? Would any of these, would all of these satisfy you, and make you to count yourself happy? If so, then certainly you are carnal and unconverted.

If not, go farther; wade into the divine excellencies, the store of His mercies, the hiding of His power, the unfathomable depths of His all-sufficiency. Does this suit you best and please you most? Do you say, 'It is good to be here. Here will I pitch, here will I live and die'? Will you let all the world go rather than this? Then it is well between God and you: happy are you, O man—happy are you that ever you were born. If God can make you happy, you must be happy; for you have taken the Lord to be your God. Do you say to Christ as He to us, 'Your Father shall be my Father, and your God my God'? Here is the turning point. "Whom do I have in heaven but You? And I desire nothing on earth but You. My flesh and my heart may fail, but God is the strength of my heart, my portion forever." Psalm 73:25-26

An unsound convert never takes up his rest in God; but converting grace does the work, and so cures the fatal misery of the fall, by turning the heart from its idols—to the living God. Now the soul says, 'Lord, where shall I go? You have the words of eternal life.' [John 6:68] Here he centers, here he settles. It is the entrance of heaven to him; he sees his interest in God. When he discovers this, he says, 'Return unto your rest, O my soul, for the Lord has dealt bountifully with you' (Psalm 116:7). And he is even ready to breathe out Simeon's song, 'Lord, now let you your servant depart in peace' [Luke 2:29]; and says with Jacob, when his old heart revived at the welcome tidings, 'It is enough!' (Gen 45:28). When he sees he has a God in covenant to go to, this is all his salvation, and all his desire (2 Sam 23:5).

Is this the case with you? Have you experienced this? If so, then 'blessed are you of the Lord'. God has been at work with you; He has laid hold of your heart by the power of converting grace, or else you could never have done this.

More particularly, in conversion—

[1] We turn to CHRIST, the only Mediator between God and man (1 Tim 2:5). His work is to bring us to God (1 Pet 3:18). He is the way to the Father (John 14:6), the only plank on which we may escape, the only door by which we may enter (John 10:9). Conversion brings the soul to Christ to accept Him as the only means of life, as the only way, the only name given under heaven. He does not look for salvation in any other but Him; he throws himself on Christ alone.

'Here', says the convinced sinner, 'I will venture; and if I perish, I perish; if I die, I will die here. But, Lord, do not let me perish under the eye of Your mercy. Entreat me not to leave You, or to return from following after You. Here I will throw myself; if You slay me, I will not go from Your door.'

Thus the poor soul ventures on Christ and resolvedly adheres to Him. Before conversion, the man made light of Christ; he minded his farm, friends, pleasures, more than Christ; now, Christ is to him as his necessary food, his daily bread, the life of his heart, the staff of his life. His great desire is, that Christ may be magnified in him. His heart once said, as they to the spouse, 'What is your beloved more than another?' (Song 5:9). He found more sweetness in his merry company, wicked games, earthly delights, than in Christ. He took religion for a fancy, and the talk of great enjoyments for an idle dream; but now to him to live is Christ. Now he says, 'But whatever was to my profit I now consider loss for the sake of Christ. What is more, I consider everything a loss compared to the surpassing greatness of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord, for whose sake I have lost all things. I consider them rubbish, that I may gain Christ!' Philippians 3:7-8

ALL of Christ is accepted by the sincere convert. He loves not only the wages—but the work of Christ; not only the benefits—but the burden of Christ. He is willing not only to tread out the corn—but to draw under the yoke. He takes up the commands of Christ, yes, the cross of Christ.

The unsound convert takes Christ by halves. He is all for the salvation of Christ—but he is not for sanctification. He is for the privileges—but does not appropriate the person of Christ. He divides the offices and benefits of Christ. This is an error in the foundation. Whoever loves life, let him beware here. It is an undoing mistake, of which you have been often warned, and yet none is more common. Jesus is a sweet Name—but men do not love the Lord Jesus in sincerity. They will not have Him as God offers, 'to be a Prince and a Savior' (Acts 5:31). They divide what God has joined, the King who rules—and the Priest who saves. They will not accept the salvation of Christ as He intends it; they divide it here. Every man's vote is for salvation from suffering—but they do not desire to be saved from sinning. They would have their lives saved—but still would have their lusts. Indeed, many divide here again; they would be content to have some of their sins destroyed—but they cannot leave the lap of Delilah, or divorce the beloved Herodias. They cannot be cruel to the right eye or right hand.

O be infinitely careful here; your soul depends upon it. The sound convert takes a whole Christ, and takes Him for all intents and purposes, without exceptions, without limitations, without reserve. He is willing to have Christ upon any terms; he is willing to have the dominion of Christ as well as deliverance by Christ. He says with Paul, 'Lord, what will you have me to do?' [Acts 9:6] Anything, Lord! He gives Christ the blank page—to write down His own conditions.

[2] We turn to the laws, ordinances, and ways of Christ. The heart which once was set against these, and could not endure the strictness of these bonds, the severity of these ways—now falls in love with them, and chooses them as its rule and guide forever.

Four things, I observe, God works in every sound convert, with reference to the laws and ways of Christ, by which you may come to know your state, if you will be faithful to your own souls. Therefore, keep your eyes upon your hearts as you go along.

(i) The judgment is brought to approve of them and to subscribe to them as most righteous and most reasonable. The mind is brought to like the ways of God; and the corrupt prejudices that were once against them as unreasonable and intolerable, are now removed. The understanding assents to them all as holy, just, and good (Rom 7:12). How is David taken up with the excellencies of God's laws! How does he expatiate on their praises, both from their inherent qualities and admirable effects! (Psalm 19:8-10, etc.).

There is a twofold judgment of the understanding, the absolute and the comparative. The absolute judgment is when a man thinks such a course best in general—but not for him, or not under his present circumstances. Now, a godly man's judgment is for the ways of God, and that not only the absolute—but comparative judgment. He thinks them not only the best in general—but best for him! He looks upon the rules of piety not only as tolerable—but desirable; yes, more desirable than gold, fine gold; yes, much fine gold.

His judgment is fully determined that it is best to be holy, that it is best to be strict, that it is in itself the most eligible course, and that it is for him the wisest and most rational and desirable choice. Hear the godly man's judgment; 'I know, O Lord, that your judgments are right; I love your commandments above gold, yes, above fine gold; I esteem all your precepts concerning all things to be right; and I hate every false way' (Psalm 119:127-128). Mark, he approves of all that God requires—and disapproves of all that He forbids. 'Righteous, O Lord, and upright are your judgments. Your testimonies that you have commanded are righteous and very faithful. Your word is true from the beginning, and everyone of your righteous judgments endures forever' (Psalm 119:138, 160). See how readily and fully he subscribes; he declares his assent and consent to it, and all and everything contained therein.

(ii) The desire of the heart is to know the whole mind of Christ. He would not have one sin undiscovered, nor be ignorant of one duty required. It is the natural and earnest breathing of a sanctified heart: 'Lord, if there be any way of wickedness in me—please reveal it. What I know not—teach me. If I have done iniquity—I will do it no more.' The unsound convert is willingly ignorant, he does not love to come to the light. He is willing to keep such and such a sin, and therefore is averse to know it to be a sin—so will not let in the light at that window. Now, the gracious heart is willing to know the whole latitude and compass of his Maker's law. He receives with all acceptance the Word which convinces him of any duty that he knew not, or minded not before, or which uncovers any sin that lay hidden before.

(iii) The free and resolved choice of the will is for the ways of Christ, before all the pleasures of sin and prosperities of the world. His consent is not extorted by some extremity of anguish, nor is it only a sudden and hasty resolve—but he is deliberately purposed, and comes freely to the choice. True, the flesh will rebel—yet the prevailing part of his will is for Christ's laws and government, so that he takes them up not as his toil or burden—but as his bliss. While the unsanctified person goes in Christ's ways as in chains and fetters—the true convert does it heartily, and counts Christ's laws his liberty. He delights in the beauties of holiness, and has this inseparable mark— he had rather, if he might have his choice, live a strict and holy life, than the most prosperous and flourishing worldly life.

'There went with Saul a band of men whose hearts God had touched' (1 Sam 10:26). When God touches the hearts of His chosen, they presently follow Christ, and, though drawn, do freely run after Him, and willingly devote themselves to the service of the Lord, seeking Him with their whole desire. Fear has its uses; but this is not the mainspring of motion with a sanctified heart. Christ does not control His subjects by force—but is King of a willing people. They are, through His grace, freely devoted to His service. They serve out of choice, not as slaves—but as the son or spouse, from a spring of love and a loyal mind. In a word, the laws of Christ are the convert's love, delight, and continual study.

(iv) The bent of his course is directed to keep God's statutes. It is the daily care of his life to walk with God. He seeks great things, he has noble designs, though he falls too short. He aims at nothing less than perfection; he desires it, he reaches after it; he would not rest in any degree of grace, until he were quite rid of sin, and perfected in holiness (Phil 3:11-14).

Here the hypocrite's rottenness may be discovered. He desires holiness, as one well said, only as a bridge to heaven, and inquires earnestly what is the least that will serve his turn; and if he can get but so much as may bring him to heaven, this is all he cares for. But the sound convert desires holiness for holiness' sake, and not merely for heaven's sake. He would not be satisfied with so much holiness as might save him from hell—but desires the highest degree. Yet desires are not enough. What is your way and your course? Are the drift and scope of your life altered? Is holiness your pursuit, and piety your business? If not, you fall short of sound conversion.

And is this which we have described, the conversion which is of absolute necessity to salvation? Then be informed—that strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leads unto life—that there are few that find it—that there is need of divine power savingly to convert a sinner to Jesus Christ.

Again, be exhorted, O man, to examine yourself. What does conscience say? Does it begin to accuse? Does it not pierce you as you go? Is this your judgment, and this your choice, and this your way, that we have described? If so, then it is well. But does your heart condemn you, and tell you of a certain sin you are living in against your conscience? Does it not tell you there is such and such a secret way of wickedness that you wish to pursue; such and such a duty that you make no conscience of?

Does not conscience carry you to your closet, and tell you how seldom prayer and Scripture reading are performed there? Does it not carry you to your family, and show you the charge of God, and the souls of your children who are neglected there? Does not conscience lead you to your shop, your trade, and tell you of some iniquity there? Does it not carry you to the public-house, or the private club, and blame you for the loose company you keep there, the precious time which you misspend there, the talents which you waste there? Does it not carry you into your secret chamber, and read there your condemnation?

O conscience! do your duty. In the name of the living God, I command you—discharge your office. Lay hold upon this sinner, fall upon him, arrest him, apprehend him, undeceive him. What! will you flatter and soothe him while he lives in his sins? Awake, O conscience! What do you mean, O sleeper? What! have you no reproof in your mouth? What! shall this soul die in his careless neglect of God and of eternity, and you altogether remain silent? What! shall he go on still in his trespasses, and yet have peace? Oh, rouse yourself, and do your work. Now let the preacher in your bosom speak. Cry aloud, and spare not; lift up your voice like a trumpet. Let not the blood of his soul be required at your hands.

(ORANGE BEACH, Ala.) CoastAL Orange Beach, 25722 Perdido Beach Boulevard, Orange Beach, AL 36561

On November 2, 2026, Tracey Gambill sat down with CoastAL Restaurant Assistant General Manager Nate McGinniss for a discussion about what sets the atmosphere, the food, and the future of this establishment apart.

Located directly – directly! –  on the Gulf of America, just a few feet from the restaurant and event venue, sits CoastAL, a delightful restaurant and event venue. The spectacular location makes it special because of the breathtaking views alone.

Nate, tell me what sets your establishment apart from any other on the Gulf Coast?

“I'm excited now that you've actually had the opportunity to try our food and get the vibe of this place. That's good. The biggest thing with CoastAL is appealing to the masses. I know that sounds odd, but when you look, it's such a massive property. It's 1,200 seats. That's a lot of seats. That's a lot of people. And with that being said, I don't think we have one specific demographic that we're looking for. When we came to menu design and culinary offerings and drink offerings and what CoastAL could do differently, it was to appeal to everyone. And I think we've been successful with that. We're pushing almost exactly four years. We opened Thanksgiving four years ago; Thanksgiving week, four years ago. So we're two weeks from hitting that four-year mark, which is great. And it's been good for us. The summer's crazy. We wouldn't have it any other way. We absolutely love the summertime and all of our tourists and being on this island. But we also equally love our off season for our locals. All of our locals and this whole island work so much to make sure all of our tourists and everyone visiting our lovely community is well taken care of, and that's hard work. Once we can get past the holidays and into this time of the year and settle down a little bit, I think that's really what sets us apart in taking care of the community and the locals around us.”

Hours that are customer friendly:

Open 7 days a week, now offering brunch and lunch from 8 a.m. - 2:00 p.m. The main restaurant reopens at 4 p.m. for dinner until 10 p.m. The Beach Bar opens at 11 a.m. each day .  CoastAL Store opens at 8 a.m. daily.  

“Having these open hours that you're open is much more conducive to so many more people, and that's important. And we're very fortunate. A lot of the businesses around us do a small little shutdown to spruce things up. We did do a little shutdown this past year in January for just five days, just to kind of do a little sprucing up that was needed, because we all take a little bit of a beating over the summertime. You need a little extra time to get it back to where it needs to be. But we're very fortunate with our locals, who really support us and love us, and I think we've done something right with that. With that being said, we do tweak our hours a little bit. But I think it's still conducive to our community and what our community needs and wants, and that's important for us to hold true to that.”

Special Events:

“Two of the biggest things that we've got coming up:  We've got ‘Gumbo Fest’ this weekend. That is actually the largest event that we do every single year. As for a specialized event, last year we had a little over 700 people come for that event. Maxed out with 20 teams, 20 amazing chefs making gumbo, and we matched that again this year. We've got 20 teams again this year. And the weather is looking perfect next weekend, as long as Mother Nature continues to do her thing, we're looking beautiful next Saturday. It's such a good event. We do a live Zydeco band on the stage. It's a full-piece band. It's just a great atmosphere. We love our Mardi Gras and that feel down here in the south and on this island. We have many of our Louisiana friends who come over and have property in the area. When we had the idea to do Gumbo Fest, it was just a good fit.”

He continues, “Coming up on November 21, we've got ‘Toast for the Coast.’ That is a little high-end gala that we are doing that benefits the hard work that goes into taking care of our environment and the beach. A lot of work goes into this island to make sure that our wildlife is protected, marine life is protected, and our beaches are beautiful. It's a perfect event to help raise funds for those organizations that work so hard to make sure that we continue to enjoy this environment and what this island life is all about. That benefits them, and that's coming up on the 21st, and then the holidays are upon us, all at the same time.”

Tell me about your chef:

“We have Chef Emilio Urban, which is our current Executive Chef. He has been with us for many years now. He's been on this island, too, for a couple of years, so he knew what was needed in that role. It's a very unique role to fill in such a high-volume, large location.
It was just a good fit with bringing Chef Emilio on, and he was able to make an impact on the team from day one. Our current menu and our culinary offerings express his background and experience with dealing with coastal seafood and what this environment entails. It’s a nice variety. And it's not an overly big menu. The offerings that are on there are diverse. There's something for everyone on there. We pay special close attention to allergies and the allergy offerings we're able to provide. Even though it's not as big as some other people's menus, the offerings are local, fresh, and they appeal to anyone who can come and enjoy CostalAL.
A big menu is too much to look at sometimes. So even though it's a little bit smaller, I think it accomplishes everything that everyone wants and what we need as well. We always need a nice glass of wine or a wonderful beer to go along with something as beautiful as some of the culinary offerings we have.”

Further adding, “We do make some small changes to the menu every year. And that was something that we hadn't had prior to this year. So that was one of the new menu items that we always tweak a little bit in the off season and then roll with a brand new menu as we roll into spring break and get into the tourist season. Adding the Caribbean Pork Chop was a big one for us,” he said.

Probably the majority's favorite is the Pimento Cheese Appetizer:

“It is absolutely everyone's favorite. It is made in house every single day, like most of our items. But there is just something about that pimento cheese, and the seasonal jam that we put on it, and the fruit. It is light and delicious. It's really perfection. We appreciate that. That is definitely our number one signature item that everyone, if they haven't, must try.

“We do make some small changes every year. A couple of items, if we don't feel like they've performed, because there's a business side to everything we do, so we'll remove a couple of items if we don't feel like they've performed. But we also look to stay up-to-date with what people are craving and what people want. So we make sure that we do our due diligence and research and add those items every year as well.”

It's nice to have something for vegetarians:

“That's exactly right. It's important. Everybody's dietary needs, wants and wishes are different, so it's important that you can make sure everyone can come in and enjoy a beautiful meal.”

The ownership is also part of the Florabama:

“Also, yes, ma'am, that is correct. John McInnis and Cam Price are the primary two owners of this location, and they do have our little sister locations down the road with the Florabama Yacht Club, Old River Grill, and the Florabama. All that. Absolutely fantastic ownership, and active in the community. You couldn't ask for better ownership.”

Are you related to John McInnis?

“I am not, just an odd coincidence with the McGinnis name. Can you believe that? Slightly different. I know, because I get that more often than anybody. They're like, ‘Which one are you?’ And I'm like, ‘Nope, mine actually has a ‘G’ in it.’ The other McInnis’s don't have a ‘G.’ So many people know John and Cam. It's a beautiful thing. I absolutely love it. Like I said, I’ve been here. Hal Buck and I both came on when it was still just a sand lot, really. We had just started construction, and then we started down the road. Hal and I have both been here since the very beginning.”

Do you know if you will ever offer Royal Red shrimp?
“I don't know. I wish I could answer that. It’s just hard to come by, and the price is certainly a factor in that.”

Food Review:

Signature House-Made Pimento Cheese Appetizer:

Featuring white cheddar pimento cheese, seasonal jam, praline pecans, house-baked crackers, and seasonal fruit. 

Guest Linda Venne praised its innovative flavor combination, versatility, and portion size, noting that it could serve two to four people. “It's unique. It's innovative, and it's got cheese in it. So how can it be bad? It’s absolutely delightful!" she said. ($16)

Shrimp and Crab Bisque:

American shrimp, crab, corn, and heavy cream. Very creamy with a nice quantity of shrimp and crab. The flavor is unique and interesting. A must try. ($11)

Caribbean Pork Chop: 

A more than generous 18 ounce bone-in pork chop, Caribbean rice pilaf, Black Eye Pea crunch, and pineapple beurre blanc. A most unusual selection of pork, 3” high, to be exact, with crunch Black Eye pea for a nice texture, topped with pineapple beurre blanc sauce. This is so unique there are no adequate words to describe it. You will have to see it to believe it!! ($32)

Bushwacker Tiramisu:

Bushwacker soaked ladyfingers, mascarpone cream, Cocoa shaved chocolate and an edible flower make up this interesting take on the traditional tiramisu dessert. The presentation is lovely. The tiramisu is quite delicious, although the soaked ladyfingers were a little heavy in comparison to the traditional tiramisu variety. The large portion is enough for two people. ($12)
 
For any questions, comments, or concerns, you can contact CoastAL at 251-240-6001.

To add to or correct any information in this report, please get in touch with me at tbird32507@gmail.com

$BJRI Q3 2026 earnings: BJ's Restaurants traffic and margins climb, while debt nearly disappears

BJ's Restaurants, the casual dining pizza and brewhouse chain, filled its dining rooms while food inflation cooled off. Comparable restaurant sales climbed 8% on an 8% traffic gain, and restaurant-level profit jumped 28% as ingredient, labor and occupancy costs all fell as a share of revenue. Chief executive Lyle Tick raised the full-year outlook again, though by our math the updated plan leaves comparable sales growth slowing to about 2% in the fourth quarter.

• Comparable restaurant sales: +𝟖.𝟏% (guest traffic +8.3% from a year ago)
• Restaurant-level operating margin: 𝟏𝟒.𝟕% (12.5% a year ago)
• Total debt: $𝟏𝟔.𝟎𝐌 (down from $85.0M at year-end 2025)
• Full-year Adjusted EBITDA outlook: 𝐑𝐚𝐢𝐬𝐞𝐝 $𝟑𝐌 (middle of the range: $151.5M (+13%))

⚖️ 𝐕𝐞𝐫𝐝𝐢𝐜𝐭: 🟢 Bullish

The story got better because the two main worries around the recovery — shrinking spending per guest and rising food costs — both eased at the same time. Upgraded pizzas, burgers and chicken sandwiches trimmed the average check decline to almost zero, food inflation slowed from 5% to 2%, and $28 million of debt repayments lowered net debt to about $3 million. One caution: remodeling write-offs and higher depreciation still held reported operating margin to 1.5%, and one of two planned store openings slipped into early 2027.

The question now is whether the surge in foot traffic is a lasting market-share gain or promotional trial that will fade when comparisons get hard in 2027. If diners are coming back for the upgraded core menu, average check will turn positive and fourth-quarter profit will beat the cautious implied plan; if they only want discount meal deals, check growth will stall. Fourth-quarter check and traffic numbers in February will tell.

Full article with charts - link in bio

🐂 𝐁𝐮𝐥𝐥 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🟢🟢 𝐓𝐫𝐚𝐟𝐟𝐢𝐜 𝐆𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐭𝐡 𝐇𝐞𝐥𝐝 𝐀𝐛𝐨𝐯𝐞 𝟖% 𝐀𝐜𝐫𝐨𝐬𝐬 𝐀𝐥𝐥 𝐒𝐡𝐢𝐟𝐭𝐬
"The third quarter marked our ninth consecutive quarter of sales and traffic growth, with both comparable restaurant sales and traffic up approximately 8%," chief executive Lyle Tick said. BJ's Restaurants runs 219 casual dining brewhouses known for deep-dish pizza, craft beer and its Pizookie cookie-skillet dessert. Sales at restaurants open at least 18 months rose 8.1% from a year ago because guest traffic climbed 8.3%.

Finance chief Todd Wilson said those gains appeared across every day of the week, shift and dining area. Casual dining chains as a group are losing foot traffic, yet the California-based chain beat the Black Box industry traffic benchmark by more than 8 percentage points. Tick credited the Pizookie Meal Deal value offer, seasonal Biscoff and Nutella desserts, and social media marketing for bringing diners back.

What to watch: fourth-quarter guest traffic against the industry benchmark when full-year results arrive in February. Beating the industry again during the holiday season would show that new guests are turning into regulars rather than just chasing promotions.

🟢 𝐌𝐞𝐧𝐮 𝐔𝐩𝐠𝐫𝐚𝐝𝐞𝐬 𝐍𝐞𝐚𝐫𝐥𝐲 𝐒𝐭𝐨𝐩𝐩𝐞𝐝 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐃𝐫𝐨𝐩 𝐢𝐧 𝐒𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐏𝐞𝐫 𝐆𝐮𝐞𝐬𝐭
A persistent worry over the past year was that the brewhouse chain had to discount heavily to fill seats, pushing the average bill down 1.8% last quarter. Tick plans to "advance menu innovation that re-enforces compelling value and drives seasonal excitement" while nudging diners toward higher-priced dishes. To do that, the restaurant group spent over $1.5 million upgrading the ingredients in its pizzas, burgers and chicken sandwiches.

The average check slipped just 0.2% from a year ago in the third quarter. Wilson noted that diners ordered more of the revamped pizzas, burgers and chicken sandwiches, which carry higher prices and better dollar profit, while orders of pricier steaks and slow-roast dishes stopped falling. For the fourth quarter, BJ's is testing a 16-ounce Hawaiian ribeye and truffle mac and cheese across all locations.

What to watch: average check growth in the fourth quarter, which Wilson previously said should turn positive. A positive reading would confirm that upgraded menu items can offset the lower-priced Pizookie Meal Deal.

🟢🟢 𝐄𝐚𝐬𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐅𝐨𝐨𝐝 𝐈𝐧𝐟𝐥𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐁𝐮𝐬𝐲 𝐃𝐢𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐑𝐨𝐨𝐦𝐬 𝐋𝐢𝐟𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐌𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐢𝐧𝐬
Restaurant-level operating margin — profit at the restaurants before corporate overhead and depreciation — rose 2.2 percentage points from a year ago to 14.7%. That pushed restaurant-level profit up 27.9% to $52.9 million, while earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization excluding one-offs (Adjusted EBITDA) rose 48.6% to $31.4 million. All three restaurant cost lines fell as a share of sales.

• Cost of sales (food and beverage ingredients): 25.3% of revenue, down 0.4 percentage points as food inflation slowed to 2% from 5% last quarter
• Labor and benefits (restaurant wages and staff costs): 36.2% of revenue, down 0.9 percentage points on better scheduling and fewer discounts
• Occupancy and operating (rent, utilities and restaurant supplies): 23.8% of revenue, down 0.9 percentage points as higher sales spread over fixed rent

What to watch: fourth-quarter cost of sales as a percentage of revenue. Holding near 25.3% while holiday ribeye promotions run would show that beef costs are staying under control.

🟢 𝐍𝐞𝐭 𝐃𝐞𝐛𝐭 𝐃𝐫𝐨𝐩𝐩𝐞𝐝 𝐭𝐨 $𝟑 𝐌𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐚𝐬 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐡 𝐖𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐭𝐨 𝐋𝐨𝐚𝐧𝐬
Over the past year, BJ's shifted its cash from buying back stock to paying off bank loans. In 2025, the casual dining chain spent $67.8 million retiring 2 million shares when the business was early in its recovery. This year, Wilson and Tick prioritized the balance sheet and restaurant remodels instead.

The company paid down $28 million of debt during the third quarter, cutting total debt to $16.0 million from $85.0 million at the end of 2025. With $12.9 million in cash on hand, net debt sits at $3.1 million by our math (or about $4 million as cited on the call). That cut quarterly net interest expense to $0.4 million from $1.2 million a year ago, while share buybacks totaled $1.0 million.

What to watch: fourth-quarter share repurchases against the $84.5 million remaining authorization. With debt nearly gone and $1.6 million already spent on buybacks early in the fourth quarter, cash is freed up to return to shareholders.

🐻 𝐁𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🔴🔴 𝐑𝐞𝐦𝐨𝐝𝐞𝐥𝐬 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐖𝐫𝐢𝐭𝐞-𝐎𝐟𝐟𝐬 𝐒𝐭𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐖𝐞𝐢𝐠𝐡 𝐨𝐧 𝐑𝐞𝐩𝐨𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐟𝐢𝐭
While management highlights restaurant-level margin at 14.7%, reported operating profit tells a tighter story because of catching up on deferred building maintenance. Reported operating income was $5.2 million, or just 1.5% of revenue. Two below-the-restaurant cost lines continue to absorb much of the dining-room gains as the chain remodels older locations.

• Depreciation and amortization (spreading build-out costs over time): $21.1 million, up 9.2% from a year ago
• Loss on disposal and impairment of assets (writing off old equipment during remodels): $2.8 million in Q3, up from $0.6 million a year ago, and $5.5 million across the first nine months
• Leadership transition expenses: $82 thousand in Q3 and $764 thousand for the nine months, excluded from profit metrics that strip out one-offs

Because the chain plans to speed up remodels in 2027 after finishing 13 this year, equipment write-offs and higher depreciation are acting like ongoing expenses rather than one-off charges. That keeps a wide gap between reported profit per share ($0.24) and profit per share excluding one-offs ($0.33).

What to watch: fourth-quarter asset write-offs and 2027 capital spending plans. Another quarter of multi-million-dollar write-offs would show that keeping the 219-store fleet fresh costs more in reported profit than restaurant margins suggest.

🔴 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐑𝐚𝐢𝐬𝐞𝐝 𝐏𝐥𝐚𝐧 𝐒𝐭𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐏𝐨𝐢𝐧𝐭𝐬 𝐭𝐨 𝐚 𝐒𝐥𝐨𝐰 𝐅𝐨𝐮𝐫𝐭𝐡 𝐐𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫
BJ's raised its full-year sales and profit targets, yet Wilson said the increase mostly reflects third-quarter results flowing through rather than a higher view of the fourth quarter. Wilson also noted that calendar shifts for Halloween and Christmas will trim fourth-quarter comparable sales by about 1 percentage point.

By our math, raising the full-year comparable sales target to 4.7% after a 5.6% gain in the first nine months leaves about 2.0% growth for the fourth quarter. Similarly, the middle of the full-year outlook implies fourth-quarter restaurant-level profit of $58.1 million (up 1.6% from a year ago) and Adjusted EBITDA of $36.5 million (up 2.7%). That is a sharp slowdown from the third quarter's 48.6% profit jump.

What to watch: fourth-quarter comparable sales against the implied 2.0% pace. Because management's mid-year outlook proved overly cautious by more than 5 percentage points in the third quarter, the fourth quarter will show whether the holiday slowdown is real or another conservative target.

🔴 𝐀 𝐃𝐞𝐥𝐚𝐲𝐞𝐝 𝐎𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐒𝐡𝐨𝐰𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐑𝐢𝐬𝐤 𝐢𝐧 𝐑𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐒𝐭𝐨𝐫𝐞 𝐆𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐭𝐡
Part of the bull case is that BJ's has fixed its daily operations and can now grow by opening new restaurants again. The restaurant count has sat at 219 for a full year, and management previously planned to open two new locations — in Joliet, Illinois, and Buckeye, Arizona — during the fourth quarter of 2026.

On the call, management said Joliet will still open in the fourth quarter, but Buckeye has slipped into the first quarter of 2027. At the same time, the company cut its 2026 capital spending plan to about $80 million from $85 million to $95 million. Tick told investors to think of four or five openings in 2027, warning that permitting and construction can shift dates.

What to watch: the formal 2027 store-opening and capital spending plan next quarter. Slipping from two openings to one in late 2026 shows how easily construction delays can slow the return to unit expansion.

🔴 𝐑𝐢𝐬𝐤𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐪𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐝𝐢𝐝𝐧'𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐬𝐰𝐞𝐫
Three standing concerns from prior quarters received no new figures in the third-quarter release or call summary, leaving them unresolved.

• Takeout and delivery sales: formerly about 17% of revenue and a stated 2026 priority after shrinking in 2025, unquantified for a second straight quarter; annual filing disclosures will test whether off-premise orders recovered.
• Alcohol sales mix: craft beer is a core brand feature that had been declining as a share of orders, with no incidence figure given; any update on beverage attachment would show if diners are still skipping drinks.
• Next year's difficult comparisons: in 2027 the chain must lap this year's 6.5% second-quarter and 8.1% third-quarter sales gains; initial 2027 outlook next quarter will show how much slowdown management expects.

— • — • —

💲 𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐊𝐏𝐈𝐬

𝐆𝐞𝐧𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐥 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐚𝐝𝐦𝐢𝐧𝐢𝐬𝐭𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐯𝐞 𝐞𝐱𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐬𝐞𝐬 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟐𝟑.𝟕 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇒ stable
Corporate overhead rose 5.6% from a year ago, slower than the 8.6% rise in revenue. As a result, general and administrative costs fell to 6.6% of sales from 6.8% a year ago and 6.8% in the second quarter, helping operating income turn positive.

𝐃𝐢𝐥𝐮𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐬𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐞 𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐭 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): 𝟐𝟐.𝟓𝟖 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇒ stable
Weighted average diluted shares ticked up 0.4% from 22.48 million a year ago and rose from 21.89 million in the second quarter. Because the brewhouse operator directed its cash toward paying off debt and bought back only 17,000 shares, share count reductions stopped boosting per-share profit this quarter.

𝐑𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐮𝐫𝐚𝐧𝐭𝐬 𝐨𝐩𝐞𝐧 𝐚𝐭 𝐩𝐞𝐫𝐢𝐨𝐝-𝐞𝐧𝐝 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): 𝟐𝟏𝟗  ⇒ stable
Unchanged from a year ago and flat across the past four quarters, with 2,847 operating weeks in both third quarters. With no net new openings over the past year, almost all of the company's 8.6% revenue growth came from higher guest traffic at existing locations.

— • — • —

🔮 𝐆𝐮𝐢𝐝𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐂𝐨𝐦𝐩𝐚𝐫𝐚𝐛𝐥𝐞 𝐑𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐮𝐫𝐚𝐧𝐭 𝐒𝐚𝐥𝐞𝐬: 𝐀𝐩𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐱𝐢𝐦𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐥𝐲 𝟒.𝟕%  ⇘ decelerating
🠅 raised from 3.0% to 4.0%
Raised. Management lifted its full-year comparable sales target by 1.2 percentage points from the middle of the prior range. It is the second raise this year (+1.5 points in Q2, +1.2 points in Q3). By our math, after 5.6% growth across the first nine months, the 4.7% full-year plan leaves about 2.0% growth for the fourth quarter, which includes a 1-point calendar drag from Halloween and Christmas.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐑𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐮𝐫𝐚𝐧𝐭 𝐋𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐥 𝐎𝐩𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐟𝐢𝐭: $𝟐𝟑𝟑–𝟐𝟑𝟕 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
🠅 raised from $228–235 million
Raised. The middle of the range moved up $3.5 million to $235.0 million, or 8.7% growth over 2025, following a $4.5 million raise last quarter. With $176.9 million already earned in the first nine months, the middle of the plan leaves $58.1 million for the fourth quarter by our math — just 1.6% above last year's fourth quarter, down from 27.9% growth in Q3.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐀𝐝𝐣𝐮𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐄𝐁𝐈𝐓𝐃𝐀: $𝟏𝟒𝟗–𝟏𝟓𝟒 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
🠅 raised from $145–152 million
Raised. The middle of the range rose $3.0 million to $151.5 million (up 13.0% for the year), after a $3.5 million raise in Q2. Because third-quarter Adjusted EBITDA jumped $10.3 million from a year ago, the raise Passes through only part of Q3's strength and leaves $36.5 million for Q4 by our math, or 2.7% growth.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐂𝐚𝐩𝐢𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝐄𝐱𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐞𝐬: 𝐀𝐩𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐱𝐢𝐦𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐥𝐲 $𝟖𝟎 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇒ stable
🠇 cut from $85–95 million
Cut. After holding the budget at $85 million to $95 million for three quarters, the chain lowered full-year capital spending by $10 million at the middle of the range as the Buckeye, Arizona restaurant opening moved into early 2027. With $59.0 million spent through nine months by our math, that leaves about $21.0 million for the fourth quarter.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐒𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐞 𝐑𝐞𝐩𝐮𝐫𝐜𝐡𝐚𝐬𝐞𝐬: 𝐔𝐩 𝐭𝐨 $𝟓𝟎 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇒ stable
🠆 unchanged from Up to $50 million
Unchanged. The ceiling stays at $50 million depending on market conditions, though actual spending is running far below it. The restaurant group has spent about $9 million on buybacks through the first three quarters and another $1.6 million early in the fourth quarter, having used its cash to pay off $69 million of debt instead.

— • — • —

❓ 𝐊𝐞𝐲 𝐐𝐮𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬

𝐖𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐰𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐜𝐚𝐩𝐢𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝐬𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐝𝐞𝐩𝐫𝐞𝐜𝐢𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐥𝐨𝐨𝐤 𝐥𝐢𝐤𝐞 𝐢𝐧 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟕?
Management plans to speed up restaurant remodels and open four or five new locations in 2027. Investors need to know when equipment write-offs ($5.5 million year to date) and rising depreciation will level off so reported profit can catch up with restaurant-level profit.

𝐖𝐡𝐲 𝐝𝐨𝐞𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐟𝐨𝐮𝐫𝐭𝐡-𝐪𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐨𝐮𝐭𝐥𝐨𝐨𝐤 𝐢𝐦𝐩𝐥𝐲 𝐚𝐥𝐦𝐨𝐬𝐭 𝐟𝐥𝐚𝐭 𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐟𝐢𝐭?
By our math, the full-year outlook leaves fourth-quarter Adjusted EBITDA up just 2.7% after jumping 48.6% in the third quarter. Even with a 1-point holiday calendar drag, management did not explain why profit flow-through would slow so sharply if food inflation stays near 2%.

𝐀𝐫𝐞 𝐭𝐚𝐤𝐞𝐨𝐮𝐭, 𝐝𝐞𝐥𝐢𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐲 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐚𝐥𝐜𝐨𝐡𝐨𝐥 𝐨𝐫𝐝𝐞𝐫𝐬 𝐠𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐰𝐢𝐭𝐡 𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐞-𝐢𝐧 𝐭𝐫𝐚𝐟𝐟𝐢𝐜?
Wilson said third-quarter sales and traffic grew across every revenue center, but the company has stopped giving numbers for off-premise orders (previously 17% of sales) and alcohol attachment. Both were multi-quarter drags that management had promised to fix in 2026.

𝐖𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐚𝐫𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐛𝐮𝐢𝐥𝐝 𝐜𝐨𝐬𝐭𝐬 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐬𝐚𝐥𝐞𝐬 𝐭𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐞𝐭𝐬 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐧𝐞𝐰 𝐬𝐭𝐨𝐫𝐞𝐬?
The Joliet, Illinois opening in the fourth quarter and Buckeye, Arizona in the first quarter mark the restart of unit growth. Management has not yet shared how much these newer prototypes cost to build or what yearly sales they need to hit return targets.

text:
Meet Olivier "Livi" Eddington, a 17-year-old from Byron Bay, Australia, who is fighting one of the rarest and most aggressive forms of brain cancer.

In January 2026, Livi woke up with a severe headache and began vomiting. After being rushed to the hospital, doctors discovered a brain tumor approximately the size of a golf ball.

He was diagnosed with Diffuse Hemispheric Glioma, H3 G34-mutant, WHO Grade 4, an extremely aggressive brain cancer that primarily affects teenagers and young adults.This cancer grows rapidly and is incredibly difficult to treat. Research suggests that the median survival for patients with this diagnosis is approximately 18 months, although outcomes vary.

Doctors performed emergency brain surgery, removing approximately 95% of the tumor. Livi then underwent chemotherapy and radiation, but these treatments offered little hope of a long-term cure.

Refusing to give up, his family traveled from Australia to North Carolina, where Livi entered an experimental B7-H3 CAR-T cell therapy trial.This treatment involves genetically modifying his own immune cells to recognize and attack cancer cells in his brain. His family believes he is the first person with his specific tumor type to receive this experimental therapy.Unfortunately, the treatment has come with devastating complications.

Following treatment, Livi suffered multiple seizures and a severe immune reaction. He was admitted to intensive care, placed on life support, and put into a medically induced coma.His condition has severely affected his ability to walk, speak, swallow, and perform basic everyday activities.

Before cancer, Livi was an active teenager who spent his days surfing, hanging out with friends, and enjoying the ocean. Now, even the simplest activities have become incredibly difficult.Despite everything, Livi continues fighting, hoping that one day he can return to the ocean and surf again.

His family is facing enormous medical expenses from experimental treatments, hospital stays, intensive care, and traveling between Australia and the United States.

Every donation goes toward giving Livi the best possible chance at fighting this disease. His fundraiser also states that any money remaining after treatment-related expenses will support brain cancer research.

Please consider donating or sharing his story. No teenager should have to experience something like this.

Official GoFundMe:
https://t.co/P8lU1MdcXs
Keep fighting, Livi. The world is rooting for you. ❤️

Interested in working in Ireland as a skilled professional?

Ireland has an official Critical Skills Employment Permit pathway for qualified foreign workers in occupations experiencing skills shortages.

It includes certain jobs in IT, engineering, healthcare, science, and other professional fields.

Here's how to explore it:
1. Visit https://t.co/2o8uHbYtdK

2. Search for "Critical Skills Occupations List".

3. Check whether your profession and specific specialisation are eligible.

4. Review the qualification and salary requirements. The standard minimum for listed critical-skills roles is approximately €40,900 annually, although other thresholds and exceptions apply.

5. Look for Irish employers recruiting people with your qualifications and experience.

6. You generally need a qualifying job offer lasting at least 2 years from an eligible Irish employer.

7. Once you have an eligible offer, you or your employer can apply for the Critical Skills Employment Permit.

8 If your permit is approved, check whether you also need an entry visa and immigration registration.

One advantage: Eligible Critical Skills permit holders may qualify for permission to work in Ireland without another employment permit after meeting the relevant residence conditions.

After a week at home without my bike, I’m looking forward to getting back out again. My legs will definitely hurt, but my mood loves it! 🥰"

Marianne Vos (Dutch professional cyclist, one of the greatest of all time with numerous world titles across disciplines) posted the message in late October 2026 on Instagram (@mariannevosofficial) and Facebook.

The post reflects a celebratory off-season close after a major title:
The 2026 UCI Gravel World Championships.
The “memorable trip to Western Australia” was the 2026 UCI Gravel World Championships in Nannup (the first held outside Europe), held 10–11 October. Vos won the women’s elite race (125.6 km with significant elevation and mixed surfaces) in 4:30:04. This was her second gravel world title (after 2024 in Leuven) and her 15th UCI world title overall across cyclo-cross, road, track, and gravel—making her the first rider to claim multiple elite gravel titles.
She outsprinted the challenge from Germany’s Rosa Klöser in the finale; Klöser crashed in a corner while chasing and finished 27 seconds back. Fellow Dutch rider Larissa Hartog took bronze. Vos noted the course was muddier and more technical than expected, with strong competition on the climbs.

She then traveled almost immediately to Ibiza, a Spanish island in the Mediterranean Sea off the eastern coast of the Iberian Peninsula. “The Art of Joyriding” is the branding used by LeBlanq (LeBlanq Tours) for the experience of their Joyride Festival. LeBlanq organizes luxury cycling escapes and festivals that pair supported riding with Michelin-level dining, wellness, music, and socializing.

Their philosophy is that “the ultimate victory is living joyfully,” balancing performance and pleasure, riding at your own pace rather than pure competitive intensity, and combining the high of a ride with recovery, food, and community. Joyride Festival Ibiza 2026 ran 15–18 October on the “White Isle.”

It is described as “the greatest celebration of cycling, wellness, food and music on the planet” and a “long weekend of wholesome hedonism” / pure escapism. The festival site centers on Atzaró Agroturismo (with its gardens and setting), with participants staying at hotels such as the Meliá or W Hotel depending on package.

Key elements include:
Riding:
Supported routes for all levels (roughly 30–50 km up to 160 km, including a full-island coastal “Ibiza 160”). Groups are color-coded by pace/terrain (Green to Black), led by experienced ride leaders (with input from local pros).
Participants can bring or hire bikes; pros join groups. Vos highlighted the “beautiful new roads” on the routes.

Wellness:
Yoga, breathwork, meditation, sea swims, hikes, and runs. Eurosport presenter Orla Chennaoui ran her “Ten Times Braver” program.

Food:
Michelin-standard/starred feasts using local produce (including from Atzaró’s vegetable garden), breakfast/lunch/dinner with drinks, Fire Food BBQ events, and dinners under the stars.

Music & Atmosphere:
Evening live music and DJs (Balearic-inspired, Pete Tong has been associated with the broader series as “King of Ibiza”), parties, and a social scene. Participants and stars described a laid-back, high-energy mix of riding, conversation, dancing, and avoiding major hangovers. Pete Tong  is a British DJ, radio presenter, record producer, and music industry figure who is one of the most influential people in electronic dance music over the past three decades.

Headline talent for 2026 included Marianne Vos, Wout van Aert (who used the trip partly as post-Worlds training after Canada and a U.S. West Coast vacation. He logged multi-day rides and a Strava KOM attempt interrupted by a squirrel), Marcel Kittel (with his wife Tess), Johan Museeuw, Dani Rowe, and others.

Guests could ride with the stars; higher packages guaranteed more direct interaction. Van Aert and Kittel also did a stage conversation with Orla Chennaoui.

Packages and pricing (approximate, for 4 days/3 nights including meals, rides or wellness, kit, and talent access):
White (Meliá Ibiza): €3,050.
Celeste (W Hotel): €4,600.
Platinum (intimate Atzaró stay): £5,250. The 2026 edition (15–18 October) was fully sold out. The official product page and booking materials listed it as sold out. It offered the most exclusive experience:
rooms/suites on-site at the 5* Atzaró Agroturismo, private airport transfers, Michelin-standard dining every day (using local produce from Atzaró’s garden), intimate post-dinner talks and drinks with headline talent, fully supported rides with the stars and support vehicles, a full bespoke LeBlanq kit (multiple jerseys, bib shorts, etc.), and the most expansive wellness programme.

LeBlanq has expanded the model to other locations (e.g., Isle of Wight) and opened waitlists for Ibiza 2027 (14–17 October).

Vos’s description aligns closely with the official concept:
Great riding on new roads, good food, strong atmosphere, and excellent company as a distinctive seasonal closer. 

After the festival Vos spent a week at home off the bike and was already eager to resume riding, acknowledging the physical cost but emphasizing the mental boost.
Other attendees (e.g., Kittel) posted similar positive reflections about the cycling, people, food, dancing, and relaxed vibe.
At the time of the post, Vos added another rainbow jersey, while also appearing in media discussing career longevity and retirement considerations. The Ibiza trip fits a pattern of high-profile cyclists mixing recovery, training, and promotional or experiential events in the off-season.

text:
Philippines nears deal to buy more BrahMos missiles – report
Manila is in advanced talks with India to acquire five additional missile systems worth up to $800 million, Reuters reports
Published 6 Nov, 2026 (FULL)
https://t.co/vudKrbuY6I
The Philippines is nearing a deal to buy more BrahMos supersonic cruise missiles from India for up to $800 million as Manila strengthens its coastal defenses, Reuters reported on Thursday.
The proposed purchase includes about five missile systems and nearly 60 missiles, two Indian sources told the news agency. The negotiations are reported to be in their final stages.
The Philippines became the first foreign buyer of BrahMos in 2022, signing a $375 million contract with India for three shore-based anti-ship missile batteries. India began deliveries in April 2024 and is nearing completion of the original agreement.
The missile was jointly developed by India’s Defense Research and Development Organization and Russia’s NPO Mashinostroyeniya and is manufactured in India. It can be launched from land, sea, and air platforms.
The Philippines has submitted a list of requested modifications to the Indian authorities, Philippines Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro said at the Delhi Defense Dialogue on Wednesday.
“We hope to increase the number of BrahMos units we have,” he said, adding that Manila wants the system tailored to the country’s operating conditions. The limited road and bridge infrastructure and lack of an active rail network pose challenges in transporting heavy military equipment, he explained.
Teodoro said Manila has also identified India as a “very important potential partner” for its military’s satellite program and air defense systems, and offered its territory to India to test satellite technologies
Philippines Defense Ministry spokesperson Arsenio Andolong confirmed that President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. wants to acquire more BrahMos missiles. Manila has been modernizing its armed forces and strengthening coastal defenses amid territorial disputes with China in the South China Sea.
The Philippines expressed interest in more BrahMos missiles during Marcos’ visit to India in August last year. The two countries also elevated their relations to a strategic partnership during the visit, agreeing to expand defense and maritime security cooperation.
India has expanded BrahMos sales to other Southeast Asian countries, with an agreement to supply the missiles to Indonesia announced in July. Indian Defense Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh confirmed in May that a deal with Vietnam had been signed.

text:
Born in 1976 in Lunga Lunga, a self-styled Kenyan doomsday preacher Paul Nthenge Mackenzie, grew up in rural Kwale County, Kenya. After completing his secondary school education, he moved to Mombasa, where he initially sold flour out of a handcart and worked various odd jobs. 

In the late 1990s, Mackenzie moved to the coastal town of Malindi and worked as a taxi driver. Fellow drivers from that period noted that he didn't initially even know how to drive, learning the skill on his sister's car with the help of a hired instructor.

Mackenzie grew up in the Africa Brotherhood Church, where he was a teenage choirmaster and Sunday school teacher. By 2002, he left after a dispute with church leadership and briefly joined a Baptist congregation.

In 2003, he teamed up with a local woman named Ruth Kahindi and officially establish the Good News International Church in Malindi. 

Paul Mackenzie and Ruth Kahindi met at a Baptist church in Malindi. Impressed by his oratorical skills, Ruth invited him to preach at her home. Together, they officially co-founded the Good News International Church (initially called House of the Lord). 

In the beginning, it operated as a completely conventional evangelical church. According to Ruth’s daughter, Naomi, Mackenzie preached normal salvation through faith, cross-examined standard biblical scriptures, and offered traditional hope.

While the local flock loved his charisma, a standard gospel in a highly saturated religious environment meant low cash flow, a lack of mass-scale followers, and faced tough competition from well established churches.

Mackenzie realized what many modern cult leaders discover: traditional messages of hope face steep competition, but fear, apocalyptic urgency, and anti-system conspiracy theories create absolute dependency.

Fear drives people to surrender their autonomy and assets. If the world is ending tomorrow, you don't need your bank account, your land title deed, or your property—you give it to the "man of God" who is preparing your passage to heaven.

By 2008, Mackenzie completely pivoted his doctrinal model. He returned from a trip to Mombasa with an altered ideology. He began aggressively preaching that formal education was satanic, modern hospitals/medicine were evil, and government infrastructure was the "Mark of the Beast".

Ruth Kahindi recognized this as dangerous brainwashing designed to exploit vulnerable followers. She actively confronted him and tried to talk him out of it, warning him that forbidding medical care and demanding people's property under the guise of an imminent apocalypse was wrong.

Instead of listening, Mackenzie weaponized the congregation against her. He accused Ruth of witchcraft and embezzling church funds to ruin her reputation among the flock. Realizing she was fighting a losing battle against a man she described as a "stubborn boy," Ruth was effectively pushed out and left the church entirely to him.

Without Ruth there to question him, he transformed a struggling local church into a highly centralized, expanding cult machine.

Mackenzie didn't just push Ruth out; he actively stripped her of her legacy by recruiting her own family members into his inner circle. 

Ruth’s son-in-law, Smart Deri Mwakalama, completely abandoned her side and aligned with Mackenzie. Mwakalama rose through the ranks during these transition years to become the official Church Secretary and, eventually, Mackenzie’s ruthless head of security and second-in-command. 

During the 2008–2015 window, Mackenzie proved that his new radical, anti-establishment message was highly marketable, and profitable. He shifted from a single location in Malindi to a multi-branch operation across the country, and established thriving new branches in major urban and rural hubs.

By planting these branches, he secured a steady, diversified stream of tithes and offerings from thousands of new followers nationwide, moving away from his early financial struggles.
