text:
ADDENDUM | An important methodological observation from Professor Jeffrey Morris

Following my assessment of the Florida Pfizer–Moderna mortality study, Professor Jeffrey Morris offered several valuable observations that deserve further attention.

He had raised related concerns when the study first appeared as a preprint in 2025.

His central point concerns the investigators’ use of negative-control outcomes to assess residual confounding.

A negative-control outcome should satisfy two important criteria:

The exposure should have no plausible causal effect on that outcome.
The outcome should share the relevant confounding structure of the primary outcome.

The second requirement is especially important here.

The Florida researchers used outcomes including homicide and suicide. But these are unlikely to reflect the same confounding structure as all-cause, cardiovascular, or COVID-19 mortality.

Why?

Because the most consequential unmeasured differences between the Pfizer and Moderna groups may involve frailty, chronic disease, and other medical comorbidities.

These are powerful predictors of mortality but are not necessarily positively associated with homicide or suicide.

Consequently, finding little difference in those negative-control outcomes would provide limited reassurance that the groups were adequately balanced on the clinical characteristics most relevant to the study’s principal findings.

Even so, one of their negative-control analyses—homicide/suicide mortality—produced an odds ratio of approximately 1.22.

Although not statistically significant, the point estimate is suggestive of possible imbalance, even for a negative control poorly suited to detecting the principal confounders of concern.

It certainly does not establish that meaningful residual confounding has been excluded.

This is an important limitation when interpreting the mortality associations as causal.

text:
Thanks for linking.

I have already critically assessed a previous version of this paper and highlighted several key issues, particularly inadequate adjustment for medical comorbidities and other important mortality-related confounders, limitations of the negative-control and sensitivity analyses, and the inability to infer vaccine-related harm simply from differences between two vaccinated groups.

The revised paper makes some meaningful improvements, including starting follow-up at the first dose, adding negative controls, and conducting additional sensitivity analyses.

However, the central concerns remain. The authors still cannot adequately account for major individual-level mortality risk factors, including comorbidities, frailty, and healthcare utilization. Their negative controls and sensitivity analyses do not rule out meaningful residual confounding, especially given the ones they chose are unlikely to share similar confounding structure with the primary analysis, which is a necessary property of an effective negative control analysis (plus one of them showed an effect almost as large as their primary effect, 1.22 vs. 1.34). And differential protection against COVID mortality and post-COVID sequelae could still contribute to the observed differences.

The study legitimately demonstrates an association between vaccine brand and subsequent mortality in a selected matched Florida cohort. It does not establish that these differences are causal, much less that they reflect vaccine-related harm.

An unvaccinated comparator isn't necessary to investigate comparative effects between vaccine brands. But without establishing the effects relative to no vaccination, one cannot conclude that either vaccine increases overall mortality, since both could reduce mortality, but to different degrees.

text:
Get the government out. Completely out. That includes the FDA and the American Medical Association. Phase out Medicaid and Medicare and let insurers produce any products they choose and individuals purchase any they choose. It is called capitalism, and it is what built the greatest healthcare system in the world in the first place. Antibiotics, anesthesia, insulin, the polio vaccine, open heart surgery. Every one of them arrived as a miracle only the rich could reach, and within a generation a working man could afford it. That is what capitalism does with every product it is left alone to make. The price falls toward the cost of production and the thing that once saved only the wealthy ends up on a pharmacy shelf.

What you are calling for profit healthcare has not existed here since 1965. What you are looking at is a mixed economy, and a mixed economy is a system in which the government has no principles and therefore no limits. Each control produces a problem, and the problem is then offered as proof that the market failed and more control is needed.

In 1942 the government froze wages to fight wartime inflation, so employers who needed workers could not offer more pay. They offered health insurance instead, and Washington ruled that the benefit did not count against the freeze and would not be taxed as income. A dollar of coverage was suddenly worth more than a dollar of wages, and within a decade insurance was something you got from your job rather than something you bought. That is why the patient stopped seeing a price. The man receiving the care, the man choosing the plan, and the man paying the bill became three different people, and nobody in that chain has a reason to ask what anything costs.

Medicare in 1965 made the government the largest buyer and put it in the business of dictating what care is worth. The FDA holds a monopoly on the right to sell a medicine. The AMA holds a monopoly on who may practice. A 1986 law compels every hospital to treat whoever walks in and shift the bill to you. And now three quarters of insurer revenue is tax money. There is no profit motive left in that structure to blame. There are men responding to the incentives a legislature wrote.

Medicine is a product of the human mind. It exists because particular men chose to study, to invent, to build, and to risk their own capital doing it. To call it a right is to claim those men. You can have the medicine men produce when they are free, or you can have the medicine men produce when they are commanded, and the record of the second is the queue.

Nobody is asking you to take capitalism on faith. Compare the fields where the government left medicine alone. Lasik and cosmetic surgery got cheaper and better every year while everything the government touched got more expensive and slower. That is what a price does when the buyer is the one paying it.

The fix is not a better plan. It is removing the premise that anyone has the right to plan another man's care, or another man's life.

Key Event: Plans for a CAIR Office in Tennessee

On or around November 7, 2025, CAIR held an event at the Memphis Islamic Center (10299 Humphrey Road, Cordova, TN): “CAIR: Memphis Protect Yourself, Your Family, Your Community.” 

https://t.co/jsOcF74Ty8

Speakers included Gadeir Abbas (CAIR’s Lead Attorney), Ayman Aishat (CAIR’s Director of Masjid Engagement), and Tayyab Yunus (CAIR’s Development Director).

The program featured a Jummah khutbah and an evening legal forum. Registration and promotional materials explicitly stated it would “introduce the vision for establishing a CAIR Office in Tennessee, marking a new chapter in statewide legal and civic advocacy.”

An Instagram post from the Memphis Islamic Center (around November 6, 2025) described the visit as beginning “to lay the groundwork for a permanent CAIR office in Tennessee — one that offers legal protection, advocacy, and a future where our children can rise beyond any obstacle,” linking it to broader themes of community empowerment (and referencing Zohran Mamdani’s election in New York as an example of representation). 

https://t.co/WF4jAsDHrf

🟨 OUR ASSESSMENT: States that welcome AI development are effectively competing for a new generation of industrial investment, not just technology jobs. Data centers, power generation, transmission upgrades, chip manufacturing, and construction spending tend to arrive together, creating economic effects that reach far beyond software companies.

The constraint is energy. Many regions can offer tax incentives, but far fewer can provide abundant electricity, land, and permitting speed at the scale AI companies now require. That shifts bargaining power toward states able to expand infrastructure quickly.

Political arguments about AI often focus on regulation and risk, yet investment decisions are increasingly being made around practical questions of power supply and project approval. The states that solve those bottlenecks first will have stronger leverage when competing for future AI facilities, long after the initial announcements and ribbon-cutting ceremonies are finished.

🔴Trump Weighs Renewed Strikes on Iran as Tehran Sends Nuclear Proposal via Qatar

📍WASHINGTON, Nov. 6, 2026 (HewadPress) — President Donald Trump met with his national security team this week to weigh whether to resume large-scale military operations against Iran, as Tehran sent Washington a nuclear proposal through Qatar in a renewed diplomatic effort to end the war. 

Senior officials told Fox News that White House meetings took place Wednesday and Thursday. U.S. Central Command was completing preparations for possible renewed strikes and had yet to receive an order to proceed, Axios reported Thursday, citing a U.S. official. 

Speaking in the Oval Office on Thursday, Trump said he would decide soon whether further strikes were needed to prevent Iran from rebuilding its nuclear program. “I would rather not destroy the rest of the country if possible, but maybe I will have to,” he told reporters. Officials cited by Fox News said the Nov. 9 new moon could offer favorable conditions for nighttime operations. Trump gave no timetable for a strike. 

Qatar relays Iran’s proposal

A senior Iranian official told Reuters that Washington was reviewing the proposal, but that Tehran would discuss it only after the United States met seven demands. Those include lifting U.S. sanctions, releasing frozen Iranian assets and paying war reparations. Washington has said Iran’s nuclear program must be addressed at the start of any negotiations. 

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi spoke Thursday with officials from Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Turkey, the United Arab Emirates, Oman and Egypt. In Moscow, Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei met Russian President Vladimir Putin and delivered a message from Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei. Rezaei said Tehran would keep the Strait of Hormuz closed and hold off on negotiations until Washington met its conditions. 

Fighting continues around Hormuz

U.S. forces carried out limited strikes near the strait on Monday after what American officials described as an apparent Iranian attack targeting a U.S. aircraft, CBS News reported. On Thursday, Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said tankers had struck mines in the waterway. The U.K. Maritime Trade Operations agency separately reported that two unidentified projectiles hit a vessel late Wednesday. The reported incidents underscore how dangerous the shipping route remains while mediators try to resolve disputes over the strait and the U.S. blockade of Iranian ports. 

The White House deliberations followed Tuesday’s midterm elections, in which Republicans lost control of Congress. Vice President JD Vance blamed the war for his party’s losses, while Trump defended the decision to launch the February offensive alongside Israel, saying it was necessary to prevent Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon.

text:
Work on Well Done Good and Faithful Servant is going great, but the following information from this morning's Bible Study is just something I felt moved to share: 
From an earthly, geo-political perspective, the events of 1 Kings 12–14 mark the exact point of structural failure. Under David and Solomon, the Abrahamic land promise appeared to reach its physical zenith: the borders stretched from the Euphrates to the river of Egypt (1 Kings 4:21), gold was as common as stone, and the tribes dwelt in safety "every man under his vine and under his fig tree" (1 Kings 4:25). To the horizontal observer, the covenant seemed completely fulfilled in physical dirt, stone masonry, and civil sovereignty.
Yet within a single generation, that tangible peak fractured into civil war, rival altars, and foreign plundering. The catastrophic collapse in 1 Kings 12–14 decisively exposed that the physical land and an earthly monarch could never be the ultimate container of the covenant promise.
The Forensic Unraveling of the Physical Shadow
The rupture under Rehoboam and Jeroboam dismantled three primary illusions that had tied the promise strictly to physical geography:
1. The Delusion of Inherent Territorial Security
Israel continually treated the land as an unconditional entitlement rather than a covenantal leasehold. Leviticus 18 and Deuteronomy 28 explicitly warned that the land itself had no loyalty to biological descendants—if they defiled it through idolatry and oppression, the soil would "vomit" them out just as it did the Canaanites.
When Jeroboam planted golden calves at Dan and Bethel, and Rehoboam erected pagan pillars and high places in Judah, the moral title to the physical soil was forfeited. The invasion of Pharaoh Shishak (1 Kings 14:25–26)—stripping the temple treasures only five years after Solomon's death—proved that stone walls and physical borders offered zero insulation against divine judgment.
2. The Failure of Earthly Dynastic Continuity
The Davidic covenant promised a throne established forever (2 Samuel 7:12–16). Yet Rehoboam’s tyrannical folly and Jeroboam’s calculated apostasy demonstrated that fallen human kings, operating within temporal political systems, inevitably turn power into predation. The split shattered the illusion that an earthly king ruling from a temporal city could bring the permanent righteousness required for cosmic rest.
3. The Collapse of the Earthly Sanctuary
Jeroboam proved how easily a physical sanctuary can be politicized, counterfeited, and replaced by human statecraft. If access to God depended on physical geography (walking to Jerusalem), it could be barred by a hostile border guard or replicated by an idol at Bethel. True communion with the Sovereign Creator could not remain anchored to a single mountain or a physical building of cedar and stone.
The Unfolding Clarification: Shadow to Substance
The collapse of the United Monarchy was not a failure of God's promise; it was the divine stripping away of the shadow so the true substance could be discerned. The physical inheritance was always designed as a pedagogical type—an earthly blueprint pointing to a transcendent reality.
The Epistle to the Hebrews exposes that even the patriarchs who first received the promise knew the physical dirt of Canaan was not the ultimate destination:
"By faith he dwelt in the land of promise as in a foreign country, dwelling in tents with Isaac and Jacob, the heirs with him of the same promise; for he waited for the city which has foundations, whose builder and maker is God... But now they desire a better, that is, a heavenly country. Therefore God is not ashamed to be called their God, for He has prepared a city for them." (Hebrews 11:9–10, 16)
Abraham stood on the very hills of Canaan and recognized that he was still a stranger and a pilgrim. He looked beyond the soil under his sandals to an unshakable city with eternal foundations.
When 1 Kings 12–14 shattered the earthly kingdom, it forced the prophets—and ultimately the faithful remnant—to look up:
The Prophetic Trajectory: As the physical kingdoms marched toward exile (Assyria in 722 BC, Babylon in 586 BC), prophets like Isaiah, Jeremiah, and Ezekiel stopped looking for a mere border restoration. They began prophesying a New Covenant written on the heart (Jeremiah 31), an eternal Davidic Branch whose government would have no end (Isaiah 9), and a cosmic renewal where the wolf and the lamb feed together (Isaiah 65).
Christ’s Judicial Declaration: When Christ stood before Pilate, He delivered the definitive verdict on the nature of the realm: "My kingdom is not of this world. If My kingdom were of this world, My servants would fight... but now My kingdom is not from here" (John 18:36). To the Samaritan woman debating whether God must be worshiped on Mount Gerizim or Mount Zion (the very boundary dispute Jeroboam weaponized), Jesus declared: "The hour is coming when you will neither on this mountain, nor in Jerusalem, worship the Father... God is Spirit, and those who worship Him must worship in spirit and truth" (John 4:21, 24).
The Cosmic Inheritance: The apostolic record expands the territorial promise from a narrow strip in the Levant to the entire redeemed cosmos. Paul writes in Romans 4:13 that the promise to Abraham was that he would be the "heir of the world" (kosmos). The land was merely the down payment; the resurrected saints inherit the New Heavens and the New Earth (Revelation 21:1–5).
The Lesson for the Seeker
First Kings 12–14 serves as a monumental historic warning against territorial and institutional idolatry.
Whenever God’s people attempt to capture the Kingdom of God inside an earthly nation, a political party, a physical plot of ground, or a human institution, it will inevitably end in the same tragedy: division, syncretism, and the replacement of gold with hollow bronze.
The crumbling of the physical kingdom in 1 Kings did not extinguish the promise; it shattered the earthly husk so that the eyes of faith could behold the true, indestructible, heavenly Kingdom that cannot be shaken (Hebrews 12:28).

The modern obsession with a physical, geopolitical "Greater Israel" represents a profound regression from biblical revelation back into the very shadow that fractured and collapsed in 1 Kings 12–14. It is the theological equivalent of looking at the torn veil of the temple, the empty tomb, and the cosmic inheritance promised in Christ, and demanding instead a return to border checkpoints, real estate deeds, and the blood of bulls and goats.
This deception persists because it caters directly to the fallen human instinct for visible, horizontal power. It exchanges the sweeping cosmic reality of the New Covenant for ethnic nationalism and political statecraft, confounding multitudes into confusing a secular geopolitical entity with the heavenly kingdom of God.
The Forensic Anatomy of the Deception
To understand why this error continues to mislead so many, several critical theological inversions must be dissected:
1. Inverting Shadow and Substance
The entire canonical trajectory—from the Pentateuch through the Prophets, Gospels, and Epistles—demonstrates that the Old Covenant economy operated in types and shadows. The land of Canaan, the temple in Jerusalem, the Levitical priesthood, and the Davidic throne were pedagogical tools designed to point toward a transcendent, universal reality.
The Land as Down Payment: Canaan was never the ultimate end; it was an earthly demonstration plot. The apostolic interpretation in the New Testament makes this explicit: the promise to Abraham was that he would inherit the entire cosmos, not merely a sliver of Middle Eastern soil.
The Error of Regression: To insist on an ultimate physical restoration of an earthly empire between the Nile and the Euphrates is to treat the architectural blueprint as more valuable than the finished cathedral. It is a catastrophic regression in redemptive history—demanding the shadow back after the substance has already arrived in Christ.
2. Re-Erecting the Dividing Wall (The Judaizing Heresy)
The central achievement of the Cross, as articulated in apostolic jurisprudence, was the absolute dismantling of the ethnic boundary marker:
The wall of separation between Jew and Gentile was legally abolished in the flesh of Christ, creating "one new man from the two, thus making peace" (Ephesians 2:14–15).
Physical lineage according to the flesh (kata sarka) confers zero spiritual equity or covenant standing. Paul settled the title deed to the covenant with surgical precision: true descendants of Abraham are defined strictly by union with Christ through faith, entirely independent of genealogy or geography (Galatians 3:7, 28–29).
The doctrine of "Greater Israel" rebuilds the exact partition wall that Christ destroyed. It reintroduces a two-tier covenant economy where biological pedigree and geographic borders trump the universal, blood-bought commonwealth of the saints.
3. Conflating the Secular Sword with the Holy Seed
Perhaps the most dangerous manifestation of this deception is the uncritical baptizing of modern secular statecraft.
When religious groups conflate an unregenerate, secular political government—operating with conventional military weaponry, international intelligence apparatuses, and geopolitical alliances—with the biblical covenant people of God, they commit the exact sin of Jeroboam and Rehoboam:
They make religion an instrument of national defense and territorial conquest.
They view military dominance and borders as signs of divine favor, ignoring whether the society itself lives in repentance, justice, and obedience to the moral law of God.
They fall into the trap of looking to an earthly capital for salvation rather than the New Jerusalem that descends from above.
The Hermeneutical Sleight of Hand
The theology fueling the "Greater Israel" narrative relies on a wooden, compartmentalized reading of the Old Testament prophets that systematically ignores how the Apostles themselves interpreted those very passages.
The Rebuilding of the Ruins: When the prophets spoke of rebuilding the fallen booth of David and gathering the dispersed, modern dispensational frameworks apply this strictly to twentieth- and twenty-first-century geopolitical migration. Yet in Acts 15:13–18, James stood before the Jerusalem Council and declared under the inspiration of the Holy Spirit that Amos's prophecy was fulfilled in the gathering of Gentiles into the resurrected body of Christ.
The New Mount Zion: The author of Hebrews does not tell the covenant people to look toward an earthly city under siege. He declares a present, spiritual reality: believers have already arrived at Mount Zion, the heavenly Jerusalem, the city of the living God, and the assembly of the firstborn enrolled in heaven (Hebrews 12:22–24).
The Universal Dominion: Christ’s Great Commission commanded His followers to go into all the world and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them and teaching them all that He commanded. His reign expands through the preaching of the gospel and the transformation of human hearts, not the military annexation of river basins.
The Pastoral and Spiritual Cost
Why does this matter for the Sentinel and the truth seeker? Because a false eschatology produces corrupted fruit in daily life:
Distorted Priorities: Millions of believers expend massive financial resources, political energy, and emotional loyalty backing foreign real estate ventures and political factions, while neglecting their own households, their local congregations, and the discipleship of their own children.
Hardened Hearts: Geopolitical tribalism forces Christians to justify violence, displacement, and political ruthlessness under the guise of "fulfilling prophecy," completely searing the conscience and extinguishing the very covenant love and mercy demanded by the Law and the Gospel.
A False Hope: It keeps men looking horizontally at troop movements, treaties, and temple blueprints, blinding them to the spiritual warfare taking place right at their own front door.
The collapse in 1 Kings 12–14 stands as a permanent canonical marker: an earthly empire based on soil, borders, and human strength will always succumb to compromise, foreign conquest, and decay. The true heir of Abraham does not fight for a physical corridor in the Levant. He builds with trowel and sword in his own domestic redoubt, keeping his eyes fixed on the city with unshakeable foundations, whose architect and builder is God alone.
Across the apostolic writings, the territorial covenant made to Abraham is not treated as a static, geopolitical land deed restricted to the Levant. Instead, the New Testament interprets the physical borders of Canaan as a provisional down payment and a physical type that expands into a universal, spiritual, and cosmic inheritance fulfilled in Jesus Christ and His people.
1. Romans 4:13 — From a Strip of Land to the Entire Cosmos
In Genesis 15:18 and 17:8, the covenant promise explicitly named the physical territory between the river of Egypt and the Euphrates. Yet when Paul provides the definitive theological interpretation of the Abrahamic covenant, he fundamentally expands the vocabulary:
The Lexical Expansion: Paul states that the promise to Abraham and his offspring was not merely the parcel of Canaan, but that he would be the heir of the world (kosmos).
The Theological Shift: Canaan served as a localized demonstration plot. Under the New Covenant, the geographical boundary markers dissolve; the true territorial horizon of Abraham's inheritance encompasses the entire created order, received through the righteousness of faith rather than legal lineage or border wars.
2. Galatians 3:16, 26–29 — The Single Seed and the Title Deed
In his legal refutation of the Judaizers, Paul tracks the exact chain of title for the covenant inheritance:
The True Offspring: The promises were spoken to Abraham and to his "seed" in the singular—which Paul identifies explicitly as Christ. Physical descent from Abraham does not convey automatic covenant title.
Universal Enfranchisement: Because Christ holds the singular title to the promise, anyone united to Him—whether Jew or Gentile, slave or free—becomes Abraham's true seed and an heir according to the promise.
Dismantling Biological Monopoly: The covenant inheritance is no longer tied to genealogies or regional passports. The heirs are defined by spiritual union with the King, who inherits the ends of the earth as His possession (Psalm 2:8).
3. Hebrews 11:8–16 — The Patriarchs Looking Beyond Canaan
The Epistle to the Hebrews exposes that even the original recipients of the land promise never viewed the soil under their feet as the ultimate destination:
Strangers in the Land: When Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob lived in the promised territory, they lived as foreigners in tents. They understood that physical possession of the dirt did not equate to possessing the ultimate reality of the promise.
The Transcendent Horizon: The author explains that they looked beyond earthly architecture toward a city with permanent foundations designed and built by God. They longed for a superior homeland—a heavenly country.
Typological Design: The physical land was designed to instill a holy longing for an unshakeable, eternal realm rather than becoming an idol of temporal real estate.
4. Hebrews 12:22–24 — The Present Arrival at the True Mount Zion
During the Old Covenant, the presence of God was localized at Mount Sinai and later centered on Mount Zion in Jerusalem. Under the New Covenant, the geographical coordinates are completely transformed:
A Realized Heavenly Assembly: The author informs believers that they have not come to a physical mountain that can be touched, but have already arrived at Mount Zion—the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, accompanied by countless angels and the assembly of the firstborn enrolled in heaven.
Transcendence Over Terrestrial Shrines: Pilgrimage to an earthly hill in the Middle East is superseded. The believer enters the true sanctuary directly through the mediator of the New Covenant, rendering physical temples and geopolitical capitals obsolete as centers of covenant access.
5. Matthew 5:5 — The Meek Inheriting the Earth
Jesus Himself directly universalized the traditional land promise found in Psalm 37:11:
From Canaan to the Globe: Where the Old Testament psalm promised that the humble would inherit the land (eretz, referring to the covenant territory of Israel), Jesus adopts the Greek equivalent (gē) in the Beatitudes to declare that the meek shall inherit the entire earth.
Subversion of Military Conquest: The land is not secured through armed nationalistic campaigns, geopolitical treaties, or ethnic displacement, but is granted to those characterized by cross-bearing humility and dependence upon God.
6. Ephesians 2:11–22 & 3:6 — One New Commonwealth
Paul addresses the deep divide between the circumcision and the uncircumcision, addressing the very mechanisms of covenant citizenship:
Abolition of the Dividing Wall: Christ tore down the hostility that separated Jew from Gentile, nullifying the ceremonial and boundary markers that created an exclusive ethnic enclave.
The New Household: Gentiles who were once excluded from the commonwealth of Israel are no longer aliens; they are fellow citizens with the saints and members of God's household.
The Living Temple: God’s dwelling place is no longer an edifice of limestone in Jerusalem, but a spiritual structure built of living stones—believers from every tribe, tongue, and nation joined together into a holy sanctuary in the Lord.
7. Revelation 21:1–5 & 2 Peter 3:13 — The Cosmic Consummation
The final biblical revelation demonstrates where the trajectory of the Abrahamic land promise ultimately terminates:
Cosmic Renewal: Rather than narrowing history down to a resurrected earthly kingdom governed from a physical city in the Levant, canonical eschatology culminates in the New Heavens and the New Earth (kainē gē).
The Descent of the City: The New Jerusalem descends out of heaven to the redeemed earth. The entire cosmos becomes the sanctuary where God dwells unhindered with His glorified people.
Summary: Shadow vs. Substance
The movement from the Old Covenant shadow to the New Covenant substance is evident across every major covenantal dimension. In terms of geographic scope, the border-limited territory of Canaan served as a provisional demonstration plot, which Romans 4:13 and Matthew 5:5 expand into a cosmic inheritance encompassing the entire earth and the redeemed cosmos. The definition of covenant lineage undergoes an identical transformation: the physical, biological descent from Jacob gives way to spiritual union with Jesus Christ by faith, establishing every believer—regardless of ethnic heritage—as a true heir of Abraham according to Galatians 3:16 and 29.
Similarly, the focus of divine governance shifts from the earthly Jerusalem, an architecture subject to conquest and decay, to the heavenly New Jerusalem celebrated in Hebrews 12:22 and Revelation 21:2. The localized sanctuary of stone on Mount Moriah reaches its ultimate architectural fulfillment in the corporate, living Body of Christ, which Ephesians 2:19–22 identifies as the true habitation of God through the Spirit. Finally, the physical rest of a military ceasefire within temporal borders points forward to the eternal Sabbath and cosmic renewal declared in Hebrews 4:8–11 and 2 Peter 3:13.
The apostolic witness demonstrates that clinging to a physical, nationalistic empire between regional rivers is to prefer the shadow after the light of the substance has dawned. In Christ, the promise to Abraham has broken out of its localized container to redeem the entire world.
The Epistemological Veil: Self-Exaltation and Horizontal Enclosure
The persistent disregard of the New Testament within Rabbinic Judaism is not merely an exegetical dispute; it is a structural necessity to preserve the illusion of biological pedigree and horizontal supremacy.
To admit the apostolic testimony is to confront the judicial verdict of the Cross: that the physical temple was abandoned to desolation (Matthew 23:38), that the genealogical claim to Abrahamic inheritance without faith is bankrupt (John 8:39–44), and that the exclusive wall of ethnic division has been legally dismantled (Ephesians 2:14).
Accepting the New Testament demands the surrender of the very idols of soil, blood, and statecraft that collapsed in 1 Kings 12–14. It requires acknowledging that "chosenness" was never a charter for perpetual tribal exceptionalism, but a temporary pedagogical stewardship (paidagōgos, Galatians 3:24) designed to deliver the Messiah to the world.
By rejecting the New Covenant, the focus remains locked entirely upon the horizontal plane—substituting the cosmic, vertical reign of the resurrected Christ for municipal real estate, geopolitical dominance, and an earthly throne.
As Paul forensically audited in 2 Corinthians 3:14–15, whenever the Old Covenant is read apart from its fulfillment in Christ, a veil remains unlifted over the heart. The rejection of the New Testament is the defensive mechanism by which the shadow is fiercely guarded against the light of the substance, enabling men to boast in physical lineage and temporal borders while remaining blind to the true, heavenly commonwealth of the saints.

Dr. R. Balasubramaniam, Member, NITI Aayog, visited the Krishnaraja Sagara (KRS) Dam in Mandya district, Karnataka, where he held discussions with officials and engineers on dam safety, operation and maintenance, technical manpower and water-use efficiency. Built under the guidance of Sir M. Visvesvaraya and completed in 1932, KRS remains a major source of irrigation and drinking water for the region.

At the Karnataka Engineering Research Station (KERS), established in 1944, he also discussed the institution's work in hydraulics, soil mechanics, dam safety aspects, SCADA for irrigation systems automation and coastal engineering. KERS has built considerable technical expertise through its research and work on projects within and beyond Karnataka. Its experience offers important lessons in engineering and water management that can be studied and adapted in other regions.

Water will be a strategic consideration in India and Karnataka's future sustainable economic growth. Also, planning for these emerging requirements alongside existing demands will call for an integrated, long-term approach to the state's water resources.

#WaterSecurity #SustainableWaterManagement

text:
Boca do Inferno: São Tomé and Príncipe🇸🇹

Located on São Tomé Island in São Tomé and Príncipe, Boca do Inferno, meaning “Mouth of Hell,” is a remarkable natural attraction known for its dramatic coastal scenery. Here, powerful Atlantic Ocean waves rush through openings in volcanic rock formations, creating impressive bursts of water and spectacular sprays.

Surrounded by rugged cliffs, lush tropical vegetation and beautiful ocean views, Boca do Inferno offers visitors a unique opportunity to witness the power of nature. It is one of the island’s fascinating coastal attractions and a memorable destination for anyone exploring the natural beauty of São Tomé and Príncipe.

text:
Below is a list of some national, international, global and local observances for November 6, 2026:

National Basketball Day (also called Basketball Day) celebrates the sport on the birthday of its inventor, James Naismith (born November 6, 1861, in Almonte, Ontario). A Canadian physical-education instructor at the YMCA Training School in Springfield, Massachusetts, he created the game in December 1891 using a soccer ball and two peach baskets nailed to a gymnasium balcony so restless students could exercise indoors without the roughness of football or rugby; the first games were chaotic, and he declined student suggestions to call it “Naismith Ball.”⁠Britannica⁠History

National Nachos Day honors the cheesy, jalapeño-topped tortilla-chip snack that became an American stadium staple, observed every November 6. In 1943 at the Victory Club in Piedras Negras, Mexico (just across the border from Eagle Pass, Texas), maître d’ Ignacio “Nacho” Anaya improvised the original “Nacho’s Special” for hungry U.S. Army wives when the cook was gone, using only available totopos, Colby or cheddar, and pickled jalapeños; the name stuck after they demanded seconds, and the dish later exploded in popularity when sportscaster Howard Cosell raved about concession versions during a 1978 Monday Night Football broadcast.⁠Edexlive⁠NYTimes

National Jersey Friday (or National Jersey Day) falls on the first Friday in November and encourages people to wear a favorite sports jersey to work, school, or around town to show team spirit. Founded by the NFL Players Association and recognized by National Day Calendar in 2016, it taps into the communal energy of fall sports seasons, when fans from youth leagues to professional ranks gather around shared memories, rivalries, and fantasy leagues.⁠Nationaldaycalendar

National Saxophone Day marks the birthday of Belgian instrument maker Adolphe Sax (born November 6, 1814, in Dinant), who invented and patented the saxophone in the 1840s. He survived a series of childhood near-death experiences—including swallowing pins in diluted sulfuric acid (thinking it was milk), falling from a third-story window, and a gunpowder explosion—before creating the brass-bodied, single-reed woodwind that blends the agility of a woodwind with the power of brass and became central to jazz, military bands, and countless other genres.⁠Centerstagemusiccenter

Love Your Lawyer Day is observed on the first Friday in November to appreciate attorneys and the justice system while discouraging lawyer jokes. Created in 2001 by Fort Lauderdale attorney and legal marketer Nader Anise (through the American Lawyers Public Image Association he founded) after he overheard a particularly unkind lawyer joke, it was later recognized by the American Bar Association’s Law Practice Division; lawyers are encouraged to do pro bono work, and the public is asked to offer thanks instead of barbs.⁠Checkiday

Fountain Pen Day falls on the first Friday in November and promotes the pleasure of handwriting with fountain pens in a digital age. Launched in 2012 by enthusiast Cary Yeager after he noticed a National Ballpoint Pen Day but nothing for fountain pens, it grew through the Fountain Pen Network community into a global event featuring sales, meetups, exclusive inks, and shared photos of nibs on paper.⁠Anydayguide

International Day for Preventing the Exploitation of the Environment in War and Armed Conflict is a United Nations observance on November 6 that highlights how warfare damages ecosystems, natural resources, and communities long after fighting ends. Established by the UN General Assembly in 2001, it draws on findings that at least 40 percent of internal conflicts over the previous 60 years were linked to natural resources (timber, oil, water, fertile land), and that such conflicts are twice as likely to relapse.⁠UN

Marooned Without a Compass Day invites reflection on feeling directionless in life, career, or personal goals, using the metaphor of being stranded without navigation tools. Created around 2005 by Mike Anderson as a lighthearted prompt for self-assessment and goal-setting, it encourages people to pause, consider their path, or even try navigating without GPS to rediscover natural cues like the sun, stars, or landmarks.⁠Digitalhygge

National Medical Science Liaison Awareness and Appreciation Day (first Friday in November) recognizes Medical Science Liaisons, the specialized professionals who bridge pharmaceutical companies, healthcare providers, and scientific research by explaining complex treatments and supporting evidence-based patient care. Observed by the Medical Science Liaison Society, it highlights their role in translating medical knowledge into better clinical outcomes.⁠Digitalhygge

Dhanteras (also Dhantrayodashi) marks the start of the Diwali festival season in the Hindu calendar and, in 2026, falls on November 6. Families worship Goddess Lakshmi and Lord Dhanvantari (associated with health and Ayurveda), light lamps at entrances, and traditionally buy gold, silver, or metal utensils for prosperity; the date is set by the Krishna Trayodashi tithi, with evening puja during pradosh kaal.⁠Grahaguru

Gustavus Adolphus Day (Gustav Adolfsdagen) is observed in Sweden on November 6 to commemorate King Gustav II Adolf, who died at the Battle of Lützen in 1632 (Julian calendar date). It is an official flag day featuring the consumption of special Gustavus Adolphus pastries topped with a chocolate or marzipan portrait of the king; the same date is Finnish Swedish Heritage Day (Svenska dagen) in Finland, honoring the Swedish-speaking minority and bilingual heritage.⁠Wikipedia

World Let’s Stop Shouting Day (or World Let’s Stop Shouting Awareness Day) promotes calmer, more respectful communication and raises awareness of how yelling affects mental health and relationships. Founded by Yasmin Shaheen-Zaffar, it encourages empathy, active listening, and alternatives to raised voices.⁠Digitalhygge

National Team Manager Day recognizes the often-unsung people who handle logistics, scheduling, communication, and organization for sports teams, youth groups, and community organizations. Established in 2017 by FlipGive to highlight the behind-the-scenes work that keeps teams running.⁠Digitalhygge

National Report Home Health Care Fraud Day urges the public to report suspected fraud in home health care services, protecting patients and taxpayers. Founded in 2017 by former government attorney Joel D. Hesch to spotlight the issue and encourage vigilance.⁠Digitalhygge

National Ladies Learning Code Day (primarily observed in Canada) supports women and underrepresented groups in building digital skills and closing gender gaps in technology. Started in 2011 by the nonprofit Ladies Learning Code.⁠Digitalhygge

These observances blend widely recognized U.S. food, sports, and music days with first-Friday floating events, a UN awareness day, reflective or professional niche observances, and culturally significant international celebrations that fall on the date.

text:
THE $35M BILL WE COUNTED AT J.B. HUNT $JBHT TOPS $50M:

J.B. Hunt Transport Services (JBHT) at $218.99, -$8.07 / -3.55% on Thursday.

J.B. Hunt passes the Quality Len5 and is still on none of the other Len5es we weigh, and Thursday's close is its lowest since April. Our post put three questions to its September-quarter report, and the October 15 results answered them. Profit landed a penny above J.B. Hunt's range. The cost behind its warning topped $50M, more than we counted, and executives said it runs into 2027. Price barely followed, with revenue per load in intermodal, its rail-container business, up 2% without fuel. Volume set a record, and J.B. Hunt still slowed bookings for lack of drivers. The driver cost fell hardest on the dedicated-fleet business we cited for staying power. A rival reported, Schneider National (SNDR) at $28.24, -$1.57 / -5.27% on Thursday. It raised prices, hauled less and grew its intermodal profit faster. The stock is 5.7% under our post, and J.B. Hunt is investigating a hacking incident.

J.B. Hunt is on none of the Momentum, Quality-Value, Deep-Value and Special-Situations, Hypergrowth or Income Len5es. Quality-Value wants a lasting business at a discount, and J.B. Hunt costs about 31 times its past four quarters' profit. What would put J.B. Hunt on the Quality-Value Len5: 2027 contracts that lift quarterly profit well past June's $1.91 a share while the price stays near here. J.B. Hunt passes the Quality Len5, with $1.12B of debt against $3.63B of owners' equity, the owners' stake on its books. What would knock it off the Quality Len5: debt above that equity.

Profit beat the range by a penny, and the cost came in above the $35M we added up. For the quarter to September 30:
- Profit: $1.82 a share, against the $1.72 to $1.81 the September warning implied and June's $1.91.
- Extra cost against the June quarter: more than $50M, about a fifth of June's operating profit, what the business earns before interest and taxes.
- Group medical claims, its workers' health bills: more than $16M of that.
Brad Delco, the chief financial officer, said on the October 15 call that slightly more than half went to hiring and training drivers. Our $35M added September's driver and fuel figures and had nothing for claims, which the company had not sized. Delco also said "some of these costs will be with us in Q4 as well as into next year." We flagged that risk in our post, and Delco confirmed it.

Price before fuel rose 2%, one point better than in June. Intermodal revenue per load:
- With fuel surcharges, the fee that passes diesel costs to customers: $3,121, +11% from a year earlier.
- Without them: +2%, against +1% in the June quarter.
- New rates: about 10% of volume in the December quarter, then about 30% in each of the next three.
Darren Field, the president of intermodal, said the last round of yearly contract talks brought "low single-digit increases." Of this round he said "we're asking for larger rate increases" and gave no figure.

J.B. Hunt hauled a record number of containers and could not take all the freight offered.
- Intermodal loads: 585,582, +8% from a year earlier, above June's record of 578,072.
Field said J.B. Hunt's own drayage, the short truck trip between rail yard and customer, became a bottleneck, and that "we had to slow down load bookings." He could not remember that happening before.

More than half of the driver hiring cost landed in Dedicated, which runs truck fleets for single customers, Delco said.
- Dedicated operating profit: $81.7M, -22% from a year earlier.
- Kept from each revenue dollar: 8.5 cents, against 12.1 cents a year earlier.
- First nine months of 2026: just under 10 cents.
- Customers kept: about 96%.
We cited Dedicated's 11 straight years of double-digit margins for the lasting half of the Quality-Value test. A twelfth year needs the December quarter back above 10 cents. Brad Hicks, the president of Dedicated, said new accounts will bring "some modest margin pressure."

Schneider, a Green Bay, Wisconsin trucker, also moves containers by rail. In the September quarter it collected about 3% more per order and hauled slightly fewer.
- Intermodal operating profit: +35% at Schneider, +18% at J.B. Hunt.
Jim Filter, Schneider's chief executive, said on its October 29 call that intermodal renewal pricing "reached its strongest level since the pandemic." He does not expect next year's increases to match this year's. Schneider is on none of those five Len5es; at about 35 times the past year's profit, its shares offer the value Len5es no discount.

The stock has trailed the market since our post.
- The day after the report: -2.8%.
- Since our post: -$13.17 / -5.67% from the $232.16 price.
- SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY) at $733.00, -$33.81 / -4.41% on Thursday. Since our post: -4.76%.
J.B. Hunt fell less than the S&P 500 fund on Thursday and has fallen about a point more since our post.

J.B. Hunt is investigating unauthorized access to what it called an isolated part of its technology systems, the Northwest Arkansas Democrat-Gazette reported on October 29. A group calling itself Whitearmor claimed the attack, and at least four proposed class-action suits for current and former workers followed in federal court. J.B. Hunt said service to customers was not disrupted and had not said whether personal data was taken.

J.B. Hunt filled more containers than ever, slowed bookings for lack of drivers, and collected 2% more per load before fuel. Executives say the cost lasts into 2027 and higher prices take part of that year to show. December-quarter results, tentatively January 15, carry the first tenth of the new rates. Field is asking for larger increases in 2027, and Filter does not expect Schneider's to match this year's.

Sony’s $400 PS5 buyback, Wolverine’s 2.4 million sales, Google’s AI rule for schools and more | The Reef Daily 
https://t.co/pjei5hwBZA

PlayStation 5 consoles and DualSense controllers. Image: Sony Interactive Entertainment

Sony wants your PS5 back, and it’s willing to pay up to $400 through a trade-in deal with Back Market, though Clownfish TV thinks eBay will treat you better. The newest episodes also cover Marvel’s Wolverine stalling at 2.4 million copies, a London Harry Potter store protest that drew about 16 people, and Google’s new rule that schools can’t drop its AI without losing Search. Below that, D/REZZED has the Ocarina of Time remake’s near-perfect reviews, plus a few Shorts and the latest podcast episodes.

New Clownfish TV episodes

Why is Sony offering $400 for used PS5s?

Because new consoles keep getting more expensive. Polygon reported that some PS5 owners are getting messages from Sony about a partnership with Back Market, a refurbished-electronics marketplace, that pays up to $400 for a console in good condition that comes with two controllers. Push Square notes that $400 is the ceiling, and the real offer depends on the hardware. Polygon also counted two big PS5 price hikes and three Xbox Series X increases in a single year, and it says refurbished PS5s already sell for $600 to $1,300.

Kneon thinks the math favors eBay. He jokes that Sony could make a few unpopular calls, buy up the cheap consoles people dump, then change its mind. And he points out that a few years ago, $400 was about what a PS5 cost new.

How many copies has Marvel’s Wolverine sold?

2.4 million, as of Nov. 4, in Sony’s own financial update. Push Square reported the number 50 days after the Sept. 15 launch, and the comparisons sting: Spider-Man 2 sold 2.5 million copies in its first 24 hours, and Ghost of Yotei hit 3.3 million in its first month. The game was reportedly about a $300 million production. It was the top-selling U.S. game of September in dollar sales, then fell to 14th on the U.S. PlayStation Store chart in October.

Kneon calls it “a catastrophic failure” for a first-party Marvel game on a console almost 100 million people own. He also blames the game’s reported ties to the consulting firm Sweet Baby Inc., and he expects layoffs at Insomniac.

Did anyone protest the new Harry Potter store in London?

About 16 people did, Variety reported, while the line to get in wrapped around a nearby alley. The flagship store sits on Oxford Street, which is set to switch on Harry Potter themed Christmas lights Nov. 9 as a tie-in with HBO’s upcoming series. Meanwhile, the New York Post reported that the town of Gibsons, British Columbia, apologized for a Halloween display that dressed a statue of its founder in a Gryffindor robe.

Kneon and Geeky Sparkles think the fight is over and Harry Potter won. Their advice to critics is simple: don’t like it, don’t buy it. They also think the pressure campaigns push regular fans the other way.

Can schools turn off Google’s AI?

Only if they give up Google Search too. The Verge, citing The New York Times, reported that Gemini, NotebookLM and Google Search will be off by default for K-12 student accounts, and administrators who turn them on can’t keep Search while leaving the Gemini features off. Google’s vice president of education, Chris Phillips, told the Times that search and AI are “deeply integrated.” Reuters separately reported that Google has expanded voluntary buyouts to employees in Canada, France, Germany, Japan and Switzerland.

The hosts read a commenter who called the opt-out “a hostage situation,” and they agree. Their answer is a real Google rival. And to any Google employee with a buyout offer: take it.

Ocarina of Time is back, and critics love it. The Switch 2 remake hit a 96 on Metacritic from 80 reviews, and every one of them counted as positive. That makes it the best-reviewed game of 2026 on the site so far, and it launched Thursday, Nov. 5. Read the story on D/REZZED.

That viral claim about Guillermo del Toro directing a live-action Akira comes from unverified X posts, and Warner Bros. let its Akira rights lapse in 2025.

Bill Skarsgard says he breaks out the Pennywise voice at home when his kids misbehave. Sometimes Nosferatu shows up too.

Cameras were rolling before EA shut BioWare down, and now Canada’s Super Channel has ordered Massive Effect: The BioWare Story, Deadline reports.

After Taylor Lorenz said she was offered “a lot of money” to post anti-AI content, Epic’s Tim Sweeney blamed “astroturfed anti-AI influence campaigns.”

Ubisoft is one of several companies bidding for Arkane Lyon, the Dishonored studio Microsoft planned to close, Bloomberg reports.

And Earth has a new mini-moon about 3 feet wide. It should drift off in December.

Roseanne Barr secretly shot an eight-episode sitcom called Meemaw in Austin with Randy Quaid and Drea de Matteo, and no network has picked it up yet. Hackers took over the fridges at hundreds of French supermarkets in October, pushing temperatures as high as 122 degrees Fahrenheit and starting fires. text:
Scientists Develop Urine Test That Detects 95% of Bladder Cancers | Mihai Andrei, ZME Science

A new urine test could make bladder cancer easier to detect — and help doctors figure out which treatments are most likely to work.

In a new study, Stanford researchers developed a test that detected 95% of localized bladder cancers. By analyzing tiny fragments of RNA in urine, the method could also help predict whether patients will respond better to immunotherapy or chemotherapy. This could pave the way for more personalized and non-invasive cancer care.

Reading cancer’s molecular messages

Bladder cancer is notoriously prone to recurrence. Even after a tumor is removed, patients sometimes need repeated cystoscopies, procedures in which a thin camera is inserted through the urethra to inspect the bladder. The procedure is an important diagnostic tool, but it’s also uncomfortable and invasive.

Researchers have long searched for a reliable urine test that could make monitoring easier. Many liquid biopsy approaches focus on tumor DNA, but Stanford’s new method takes a different route. It looks for RNA.

While DNA contains the genetic instructions of a cell, RNA helps carry out those instructions. By examining which RNA molecules appear in urine, scientists can identify patterns of gene activity associated with cancer, rather than just looking for cancer-linked mutations.

“Analyzing RNA can tell us not only whether a cancer is present — but also what it’s doing,” said Maximilian Diehn, a professor of radiation oncology at Stanford and senior author of the study, in a press release.

A urine test that outperforms standard results

The researchers developed a technique called uRARE-seq, which isolates and sequences tiny fragments of cell-free RNA floating in urine. They focused on genetic messages that are uncommon in healthy urine but frequently produced by tumors.

The study analyzed 683 urine samples from 515 individuals. Researchers trained their bladder cancer detection model on 251 samples and evaluated it using another 282 samples.

The test detected about 95% of localized bladder cancers at 90% specificity. In other words, it correctly identified 95% of cancers, and produced a false positive in 10% of cases. Performance was similar in the independent validation cohort.

This isn’t perfect, but it’s better than existing, conventional urine sampling.

Among 93 samples tested using both methods, uRARE-seq detected 89 cancers. Standard urine cytology, which involves examining urine for abnormal cells under a microscope, detected just 32.

The difference was especially pronounced for low-grade tumors, which conventional cytology often struggles to detect.

Unlike some DNA-based approaches, the test also worked without first sequencing an individual patient’s tumor.

Knowing whether cancer is really gone

Finding cancer is only part of the challenge. Doctors also need to know whether treatment has eliminated it completely.

For patients with non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer, surgery is often followed by something called Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) immunotherapy. This treatment uses weakened bacteria, originally developed for tuberculosis vaccination, to stimulate an immune attack against cancer cells.

But BCG doesn’t work for everyone.

The researchers followed 36 patients who underwent surgery followed by BCG, analyzing urine before surgery, before immunotherapy, and after treatment.

Among 23 patients who did not develop high-grade recurrence during follow-up, none had detectable bladder cancer RNA after BCG treatment. By contrast, 12 of the 13 patients whose cancer subsequently returned still had detectable tumor signals.

The test could also distinguish patients whose cancer appeared to have been eliminated by surgery alone from those who needed BCG to achieve a complete molecular response.

Could a urine test help choose the right treatment?

Perhaps the most intriguing finding is that RNA could also reveal which treatment a patient is more likely to benefit from.

Patients who responded well to BCG tended to have stronger immune-related gene activity in their urine before treatment. Those who responded poorly showed greater activity in genes associated with rapid cell division.

Using these patterns, the researchers developed a model that could predict treatment response. Across analyses involving 114 patients, the results suggested that people less likely to benefit from BCG might instead respond better to chemotherapy delivered directly into the bladder.

That’s potentially important because BCG supplies are frequently limited. A reliable predictive test could help doctors reserve the treatment for patients most likely to benefit, while directing others toward alternatives sooner.

Not yet ready for hospitals

Despite the encouraging results, uRARE-seq remains experimental.

The study was largely retrospective, drawing on samples collected at two closely affiliated medical institutions. Some treatment analyses involved relatively few patients, and treatment selection was not randomized.

The test isn’t yet ready to replace cystoscopy, and researchers will need larger studies across multiple hospitals to establish its clinical usefulness.

Still, the research points toward an appealing possibility. Doctors could identify bladder cancer with a simple, non-invasive urine test. Then, they could use further urine samples to monitor its activity, check whether treatment has worked, and potentially identify which therapy offers the best chance of preventing recurrence.

A lot of information from something as ordinary as a urine sample.

My $hg $hgraf dreams…

As we are approaching year end and the opportunity to add shares on over all market weakness and possible tax related selling, redomicle confusion, I’ve been given a lot of thought to risk / reward today vs 2 summers ago when I first began accumulating shares. 

The conclusion I come to, which is solely my opinion and not advice :) is that the risk reward today is better than it has been at anytime.  Including when I first bought.   Amazingly even though the stock is currently up 10x from the time of my initial posts and interviews with Kjirstin and Dr Sorensen. 

When I first started buying I hadn’t visited the facilities and see the Hyperion.  They had no approvals to produce at scale anywhere.  Where forced to only use canisters of acetylene and the gas plant was just talk.   

They also had minimal cash on the balance sheet and a huge amount of warrants to keep a lid on the stock.  I think around 70 mln warrants back then.  

Despite this, when I dug deep and spent the time interviewing Kjirstin and Dr Sorensen as well as using AI to help educate me and analyze turbostratic fractal graphene and it’s surprising superior quality I felt so strongly about science and believed in Dr Sorensen, when he told me it would change the world, I bought heavily into the company and even offered to do a private placement at one point at $50c but it was rejected as they felt they would be soon rated higher and that’s what happened.  

The short sellers generated a fraudulent assessment of the company which still corrupted the AI engines today.  They said that EPA approval would take 5 years if ever. And that it’s a hazardous material that companies won’t want to work with.   They made ridiculous claims about the safety of the Hyperions. 

When I visited the facilities over a year ago I was pleased to review the tech with Mr Corkhill the lead engineer and designer of the Hyperion.   I went over the numbers.  The grams per second data on his screens showed long run time history and steady improvements over time. Over a year of data I think.  Very consistent.  The pressure max was modest and over engineered for by 10x.  The heat build up is minimal and the chambers can run for I think over an hour or at least 30 mins before needing a simple water cooling system to be turned on.  It actually is said to perform better as it warms up.  
The combustion cycles per minimum or single digits vs car engines with rpm’s in the thousands and moving parts (pistons) that generate friction and extreme heat fast.  Bottom line. I gained 100% confidence in the machines and that they are cookie cutter and likely to outperform specs stated so far by a wide margin over time. 

The company took a few months longer than expected to get epa approval.   But their only mistake was believing regulators that timelines would be met.  A learning process for a new technology team.   I was really pleased that at the same time as getting epa they got EU and Uk approvals to produce and sell. 

They then took probably 6-8 months longer than expected to get western gas pipeline deal finalized.  But with a Japanese conglomerate in control the number of approvals and signatures required takes time.  Especially as the world has literally been on fire with huge disruptions for all manufacturers and supply chains.  Getting new things done in this environment is so challenging and the achievements should be celebrated.

So now…
 
In my mind… 

Scale up risk, permitting risk, manufacturing tech risk has been eliminated, 

With the financings that have taken place the balance sheet is also strong.  

The team is growing daily.  So many great adds over the last year.   I’m not sure how many scientists and particularly nano tech / graphene PhD’s they have but no doubt they are now a force. 

They have plenty of patents and continue to add more.  Likely filing more each month now.  That’s only going to scale up as they have more scientists doing more experiments

text:
$LITE: The Most Scarce “Laser Source” in AI Data Centers Has Just Secured a Major Order, Yet Its Stock Price Has Plummeted from 1,100 to 500

Copper cables are no longer sufficient for high-speed data transmission in AI clusters, making optical interconnects essential. Lumentum specializes in the most critical and difficult-to-mass-produce components for these optical pathways: laser chips, pump lasers, and optical circuit switches (OCS). Many products are already sold out through 2029, and production capacity cannot keep up with demand.

Two Recent Developments
Earnings Beat Expectations: For Q1 of fiscal year 2027, revenue was $1.26 billion (up 136% year-over-year), non-GAAP EPS was $4.57 (exceeding expectations), and non-GAAP operating margin was 42.3%. Guidance for the next quarter calls for revenue of $1.575–$1.625 billion, EPS of $5.90–$6.20, and an operating margin set to rise further to 45–46%.
At the same time, the company secured its second major CPO/NPO order, with procurement commitments exceeding $5 billion. The primary drivers of growth are pump lasers and optical circuit switches, with gross margins significantly outperforming those of peers who are still selling large volumes of transceivers.

The company was subsequently acquired by Marvell in an all-stock deal
Announced on November 2: 4.5 shares of MRVL for every 1 share of LITE, an all-stock deal with no cash floor. At the time of the announcement, based on the then-current price, this equated to approximately $1,132 per share (a premium of about 24%); LITE shareholders would ultimately hold approximately 33% of the combined company. The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2028, subject to shareholder and regulatory approval. The issue is that MRVL’s stock has also plummeted, causing the value of the share swap to drop accordingly. Currently, LITE’s stock price is significantly below the initial “offer” and also below many analysts’ estimates of its “stand-alone value.” The market is also concerned about dilution, whether synergies will materialize, regulatory scrutiny, and the lengthy waiting period.

It closed yesterday at approximately $510 (down about 19% on the day) and is trading near $550 in pre-market trading today, rebounding by about 8%.
Today: If sentiment toward tech stocks continues to improve, the stock may test the $560–$590 range; if the broader market comes under pressure again or MRVL weakens, it may fluctuate between $520 and $560.
Short Term (Next Few Weeks to 1–2 Months): The stock price is now driven more by MRVL and the transaction premium/discount than by its own fundamentals alone. If MRVL stabilizes and rebounds, LITE is expected to recover toward the $600–$700 range; if concerns over AI capital expenditures persist or transaction risks escalate, it may continue to fluctuate within the $500–$600 range.

Analysts have recently lowered their price targets, but some still offer independent or transaction-related targets of $700–$1,000+.

text:
Comfy-Org launches RelayVSR for real-time video upscaling

It’s that time of the week when we dive into some serious tech talk. Today, we’re focusing on a new development in real-time video processing: ComfyUI’s RelayVSR. This technology promises to enhance how we handle high-resolution content in collaborative environments. But is it all hype or does it deliver?
What Is RelayVSR and Why Should You Care?

RelayVSR is an advanced system designed for real-time upscaling of videos, capable of pushing the boundaries of resolution without sacrificing performance. The key innovation here lies in its Sparse Generative Relay architecture, which uses a large generative model to create detailed latent references only for sparse key frames. These references are then applied across all intermediate frames using a lightweight transformer with dual memory.
How Does It Work?

The magic behind RelayVSR is its ability to use sparse key frames and a dual-memory transformer to distribute details efficiently. This approach minimizes the computational load while maintaining high-quality output, thanks in part to INT8 quantization techniques that reduce video memory usage significantly. The system can achieve 30 frames per second at 1080p resolution on consumer-grade GPUs with just 14GB of VRAM.
Performance Metrics and GPU Requirements

While the performance metrics are impressive—delivering real-time upscaling at 1080p—the full potential of RelayVSR isn’t unlocked without a powerful GPU like an A100. This means that while you can enjoy benefits at lower resolutions, scaling to 4K requires substantial hardware investment.
Model Configurations and Optimizations

The system’s performance relies heavily on specific model configurations such as `relayvsr_x4_int8_convrot` and `relayvsr_x2_lightx2v_int8_convrot`. These optimizations are crucial for achieving real-time speeds even at lower resolutions. Without them, the computational load would be too high.
Use Cases and Applications

For professionals in video editing or streaming who need real-time upscaling capabilities, RelayVSR could indeed be a game-changer. It offers efficient processing that opens doors to new applications and workflows, making it particularly appealing for those working with specific constraints or having access to powerful hardware.

Imagine you’re a video editor tasked with enhancing the resolution of a 1080p video in real-time for a live stream. With RelayVSR, you can achieve this without breaking a sweat on your consumer-grade GPU. The system’s ability to handle such tasks seamlessly could save countless hours and reduce stress during tight deadlines.
Limitations and Accessibility Concerns

Despite its impressive performance, the requirement for high-end GPUs like A100 limits accessibility. For now, RelayVSR is more of a luxury than a necessity unless you’re already equipped with top-tier hardware. This makes it less appealing for everyday users or those working on modest setups.
What Is Stored and Excluded

RelayVSR stores model configurations and optimized files necessary for real-time upscaling. It excludes any user-specific data, ensuring that the system remains lightweight and focused solely on its core functionality. The repository includes detailed instructions for deploying these models in various environments, from local apps to cloud-based solutions.
User Controls and Privacy

Users have control over how they deploy RelayVSR within their workflows. Whether you’re integrating it into a video editing suite or using it for live streaming, the system’s flexibility allows customization based on your specific needs. Additionally, since RelayVSR does not store user data, privacy concerns are minimal.
Availability and Deployment

RelayVSR is available through the Comfy-Org repository on Hugging Face. The developer page provides detailed information and instructions for deployment across different platforms. You can find the necessary files in the following folders:
• `ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models/relayvsr_x4_int8_convrot.safetensors`
• `ComfyUI/models/vae/relayvsr_flash_vae_x4_fp32.safetensors`

These files are essential for achieving real-time upscaling at various resolutions, and the repository also includes optimized configurations to ensure smooth performance.
What This Does Not Prove

While RelayVSR demonstrates impressive capabilities in real-time video processing, it does not prove that all future developments will be equally accessible. The current reliance on high-end GPUs like A100 highlights a gap between cutting-edge technology and everyday use cases. However, ongoing advancements in hardware optimization and model efficiency could bridge this gap in the near future.
Practical Takeaway

If you’re working with video content and need real-time upscaling capabilities, RelayVSR offers a powerful solution that can enhance your workflow significantly. Whether you’re editing videos or streaming live content, the system’s ability to handle high-resolution tasks efficiently makes it an attractive option for those with access to suitable hardware.
Where Can You Learn More?

For those interested in diving deeper into RelayVSR or contributing to its development, check out the [Comfy-Org/RelayVSR repository on Hugging Face](https://t.co/pvvnyUEDRm). The developer page also provides detailed information and instructions for deployment.

The Motorola Signature 27 launched in the US yesterday, but no cigar for people waiting for GrapheneOS support. The world needs an alternative to iPhone and standard Android, and this could be it.

US pre-orders open on 19 November, with sales beginning on 26 November at $1,599.

GrapheneOS is an operating system built from the open source foundations of Android, with additional privacy and security protections against surveillance, malicious applications and attempts to exploit vulnerabilities.

It runs Android apps, but Google's apps and spyware-like services aren't built into it by default. People can install Google Play if they want, but it won't have any more access or control over their phone than other ordinary apps, unlike its privileged position on standard Android.

Google has a proven track record of lying to customers and the media about location tracking. It continued collecting and storing location data even when people disabled Location History, using other settings, Google apps, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and IP addresses to identify where they were. US authorities found that Google had misled customers and forced it to pay $391.5 million in 2022 and another $93 million in 2023.

Turning off location tracking didn't necessarily stop Google from tracking everyone's movements. Google and mobile device OEMs can also use Android updates to install or update services, introduce new features and change settings. Some updates happen automatically, while others prompt people to accept new permissions or services. This gives companies ongoing control over the software on people's phones, usually without them fully understanding what's changed. GrapheneOS stops all of that.

GrapheneOS gives people greater control over what applications can access. They can block an app's internet access, restrict which contacts and files it can see.

You can also create separate profiles for different activities. Each profile contains its own apps, accounts, contacts, files and settings. For example, someone could keep private messaging in one profile, work in another, and social media and Google services in a third. Apps in one profile can't access the apps or their data in another.

Each profile can also have its own PIN or password. When you end a secondary profile's session, its apps stop and its data stays locked until you unlock it again. 

Motorola makes the device and supplies the software that operates its components. GrapheneOS creates the operating system that people can install instead of Motorola's standard software. Both organisations are working together to make that combination secure and reliable.

The Signature 27 is intended to become the first Motorola phone that can run GrapheneOS. Currently, GrapheneOS only works on Google Pixel phones. Although Google makes the Pixel, it can't exercise the same control, collect the same information or impose its usual services when the phone runs GrapheneOS instead of standard Android.

Announcing a new phone doesn't mean GrapheneOS is ready for it. The operating system must work properly with its cameras, modem, fingerprint reader and other components while preserving its security protections. The combined software also needs extensive testing and a reliable process for future security updates.

The Signature 27 includes Qualcomm's Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 processor, a 6.8-inch display, a 7,000 mAh battery and a 200 MP telephoto camera. Motorola promises 7 operating system upgrades and up to 7 years of security updates, subject to market and model conditions.

Motorola's decision could pressure other manufacturers to follow.

People are fed up with mobile device manufacturers, network operators and tech companies that collect, analyse and share their personal information, usually without their knowledge or consent. Market conditions for mobile devices that put privacy and personal safety first have never been more compelling.

Most people don't realise that even their banking apps can detect other apps installed on their phones. Android allows qualifying banking apps to request access to lists of installed apps for so-called fraud detection, while iOS allows apps to check for specific other apps.

This is an invasion of everyone's right to privacy. Banks have no business knowing what other apps and services their customers use.

That's just one example of how an app installed for one purpose can collect information about other aspects of someone's life.

For people who need stronger protection for private communications and personal information, the Signature 27 could become a compelling alternative to an iPhone or a phone that runs standard Android. It combines premium hardware and Android app compatibility with greater control over personal information.

Personal safety still depends on the apps and services people choose. A messaging service can retain information, a cloud backup can create another copy, and someone who sends or receives a private message can share it with third parties through an AI integration.

Changing the operating system doesn't eliminate those risks, but GrapheneOS adds a significant layer of protection beyond what iPhones and standard Android phones offer today.

This is more important than ever because Apple's direction and its deep reliance on their latest technology developed in Israel, the world's biggest exporter of state sanctioned spyware.

Apple's Israeli engineering teams have helped develop its M1 Pro and M1 Max processors for Macs, wireless connectivity chips, data storage technology, cameras and biometric systems.

Apple also acquired Israeli companies whose technology contributed to some of its most sensitive capabilities. PrimeSense helped create Face ID, Anobit built flash memory technology, LinX specialised in advanced smartphone cameras, and RealFace built facial recognition.

In January 2026, Apple acquired Israeli company Q(.ai for about $1.6 billion. Its technology can analyse whispered speech and tiny facial movements. Its patents describe capabilities to identify people and assess emotions, heart rate and breathing.

Apple's own Israeli engineering chief said it's difficult to find an Apple product without an Israeli contribution. These aren't minor components. They include technology responsible for processing information, communications, authentication and AI.

Combined with Apple's recent Siri and Apple Intelligence updates, which introduce new ways for AI to access and process personal information, I no longer trust Apple to protect the privacy and personal safety of its customers.

I founded one of my first companies in 2002. It was the first specialist telecom testing company to join the GSMA and was one of the most trusted companies of its kind in Europe at the time. My team was responsible for testing and certifying every mobile device launched on O2's UK network during the 2000s. I also signed an NDA to certify the first iPhone released outside the US.

I have extensive experience in mobile technology and security, so I don't simply take a company's word about how secure its products are, as I did with Apple for many years.

Instead, I examine what's technically possible based on the design of the hardware, operating system, firmware and apps, including how they can be used to compromise privacy and personal safety through partner integrations/relationships.

The world desperately needs an alternative to iPhones and standard Android devices that puts everyone's right to privacy and personal safety first. Motorola and GrapheneOS can deliver it, but it can't come soon enough. I hope both companies commit the resources needed to make it happen as soon as possible.

No. 1 Miami at No. 4 Notre Dame
4:30 PM PT (7:30 PM ET) | NBC
South Bend gets the weekend's main event.

Miami arrives 8-0 after escaping North Carolina 38-35. Notre Dame is 7-1 after beating Navy 35-13, and the stakes reach well beyond the nostalgia attached to these uniforms. This is the programs' first meeting with both teams in the AP top five since 1988.

Darian Mensah and CJ Carr give the game an appealing quarterback matchup, while Miami receiver Malachi Toney against Notre Dame cornerback Leonard Moore offers a compelling battle outside, provided Toney's ankle lets him play his usual role.

For the Irish, beating the nation's top-ranked team would provide the kind of signature result that changes a resume immediately. For Miami, winning in South Bend would make its unbeaten record considerably harder to question.

Watch how aggressively both offenses attack early. A conservative start might settle the nerves, but neither side should want to spend the second half chasing the other.
