text:
NQ / NASDAQ — POST-OPEN REGIME RADAR
Semiconductors Recover as Strong US Payrolls Revive Fed Rate-Hike Risk — 6 November 2026

6 NOVEMBER 2026 | 16:28 SWITZERLAND | 09:28 CME/CHICAGO | 10:28 NEW YORK
SECOND REPORT OF THE DAY — US CASH SESSION

MAIN CONCLUSION
The US cash session has confirmed a sharp rebound in semiconductor shares following Thursday's historic technology sell-off, but the recovery is not broad across Wall Street. At 09:57 New York (15:57 Switzerland), Reuters recorded the Nasdaq Composite up 1.82%, the S&P 500 up 1.02% and the Dow down 0.22%. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index recovered more than 6% after losing over 12% the previous day. Meanwhile, the US economy added 165,000 jobs in October, far above the roughly 65,000 expected, and unemployment eased to 4.1%. The resulting rise in Treasury yields and expectations of a December Federal Reserve rate increase creates an important tension: chip buyers are returning while the cost-of-capital outlook remains demanding.

KEY CONFIRMATION / RISK
NVIDIA rose around 6.5% and AMD, Intel and Micron gained between approximately 7% and 13% in Reuters' early cash-session observation. The advance has spread into selected AI infrastructure operators, but six of the eleven S&P 500 sectors remained negative. The preliminary November University of Michigan consumer sentiment index improved to 51, while one-year inflation expectations eased to 4.3%. That is constructive for consumer confidence, but inflation expectations remain elevated and the strong payroll report has revived rate-hike expectations. The immediate test is whether semiconductor participation remains strong enough to support NQ despite weaker market breadth and rising yields.

WHAT CHANGED SINCE THE FIRST REPORT

Before the cash opening, Nasdaq-100 futures were up 1.41% in a Reuters observation, with chipmakers recovering from a severe decline. At that stage, the payroll release had not yet been published and the rebound had not been tested by regular US equity trading.

We now have three new pieces of evidence. First, the semiconductor recovery is occurring in the cash market, not just in thin pre-market trading. Second, the official October employment report has significantly exceeded forecasts. Third, the Michigan survey has delivered stronger sentiment and lower inflation expectations.

The important limitation is that a positive Nasdaq Composite does not mean all American equities are rising, and it must not be substituted for an unverified live quotation of the NQ futures contract.

US CASH MARKET — TIME-STAMPED OBSERVATION

REUTERS | 09:57 NEW YORK / 15:57 SWITZERLAND:

NASDAQ COMPOSITE: 24,758.34 | +1.82%.

S&P 500: 7,428.96 | +1.02%.

DOW JONES INDUSTRIAL AVERAGE: 51,410.10 | −0.22%.

VIX: approximately 23.88.

PHILADELPHIA SEMICONDUCTOR INDEX: more than +6%.
These figures come from a published observation, not a synchronised market snapshot at 16:28 Switzerland. The Nasdaq Composite is a cash index; NQ is a futures contract tracking the Nasdaq-100. Their values and percentage changes should not be represented as identical.

The relative performance shows a technology-led rebound rather than a uniform recovery in the wider equity market. Six of the eleven major S&P 500 sectors were still negative, with consumer staples and utilities among the weakest in that observation.
SEMICONDUCTORS — THE MAIN SOURCE OF THE REBOUND

NVIDIA gained approximately 6.5% after Thursday's exceptionally sharp decline. AMD, Intel and Micron were up between approximately 7% and 13% in the Reuters morning report. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index climbed more than 6% after losing over 12% in the previous session.
The size of the recovery is material, but it must be compared with the size of the preceding decline. A sharp rebound can recover part of a loss without restoring the previous price level, valuation or market breadth. Today's evidence confirms buying in semiconductor shares; it does not establish that the broader debate over AI infrastructure investment has ended.

For NQ, the critical distinction is whether this demand remains distributed across chipmakers and large technology constituents or becomes increasingly dependent on a few individual names.
AI INFRASTRUCTURE OPERATORS — DIFFERENT BUSINESS MODELS, DIFFERENT RISKS

Reuters reported recoveries in IREN, Applied Digital, CoreWeave and Nebius, alongside power and equipment suppliers including GE Vernova and Constellation Energy. Associated Press reported IREN up approximately 19% around 10:00 New York following stronger quarterly results and two additional signed contracts. CoreWeave advanced roughly 5.7%, while Micron rose around 9.5% in the same AP observation.

These companies occupy different positions in the AI investment chain. Chip suppliers earn revenue from equipment demand; data-centre operators carry construction, leasing, power and financing obligations; energy and electrical-equipment businesses depend on the pace at which capacity is built and connected.

A rebound in all three groups is encouraging, but neither earnings growth nor a share-price rally guarantees that projected infrastructure capacity will be installed on schedule or will generate the expected free cash flow.

LAM RESEARCH AND CLOUD INFRASTRUCTURE — COMPANY-SPECIFIC SUPPORT

Associated Press reported Lam Research advancing approximately 10.9% after the company authorised a share repurchase programme of up to $25 billion. Cloudflare also attracted strong interest following its quarterly results, which showed revenue growth of approximately 39% to $782.5 million in company-reported figures.

These developments underline the importance of distinguishing company-specific financial news from the broader market regime. Some businesses are being rewarded for earnings momentum or capital returns even as the overall technology sector remains vulnerable to financing concerns and changing risk appetite.

THE OCTOBER JOBS REPORT — A CLEAR POSITIVE SURPRISE

Released at 14:30 Switzerland / 08:30 New York, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported:

NONFARM PAYROLLS: +165,000.

REUTERS CONSENSUS: approximately +65,000.

UNEMPLOYMENT RATE: 4.1%, down from 4.2%.

PRIVATE-SECTOR HOURLY EARNINGS: +0.4% month on month.

ANNUAL HOURLY EARNINGS GROWTH: +3.1%.

AVERAGE PRIVATE WORKWEEK: 34.4 hours, unchanged.

LABOUR-FORCE PARTICIPATION RATE: 61.9%, little changed.

The headline employment gain substantially exceeded expectations. The fall in unemployment is consistent with a resilient labour market. However, the wage increase is also relevant for monetary policy, especially while underlying inflation remains above the Federal Reserve's target.

A stronger labour market supports consumer demand and corporate revenue, but it also gives policymakers less reason to ease financial conditions rapidly.

PAYROLL REVISIONS — IMPORTANT ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

The BLS revised August and September payroll gains upward by a combined 84,000 jobs. September's increase was revised to approximately 60,000 from the initially reported 29,000. The upward revisions reinforce the stronger headline and suggest that recent hiring was less fragile than earlier estimates indicated.

This distinction matters because the Fed evaluates patterns, not just the latest monthly figure. Nevertheless, payroll estimates can be revised again; the published release is evidence available today, not a permanent final measurement of every job created.

WHERE JOBS WERE CREATED

Professional and business services added 70,000 jobs in October. Health care gained 42,000, transportation and warehousing 25,000, and manufacturing approximately 19,000. These sectors explain much of the headline improvement.

The gains demonstrate that employment strength is not restricted to a single narrow industry. But the household survey also showed the number working part-time for economic reasons increasing by 339,000 to around 4.8 million. That is a reminder that strong headline payroll growth can coexist with underlying labour-market weaknesses.

Consequently, the employment report supports the growth outlook without proving that every aspect of the labour market is strengthening.

FEDERAL RESERVE — A HIGHER PROBABILITY OF TIGHTER POLICY

After the payroll release, Reuters reported that market-implied odds of a 25-basis-point Federal Reserve rate increase in December rose to approximately 78%, from about 70% earlier. A separate later account showed higher implied odds, illustrating how quickly rate pricing can change after a major release. These percentages are observations of futures-market pricing, not a guaranteed policy decision.

The next Fed decision is scheduled for 9 December, after the 8–9 December meeting. Inflation and energy costs remain central to the policy outlook. A strong labour market gives the Fed greater flexibility to focus on persistent price pressure, even as equity investors confront large losses and uncertainty over AI valuations.

TREASURY YIELDS — THE BOND MARKET'S RESPONSE

Reuters reported the 2-year Treasury yield around 4.52%, approximately six basis points higher following the jobs report. The 10-year yield was near 4.87%, up roughly three basis points, and the 30-year around 5.27%, up about two basis points in the cited observation.

Associated Press subsequently reported the 10-year yield near 4.86%, compared with 4.84% late Thursday. These readings belong to different observation times.

Higher yields can increase discount-rate pressure on expected long-term earnings. For businesses financing data centres through debt or leases, company-specific borrowing spreads and financing terms matter in addition to government yields.

The Nasdaq's advance alongside rising yields demonstrates that earnings expectations and short-term buying can outweigh discount-rate concerns during a particular session. It does not make higher financing costs irrelevant.

THE DOLLAR — STRONGER AFTER PAYROLLS

Reuters reported the dollar index approximately 0.7% higher at 102.22 in its post-employment observation. This is consistent with the upward repricing of US rates following stronger hiring and wages.

A firmer dollar can tighten international financial conditions, but the relationship with NQ is not mechanical. Dollar movements should be assessed alongside Treasury yields, semiconductor participation and the wider equity response.

MICHIGAN CONSUMER SENTIMENT — BETTER THAN EXPECTED

Released at 16:00 Switzerland / 10:00 New York, the University of Michigan's preliminary November survey showed:

CONSUMER SENTIMENT: 51.0.

OCTOBER FINAL: 48.0.

MARKET CONSENSUS: approximately 48.0.

ONE-YEAR INFLATION EXPECTATIONS: 4.3%, down from 4.7%.

LONG-RUN INFLATION EXPECTATIONS: 3.4%, down from 3.5%.

The improvement is meaningful but should be viewed in context. Consumer confidence remains weak historically, and expected inflation is still elevated. The survey also found continuing concern about the cost of living. It was conducted between 20 October and 2 November, before the midterm election, so the reported improvement should not be attributed to the election result.

WHAT THE TWO ECONOMIC RELEASES MEAN TOGETHER

The payroll report strengthens the growth and employment outlook, while the Michigan survey shows modestly better confidence and somewhat lower inflation expectations. These are not contradictory signals.

For NQ, the complication is monetary policy. Strong employment and monthly wage growth support the case for the Fed to remain restrictive; declining inflation expectations offer some counterweight. The market will need to weigh the two alongside next week's official inflation release.

A positive economic surprise is useful information, but it is not a stand-alone trading instruction.

MARKET BREADTH — A CRITICAL LIMITATION OF THE RALLY

Reuters reported that six of the eleven major S&P 500 sectors were negative at 09:57 New York, despite gains in the technology-heavy Nasdaq and the broader S&P 500 index. Associated Press also reported more declining S&P 500 stocks than advancing stocks around 10:00.

This internal divergence matters. The index recovery is receiving substantial support from large AI and semiconductor businesses rather than an equally broad improvement across the entire US equity market.

A more durable recovery would ideally show strengthening participation beyond chipmakers. If the number of declining stocks remains high while NQ advances, the rebound is still relatively concentrated and vulnerable to changes in leadership.

VOLATILITY — LOWER, BUT STILL ELEVATED

The VIX eased to approximately 23.88 in Reuters' morning observation after surging on Thursday. A decline in implied volatility can accompany reduced demand for equity protection, but a level near 24 remains materially different from calmer trading conditions.

For leveraged NQ and MNQ contracts, this matters because the speed of movement and execution slippage can differ markedly from normal sessions. A lower VIX reading does not eliminate intraday volatility or guarantee more favourable fills.

ASIA AND EUROPE — THE OVERNIGHT DAMAGE REMAINS

Asian markets remained under pressure on Friday after Thursday's US sell-off. Associated Press reported declines around 6% in both Japan and South Korea, while the German DAX lost more than 2% during European trading.

These international losses help explain the fragile starting conditions for the US session. However, the subsequent American semiconductor recovery demonstrates that markets can diverge across regions and trading hours. Asian closing losses are historical observations, not forecasts for the US afternoon.

OIL AND ENERGY — INFLATION RISK CONTINUES

Reuters reported Brent crude slightly lower during Friday's US morning, although energy prices remain subject to sharp changes linked to the conflict involving Iran and wider supply concerns. Associated Press observed Brent near $99 per barrel in a separate report.

Oil matters both through inflation and through the cost of powering large data centres. Even when chip demand is strong, electricity access and long-term energy contracts remain material to infrastructure economics.

The broader point is that a one-session fall in crude does not eliminate geopolitical supply risk, just as one session of stronger semiconductor buying does not settle the question of future AI investment returns.

AI POLICY — UNCERTAINTY, NOT AN ENACTED NATIONAL BAN

Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in the 3 November midterm elections. Investors have reassessed possible future oversight of AI and the pace of data-centre construction. However, new congressional control takes effect in January 2027, and President Trump retains veto authority.

Potential restrictions on the construction of data centres may also depend on state and local decisions concerning electricity, planning and water use. Market fears about future regulations should not be presented as laws already enacted nationwide.

The effect on technology valuations will depend on concrete measures and on the financial structure of individual companies.

TODAY'S COMPANY-SPECIFIC DIVERGENCE

Airbnb advanced after raising its full-year revenue growth outlook. Atlassian declined sharply following its earnings reaction, while Axon and Charter Communications also fell after disappointing figures in Associated Press reporting.

This dispersion shows that investors continue to differentiate between operating results and guidance, even amid the broader rebound. A rising Nasdaq does not mean all technology-related businesses are being repriced higher.

WHAT REMAINS ON TODAY'S CALENDAR — SWISS TIME

22:00 — US regular cash-market close. Closing semiconductor performance, relative NQ/ES strength and the balance of advancing and declining shares will help establish how much of Thursday's sell-off has been recovered.

NEXT TUESDAY, 10 NOVEMBER, 14:30 SWITZERLAND — October US Consumer Price Index. This is the next major scheduled inflation release and will be especially important after today's stronger payroll and wage numbers.

NEXT FRIDAY, 13 NOVEMBER, 14:30 SWITZERLAND — October US Producer Price Index.

CROSS-MARKET CONFIRMATION FRAMEWORK

SOX, NVIDIA, AMD AND MICRON — Is semiconductor buying sustained and broad within the sector?

DATA-CENTRE OPERATORS — Does confidence extend to businesses financing construction and computing capacity?

US 2Y AND 10Y — Are monetary expectations tightening after payrolls?

DXY — Is a stronger dollar reinforcing financial pressure?

VIX AND S&P 500 BREADTH — Is the recovery broadening or narrowly concentrated?

BRENT — Are energy-price movements easing or worsening inflation risk?

NQ RELATIVE TO ES — Does Nasdaq outperformance persist after the early rebound?

These are diagnostic references. No unverified live NQ price, VWAP, POC, support or resistance level is inserted into this report.

BULLISH SCENARIO — CONDITIONS FOR A STRONGER RECOVERY

The constructive case requires semiconductor gains to remain substantial after the early rebound, improved buying across the Nasdaq and continued stabilisation among data-centre operators. A moderation in Treasury-yield pressure would help, while lower inflation expectations may support the broader financial environment. The key confirmation would be wider equity participation and sustained demand rather than a rebound concentrated in yesterday's largest losers.

BEARISH SCENARIO — CONDITIONS FOR RENEWED PRESSURE

The weaker case would gain support if chip gains fade, Treasury yields climb further following strong payrolls, or funding-sensitive AI companies begin underperforming again. Negative breadth in the wider S&P 500 already shows that the recovery is not universal. The upcoming CPI release and unresolved data-centre financing risks may also limit the willingness of investors to maintain risk over the weekend.

These are conditional scenarios, not statistically calibrated probabilities of NQ's next movement.

ANALYTICAL EDGE

TECHNOLOGY-LED CASH-SESSION RECOVERY WITH MIXED BROADER PARTICIPATION AND A MORE HAWKISH RATES BACKDROP. The evidence is the Nasdaq's 1.82% rise, semiconductor gains above 6%, strong payrolls and increased expectations of a December rate rise. Thursday's damage and the weak participation of other sectors remain important limits to the interpretation.

CURRENT REGIME

POST-SELLOFF SEMICONDUCTOR RECOVERY / STRONGER US EMPLOYMENT / HIGHER POLICY-RATE EXPECTATIONS / MODESTLY IMPROVED CONSUMER SENTIMENT / EASING BUT ELEVATED VOLATILITY / AI FINANCING UNCERTAINTY.

OPERATIONAL CONCLUSION

The macroeconomic and corporate information now available is more complete than it was before the opening. It describes a market in which semiconductor buyers have returned despite an increasingly restrictive interest-rate outlook. That is a useful observation, not a guaranteed entry signal. For NQ and MNQ, position sizing, predefined protective stops, execution costs and maximum acceptable loss remain essential, especially after a week of unusually large intraday moves.

FINAL ANALYTICAL VIEW

WHAT CHANGED: The pre-market semiconductor rebound has been confirmed in US cash trading. At 09:57 New York, Nasdaq gained 1.82% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index more than 6%, while the Dow was negative.

WHAT THE DATA ADDED: October payrolls rose by 165,000, unemployment eased to 4.1% and hourly earnings increased 0.4% monthly. November Michigan sentiment improved to 51 and one-year inflation expectations fell to 4.3%.

WHAT REMAINS UNRESOLVED: The financing and regulatory outlook for AI infrastructure, the effect of stronger employment on Fed policy and weak participation in several non-technology sectors.

WHAT MATTERS NEXT: Semiconductor breadth, Treasury yields, the US dollar, closing market breadth and Tuesday's October CPI at 14:30 Switzerland.

text:
#PrinceOnThisDay - First Full ‘Greatest Romance’: The Pre-Rave Paisley Park Summit

On the early morning of 6 November 1999, Prince (performing under the unpronounceable Love Symbol) hosted one of his signature intimate late-night one-offs at Paisley Park Studios in Chanhassen, Minnesota. With the soundstage’s capacity of 1,375, these home-base gatherings offered dedicated fans rare up-close access just three days before the release of Rave Un2 the Joy Fantastic (9 November 1999 on NPG/Arista). The set balanced fresh material with classics and deep funk covers, capturing the symbol-era band at full power.

Band: Prince (vocals, guitar, keyboards), Kirk Johnson (drums), Larry Graham (bass, vocals), Morris Hayes (keyboards), Kip Blackshire (keyboards, vocals), Mike Scott (guitar), and The Hornheadz—Michael Nelson (trombone), Dave Jensen (trumpet), Kathy J. (baritone saxophone). Backing vocalists Johnnie Blackshire and DuJuan Blackshire joined as guests. Larry Graham, the Sly & the Family Stone/Graham Central Station legend and frequent 1998–99 collaborator, anchored the low end and added vocal fire.

Setlist (per Prince Vault and contemporary accounts):
When Will We B Paid? (Staple Singers cover) · The Greatest Romance Ever Sold (first full performance) · Baby Knows · Ain’t No Sunshine (Bill Withers cover) · Free · Everyday Is a Winding Road (Sheryl Crow cover) · Purple House (Prince’s take on Jimi Hendrix’s “Red House”) · Let’s Go Crazy · She’s Always in My Hair · U Got the Look · Kiss · Gett Off / Gett Off (Houstyle) · Talkin’ Loud and Sayin’ Nothing (James Brown cover, into It’s Alright) · Come On (New Power Generation) · Release Yourself (Graham Central Station cover) · Come and Dance With Me (Kip Blackshire lead vocals).
Cool facts: This marked the first complete live performance of “The Greatest Romance Ever Sold,” the album’s lead single (released 5 October). On the prior 23 October Paisley Park show, it had appeared only as an instrumental loop behind “Come and Dance With Me.” 

The video for the single was filmed at Paisley Park between 6–8 November. “Everyday Is a Winding Road” (Prince’s cover featured on the forthcoming album) and “Baby Knows” previewed the Rave material. The inclusion of Graham Central Station and Staple Singers material continued Prince’s deep engagement with funk lineage, while the Hendrix-rooted “Purple House” showcased his guitar prowess in the intimate setting. These affordable, fluid Paisley Park a.m. sessions remained a constant through the late ’90s—no rigid setlist, just the band locked in at home base before European TV promotion and the New Year’s Eve Rave Un2 the Year 2000 pay-per-view.

A pure late-night symbol-era groove that bridged the vault past and the millennium’s rave.
@prince

text:
Austin recorded nearly three price reductions for every pending event heading into the weekend. Houston added almost two new listings for every pending. Across all four Texas metros, sellers cut prices more often than buyers put homes under contract.

Austin had 1,714 price reductions, 618 pending and 594 new listings. Pending activity edged past new listings by 24, but sellers still recorded 2.77 price cuts per pending. Buyers were making offers. Sellers already on the market were giving them reasons to take another look.

DFW led in both price reductions and pending activity. Its 2,341 new listings nearly matched its 2,297 pending, while 4,334 price cuts worked out to 1.89 per pending. San Antonio showed a similar pricing pattern, with 1,190 reductions against 626 pending, or 1.90 cuts per pending. Another 729 listings came to market there.

Houston had the widest gap between new listings and pending activity. Sellers brought 2,822 listings to market against 1,461 pending and recorded another 2,642 price reductions. Buyers heading out this weekend have fresh listings to tour and a reason to revisit homes they passed on at the old price.

Mortgage rates have trended lower over the past four weeks. What I’m watching next is whether that payment relief brings enough buyers back to narrow Houston’s gap and whether more Austin sellers can find a buyer at their asking price.

Figures reflect seven-day residential MLS activity. Pending includes active under contract and equivalent statuses. A listing can appear in more than one category.

text:
Ever wonder why your 5GHz Wi-Fi hits 500 Mbps right next to the router, but dies the second you step behind a bedroom wall? High frequencies pack lightning speed, but basic wave physics makes them terrible at penetrating solid brick. 📶🧱

🎙️ #005 • Everyday Tech Explained: 2.4GHz vs. 5GHz Wi-Fi

The Physics of Home Wi-Fi:
🌊 Longer Waves Penetrate Concrete: 2.4GHz travels on ~12 cm radio waves that bend around obstacles and pass through solid brick or drywall with minimal signal loss. 5GHz waves are ~6 cm, meaning dense walls absorb or scatter their energy instantly.
🚀 The Bandwidth Highway: 5GHz offers wider, uncongested channels capable of pushing gigabit speeds without lag. 2.4GHz is narrow, practically maxing out around 100–300 Mbps in everyday homes.
📻 The Interference Traffic Jam: Old cordless phones, microwave ovens, Bluetooth earbuds, and your neighbor's router all crowd into 2.4GHz, causing packet drops and stutter during peak hours.

💡 The Rule of Thumb: Put gaming rigs, 4K TVs, and work laptops within line of sight on 5GHz. Offload smart plugs, security cams, and distant phones to 2.4GHz.

Do you split your home Wi-Fi into two separate network names (2.4G & 5G), or do you let your router auto-switch with Smart Connect? Drop your setup below! 👇

text:
THE SI UPSIDE | SPECIAL EDITION
What does an AI data center actually bring to a community?

After the midterms, Kevin O’Leary told Piers Morgan he expects states to rethink their opposition to AI data centers once they see the jobs, new power infrastructure, and investment these projects can bring.

I work in enterprise infrastructure, and I think the upside deserves a closer look. So do the questions residents are asking about power bills and water.

👷 JOBS. Virginia’s legislative auditors reported around 1,500 workers on site at peak construction for an individual data center build. A typical 250,000-square-foot facility may have about 50 full-time workers once it’s operating. A campus built in phases can keep electricians, pipefitters, and fiber installers busy for years. When you hear “thousands of jobs,” ask how many are construction jobs, how long they last, and how many stay after opening.

💰 TAXES. Loudoun County, Virginia, reports $1.2 billion in data center property taxes in FY2026. That’s a substantial benefit in an established market. What another county keeps depends on its tax rates, incentives, and the public costs of serving the project.

⚡ POWER. Seven major tech companies pledged in March to build, bring, or buy new power and pay for the infrastructure upgrades their data centers need. The pledge is voluntary. Ohio offers an example of an enforceable rule. Qualifying new AEP Ohio data centers must pay for at least 85% of their contracted capacity for up to 12 years, even if they use less. That helps protect households from paying for unused capacity. Whether household bills actually go down is a separate question.

💧 WATER. “Closed loop” tells you the coolant circulates. You still need to know how the heat leaves the building. An evaporative tower consumes water. A dry system can reject heat to outside air with very little on-site cooling water. The numbers I’d ask for are peak-day freshwater demand and how much the facility can draw during a drought.

🏗️ A FEDERAL PAUSE. The bills introduced this year would halt covered AI data center construction and upgrades, including work already underway, with no fixed end date. We already rely on data centers to shop, stream, send email, fill prescriptions, and move money. Those services would keep running. The immediate impact would be on construction crews and suppliers. Over time, the pause would also limit how quickly the U.S. can add computing capacity.

My take is that projects should have a path to get built when developers can show who pays for new power, how the project fits within local water limits, and what jobs and tax revenue the community can realistically expect. Put those commitments in writing so residents can judge the deal for themselves.

text:
Most experts think they already know who they serve.

I've sat through a lot of one-day Funnel Days. Over and over, the same gap shows up: the offer is clear, the customer is fuzzy.

I use 5 questions to pin it down.

1. What are 3 to 5 attributes of your perfect customer?
For me: they're among the best at what they do, results-driven, legacy-minded, they've produced results for other people, and they can invest.

2. What are their biggest problems?
Mine struggle with consistent leads and sales, systems to scale, the tech, and selling premium offers.

3. What outcomes do they want?
Not a laundry list. Three to five results you'd actually help them get.

4. What do they weigh before they buy?
Results from people like them. Shared values. Proof you take care of your own business.

5. Who has their ear right now?
Study those voices. Get on their lists. Understand the narrative your customer already hears.

It took me over a decade to realize I am not in the business of serving local businesses. I serve experts who want to make a difference in other people's lives.

The more specific your customer, the more universal your message becomes.

Which of the five is still fuzzy for you?

text:
The AM Brief, Friday November 6, 2026 Part 1

Good morning, 

It’s 10am in Miami and here is a recap of market related events that caught my eye. Part 1

     U.S. equities cratered Thursday in a historic selloff that completely erased the previous day's post election gains, driven by growing fears that Democratic victories will derail the AI data center buildout. The Nasdaq plunged 5.52% into correction territory, erasing $2.5 trillion in overall value and shedding $2.3 trillion from the Nasdaq 100 alone, while the S&P 500 sank 4.36% and the Dow surrendered 1,833 points (-3.44%). Semiconductor stocks faced brutal liquidation as the PHLX Semiconductor Index plummeted 12%, led by historic losses in Nvidia (-$450B), AMD (-17%), and Micron (-17%).

     Chinese equities surged on Thursday driven by a massive rally in Hong Kong where the Hang Seng Index jumped 3.67% to 24,796.98, its strongest session since February 2025. The Hang Seng Tech Index outpaced the market with a 5.5%–5.6% gain, led by Alibaba and Tencent surging over 7%. Mainland benchmarks also rose, with the Shenzhen Component (+1.19%), ChiNext (+0.9%), and STAR board outperforming on strength across semiconductors, solar, and computing power. Sentiment was buoyed by ongoing state support and US midterm election results easing policy friction, propelling the Nasdaq Golden Dragon China Index up 3.5%.

     Benchmark equity indexes in both Japan and South Korea registered heavy losses, with both the Nikkei 225 and the KOSPI plunging by roughly 6% over a single session. Regional tech supply chain stocks, semiconductor manufacturers, and consumer exporters bore the brunt of the market drawdowns as global investors rushed to de-risk portfolios amidst mounting macroeconomic policy uncertainty.

     Wall Street's volatility gauge experienced an extraordinary breakout on Thursday as the VIX surged approximately 70% from 16.61 to 28.18. Marking the third largest single day percentage gain on record and the biggest spike since December 2024, the dramatic move was mathematically magnified by a depressed starting level. Historical precedent offers a surprisingly counter intuitive signal for long term equity investors: following each of the previous five largest single day percentage spikes in the VIX, the S&P 500 benchmark managed to trade higher one month later.

     Semiconductor stocks are currently trading at 13.8 times forward earnings, reflecting a significant 25% discount to the broader S&P 500 and marking the widest valuation gap since December 2018. Investors are weighing whether macroeconomic headwinds and cyclical smartphone weakness outweigh long term tailwinds from artificial intelligence infrastructure and ongoing enterprise hardware upgrades across global markets.

Sources : Opening Bell Daily (11-6), 1% Better (11-6), The Capitalist (11-5)

Thank you for reading
Live your best life,
AL Maulini

It has been a month, and I still can't use AWS. Honestly, I have given up on setting it up.

Here is what happened:

- When you are new to AWS and want to open an account, you will probably create a "Builder Account" on https://t.co/5SG7De5LWH. Supposedly, you can still create servers, but it's not the one you should be using? Either way, this is the one I created, without knowing anything at first.

- To start building, you need to enter your contact details, but for whatever reason, the devs either vibecoded it or are too incompetent to create a working contact details form. Long story short, it doesn't work and prompts you to try again or contact support.

- You contact support, but they never reply. After complaining here on X, David Nalley (@ke4qqq) from Amazon messaged me and offered to help. He took the time to connect with me on LinkedIn, listen to my problem, and forward it internally. It really impressed me, and this is exactly how customer support should be.

You will go far buddy. I wish you all the best.

- Tech support started contacting me on my phone. They told me to log in to the Console, but somehow it didn't work. They said they would try to fix the issue.

- A few days later, they sent me an email stating they had found the issue and resolved it. So I went into my Builder Account and still couldn't enter my contact details. So what did they fix exactly? None knows.

- In the meantime, I had figured out on my own that the Console requires a completely different account, and this is actually the "normal" one. So I created one with the same email address.

- However, ENTERING MY PAYMENT INFO DIDN'T WORK on this one. Jesus Christ, nothing worked. At least this time, it showed an error code, so tech support surely should be able to resolve it?

- I updated my ticket to say that it still didn't work. Tech support called me again, this time a different guy. I explained both problems to him, and he asked me why I was using a "Builder Account" in the first place (this is the default one?). He also said he couldn't enter my contact details manually and would look into it.

- We scheduled a call for the next day at the exact same time. However, I received calls at completely random times when I wasn't available. They stopped contacting me, or maybe reached out from unknown numbers, which I am not accepting.

- Later, they told me I should change my email address on one account and try again, since having two accounts with the same email address may cause problems?

I am sorry, but this is the biggest bullshit ever, and I am not going to spend additional time and effort on this.

Anyone had a similar experience?

text:
This is the abandoned Dunnington Mansion (also known as Poplar Hill), in Farmville, Virginia (Prince Edward County). It is a Victorian/Romanesque Revival mansion (expanded in 1897) with a distinctive conical turret, heavy ivy, and a rare surviving Victorian conservatory with a green-glass dome.

The property has deep history dating to the 1700s as Poplar Hill. Walter Grey Dunnington (a tobacco businessman) and his wife India significantly expanded it in 1897, adding the tower, front entrance, and conservatory (where India grew plants, including a lemon tree). It was abandoned for decades after failed development plans tied to the surrounding Manor Golf Course and suffered water damage and neglect. 

A local nonprofit (Dunnington Mansion Foundation) has been working to preserve it and offers occasional guided tours or photography access. I'm always so glad when a property is preserved, especially one with history like this one.

text:
Musk is claiming that SoftBank has stopped paying for, or is backing out of, orders for the gas turbines meant to power its AI data centers. He’s suggesting SoftBank is running short of cash. It’s an unverified claim. The post names no supplier, no order and no amount, and Musk offered no evidence in it. SoftBank hadn’t responded publicly as of this morning. fourweekmba
Why turbines matter. AI data centers need huge amounts of electricity, and many are building their own natural-gas power plants rather than waiting years for a grid connection. SoftBank’s biggest project is in Ohio: a $33.3 billion power plant with a “large-scale” power generation capacity of 9.2 gigawatts, built to run a 10-gigawatt data center complex. Turbines are extremely scarce, with gas turbine wait times running as long as seven years, according to S&P Global, any lost orders could threaten SoftBank’s plans to deliver OpenAI’s Ohio data centers from 2028. A company doesn’t give up a spot in that line lightly. If the claim is true, this would be the first public sign of an AI “sponsor” walking away from power equipment orders. https://t.co/pvd4fXU1DZ +2

Why to be skeptical.
Musk isn’t neutral. He’s in a long-running feud with Sam Altman of OpenAI, SoftBank’s main bet, and his own company xAI competes with OpenAI.
He’s doubted SoftBank’s finances before. When OpenAI, SoftBank and Oracle first announced the $500 billion Stargate Project in January 2025, Musk shot back on X that the companies involved didn’t really have the money, and claimed SoftBank had secured well under $10 billion of it — a claim Sam Altman publicly disputed. officechai

A missed payment on one order wouldn’t be a debt default, and SoftBank’s bonds aren’t in default.

Why markets are taking it seriously anyway. It landed on a bad week for SoftBank:
Shares fell 11% today and are down almost 50% since September. Substack
Its default protection is now more expensive than the 424 bps I mentioned earlier. SoftBank’s debt insurance costs reached 466 basis points Friday, their highest since October 2022. benzinga
Musk was replying to a post about an anonymous seller auctioning roughly $500 million in data centre loans. The package included a $25 million slice linked to a Stargate site in New Mexico. Substack

The tweet adds to existing worries that SoftBank has overextended itself on AI. The specific claim is still unproven, so watch for a response from SoftBank or the turbine makers (GE Vernova, Siemens Energy, Mitsubishi).

text:
This little auction matters more than everything the Nasdaq 100 lost the same day.

Stocks trade every second, so everybody knows what Nvidia's worth at any moment.

Private data center loans almost never get priced in public like this. And for 2 years, the whole AI boom has been funded on the assumption that this paper's safe.

In 13 days, real buyers have to name a real price.

ING is seeking offers on a dozen loans through a bids wanted in competition process, with bids due November 19 and a $10 million minimum.

The pile includes debt tied to Vantage Data Centers and CyrusOne.

And it includes a $25 million piece tied to the New Mexico site in Stargate, the venture backed by OpenAI, SoftBank and Oracle.

Bloomberg calls this a rare auction of only data center debt. No price has been reported, and ING declined to comment.

$25 million is pocket change on a campus reported at $165 billion, and I won't pretend otherwise.

But just look at which campus it is:

Oracle sent a force majeure notice to the developer of that site in September. That's the legal notice saying events beyond a company's control may excuse it from its obligations. Oracle says the schedule hasn't changed, and it calls these notices commonplace on projects this size.

New Mexico regulators have until November 23 to decide the air permit for the site's power plant.

That's 4 days AFTER the bids are due.

The FT has already reported the project's roughly $18 billion construction loan trading at stressed levels.

So anybody bidding on that slice is putting a price on a permit nobody has yet.

And ING isn't alone:

Startup Fortune, citing Bloomberg, says JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley, SMBC and MUFG have been shopping pieces of AI debt they helped underwrite.

Andrzej Skiba of RBC's BlueBay unit told Bloomberg he's seeing a "massive hedge fund capitulation" in the space.

CoreWeave's 9.625% notes due 2032 last traded around 76 cents on the dollar, for a yield of about 16%.

The cost of insuring CoreWeave's debt was reported around 1,164 basis points this week, close to its October record.

SoftBank's shares fell more than 9% in Tokyo on Friday, and its default insurance hit a 4-year high.

Meanwhile Apple went out for about $7 billion of bonds this week and drew about $31 billion of orders.

That's the tell for me, because lenders still have plenty of money. They're just getting pickier about AI paper.

And the AI trade has needed the opposite. The money behind these campuses has to keep rolling from one lender to the next, and that only works if someone's always willing to take the paper at a good price.

If the next buyer wants a big discount, the bank thinks twice about the next loan. Then the next campus costs more to finance, and eventually somebody's forecast for 2028 falls apart.

Now, a smart person would say I'm making a mountain out of a molehill.

$500 million is a rounding error in a market this big. Banks sell loans every day to manage their books. ING may have decided this months ago for reasons that have nothing to do with AI. Investment grade credit held up fine on Thursday, with LQD up 0.15%. And Oracle reportedly can't terminate the New Mexico lease, which should comfort the lenders.

If ING gets close to full price, I'm wrong and the panic was overdone.

But I think that's the point of watching this, and I'd bet the result leaks.

CoreWeave reports November 10. Nvidia reports November 17. Then the ING bids land on November 19.

I'd pay more attention to the third one.

So who wins this one: ING getting close to full price for those Stargate loans, or a buyer demanding a serious discount?

text:
Banks are starting to run from AI data center debt.

ING has put about $500 million of data center loans up for sale all at once, Bloomberg reports. 

That's 12 loans, including a $25 million piece of OpenAI, SoftBank and Oracle's Stargate site in New Mexico.

Banks are the ones closest to these projects. They see the contracts, the power deals and the delays before anyone else.

And at Stargate, the warning signs are already there. 

Oracle has sent the developer a force majeure notice, a legal step that can excuse it from its obligations if events beyond its control get in the way.

Now the market is turning too.

Yesterday, the S&P 500 lost $3 trillion in a single day as fears grew that Democrats will go after AI and data centers. Junk bonds tied to data center companies like CoreWeave were among the hardest hit.

The whole AI buildout runs on borrowed money. 

Big Tech has raised $326 billion in debt and new shares this year alone to keep it going.

If the lenders are heading for the exit, who'll fund the AI build up?

text:
Good Morning! I’ve had a good sleep and a quiet morning reading fall recipes! 

Pop pop is wanting to go shopping this morning and to the post office, so cabin cleaning is off the itinerary again 🤣😂!!! 

I start to understand why old people have cob webs on their lamp shades…

It was a VERY CRISP 42F this morning and while I was sipping my coffee I saw that “Charles” was migrating from under the tv entertainment center toward the kitchen. “He” goes back and forth as he runs himself out of resources… He also “waters” out of the dog bowl at night. I know  because he taps his durn feet on the hollow stainless steel sides. 

Twice I’ve heard that, got up to see WTF and it was the spider (who also had a WTF moment when I shined an iPhone light at him..). We leave him be, you will find bug skeletons where he’s been hanging out. BUT… if I ever find him on my bed, or on the sofa it’s bye bye 👋🏻 Charles…. 

This is definitely the time of year to check your pockets and shoes for the “Charles or Charlottes” out there.

Pop pop doesn’t often offer to take me shopping, and I don’t often want to go but there are pumpkins (maybe) in a sale bin and a lot of odd things that need to be bought. Water filters, mopping supplies, random things he doesn’t usually have to look for; so I will go. Perhaps I’ll snag a nice candle out of the trip, or some Ohio Apple Cider. Taking me means going over budget 🤣😂 but he knows that. 

Last night the wilds were crazy outside and I had to get up and fuss at the dog twice. We’ve given up (as of last year) in trying to ward off coyotes or whatever else is out there, it’s tiring and impractical. We just do a head count the next morning and if a cat is lost it can’t be helped 😑 in fact this year I’d almost encourage natural selection!!! Next week he have to begin the catch, fix, and release and it is going to be expensive, but not as expensive as more forest cats. 

Oh pop pop is home, here comes my day trip anxiety 🤣. I’m going to try and enjoy the trip, he needs to eat his breakfast first anyway. 

I found some new recipes this morning and one of them is a deer beefy onion and mushroom “meat loaf” in thin slab baked in a casserole or deep sheet pan, this will probably be on meal line up this weekend. Looks like a fall dish, and like it would be amazing in a pie crust or layered with thin slices of potato. I better eat before we go shopping too, or it will be a two buggy trip!

I’m craving baked cabbage so I know that will be on the list, maybe some collards if they are from down here. I need to get the fall 40lb box of Miss Sweet Potatoes 🍠 but we might have missed the window on that this year, and I’m not driving down to dang Vardamon for them!  

Pop Pop is over here laughing at his IG and being a nut 🤣 he’s in a good mood, the cold weather being back is nice. 

I’m going to try real hard to not get beer today. He won’t stay out of it, and so it just needs to be thrown out again. I may have to do like daddy and start hiding “nerve tonic” out in the pump house 🤣🤣🤣!!! 

My mom used to go around looking in his rubber boots, baskets or garden buckets for hootch. She’d smell a whiff of whiskey, and find a bottle of crown - then pour it out. But sometimes he’d get hold of some moonshine and you can’t smell that. We’d have a family party or reunion up here and out of the blue he’d just be half drunk 😂😂😂 and out of control making his bean jokes!!! 

My moms people are all half “inside the spectrum” and were not always prone to finding daddy’s fart jokes (OR WORSE), the actual farts, funny!!! Inevitably then someone would just leave, mother would be mad, and daddy would be laughing so hard he’d have to lay down! Daddy always said it was just cheap entertainment… 😂

Well I’m out of room (plus need to get dressed) I’m going dressed as bad lady! I hope everyone has a great FRIDAY!!!!

text:
Grocery Shopping With a Service Dog in Tampa Bay
Friday, Nov 6, 2026

A grocery run with a working dog is routine under federal and Florida rules. Publix and other Tampa Bay stores welcome trained service animals, not pets or emotional support animals alone.
US Department of Justice ADA guidance says food selling businesses must generally allow a service dog in public areas even when health codes ban animals. Staff may ask only two questions when the need is not obvious: is the dog required because of a disability, and what work or task is it trained to perform. No vest, ID or papers are required. Removal is allowed only if the dog is out of control or not housebroken, and the store must still offer goods without the animal.
Publix Super Markets Service Animal Policy permits a dog or miniature horse trained for disability tasks. Emotional support or companionship alone do not qualify. Keep the animal on a harness, leash or tether unless the disability prevents it. A service dog may not ride in a Publix shopping cart or wheelchair basket attachment. If staff remove an animal that is out of control, a health threat or not housebroken, the shopper may continue with personal shopping help.
Florida Statutes 413.08 treats grocery stores as public accommodations. You may bring a service dog into areas customers normally use. No surcharge is allowed. Unlawful denial can be a second degree misdemeanor.
Clearwater Public Library System bars non service animals indoors, so working dogs belong with their handlers in reading rooms too.
Here in Tampa Bay, teams like Odin and Ski know a calm grocery run takes practice.
If a store turns you away, contact @PinellasGov Office of Human Rights at 727 464 4880, or the ADA Information Line at 800 514 0301.
Watch Dogs of Service from Iowa PBS on YouTube

Sources: US Department of Justice ADA Requirements Service Animals, Publix Super Markets Service Animal Policy, Florida Statutes 413.08, Clearwater Public Library System Code of Conduct, Pinellas County Office of Human Rights, photos via Wikimedia Commons and Odin by DigitalAssetsUS.

text:
The Charges
•Primary Charge: Class C Felony (Vehicular Homicide by reckless, willful, or wanton disregard under Iowa Code § 707.6A). Under Iowa law, using an electronic/cell phone device while driving serves as prima facie evidence (legal presumption) that you were driving recklessly. [1, 2]
•
•Alternative/Plea Options: Prosecutors may alternatively charge or offer a plea deal for involuntary manslaughter (also a Class D felony or aggravated misdemeanor depending on the specific circumstances). [1, 2]
•

Prison Time and Penalties
•Maximum Prison Sentence: Up to 10 years in a state prison for a Class C felony vehicular homicide conviction. [1]
•
•Fines: A criminal fine ranging from $1,000 to $10,000 (plus court costs, surcharges, and mandatory restitution—which can include $150,000 or more to the victim's family). [1, 2]
•
•Actual Time Served:
◦A 10-year maximum sentence does not automatically mean a full 10 years behind bars; actual time served depends on parole board decisions, good behavior credits, and the specifics handed down by the judge.
◦Past Iowa sentencing examples for fatal phone-related crashes range from probation or a couple of years in prison to full multi-year prison sentences (for instance, recent Iowa sentencings for cell phone vehicular homicide have resulted in up to 10 years in prison). Judges have the discretion to suspend parts of a sentence or grant probation depending on your criminal history and the nature of the crash, though prosecutors often push for active prison time.[1, 2, 3]

Good morning, 

It’s 10am in Miami and here is a recap of events in the Robotics space that caught my eye. Part 5

     Agility Robotics has officially become the first humanoid robot company to go public in the United States, marking a major milestone for commercial automation. Spun out of Oregon State University, the firm manufactures Digit, a bipedal robot designed to handle repetitive manual tasks and physical labor in logistics and warehousing operations where labor shortages remain acute. Wall Street is watching the listing closely to see if general purpose humanoid robots can transition from specialized technology demonstrations into scalable, profitable commercial deployments.

     Startup Undaunted has deployed human operated robot dogs to patrol an Atlanta apartment complex at night. A viral video featuring the quadrupeds racked up nearly two million views, while company representatives claim reported burglaries at one monitored property stopped entirely following their adoption. The successful pilot showcases growing commercial demand for teleoperated robotic security units to deter local crime and monitor residential communities cost effectively.

     Moonwalkers Dusk offers an innovative leap in personal transportation through AI-powered robotic shoe attachments. Using onboard algorithms that continuously adapt to the wearer's unique stride, these lightweight devices smoothly accelerate standard walking speeds up to a full running pace with minimal effort or loss of balance. Designed to blend human biomechanics with robotics, Moonwalkers Dusk provides a hands free, energy efficient mobility option ideal for urban commuters, warehouse workers, and individuals seeking efficient travel without altered movement dynamics.

This was a multi-agency effort. The U.S. Marshals Service (including the Western District of Tennessee, which had been assisting since the escape at the request of the Tennessee Department of Correction, plus other districts and the Midwest Violent Fugitive Task Force) participated throughout the manhunt and in the apprehension alongside MSHP, Kansas City and Independence police, Homeland Security Investigations, local Illinois and Missouri agencies, the TBI, Tennessee Highway Patrol, and others. U.S. Marshal Tyreece Miller stated the Service and partners had been in “relentless pursuit” for nine days. 

Earlier, a combined reward of up to $17,500 (including contributions from the U.S. Marshals, TBI, and Tennessee officials) had been offered.

A deputy U.S. Marshal later interviewed Morley at the Lafayette County jail; he admitted to the escape, the truck thefts, and taking the firearms. He faced federal charges in Missouri for being a felon in possession of a firearm, plus planned additional state charges in Tennessee (and likely Illinois/Missouri) related to the escape and thefts. He was held pending return to Tennessee custody.

🔺Background🔺
Morley was serving a life sentence (with a distant parole eligibility date) after a 2025 conviction for the 2022 first-degree murder of co-worker Cody Birchfield in Carter County, Tennessee. Birchfield’s body was found in a box under Morley’s home after he had been missing for weeks; Morley was also convicted of aggravated burglary, tampering with evidence, vandalism, and evading arrest. When deputies came to his home in 2022, he fled and led officers on a chase into North Carolina. Descriptions listed him as roughly 5’11”–6’0”, 240–270 lbs, with brown hair and green eyes; post-escape photos showed him with a fuller reddish beard, glasses, and a cap.
Photos from the scene show him in custody wearing a camouflage hoodie (reportedly from a local business in the Marion area) near the stuck truck.

text:
One cool thing about the whole MCU, to me anyway, is that Iron Man was a left over. When Marvel was going bankrupt, they offered the movie rights to Sony for 25 million dollars. Sony said "Nah, we just want Spider-man" Fox snapped up The X-men and Fantastic Four, and those were the 3 biggest sellers in the Marvel Line. Iron Man, Thor, Captain America, Hollywood didn't give a damn about.
Then Iron Man came out. and it was incredibly well done. It offered a compelling story, good acting, decent special effects. And it only offered the opportunity of future fun stories like that at the end. Not even the end but the post credit scene with Nick Fury. 
Iron Man seduced you into liking the MCU. It was a story Just about Iron Man, It had the Iron Man characters like Pepper Pots and Jarvis, but no extra characters. No hint of a bigger universe until after the end.
Universal tried to create their own cinematic Universe and it makes sense. It is easier and I imagine cheaper to tell stories in a shared universe than having to rebuild the world for each release. It helps if the audience already knows something about the world the story takes place in. 
But they blew it. First they introduce Russell Crowe as Henry Jeckyll, exposing the idea of a shared universe way to early. Where Iron Man was, again, after the end of the movie, "Hey, if you like we can see each other again" Universal's Mummy came across as someone who wanted a relationship on the first date and brings the kids on that first date.
Fan investment in a franchise is just that, an emotional investment. The MCU did have a break in that dealing with these "forgotten" stories and characters, the stories are less well known. Everyone knows Bruce Wayne is Batman and Superman grew in Kansas, far fewer folks knew who Tony Stark was, or how Cap ended up with the Super Soldier Serum running through his veins. But the MCU also took it slow, rolled the characters out one by one before teaming them all up. That made a huge difference.
In both respects, The MCU and the DCU are mining almost 80 years of comic book history. Who does it better is in the eye of the audience.

text:
Elon Dismisses American Culture 

When Musk or others argue for the H1-B program they forget that American will be displaced and American culture will go with it.

He and others also forget that the great Milton Friedman lived at a time when international travel and global interactions were uncommon. That an immigration attorney was often required to make it happen and the numbers so small that culture would not be changed. None of that is true today. Anyone with access to the internet can fill out the forms and they are off and running.

People like Elon will often say "it makes all of us wealthier" yet they forget that a living and breathing. person was displaced and in this Americans view, long before Elon, it's one person too many. 

When in a bar or a club and discussing the topic with your friend remember that the rush to the top is artificial. Worse, it's grounded in ideas antithetical to the founding of this country. Elon wouldn't know that because his forefathers were not there.

We don’t have to default to “we don’t have enough of X right now, so let’s import Y from country Z.” 

There are multiple ways to solve labor shortages using American workers: higher pay, better conditions, training, relocation incentives, and waiting for domestic supply to respond.

Immigration should return to a small, lottery-based system, plus marriage, with a limited, capped number of reciprocal work visas. Reciprocal seasonal work visas would also be reasonable.

The so-called “genius” visa is largely unnecessary. With modern communications and remote work, top talent doesn’t need to relocate here to contribute. 

The “talent” visa is worse in a different way: it undercuts the long-standing American idea that anyone can learn and improve. It accelerates the shift toward pure credential-chasing and treats ability as something that must be imported rather than developed. 

There’s also no guarantee their children will maintain that edge regression to the mean is common when starting from the top.

Why do we need these expansions now? A company can train a college graduate. A town can wait for someone to finish a trade certification. A hospital can raise pay and offer relocation assistance to get a nurse to Rock Springs, Wyoming, or anywhere else. Domestic adjustments take time, but they keep the system from permanently expanding.

𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗽𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗺 𝗮𝗹𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗱𝘆 𝗵𝗮𝗻𝗱𝗹𝗲𝘀

SunPump (https://t.co/7fcQGGdBj7) was TRON's first meme token launchpad, and the same rules apply to every token on it:

➜ No presale
➜ No team allocation
➜ Price found on a bonding curve
➜ Graduation to SunSwap V2 liquidity, automatically, once the curve fills

So there's no way to set aside a private bag before launch. If you want some of your own token, you buy it from the curve on the same terms as everyone else.

I'd call that an advantage. Hidden supply is the top reason buyers walk away from new memes, and here that worry is settled before anyone raises it.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗰𝗼𝘀𝘁 𝗼𝗳 𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗿𝘆

As of Oct 2026:

➜ About 20 TRX to create a token
➜ A 1% fee on each trade while the token sits on the bonding curve

Cheap enough to experiment, yet not so free that spamming costs nothing. And because 100% of SunPump protocol revenue goes into the SUN buyback, your launch fee ends up feeding the broader ecosystem too.

𝗕𝗲𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗲 𝘆𝗼𝘂 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱: 𝗳𝗶𝗻𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗿𝗲𝗮𝘀𝗼𝗻

Can you finish this sentence? "Someone would hold this because…"

➜ It's an in-joke your community already laughs at
➜ It captures a moment or a culture people care about
➜ It gives an existing group a flag to rally around

If that sentence stays blank, the market will probably leave it blank too.

𝗪𝗵𝗶𝗹𝗲 𝘆𝗼𝘂 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱: 𝗴𝗲𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗱𝗲𝘁𝗮𝗶𝗹𝘀 𝗿𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁

On-chain, the name, ticker, image and description you pick are permanent. There's no second first impression.

➜ Choose a ticker that's simple to say and unlikely to be mistaken for one that already exists
➜ Describe the token truthfully, with zero promises about returns
➜ Use art you made or have rights to, never another brand or a real person's likeness

And never hint at a tie to a project, person or company unless that tie is real. Nothing burns trust faster.

New to all this? Since December 23, 2024, SunPump has offered a chat assistant it calls "the first AI agent on TRON", and with it, creating a token is just a conversation. You explain what you want in everyday language and it guides you through the launch. Still, check every field before confirming, because your wallet signs and the result is yours.

𝗔𝘁 𝗹𝗮𝘂𝗻𝗰𝗵: 𝗯𝗲 𝗲𝗮𝘀𝘆 𝘁𝗼 𝘁𝗿𝘂𝘀𝘁

The rules take care of supply. You take care of reputation.

➜ Post the contract address from a single official place, so copycats can't fool anyone
➜ Promise nothing about price, returns or "guarantees"
➜ Holding part of the supply yourself? Disclose it plainly
➜ Plan to be around after launch day, not only on it

𝗔𝗳𝘁𝗲𝗿 𝗹𝗮𝘂𝗻𝗰𝗵: 𝗴𝗿𝗮𝗱𝘂𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗶𝘀 𝗮𝘂𝘁𝗼𝗺𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗰

You have no say in that step, and that's exactly where the value lies. Nobody, you included, can remove that base liquidity afterwards, which tells buyers the rules can't be bent.

INSANE STORY 👇

John Harbaugh was reportedly FURIOUS after the Titans shut the Giants out of trade discussions for star DT Jeffery Simmons, per Michael Silver of The Athletic.

Titans GM Mike Borgonzi and Bears GM Ryan Poles, who are longtime friends and former roommates, reportedly worked out a deal behind the scenes without allowing other interested teams to negotiate.

Silver reports:

“What bothered Harbaugh, along with several current and former GMs I’ve spoken to, is that the Simmons deal appeared to be an off-the-grid transaction, the product of a private pact between two friends.”

After Giants GM Joe Schoen was unable to get anywhere with Tennessee, Harbaugh reportedly took matters into his own hands.

“When Schoen got nowhere with Borgonzi and Harbaugh began hearing chatter that a Simmons trade might be in the works, he essentially said, ‘To hell with this,’ and reached out to Borgonzi’s boss.”

Harbaugh personally contacted Titans owner Amy Adams Strunk in an attempt to open trade discussions.

That move reportedly upset some NFL executives, with one GM accusing Harbaugh of violating an unwritten “code” that primary decision-makers should only deal with one another.

Silver described Harbaugh’s reaction:

“Harbaugh’s reaction to that (and mine, for that matter): disdainful laughter.”

However, Silver clarified that the Giants likely weren’t going to beat Chicago’s offer anyway:

“The point wasn’t that the Giants would have outbid the Bears — in this case, they wouldn’t have — but that shutting them out of the process was absurd.”

Harbaugh wasn’t necessarily upset about losing out on Simmons. He was upset that the Giants were never given a chance to compete for him.

Harbaugh clearly isn’t afraid to step on some toes to improve his roster. 👀

text:
answer to your question: @I_Am_JohnCullen 

The Learjet 60 (N722BD) was flying from Austin, Texas to North Eleuthera (ELH) in the Bahamas. During the flight the crew requested and received clearance to route via FIMED and then direct to Freeport (a common routing toward the Bahamas).
The claim that the plane was deliberately 50+ miles off course to target Mar-a-Lago is not supported by the available data. The aircraft was flying over South Florida while heading east toward the Bahamas. Air traffic control had warned the crew about heavy precipitation on the turn toward Freeport and had explicitly approved left or right deviations for weather, with “Freeport when able.” 

The crew reported manageable ice and moderate turbulence and indicated they were proceeding direct to Freeport. Shortly afterward the plane entered a rapid, uncontrolled descent and crashed in Greenacres, roughly 6–7 miles from Mar-a-Lago.ATC does not normally force a turn when a crew requests weather deviations and says they are managing conditions. 

Once the Mayday was declared with extreme descent rates, controllers could only monitor and offer assistance—they cannot physically control the aircraft. The NTSB investigation is focused on weather (icing, turbulence, precipitation) and the apparent in-flight breakup.
